item:99-year-old-port.text: 99-Year-Old Port. At Ratchet's docks, a bottle of 99-Year-Old Port has gone missing. Mad Magglish took it in a cargo spill and fled toward the Wailing Caverns. Crane Operator Bigglefuzz overloaded his crane while unloading a large shipment from Booty Bay in Ratchet. Crates crashed across the docks. In the confusion, Mad Magglish seized a bottle of 99-Year-Old Port and fled into the hills toward the Wailing Caverns.

item:a-bloodstained-journal-page.text: A Bloodstained Journal Page. During the investigation into Stalvan Mistmantle, Commander Althea Ebonlocke has a torn, bloodstained journal page examined. A few words remain legible, so she asks Clerk Daltry to compare its handwriting with the Town Registry. Commander Althea Ebonlocke watches over Darkshire and asks for the handwriting on a torn, bloodstained page to be examined. Thick blood covers it, but a few words remain legible. Clerk Daltry is asked to compare them with the Town Registry.

item:a-clue-to-sanders-treasure.text:
A Clue to Sanders' Treasure. In Westfall, A Clue to Sanders' Treasure leads seekers farther along Captain Sanders' trail. It marks the second step in a hunt across the bluffs and coastlines. After following Captain Sanders' first treasure map, you find a parchment pointing farther inland into Westfall. Its scrawled note sends you east from the coast and up the bluffs toward the main road.

Near crumbling stone ruins and an abandoned chimney, an old barrel marks where Sanders hid the next clue. The trail leads deeper into the troubled farmlands.

item:a-dusty-unsent-letter.text:
A Dusty Unsent Letter. In Moonbrook, an unsent letter bears on Stalvan Mistmantle’s past. Found in an old footlocker, it confirms that he lived there before his disappearance. Investigators searching Moonbrook find an unsent letter in an old footlocker. Darkshire’s town registry still lists Stalvan Mistmantle’s last address as the Moonbrook Schoolhouse. Clerk Daltry wants to know if he truly lived there. The letter confirms that Stalvan resided in the Westfall township for a time.

Finding the letter disturbs a vengeful Forlorn Spirit. The spirit guards the remnants of Stalvan’s past with bitter malice.

item:a-faded-journal-page.text: A Faded Journal Page. In eastern Elwynn, an old page lies unread in Marshal Haggard's home, tied to Stalvan Mistmantle's grim history. For years, the Faded Journal Page lay in an old trunk at Marshal Haggard's home near Elwynn Forest's eastern border. Haggard had retired there, but failing eyesight kept him from reading the weathered parchment. The page remained neglected until investigators seeking the truth about Stalvan Mistmantle retrieved it.

item:a-letter-to-grelin-whitebeard.text: A Letter to Grelin Whitebeard. A letter from Ironforge reaches Grelin Whitebeard at his camp in Coldridge Valley. Its news and instructions bring the mountain capital close to the snowy frontier. Grelin Whitebeard receives a dispatch from Ironforge at his camp in Coldridge Valley. Anvilmar offers shelter, but the valley lies far from its safety. Letters link scouts and scholars in the field with the halls of the mountain capital. This one has come south along the mountain paths to reach him.

item:a-mysterious-message.text: A Mysterious Message. In Westfall, a courier's intercepted message gives the People's Militia proof of who directs the Defias Brotherhood.

item:a-simple-compass.text: A Simple Compass. At the burned Alexston Farmstead in Westfall, A Simple Compass lies in a small chest. It belonged to Baros Alexston before he became Stormwind's City Architect. Baros Alexston grew up working his family's farm in Westfall. His first instrument for finding his way was a simple compass. It may have kindled his interest in geometry, drafting, and exploration. Then the Defias Brotherhood raided and burned the farmstead, leaving the compass in a sturdy chest among the ruins as bandits overran the farmland. Baros's father escaped the destruction, but could not carry the family's possessions to safety. Inside Stormwind City's stone walls, the compass has little use to a master builder. Yet it means much to Baros. Its return would restore a rare, intact link to his humble beginnings and the peaceful countryside of his childhood.

item:a-stack-of-letters.text:
A Stack of Letters. In Coldridge Valley, a stack of letters has come through the mountain pass for scouts in the snowy wilderness. Letters for Coldridge Valley come from Anvilmar by way of travelers crossing the pass. The road to the remote camps in Dun Morogh's mountains is hard, so postal runners rely on travelers to carry each bundle onward. This one is bound for scouts deeper in Coldridge Valley.

Until the letters are sorted, Talin Keeneye at his lakeside camp is thought to be the only recipient. Among them is a missive for Grelin Whitebeard, a mountaineer.

item:a-torn-journal-page.text: A Torn Journal Page. In Stormwind, A Torn Journal Page carries a clue to Stalvan Mistmantle's past. Its worn script points toward old records in Elwynn Forest. A Torn Journal Page rests in a sealed storage crate beside Stormwind City's canals. Forgotten personal effects surround it, including old books, family heirlooms, and a ceramic vase. The writing points to Stalvan Mistmantle's past, though the page is damaged and hard to read. Who in the kingdom might know that hand?

item:abercrombie-s-crate.text: Abercrombie's Crate. Near the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound, Abercrombie's Crate waits for its owner. Ogres drove him off while he gathered herbs, leaving his delicate tools behind. Abercrombie left his shack in western Duskwood to gather plants. Far from home, he met a hostile band of ogres and fled for his life. He left his crate of instruments and gathered plants behind. The ogres carried it to the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound, where the heavy chest rests near the cave mouth.

item:admiral-proudmoore-s-orders.text: Admiral Proudmoore's Orders. Kul Tiras forces still hold the coast in Durotar, guided by Admiral Proudmoore's Orders. Written before Daelin Proudmoore fell at Theramore, the papers describe a campaign against the Horde. At Tiragarde Keep, Kul Tiras forces still mean to fight. Lieutenant Benedict's garrison holds papers detailing long-term maneuvers and fortifications against the Horde. Daelin Proudmoore's offensive in Durotar was an organized campaign, planned to continue after his death. For the Horde, these papers reveal Kul Tiras operations and possible reinforcements along its borders.

item:ados-fragment.text: Ados Fragment. At Whelgar's Excavation, Ados Fragment lies among three lost pieces of the Goaz Stone. The four shards together form an ancient relic carved with Titan inscriptions. Ados Fragment is one of four pieces Prospector Whelgar needs to restore the Goaz Stone at Whelgar's Excavation. Before raptors overran the dig site, Whelgar began translating the main tablet. Its inscriptions broke off at crucial moments. The four pieces are named Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru. They were lost across the ruins in ancient containers and dirt mounds, among prowling beasts.

item:agamand-family-axe.text: Agamand Family Axe. At Agamand Mills, the family’s old axe is among the arms Coleman Farthing seeks. Once held by wealthy mill owners, it now figures in his effort to strip the undead Agamands of their remaining dignity. Before the Third War, the Agamand dynasty held land across the northern hills of Tirisfal Glades. Vast mills and a family crypt marked their estate. The Agamand Family Axe rested with the ancestral arms, beside the buried patriarchs and warriors. The Scourge overran the estate and slaughtered its people, but the weapons stayed on racks underground. The Scourge raised the fallen Agamands as mindless thralls to the Lich King. Their former servant Coleman Farthing survived in undeath, bitter toward his old masters. He blames the family for his own death, so he sends Forsaken wanderers into the crypt to take the axe, sword, mace, and dagger from the racks. Farthing wants every last trace of the Agamand heritage erased.

item:agamand-family-dagger.text: Agamand Family Dagger. In northern Tirisfal, Coleman Farthing seeks the Agamand Family Dagger and the household’s other arms. He means to strip his former masters of their legacy and honor. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held vast estates and grain mills in northern Tirisfal Glades. The Scourge broke their power, yet their weapons remained in the family crypt north of Agamand Mills. Restless members of the household and mindless servants of the Lich King guard the dagger. It recalls the martial heritage and standing the family once held above its servants and tenants. Coleman Farthing lives at Brill, but he died in the Agamands’ service. He blames the family for his death, so the dagger means resentment to him, not noble lineage. Farthing sends adventurers into the Agamand Family Crypt for the dagger, sword, axe, and mace. He seeks to rob the Scourge patriarchs of their last dignity and extinguish the Agamand name.

item:agamand-family-mace.text: Agamand Family Mace. At Agamand Mills, the Agamand Family Mace remains sealed in the family crypt. Once the heirloom of a proud family in northern Lordaeron, it is now sought by their former servant, Coleman Farthing. Before the Third War, the Agamands held vast farmlands and windmills in northern Tirisfal Glades. Like the region’s other aristocrats, they fell to the plague of undeath. The Scourge raised them as mindless thralls in service to the Lich King, and now they wander their ruined estate. Their ancient treasures remain locked in the family crypt. Among them lies the Agamand Family Mace, a remnant of a lineage brought low.

item:agamand-family-sword.text:
Agamand Family Sword. In northern Tirisfal, the Agamand Family Sword remains in the family crypt. The tarnished blade once marked the wealth and standing of the mill-owning dynasty. Coleman Farthing now seeks it to erase their legacy. The Agamands once held wealth and influence through their mills in northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, the family met a gruesome end. Their bodies rose as mindless thralls of the Lich King.

Their ancestral weapons, including the ceremonial sword, were sealed inside the Agamand Family Crypt at the northern edge of the mills. Taking the blades from their burial racks is meant to break the memory and noble standing of the fallen household.

item:ahanu-s-leather-goods.text: Ahanu's Leather Goods. At Ahanu's Leather Goods, finished leather armor and supplies leave Thunder Bluff for the Crossroads. Ahanu sends them to travelers in the Barrens. Ahanu prepares leather goods in Thunder Bluff for trade beyond Mulgore. The leatherworker turns raw hides into finished apparel and gear for Jahan Hawkwing, a merchant at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Overland travel across the plains is slow, so the tauren send the parcel by air. Tal and Devrak's trained wind riders carry goods swiftly over long distances.

item:alaric-s-remains.text: Alaric's Remains. In Silverpine Forest, Alaric's bones lie far from the Fenris Isle he called home. His spirit asks travelers to carry them past the Rot Hide gnolls and into Fenris Keep. Alaric's bones were unearthed from a shallow grave in Silverpine Forest. He once lived on Fenris Isle and cherished the place. Now his spirit asks whoever finds his bones to leave behind his ill-fitting boots and carry his remains directly into Fenris Keep, beyond the reach of mainland scavengers.

item:alien-egg.text: Alien Egg. Wind serpents guard an unfamiliar clutch in Thousand Needles, and tauren scouts at Freewind Post want to know why. Alien Egg lies at the base of spires south and northeast of Freewind Post. Native wind serpents guard it beside their own nests, though such a clutch is strange among the life on the canyon floor. Hagar Lightninghoof, a tauren brave watching from Freewind Post, wants to retrieve it. He hopes to learn whether it threatens the mesa settlements or is simply an unusual local reptile.

item:alterac-granite.text: Alterac Granite. Near Darrow Hill in the northern Hillsbrad Foothills, Alterac Granite draws master stonecutters with its resilience and grain. King Magni Bronzebeard’s royal mason insists on the stone for a tribute to fallen soldiers. King Magni Bronzebeard ordered a monument to Sully Balloo, a brave dwarven defender who died in the tragedy at the Thandol Span. Grand Mason Marblesten was charged with sculpting it in Ironforge. He insisted on Alterac Granite instead of ordinary quarry stone. Few stones in the Eastern Kingdoms are finer, and its durability keeps a fallen hero’s likeness and memory untarnished for generations. Alterac Granite lies around Darrow Hill in the northern Hillsbrad Foothills, near the ruined territories of Alterac. Hostile wildlife, syndicate brigands and lingering strife make the journey perilous. To bring unblemished slabs to Ironforge’s artisans, you must venture deep into contested lands.

item:altered-snapjaw-shell.text:
Altered Snapjaw Shell. At the Lushwater and Stagnant Oases, snapjaws bear altered shells that concern a druid. Their carapaces may show how the Barrens’ deep fissures affect local wildlife. Oasis snapjaws have changed in ways that trouble those who study the land. The freshwater turtles of Lushwater and Stagnant Oases are believed to drink from springs fed by mysterious underground fissures. Their altered carapaces have drawn the attention of researchers at the Crossroads.

Tonga Runetotem, a tauren druid, gathers the shells to learn about the land’s health. He seeks to discover whether energies rising from deep below are an unnatural blight or something stranger.

item:ambercorn.text: Ambercorn. Across Mulgore, tauren gather ambercorn beneath ancient trees for the Water of the Seers, a brew used in the Rite of Vision. Beneath Mulgore’s great trees, ambercorn falls onto the grass for tauren to gather. Tauren see these nuts as bearers of the land’s spiritual vitality and latent magic. Their mystics have understood and used that power for generations. Young hunters and wanderers learn to watch the ground beneath the canopy and honor the Earth Mother’s gifts. In Bloodhoof Village, seer Zarlman Two-Moons prepares young tauren for the Rite of Vision with ambercorn. He combines it with stones gathered from the plains’ water wells to make the Water of the Seers. Initiates drink the ceremonial brew before the ancestral flames. Their senses shift, revealing a guiding spirit animal meant to lead them to their next destination.

item:amethyst-phial.text:
Amethyst Phial. In Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage entrusts travelers with the Amethyst Phial. They take it to the Oracle Glade and gather water from the moonwell beneath the Oracle Tree. Corithras Moonrage gives travelers on Teldrassil the Amethyst Phial. It is the final vessel in the Crown of the Earth pilgrimage. They carry it to the Oracle Glade in the far northwest of the boughs.

Beneath the Oracle Tree’s ancient canopy lies the island’s first and most potent moonwell. Travelers dip the phial into its radiant waters to gather the essence of Elune’s grace. Druids and priestesses study and tend the World Tree’s unpredictable growth with that water.

item:an-undelivered-letter.text: An Undelivered Letter. In Goldshire, an old letter waits in the Lion's Pride Inn, carrying a clue to Stalvan Mistmantle's past. Years ago, a storm drove a traveling courier to the Lion's Pride Inn for shelter. Near midnight, fear sent the messenger downstairs in his sleeping clothes and out into the pouring rain. He vanished and never returned. In an upstairs chest, he left his belongings and a letter from Stalvan Mistmantle addressed to an estate in Stormwind City's Canal District.

item:anaya-s-pendant.text:
Anaya's Pendant. Across Ameth'Aran, Anaya's Pendant remains with the tormented spirit of Anaya Dawnrunner. Cerellean Whiteclaw still grieves for the love he lost when the Sundering shattered their world. Ten thousand years ago, the Well of Eternity was destroyed and the ancient kaldorei city of Ameth'Aran fell into ruin. Cerellean Whiteclaw believed his beloved Anaya had perished. He carried his grief into a long sleep beside Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage.

After waking, Cerellean wandered Darkshore and found Anaya's tormented apparition drifting through Ameth'Aran with the pendant. He cannot raise a hand against her himself. So he asks travelers to free her spirit and recover the heirloom.

item:ancient-moonstone-seal.text: Ancient Moonstone Seal. In Bashal'Aran, the Ancient Moonstone Seal holds Asterion captive among the ruins. The Highborne forged it long before the Sundering, binding his spirit with arcane magic. Athrikus Narassin, Asterion's former master, forged the Ancient Moonstone Seal to bind his soul to Bashal'Aran's pillars. The Highborne sorcerer made it an unbreakable anchor while the Well of Eternity still stood and Queen Azshara reigned. More than ten millennia later, Asterion remains a spirit bound by its magic. No strength or spell he commands can break the ward.

item:ancient-statuette.text:
Ancient Statuette. On Ashenvale's northwestern shore, Talen searches for the Ancient Statuette he recovered from Zoram's sunken ruins. The night elf effigy came from a city lost beneath the waves. Off Ashenvale's northwestern shore, Zoram lies beneath the waves. The night elven city was lost in the Sundering ten thousand years ago. Recently, explorer Talen surveyed its ruins from a small craft, seeking relics from the past. Then naga attacked and drove him ashore.

Talen fled and left most of his belongings behind. Among them was the Ancient Statuette he had dredged from the ruins. It lies in the tideline sand near his scuttled skiff. Talen calls the statuette his most prized possession. It was the reason he braved the monster-infested coast. He believes the effigy can help him decipher Zoram's architecture, history, and arcane secrets. All lie hidden beneath the surf of Zoram Strand.

item:andron-s-ledger.text: Andron's Ledger. In the Undercity, Andron's Ledger draws the Deathstalkers' attention. A Forsaken operative has uncovered information about threats to their realm.

item:another-clue-to-sanders-treasure.text: Another Clue to Sanders' Treasure. In Westfall, a scrap of Captain Sanders' parchment points toward his next hidden marker. Captain Sanders hid his stolen riches across Westfall, leaving riddles and buried markers instead of one map that could be seized. This scrap carries the trail onward from the previous hiding place. It says to turn north and seek a discarded jug beside a lonely windmill above the sea cliffs.

item:arikara-serpent-skin.text: Arikara Serpent Skin. At Darkcloud Pinnacle, Arikara is called into the world and slain. Her hide is carried to Whitereach Post as proof the wind serpent is dead. Arikara is a mighty wind serpent bound to ancient tauren legend. Some say she seeks revenge on Cairne Bloodhoof as tauren ways change. At Elder Magatha Grimtotem's bidding, champions ready enchanted Incendia Powder. They cast it onto the sacred fire atop Darkcloud Pinnacle's burial bluffs and draw the spirit-beast into the physical realm. Arikara's hide is taken as proof of her death.

item:arnak-s-hoof.text:
Arnak's Hoof. On Darkcloud Pinnacle, Arnak Grimtotem awaits execution for murder and kidnapping. Freewind Post's defenders marked him for death after he killed a fellow tauren and took the tauren's sister. Across Thousand Needles, Arnak Grimtotem is feared as an outlaw. His brutality has crossed even the bitter divisions among tauren clans. He murdered a fellow tauren and abducted the victim’s sister, Lakota Windsong.

So the defenders of Freewind Post marked him for execution and set a bounty on his death. Arnak took refuge on Darkcloud Pinnacle, guarded by Grimtotem. His severed hoof proves to Cliffwatcher Longhorn at Freewind Post that the murderer has answered for his crimes.

item:astor-s-letter-of-introduction.text: Astor's Letter of Introduction. Astor Hadren carries a letter between Silverpine Forest and the Undercity. Deathstalkers use it to investigate Andron Gant, a shopkeeper Lord Varimathras suspects of leaking Forsaken intelligence. Astor Hadren carries messages between Silverpine Forest and the Undercity. His letter gives its bearer credentials with illicit contacts in the city. Mennet Carkad, a Deathstalker handler, needs to investigate suspicious leaks there. Astor's travels make him a target. An operative can kill him and take his papers, then assume his identity and intercept the covert messages meant for him.

item:ataeric-s-staff.text:
Ataeric's Staff. At the Sepulcher, Ataeric's Staff marks a victory over Dalaran's reach in Silverpine Forest. Archmage Ataeric wielded it to command the local ley lines. Shadow Priest Allister feared Dalaran's growing reach in magic, so he ordered Ataeric killed and demanded the staff. Once Ataeric was slain and the staff recovered, the concentrated ley energies sank back into dormancy.

The staff's arrival at the Sepulcher marked a clear victory over Dalaran's ambitions. Power still lies latent in the earth, and the Forsaken remain watchful.

item:athrikus-narassin-s-head.text: Athrikus Narassin's Head. At the Tower of Althalaxx, Athrikus Narassin's Head proves the ancient warlock is dead. The coven's demonic work in northern Darkshore has been disrupted.

item:bag-of-empty-ooze-containers.text: Bag of Empty Ooze Containers. In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle supplies empty jars for his study of Azeroth’s oozes. He means them to hold clean slime gathered in the wild. Laris Geardawdle studies the strange biology of Azeroth’s oozes. He found that they quickly take on the corruption around them, including Felwood’s tainted residues. So he commissioned sturdy jars that can hold acidic specimens without harming them. The bag carries enough jars to gather clean slime in wild regions, especially Un’Goro Crater, where ancient glutinous oozes live free of demonic taint.

item:balnir-snapdragons.text: Balnir Snapdragons. At Balnir Farmstead, snapdragons still bloom as the Scourge's corruption presses toward Tirisfal Glades. The Forsaken study their sensitivity to magic to watch that corruption's spread. Balnir Snapdragons still bloom in the garden of Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades. The homestead lies in ruin after Lordaeron fell and the Scourge rose. To the east, the Plaguelands border Tirisfal. The Lich King's blight presses against the region here, and the flowers give the Forsaken a place to watch its spread. Balnir Snapdragons are unusually sensitive to atmospheric magic, so they serve as living barometers for magical blights. Anastasia Hartwell and the Forsaken mages in the Undercity seek fresh flowers from the farmstead's window boxes. They send them to the Royal Apothecary Society for study, hoping to measure how far the Lich King's plague has seeped across the border into Tirisfal's soil.

item:baron-longshore-s-head.text: Baron Longshore's Head. Along the Merchant Coast, Baron Longshore's Head proves the pirate captain is dead. Gazlowe offers a bounty for identifiable remains to protect Ratchet's commercial shipping. From camps along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, Baron Longshore led Southsea Freebooter raids. His flagship, the Heedless, threatened goblin trade lanes between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. So Gazlowe, Ratchet's Chief Engineer, offered a bounty for proof of Longshore's death. The port authority pays a monetary reward when the pirate's head is delivered.

item:barrel-of-barleybrew-scalder.text: Barrel of Barleybrew Scalder. At Kharanos, Marleth Barleybrew sends a cask of Scalder toward the Thunderbrew Distillery. He means to prove his brewing can rival the Thunderbrews, his chief competitors. The Thunderbrews and Barleybrews contend fiercely over brewing in Dun Morogh. The Thunderbrews are renowned for their busy distillery in Kharanos. Marleth Barleybrew will not live in their shadow. So he brews fiery Scalder to show his recipes can rival theirs. He hopes those who taste it will see the Thunderbrews do not own the art of fine dwarven drink.

item:barrel-of-shimmer-stout.text: Barrel of Shimmer Stout. In Dun Morogh, a barrel of Shimmer Stout is bound for the mountain watch. Rejold Barleybrew sends his experimental ale to the high passes, where drinkers say it brightens their vision. Rejold Barleybrew made Shimmer Stout from ingredients gathered across Dun Morogh. The recipe is the newest work of the Barleybrew family. Its dwarven brewers vie to make ales hearty enough for the mountain cold. Rejold brewed this stout to warm the gut and sharpen the senses of those posted in the wind. The barrel is bound for Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew at the southern tower on the pass into Loch Modan. Mountaineers there endure cold and long watches between skirmishes with troggs and wildlife. A cask of family ale brings a taste of home. Its kick can leave a tired sentry feeling able to see clearly in the dark.

item:barrel-of-thunder-ale.text: Barrel of Thunder Ale. In Kharanos, the Thunderbrew Distillery has lost a barrel of Thunder Ale. Marleth's Barleybrew Scalder was meant to take its place, turning a brewing feud into foul play. The Thunderbrews of Kharanos and the Barleybrews of Brewnall Village are bitter rivals. Marleth Barleybrew tried to slip a barrel of his Barleybrew Scalder into the Thunderbrews' cellar. He hoped their patrons would choose his brew. The Thunder Ale barrel was seized in the exchange, proof that the switch succeeded despite the local guards.

item:barrow-key.text:
Barrow Key. Deep beneath Stonetalon Peak, three druidic keys guard the Talon Den's ancient hoard. The Barrow Key lies locked within the den. Night elf druids warded the underground barrows of the Talon Den to keep intruders from their relics. Among the passages, the Barrow Key rests in a hidden cache. Reaching it means passing through the druids' layered defenses.

Only the Gatekeeper's Key opens the cache. A seeker must know how those defenses work to claim the Barrow Key.

item:bartleby-s-mug.text: Bartleby's Mug. In Stormwind, Burlguard asks a young warrior to win Bartleby's Mug from its stubborn keeper. Bartleby surrenders it only after a tavern fight leaves him beaten. Bartleby clings to his beloved mug until a fight leaves him beaten. Even then, he drains every last drop before handing it over. The mug proves the warrior could force an uncooperative opponent to yield.

item:bathran-s-hair.text: Bathran's Hair. In the ruins of Bathran's Haunt in northwestern Ashenvale, Bathran's Hair remains a rare herb. Night elf healers value it against afflictions of the flesh and spirit. Bathran's Hair grows among the ancient ruins north of Maestra's Post, where night elf healers have long valued it. Common herbs soothe wounds of the body. Bathran's Hair is said to restore the spirit as well. When a young night elf in Astranaar falls gravely ill, herbalist Orendil Broadleaf seeks the rare plant to prepare a remedy.

item:battleboar-flank.text: Battleboar Flank. In Mulgore, young hunters gather Battleboar Flanks from beasts invading tauren hunting grounds. The meat feeds the tribe's youth. Bristleback quilboar train battleboars in Brambleblade Ravine to enter tauren hunting grounds. Their attacks threaten young tauren at Camp Narache. Grull Hawkwind sends novice hunters to take the flanks and snouts from the beasts they kill. The flank meat becomes stew for the tribe's youth, turning the quilboar's weapon against them into food.

item:battleboar-snout.text: Battleboar Snout. Near Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren hunters gather Battleboar Snouts as the Bristleback press into their hunting grounds. The snouts also go into stews for the young in Camp Narache. Bristleback quilboar train battleboars in Brambleblade Ravine, beneath Red Cloud Mesa. They send the beasts into tauren hunting grounds. Grull Hawkwind sends young braves to drive them back. A snout proves a battleboar has been brought down, and the tauren cook snouts with flank into rich stews for their young.

item:battleworn-axe.text: Battleworn Axe. In Redridge, Battleworn Axe blades show where Blackrock orcs are invading the mountains. Marshal Marris takes the recovered weapons in Lakeshire as proof of the danger to its people. Blackrock reavers carry heavy, nicked axes as they push south from the Burning Steppes into Redridge. Marshal Marris and Lakeshire's hard-pressed town watch gather the blades. Each one confirms another marauding orc has fallen and shows how well armed the warband is. Blackrock invaders have fortified Stonewatch Keep and seized footholds in southeastern Redridge. Their advance has trapped townspeople in Lakeshire. Taking the battleworn weapons leaves fewer arms to the warband and clears roads for Alliance travel.

item:berard-s-journal.text: Berard's Journal. In Pyrewood Village, Berard's Journal holds research the Royal Apothecary Society seeks. Berard studied an ancient plague that wiped out Lake Lordamere's aquatic life. Before Arugal's shadow magic reached Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Berard was one of the Royal Apothecary Society's brightest minds. From Pyrewood Village, he studied an ancient blight that had wiped out all aquatic life in Lake Lordamere centuries before. Arugal's curse took hold of the village, and Berard lost his mind and became a thrall. His field notes remained on a bookshelf in his quarters at the Pyrewood Village Inn.

item:bernice-s-necklace.text: Bernice's Necklace. At Stonefield Farm in Elwynn Forest, Bernice keeps her late husband's necklace close. Auntie Bernice Stonefield keeps her husband's necklace at Stonefield Farm. He was a veteran of Stormwind's military campaigns and carried the charm into battle for good fortune. Bernice says tragedy came only in his final campaign. That was the one expedition when he forgot to bring it. Since his death, the keepsake has remained among her most cherished possessions.

item:besseleth-s-fang.text: Besseleth's Fang. In Sishir Canyon, Besseleth's Fang brings an end to the spider's deadly threat. Besseleth and her brood make Sishir Canyon perilous for travelers. At night, the giant spider turns the Webwinder Path into a death trap for those crossing the gorge. Her fang is nearly two feet long and drips with potent venom. Local defenders have suffered her venomous strikes, so its arrival brings them relief.

item:bethor-s-scroll.text: Bethor's Scroll. At the Sepulcher, Bethor Iceshard writes counter-incantations for Apothecary Renferrel. The scroll may help him brew a protective draught against Thule Ravenclaw's dark sorcery on Fenris Isle.

item:bingles-blastencapper.text: Bingles' Blastencapper. Troggs hold Bingles' Blastencapper after his gyrocopter fell into the Loch. Without it, Bingles' plans to aid Gnomeregan's liberation are in danger. Bingles Blastenheimer built the Blastencapper to strike from the air at the troggs and leper gnomes who overran Gnomeregan. Mechanical failure sent his gyrocopter into the Loch, but Bingles survived. Troggs from the northern islands raided the wreckage and carried the volatile weapon to their camps. Bingles needs the Blastencapper to help retake Gnomeregan. The exiled gnomes are preparing to reclaim their radioactive home, and he counts on his gyrocopter and signature munitions for the air assault. In trogg hands, the explosive could accidentally cause a catastrophe in Loch Modan. Recovering it would preserve a valuable weapon for the gnomish resistance.

item:bingles-hammer.text: Bingles' Hammer. At his crash site in Loch Modan, Bingles Blastenheimer needs Bingles' Hammer back from the troggs. With his gear restored, he can repair his flying machine and help free Gnomeregan. Troggs raided Bingles Blastenheimer's crash site on the freshwater islands. They took his hammer and high-potency explosives. The hammer is needed to repair the dented airframe and adjust the gyrocopter's mechanical parts. Without his equipment, Bingles cannot fly support runs for the gnome forces fighting to reclaim Gnomeregan.

item:bingles-screwdriver.text: Bingles' Screwdriver. Across Loch Modan's northern islands, Bingles' Screwdriver lies among the gear lost in a crash. Troggs carried it off with the tools of pilot Bingles Blastenheimer. When Bingles Blastenheimer crashed into Loch Modan, he lost the tools needed to repair his gyrocopter. Troggs on nearby islands carried off his tool buckets, and the screwdriver was packed in one of them. Bingles needs it for fine adjustments as he repairs the craft and handles its armaments. Bingles works to free Gnomeregan from troggs and leper gnomes. He means to join his flying skill with volatile Blastencapper munitions in an aerial assault. The screwdriver, wrench, and hammer will help him rebuild his gyrocopter and keep the airborne counteroffensive alive.

item:bingles-wrench.text:
Bingles' Wrench. In the Loch, Bingles' Wrench is missing with the pilot's other tools. Troggs took it after Bingles Blastenheimer crash-landed his flying machine. Bingles Blastenheimer survived when his gyrocopter crashed into the Loch. Then the troggs raided the crash site on the small northern islands. They took his specialized supplies and scattered his tools among buckets in their camps.

Bingles' Wrench is one of three critical hand tools, alongside his high-yield Blastencapper explosives. Without the wrench, Bingles cannot repair his downed gyrocopter. His planned aerial offensive to aid the exiled gnomes fighting to reclaim Gnomeregan must wait.

item:black-claw-stout.text: Black Claw Stout. Beneath Stormwind, Zardeth of the Black Claw prepares a drink for Lord Wishock. The stout reaches him as an ordinary tavern beverage.

item:black-feather-quill.text: Black Feather Quill. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Black Feather Quill is needed to wake the Druids of the Talon. The Black Feather Quill is one of four sacred focuses that wake the Druids of the Talon from hibernation. The others are the Raven Claw Talisman, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting. Together, the focuses call slumbering druids back from the Emerald Dream. Without them, a druid may remain trapped in the Dream, unable to return to their waking body. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran Ban'ethil Barrow Den and threatened the chests that held the relics. Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar ordered their swift recovery. The captive druids had to be freed before they were lost to the Dream.

item:blackened-skull.text: Blackened Skull. At Agamand Mills, Blackened Skull trophies mark the Forsaken fight against the Scourge. Deathguard Dillinger in Brill wants proof that the Darkeye Bonecasters are being destroyed. Darkeye Bonecasters haunt Agamand Mills. These skeletal spellcasters turn their necromantic malice against the living and the Forsaken. They seek a forward base for the Lich King's armies in northern Tirisfal. Deathguard Dillinger in Brill asks for their ruined skulls as proof that the Scourge's spellcasters are being beaten back.

item:bloodfeather-belt.text: Bloodfeather Belt. In northern Teldrassil, Bloodfeather harpies crowd the Oracle Glade in crude leather belts. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak gathers the belts as proof that nearby nests are being cleared. Bloodfeather harpies have made aggressive nests in the boughs around the Oracle Glade. Their presence threatens the ancient Oracle Tree and blocks travel through northern Teldrassil. After the flock ambushed and killed a runner carrying reports to Darnassus, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak called on travelers to strike at the nests. Belts taken from fallen harpies show the flock is being thinned and the paths secured, so messages can reach the capital again.

item:bloodfury-ripper-s-remains.text:
Bloodfury Ripper's Remains. At Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran Earthbinder needs Bloodfury Ripper's Remains to know the harpy leader is dead. Her fall means less danger for the tauren settlement. Bloodfury Ripper leads the harpies of the Charred Vale with fierce, territorial aggression. They nest among the scorched ruins and threaten travelers and shamans across the Stonetalon Mountains. Culling the flock brings only brief relief. Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat knows the danger will last while their leader remains.

Bloodfury Ripper rules almost like a queen and directs the harpies' attacks on their territory. Her remains prove she is dead. With the flock thrown into disarray, tauren seeking to heal and secure their rugged lands can know greater peace of mind.

item:bloodstone-choker.text: Bloodstone Choker. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder’s Bloodstone Choker binds a warlock’s rite to the void. His apprentice stole the talisman and fled to the Defias Brotherhood. Carved from bloodstone, the choker bridges the mortal world and the twisting shadows of the Twisting Nether. In the crypts beneath the tavern, Gakin channels its magic at the summoning circle. A hostile Voidwalker answers from the void. A warlock must face the furious creature in direct combat and subdue it while wielding the talisman. Only then is the will to command such a guardian proved.

item:blueleaf-tuber.text: Blueleaf Tuber. Deep beneath Razorfen Kraul, Blueleaf Tuber draws wealthy gourmands and traders from across the world. Blueleaf Tubers grow beneath Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens. Dense roots and quilboar briars keep them from casual foragers. The ground is harsh, yet wealthy gourmands and traders across the world pay an exorbitant price for their distinct flavor. In Ratchet, the goblin Mebok Mizzyrix devised a way to find the hidden roots. He trains native snufflenose gophers to scent tubers from fifty paces away. With specialized command sticks, adventurers guide the gophers and unearth the roots before quilboar patrols catch wind of the intrusion.

item:book-from-sven-s-farm.text:
Book from Sven's Farm. In Duskwood, a hidden journal at Sven's ruined farm holds fragments of the attack on his family, seen by an unknown onlooker. A damaged journal lies beneath loose dirt among the charred remains of Sven's farm in southern Duskwood. Its anonymous writer left frantic, incomplete notes about the tragedy at the homestead. The pages support Sven Yorgen's suspicion that someone watched from the shadows as his family was slain. The account breaks off without naming the writer or telling what happened next.

Sven's clue leads investigators to carry the book to Darkshire. They hope someone there will recognize the handwriting.

item:book-stresses-of-iron.text: Book: Stresses of Iron. In Stormwind Keep, Margulf Blaggon’s book on metallurgy is away at Northshire Abbey for copying. Margulf Blaggon wrote about metallurgy in practice and in theory. Milton Sheaf cared for the volume in the Royal Library of Stormwind Keep. The library lent it to Northshire Abbey, where Brother Paxton copied it by hand for his own collection. The work took far longer than expected. So Brother Kristoff waited anxiously in Cathedral Square for the book to return to the city.

item:bottle-of-disease.text: Bottle of Disease. Near Dor'Danil Barrow Den in Ashenvale, Forsaken alchemists brew disease. Their encampment holds bottles of virulent concoctions. Beyond the Warsong Outriders' front lines, Forsaken alchemists brew contagions near Dor'Danil Barrow Den. The bottles give the night elves at Forest Song proof of an attack aimed at the woods. The Forsaken seek to sicken the soil and wildlife instead of facing the sentinels in open combat.

item:bottle-of-moonshine.text: Bottle of Moonshine. In Darkshire, a Bottle of Moonshine is bound for Lakeshire’s tavern. Barkeep Daniels needs it while Blackrock orcs keep regular supplies from reaching town. Blackrock orcs have cut off Lakeshire’s regular supply caravans. So Barkeep Daniels seeks drinks from the region to restock the tavern for guards and townsfolk. One comes from the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire, where locals favor strong drinks.

item:bottle-of-zombie-juice.text: Bottle of Zombie Juice. In Darkshire, Bottle of Zombie Juice is bound for Abercrombie, a reclusive hermit in Duskwood. He says the potent liquor, brewed from rot blossom, keeps him warm. Rot blossoms gathered in Duskwood go into this harsh brew. The bartender in Darkshire warns it is potent enough to raise the dead. Most folk want nothing to do with such a vile drink. Yet Abercrombie, an eccentric hermit, says it alone keeps him warm on cold, damp nights by his lonely shack.

item:bottom-of-gelkak-s-key.text: Bottom of Gelkak's Key. Along Darkshore, the bottom fragment lies among the remains of a shattered winding key. It belonged to the shipwrecked gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast, and reef crawlers scavenged it from the shore. Threshadons sank Gelkak Gyromast's ship off Darkshore. The wreck cast the gnome and his belongings ashore, including the winding key that activated his mechanical first mate. Coastal rocks broke the key into three pieces, and local scavengers came upon the debris. Reef and tide crawlers seized the bottom fragment as they searched the tideline.

item:branch-of-cenarius.text:
Branch of Cenarius. In eastern Ashenvale, Geltharis holds the Branch of Cenarius, sacred to the dryads. Anilia died defending it, with one last wish: see the relic recovered. The Branch of Cenarius is sacred to the dryads who follow the Forest Lord. Anilia and her sister Illiyana treasured it. Then corrupt satyrs ambushed them near the tainted ruins of eastern Ashenvale. Their leader, Geltharis, seized the branch and mortally wounded Anilia.

As she lay dying, Anilia pointed north toward the arch where Geltharis lurks. She pleaded for a champion to reclaim the bough and return it to the dryads at Forest Song.

item:brass-collar.text: Brass Collar. At the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, Princess wears the collar Ma Stonefield wants as proof the sow is gone. Princess is the Brackwell family’s huge, prize-winning sow. She roams east of the Maclure homestead, and her hunger often carries her into Stonefield Farm’s crops. After losing valuable vegetables to Princess, Ma Stonefield seeks someone willing to slay her. The collar proves the sow has been put down, so she can no longer raid Stonefield’s fields.

item:bristleback-attack-plans.text: Bristleback Attack Plans. At Camp Narache, the Bristleback prepare to lay siege to the tauren settlement. Quilboar in Brambleblade Ravine drew crude maps and notes for an assault meant to overrun it. The Bristleback quilboar are preparing a sustained assault on Camp Narache. Their leaders mean to move beyond border skirmishes on Red Cloud Mesa and wipe out the young tauren training there. The plans lie deep in a dirt cave in Brambleblade Ravine. Chief Hawkwind can send for reinforcements from Bloodhoof Village, giving Camp Narache a chance to blunt the invasion before it begins.

item:bristleback-belt.text: Bristleback Belt. In Camp Narache, young tauren gather Bristleback Belts to prove their valor. The belts come from quilboar in Brambleblade Ravine and mark a step in the Rite of Strength. The Red Cloud tribe tests youths who seek respect in Thunder Bluff through the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. Their first trial is the Rite of Strength. Each initiate must protect the tribe from threats. Bristleback quilboar raid food supplies and ambush hunting parties outside Camp Narache, so Chief Hawkwind demands their belts. Bring him twelve to prove you can face danger and help defend the tribe. Bristleback warriors and shamans in Brambleblade Ravine wear belts made from rough hide, twine and scrap. A tauren warrior has little use for one as apparel, but the quilboar make marks it as evidence of a slain enemy. Bring the belts back to the camp circle to fulfill the rite's proof.

item:bristleback-quilboar-tusk.text: Bristleback Quilboar Tusk. Across the northern and central Barrens, Bristleback Quilboar Tusk are taken from slain quilboar. Mankrik gathers them as proof of slaughter and tokens of vengeance. Bristleback quilboar defend their territory across the Barrens from Horde expansion. Their jagged ivory tusks are weapons in close combat. Mankrik, a veteran orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads, lost his wife in a vicious quilboar ambush. He gathers dozens of tusks in retribution, counting the suffering he means to return to the Bristlebacks.

item:brock-s-list.text: Brock's List. At Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker sends a list of mining pupils honored with picks from Ironforge's guild halls. In Khaz Modan, apprentices must prove their skill before taking on serious work in the mines. Brock records those who excel in their lessons. He entrusts the list to travelers bound for Ironforge, where the honored names can be engraved on the picks. A gryphon carries Brock's List from Thelsamar's roost to Golnir Bouldertoe at the Deep Mountain Mining Guild in Ironforge's Great Forge. There, the students' names are engraved on their honorary picks.

item:broken-and-battered-samophlange.text: Broken and Battered Samophlange. In the northern Barrens, Broken and Battered Samophlange lies damaged after a failed inspection. It must reach goblin experts in Orgrimmar, where someone may understand its workings. The Venture Company made samophlanges for its work in the northern Barrens. Wenikee Boltbucket tried to inspect and alter one, adding gauges, levers, and dials to measure its stability. Her changes weakened the mechanism and left it battered, close to ruin. Fearing more additions might make it fail completely, she sent the fragile device to someone with factory experience. The device needs repair by someone who knows Venture Company production lines. Rilli Greasygob, a former Venture employee, works at Nogg's Machine Shop in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. The battered apparatus catches the engineer's eye. Anyone who scavenges from goblin operations may seem daring, or simply foolhardy.

item:broken-samophlange.text: Broken Samophlange. In the northern Barrens, a broken samophlange has drawn curious engineers. Its shifting parts and fine gears still hint at a purpose no one has uncovered. From the northern Barrens comes a broken samophlange, its fine gears and moving assemblies still showing careful workmanship. Sputtervalve, a goblin in Ratchet, damaged the delicate device by accident before anyone could record how it worked. Hoping to send working results to curious colleagues in Undermine, its finder sought someone who could repair it. Wenikee Boltbucket, a clever tinkerer near Mor'shan Rampart, was the one they turned to. Wenikee Boltbucket cannot tell what a samophlange is meant to do, even after studying its ruined parts. Its clockwork sounds and shifting motion catch her interest. Rather than cast it aside as junk, she sets out to repair it and see its mechanisms working at full capacity.

item:broken-tools.text: Broken Tools. At the dig northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven picks lie broken at the forge. Baine Bloodhoof seeks proof that the excavation threatening Mulgore's land and wildlife has stopped. Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven excavators search Mulgore's hills for traces of ancient history. The tauren see the digging as a defilement of the Earth Mother. Its noise and destruction unsettle the local wildlife, especially the roaming kodo herds. So young Baine Bloodhoof orders defenders to take the prospectors' iron picks and break them at a forge. With the picks ruined, the expedition cannot gouge farther into the earth.

item:bundle-of-crocolisk-skins.text: Bundle of Crocolisk Skins. Hunters in the Wetlands send crocolisk skins west to Menethil Harbor. There, leatherworkers put the hides to use. In the Wetlands, hunters gather and cure tough, water-resistant crocolisk skins for Menethil Harbor. James Halloran is among the artisans who receive them. Einar has gathered this bundle, but asks a traveler to carry it into town. He hopes to avoid going home to face the temper of his frustrated wife, Sida.

item:bundle-of-hides.text: Bundle of Hides. Across the Barrens, a Bundle of Hides rides with the Horde’s wind riders toward Thunder Bluff. The cured skins are bound for the leatherworkers, and their delivery shows travelers how the wind rider network carries goods. Hunters cure the hides of beasts found across the Barrens. Kodo graze the plains, while lions prowl and raptors roam. The leatherworkers of Thunder Bluff use these skins for gear, pouches, armor, and bindings for the Horde. Couriers carry the bundle from the Crossroads to Thunder Bluff on Devrak’s trained wyverns. The overland way through the Barrens and into Mulgore is slow and dangerous, with quilboar and centaur raiders abroad. By wind rider, the hides cross Kalimdor’s broken terrain swiftly.

item:bundle-of-wood.text: Bundle of Wood. Eastvale Logging Camp needs wood sent west for Stormwind's rebuilding. Eastvale Logging Camp sends freshly chopped timber west for buildings and other construction in the Kingdom of Stormwind. But bears and wolves have entered the groves northwest of camp. The frightened loggers fled, leaving their Bundles of Wood among the trees. With the shipment deadline near, overseer Raelen needs travelers to recover the timber before the lumber contracts are breached.

item:burning-blade-medallion.text: Burning Blade Medallion. In Durotar, the Burning Blade Medallion threatens the Horde's young warriors. Cultists carry it in the Valley of Trials, and Yarrog Baneshadow holds it deep in the Burning Blade Coven. Zureetha Fargaze's divinations lead to the medallion in the Burning Blade Coven. Yarrog Baneshadow serves the Burning Blade cult and carries it deep in the winding caverns. The trinket channels dark power among the cult's impish familiars and felstalkers. Defeating Yarrog and taking the medallion ends the cult's attempt to undermine the Horde's training grounds from within Durotar.

item:burning-blood-quest-item.text:
Burning Blood (quest item). In Duskwood, Nightbane worgen blood draws Grimand Elmore's interest. He needs twenty vials for experiments in smithing. Nightbane worgen prowl Duskwood in a strange fury. Their blood burns with real heat. It can be drawn from worgen haunting the timberlands and Roland's Doom. Armorers seek its heat to temper resilient plate. Grimand Elmore is an armorer in Stormwind's Dwarven District. He wants to test smithing methods devised by his former student Furen Longbeard.

For the experiment, Elmore needs Burning Blood and a dense burning rock held by the worgen chieftain Gutspill. Bring him the bubbling fluid, and he promises sturdy warrior armor from his forge.

item:burning-rock.text: Burning Rock. In Duskwood, Burning Rock smolders within Roland's Doom. Gutspill, leader of the Nightbane worgen, carries it, and Grimand Elmore in Stormwind needs it with fiery worgen blood to forge enchanted armor for promising warriors. Gutspill carries Burning Rock through the shafts of Roland's Doom. Grimand Elmore in Stormwind wants its heat for armor made with fiery worgen blood. He tests smithing techniques developed by his peer Furen Longbeard, hoping to make tough plates for veteran fighters.

item:cache-of-zanzil-s-altered-mixture.text: Cache of Zanzil's Altered Mixture. At the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen, a cache of Zanzil's Altered Mixture lies locked away. The potent poison bears the name of Zanzil, a jungle troll witch doctor. North of the Sludge Fen in the Barrens, the Venture Company holds a tower outpost. Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix keeps a cache of altered mixture bearing the name of the troll witch doctor Zanzil in his private strongbox at the summit. A poison has weakened everyone in the tower, leaving its goblin inhabitants vulnerable to a bold intruder.

item:cactus-apple.text: Cactus Apple. In the Valley of Trials, Cactus Apples give orcs a rare source of moisture in Durotar’s dry heat. Across the Valley of Trials, cactus apples grow in clusters around thick cactuses. Gathering them means working among the thorns, but the fruit eases the thirst of Durotar’s heat. Galgar, an orc in the valley, gathers the apples for Cactus Apple Surprise. Recruits enduring their early training can cool themselves with his treat.

item:calor-s-note.text: Calor's Note. In Duskwood, Calor's Note carries a woodsman's recommendation to Master Jonathan Carevin. Calor writes it on a scrap of faded parchment for a proven adventurer, opening a path to a hidden band that fights beside Darkshire's militia but remains apart from it. Calor is hard to impress, and Duskwood gives strangers little warmth. Survive the bloodthirsty worgen stalking the woods, and he grants his respect with a brief message. Written on faded parchment, the note travels to Darkshire and introduces the outsider directly to Jonathan Carevin. Darkshire relies on the Night Watch for public defense. Calor and Carevin pursue a grimmer, hidden fight apart from the town guard. Calor laments that the guard outnumbers them, and hopes to find enough capable fighters to advance their private war. Hand over the note, and Carevin admits you to his campaign against demons, undead, and the hidden sympathizers aiding Duskwood's decline.

item:candle-of-beckoning.text:
Candle of Beckoning. On Brightwater Lake, Gunther Arcanus keeps an enchanted candle for a summons. Light it on a nearby islet, and Lillith Nefara's restless spirit answers. Gunther Arcanus keeps the Candle of Beckoning in a crate beside him on his island in Brightwater Lake. He is a fiercely independent undead sorcerer who broke free of the Lich King's command on his own. Still wary of both the Scourge and the Forsaken, Gunther asks you to carry a candle southwest to a smaller islet. Set it on the old, bloodstained table and light it.

The flame pierces the veil between worlds and summons the dormant, restless shade of Lillith Nefara. She is a powerful Scourge agent, and Gunther means for her to be destroyed.

item:cantation-of-manifestation.text: Cantation of Manifestation. In the Undercity, Anastasia Hartwell sends apprentices to reveal unseen beings in Algernon's shop. The Cantation of Manifestation brings beings hidden by magic into sight. Anastasia Hartwell keeps the scroll in the Magic Quarter and entrusts it to capable mages sent to contain rogue magical anomalies. In the Apothecarium, Algernon's alchemical workshop is troubled by arcane instability. Read aloud there, the cantation reveals stray rift spawns so the caster can subdue them and seal them in containment coffers for study.

item:canvas-scraps.text: Canvas Scraps. At Razor Hill, Canvas Scraps go to Furl Scornbrow for travel sacks for new Horde recruits. The cloth comes from human invaders and centaur tribes in Durotar. Kul Tiras marines and sailors carry canvas along Durotar’s eastern shore. Their gear and sails leave scraps behind. Inland, Kolkar centaur reuse coarse cloth taken from supply caravans and past conflicts. Their camps and gear hold scraps for salvage. Furl Scornbrow watches for invaders from the Razor Hill watchtower. The aging veteran has left his fighting days behind, but puts cloth taken from enemies to use. He stitches it into sturdy carrying bags for younger soldiers. The bags help the new generation defend the Horde’s borders.

item:cask-of-merlot.text: Cask of Merlot. In Stormwind, Cask of Merlot helps supply Lakeshire as Blackrock orcs sever its trade routes. Galina Winery makes its merlot in the heart of the kingdom. Its cellars lie along the canals by Stormwind's Trade District. Winemaker Roberto Pupellyverbos tends the vintages for the capital's refined tastes. Unlike Duskwood moonshine or Elwynn spirits, this wine bears the craft of human vintners working within the city's walls. When the Blackrock clan invaded the Redridge Mountains, supply routes failed and Lakeshire lost its usual merchant shipments. The locals were left parched and frightened. So Barkeep Daniels sends willing couriers across the kingdom to refill his tavern's cellars. By Lake Everstill, defenders and refugees can wash down their rations with the cask's gentle wine.

item:cask-of-scalder.text: Cask of Scalder. In Stormwind, a cask of Barleybrew Scalder is bound for an old acquaintance. The fiery ale carries a favor between dwarves. Travelers who have proved themselves across the Rethban Gauntlet bring Barleybrew Scalder to Furen Longbeard in Stormwind's Dwarven District. Furen is an artisan shieldsmith, and he finds dry times intolerable. The cask gives Yorus Barleybrew a way to call in an old favor and secure fine dwarven craftsmanship.

item:cask-of-shimmer-stout.text: Cask of Shimmer Stout. In Dun Morogh's cold heights, Cask of Shimmer Stout is bound for the eastern mountains. Rejold Barleybrew brewed the potent new ale, and his brother sends a cask east as a gift for fellow dwarven mountaineers. Rejold Barleybrew brews Shimmer Stout in Brewnall Village. Local patrons and mountaineers who brave Dun Morogh's biting frosts take to it quickly. Impressed by the brew, his brother Mountaineer Barleybrew commissions a cask for the journey through the eastern pass into Loch Modan. Dwarves prize strong drink for company and warmth in the mountain chill. Sharing fresh ale with comrades on distant patrols is a military tradition. During his watch in Thelsamar, Mountaineer Kadrell opens the cask and samples the brew. Shimmer Stout lives up to its name: one draught is said to lighten the limbs and make a soldier feel as though he could fly. A dwarven scout on a long, lonely patrol along the high roads might welcome such an invigorating drink.

item:cats-eye-emerald.text: Cats Eye Emerald. At Boulder Lode Mine, the Cats Eye Emerald is under guard while Wharfmaster Dizzywig seeks a buyer. The fist-sized gem has drawn his eye from Ratchet's docks. Venture Company laborers found a massive emerald at Boulder Lode Mine, northeast of the Sludge Fen. News spread quickly across the savanna. In goblin country, rare gemstones do not stay secret for long. Trade gossip carried word from Ratchet's docks to Booty Bay, where Wharfmaster Dizzywig heard of the prize. He began plotting to send it to the open market in Undermine. Venture Company management keeps the emerald inside the mine under heavy guard. Overseers, Enforcers, and chief operators such as Boss Copperplug defend it from rival cartels and fortune-hunters. Dizzywig has promised a fifty-percent cut to those who help him secure the gem.

item:cenarion-lunardust.text: Cenarion Lunardust. Turak Runetotem gives young tauren druids Cenarion Lunardust on Thunder Bluff. At an ancient Moonkin Stone between Mulgore and the Barrens, they use it to awaken Lunaclaw. Cenarion Lunardust bears the Cenarion Circle’s blessing for druids ready to join the Druids of the Claw. At the Moonkin Stone west of Camp Taurajo, the dust calls Lunaclaw, a sacred beast bound to test each initiate. The trial measures strength and resolve. In facing it, a young druid learns the strength of body and heart needed to take the form of a bear.

item:cenarion-moondust.text: Cenarion Moondust. At the Moonkin Stone east of Auberdine, Cenarion Moondust summons Lunaclaw. Night elf druids use it in their final trial to become Druids of the Claw. Mathrengyl Bearwalker gives Cenarion Moondust to young druids in Darnassus for their final trial of heart and body. To face Lunaclaw, an initiate travels to the moonkin dens east of Auberdine in Darkshore. Scatter the powder on the ancient Moonkin Stone, and Lunaclaw comes to test the druid in combat. Through the trial, the initiate gains the enduring strength needed to channel bear form.

item:centaur-bracers.text: Centaur Bracers. Across the Barrens, Centaur Bracers are taken from fallen Kolkar warriors. Regthar Deathgate gathers them west of the Crossroads as proof the centaur raiders have been culled. Kolkar raiders threaten the Horde’s foothold across the Barrens. Their fallen warriors leave leather and iron bracers behind, proof that a raider has been removed from the trade roads. Regthar Deathgate is an orc scout stationed on the bluffs west of the Crossroads. He offers a standing bounty for these trophies to curb the tribe’s aggression.

item:charred-horn.text:
Charred Horn. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard needs Charred Horns from young chimaeras in Stonetalon. Their resistance to flame, blunt force, and harsh elemental forces makes them useful in strong armor. Fledgling and young chimaeras in the Stonetalon Mountains provide Charred Horns. Their resistance to flame and blunt force makes them useful to Furen Longbeard, a dwarven armorsmith at his forge in Stormwind. He needs twelve horns to make fire-hardened mail.

Furen combines them with venomous spider fangs from the Wetlands, phlogiston from Razorfen Kraul, and the galvanized horn of a chimaera matriarch. The Charred Horns reinforce the mail's rings and plates with heat-treated material.

item:chest-of-containment-coffers.text: Chest of Containment Coffers. In the Undercity, mages keep the Chest of Containment Coffers close at hand. Its enchanted vessels can hold unstable magical forces. Arcane creatures may emerge from experiments or sudden rifts between planes. Ordinary cages cannot hold beings made of magic. The Chest of Containment Coffers holds enchanted vessels that bind subdued creatures alive. Senior instructors keep it nearby, including Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity and Jennea Cannon in Stormwind. They give initiates coffers to survey anomalies before those forces unsettle their surroundings.

item:chief-sharptusk-thornmantle-s-head.text: Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle's Head. Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle's Head marks the end of a threat to Red Cloud Mesa. The Bristleback leader threatened the young tauren braves, and his head was recovered from deep in Brambleblade Ravine as proof of victory. The Bristleback quilboar of Brambleblade Ravine attack the tribes of Camp Narache. Their chieftain, Sharptusk Thornmantle, leads them. The tauren guard their homeland in Mulgore with vigilance and strength. Sharptusk's head proves he is dead and warns the surviving quilboar clans to keep clear of the mesa borders. Brave Windfeather asks young hunters and tribal defenders to bring back Sharptusk's head as a rite of passage. An enemy who can strike back and lead a war band tests a young fighter's skill in battle. Presenting the head completes that trial and earns the fighter a name among the braves of Red Cloud Mesa.

item:chok-sul-s-head.text:
Chok'sul's Head. In Thelsamar, Chok'sul's death is proved by the head Magistrate Bluntnose demands. The local dwarven authorities set a bounty, and he requires this proof before paying it. Ogres from Mo'grosh Stronghold threaten Loch Modan's settlements. They strike Thelsamar, excavation sites, and the Stonewrought Dam. Magistrate Bluntnose placed a bounty on Chok'sul, the brute believed to direct these attacks.

The northeastern hills are in turmoil, so the magistrate demands proof before releasing township funds. Chok'sul's severed head gives the dwarven council the certainty it needs to mark the bounty fulfilled.

item:clarice-s-pendant.text: Clarice's Pendant. In the Pools of Vision in Thunder Bluff, Clarice Foster keeps the pendant her former husband gave her. Yuriv’s devotion to the Light left her and their children behind. Before the Third War consumed Lordaeron, Yuriv left Clarice Foster and their children to fight the undead. He believed the Holy Light came before all else. Yuriv died, and the Scourge he had set out to fight took his family. Now Clarice is Forsaken, and she sees the pendant he gave her as an insult. It reminds her that she and the children came second to his zeal and duty.

item:claw-key.text: Claw Key. Within the Talon Den on Stonetalon Peak, three druidic keys guard an enchanted hoard. Night elf druids built the Talon Den high on Stonetalon Peak as a sanctuary and storehouse for powerful relics. They hid its treasures behind several layers of protection. Three enchanted locks seal the hoard: the Barrow Key, the Sleepers' Key, and the Claw Key. Each key rests in a druidic cache shaped like a torch, hidden in the barrow den's winding tunnels. The druids kept the keys guarded and hard to reach. Near the barrow entrance, the Gatekeeper's Key opens the cache that holds the Claw Key. The Claw Key helps break the druids' seal and reach the riches hidden deep within the mountain.

item:cliffspring-river-sample.text: Cliffspring River Sample. At Cliffspring River's waterfall in Darkshore, foul water gathers in a pool. Drawn for Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine, the sample shows corruption moving toward the coast. The Cliffspring River runs from Darkshore's eastern heights, past ancient stone bridges, and into the sea at Mist's Edge. Its clear water has turned foul and visibly corrupted. Thundris Windweaver, a night elf in Auberdine, fears the tainted flow will reach the settlement's shore and water supply. He sent travelers to draw water from the pool beneath the river's lower waterfall. The sample confirms that unnatural rot is moving downstream toward the coast.

item:cloth-request.text: Cloth Request. At the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, Rema Schneider receives Harlan Bagley's request for fresh cloth and knitted goods. His shelves are emptying quickly. Harlan Bagley asks Rema Schneider for fresh cloth and knitted garments. Trade has surged without warning. Citizens and travelers buy armor and sturdy clothing as if a brutal season were coming. The rush leaves Rema puzzled and wary. The House of Nobles has announced no open war, so she wonders why city folk are quietly armoring themselves and whether the crown's leaders are hiding unrest.

item:cloven-hoof.text:
Cloven Hoof. Deep in Thousand Needles, the Galak centaur guard the Cloven Hoof at Splithoof Hold. Tauren scholars at Freewind Post seek to learn what its strange energy reveals. At Splithoof Hold, the Galak centaur keep the Cloven Hoof in an ancient brazier. Magical fire surrounds it, and blessed water must quench the flame briefly before anyone can handle the relic. The centaur clans are divided and violent, yet their care for the brazier points to a ritual bound to their origins.

At Freewind Post, Rau Cliffrunner and other tauren observers hope the hoof's strange aura will teach them about the centaur who have long troubled Kalimdor's plains.

item:comar-s-heart.text: Comar's Heart. In the Undercity, warlocks seek Comar's Heart to draw a succubus into their service. It belonged to Comar Villard, a human searching the Wetlands for his lost wife. Comar Villard still searches the Wetlands for his lost wife. Turmoil has swept the Eastern Kingdoms, yet he will not abandon the search. Carendin Halgar's disciples in the Undercity prize such fidelity as rare and pure. To bind a succubus, capricious and predatory, warlocks need devotion like his for bait. Comar's steadfast love marks him for slaughter, and his heart becomes the lure for a demonic servant.

item:consecrated-rune.text:
Consecrated Rune. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, the Consecrated Rune calls fledgling dwarven paladins to their formal duties as Knights of the Silver Hand. Among the Knights of the Silver Hand, a Consecrated Rune marks a novice dwarf’s place. Dwarven paladins receive one in Coldridge Valley after proving their basic skill in arms. Sacred words are inscribed upon it, and the Holy Light blesses the rune.

Bromos Grummner, the paladin trainer inside Anvilmar, sends it as an official summons. Dwarves greatly respect the Holy Light traditions their human allies introduced to them. Reading the rune confirms a novice’s place in the order and marks the beginning of service.

item:console-key.text: Console Key. At the Venture Company digsite in the Barrens, Tinkerer Sniggles keeps the Console Key. It opens the main control terminal and frees the samophlange after the apparatus shuts down. The Venture Company runs an industrial outpost in the northern Barrens, powered by steam-driven machinery. At its heart is a device called a samophlange. The console is locked, and only Tinkerer Sniggles, the chief technician on site, carries the Console Key. It opens the terminal casing so the rig can be powered down.

item:control-console-operating-manual.text: Control Console Operating Manual. At the Venture Company site southwest of Sludge Fen, workers turn to the Control Console Operating Manual to handle the machinery. It gives the valve sequence for disengaging the samophlange. The Venture Company runs a drilling and research site in the northern Barrens, southwest of Sludge Fen. Gauges and pressurized valves connect to mechanisms that drive a device called a samophlange. Without the right instructions, the volatile controls can fail dangerously or lock the system. The manual shows workers how to disengage the core apparatus without causing an explosion.

item:corroded-shrapnel.text: Corroded Shrapnel. In Stonetalon, jagged fragments remain buried in the forest’s corrupted treants. The Venture Company’s munitions left them there as the goblins fled. The Venture Company’s goblins fled Stonetalon’s groves under cover of reckless munitions. Their blasts drove shrapnel into the treants defending the valley, where it lodged deep in bark and core. The ancient guardians slowly succumbed to corruption. Their wood darkened, and they turned their fury on anyone entering the vale. Kaela Shadowspear seeks the rusted fragments for Gaxim Rustfizzle, a gnome who wants to study how the weapons brought on the treants’ corruption.

item:corrupt-manifestation-s-bracers.text: Corrupt Manifestation's Bracers. On Silverpine Forest’s coast, Corrupt Manifestation's Bracers remain from a corrupted water elemental. During the Call of Water, shaman initiates cast them into the Brazier of Everfount with pure water, cleansing the shrine and summoning a pure water spirit. The Scourge’s plague reached Lordaeron’s spirits. Along Silverpine Forest’s coast, west of the Sepulcher, corruption overcame a sacred water shrine. Its water manifestation became an aggressive shade, and shaman initiates must defeat it to recover the bracers. At the Brazier of Everfount, they cast the bindings into the flame with pure water. The rite lifts the shrine’s corruption and calls forth an unblemished water spirit.

item:corrupted-brain-stem.text: Corrupted Brain Stem. In Blackfathom Deeps and along Ashenvale’s coast, Corrupted Brain Stem specimens come from naga and satyrs twisted by magic. Gershala Nightwhisper of Auberdine studies their deformities, hoping night elf scholars can learn how to keep the blood elves from the same fate. Forbidden magic and demonic pacts mark the naga and satyrs. Long ago, reckless kaldorei highborne became serpent-like aquatic beasts and demonic horned fiends. Their brain stems bear heavy mutations, showing how deeply corruptive energies altered the nervous systems of beings once known as elves. From Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper watches troubling rumors about the blood elves of the Eastern Kingdoms. He fears their demonic sorcery will create another generation of monsters on Azeroth. So he sends adventurers into Blackfathom Deeps to examine naga and satyr tissues. He hopes to trace magical degeneration before another elven culture is lost.

item:corrupted-kor-gem.text: Corrupted Kor Gem. Near Blackfathom Deeps, naga rites taint Kor gems. Sorcerers prize their arcane power, though the corruption must be cleansed before a gem can be used in righteous smithing. Kor gems hold great stores of magic, making them useful to sorcerers and enchanted smiths. Near the ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, naga oracles and tide priestesses claim the stones for their rites. Their enchantments corrupt each gem with magic from the sea. The taint leaves the stone's latent power intact, so those seeking a potent focus still look among the naga.

item:cougar-claws.text:
Cougar Claws. Across Mulgore’s central plains, tauren hunters gather Cougar Claws for a cleansing ritual. The claws come from flatland cougars, among the grasslands’ apex hunters. Flatland cougars hunt by instinct among Mulgore’s grasslands. For the tauren, gathering their claws is neither slaughter for its own sake nor trophy hunting. It gathers the beasts’ natural spirit.

When goblin operations defile the plains’ ancestral waters, Mull Thunderhorn asks young hunters to gather Cougar Claws and prairie stalker claws. The tauren weave native beasts’ pure predatory instincts into a ritual totem. They mean it to scour toxins and foul sorcery from the poisoned Thunderhorn Water Well.

item:courser-eye.text: Courser Eye. In Stonetalon's highlands, coursers are hunted for a brew Witch Doctor Jin'Zil calls forest magic. At Malaka'jin, he wants many eyes for his concoction.

item:covert-ops-pack.text: Covert Ops Pack. In Stonetalon, Alliance agents use the Covert Ops Pack to disrupt Venture Company sites and take their plans. Its charges and schematics are aimed at the company’s work in Windshear Crag. The Covert Ops Pack brings charges and plans into Venture Company territory. Red and blue NG-5 explosives come with remote detonators, while Plan Alpha and Plan Beta guide the strikes. The charges target the lumber mill at Cragpool Lake and the eastern mine. When goblins rush to fight fires and inspect broken machinery, an infiltrator can pass through the confusion and take documents and schematics. Night elf Sentinels and Alliance engineers in Stonetalon both gain from the Covert Ops Pack. Its blasts and stolen plans hinder clear-cutting and excavation on the sacred mountainside. The Venture Company engineering plans also reveal how goblin heavy machinery works. They show where the machines can fail and give Alliance engineers ideas to adapt for their own designs.

item:crate-of-crash-helmets.text: Crate of Crash Helmets. At the Shimmering Flats, Wizzle Brassbolts and his brother need helmets for their rocket car test drivers. Heavy dwarven Siege Engine headgear is bound for Thousand Needles to guard pilots against concussions. Gnome engineers race rocket cars across the Shimmering Flats. Wizzle Brassbolts and his brother build machines that outrun their drivers’ ability to steer. Crashes leave test pilots with head injuries, and leather caps no longer suffice. So heavy dwarven Siege Engine helmets are shipped across the sea to keep the drivers conscious and alive.

item:crate-of-horseshoes.text: Crate of Horseshoes. In Elwynn, Crate of Horseshoes carries fifty iron shoes toward Lakeshire. Smith Argus forged fifty fresh horseshoes in Goldshire, then packed them into a crate and hammered it shut. Verner Osgood ordered them for Lakeshire, where pressure from gnolls and orcs leaves local craftsmen reliant on Elwynn for essential metal goods. The delivery meets Verner's desperate need for equipment, and Argus includes a stern bill of sale so the Redridge craftsman knows frontier survival comes at a steep price.

item:crate-of-inn-supplies.text: Crate of Inn Supplies. In Coldridge Valley, travelers are needed to carry the Crate of Inn Supplies to Kharanos. Troggs have closed the mountain pass, leaving the Thunderbrew Distillery dependent on their help. Near Anvilmar, the Crate of Inn Supplies waits for a safe passage through Coldridge Pass. Troggs have cut off the route, keeping civilian couriers from carrying goods until the Mountaineers clear the road. Hands Springsprocket packed tavern provisions for Tannok Frosthammer in Kharanos, where the supplies are needed.

item:crate-of-lightforge-ingots.text: Crate of Lightforge Ingots. In Stormwind, the Crate of Lightforge Ingots carries Duskwood's hope against Morbent Fel. Lightforge iron is rare, and its consecrated metal channels holy power against dark entities. Morbent Fel's protections turn aside ordinary steel, so Duskwood looks to these ingots against the necromancer. Only an artisan who knows the metal's temper and honors its sacred nature can work it.

item:crate-with-holes.text: Crate With Holes. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix readies a crate for a Snufflenose Gopher. Mebok Mizzyrix sends trained Snufflenose Gophers into Razorfen Kraul to find Blueleaf Tubers. The gophers cannot cross the Barrens on foot beside an adventurer, so Mebok places each one in a wooden crate with air holes. Once inside the quilboar stronghold, the crate opens. The gopher follows its keen nose toward the buried tubers.

item:crawler-leg.text:
Crawler Leg. Along Darkshore's misty coast, crabs lose legs most travelers have no use for. Their tough limbs can keep a gnome's communication device working. Darkshore's crabs leave sturdy legs along the shore, from pygmy tide crawlers to reef crawlers. The night elf sentinels pay them little mind. But gnome engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle has found a use for them.

From Auberdine, he designed prototype long-distance communication devices called buzzboxes to work with improvised local parts. Crawler legs have segmented joints and durable chitin, giving the friction and leverage needed to repair Buzzbox 827 just south of town along the shore.

item:creeper-ichor.text: Creeper Ichor. Across the Hillsbrad forests, moss creepers yield Creeper Ichor to the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill. The Society seeks the fluid as a biological agent for new plagues against the living. Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill seeks natural toxins and catalysts for deadly new brews. He means to eradicate the surrounding human population, and the foothills’ clean air and vibrant life offend him. Among the forest’s giant arachnids, mature moss creepers hold an elusive ichor. It makes an ideal base for his Elixir of Suffering. Mixed with gray bear tongues and other reagents, the fluid helps the Forsaken perfect their lethal alchemy.

item:crocolisk-skin-classic.text: Crocolisk Skin (Classic). At Farstrider Lodge in Loch Modan, hunters brave the Loch’s crocolisks for hides sought by merchants and leatherworkers. Crocolisks make dens along the islands and shores of the Loch’s cold waters. Their sharp teeth and thick scales make them dangerous quarry. Still, hunters based at Farstrider Lodge pursue them for their tough skins. Tailors and distant merchants seek the hides for sturdy garments and armor, so an undamaged skin brings a good price nearby.

item:crocolisk-tear-classic.text: Crocolisk Tear (Classic). At the Stonewrought Dam, Chief Engineer Hinderweir needs Crocolisk Tear to counter Dark Iron explosives. Crocolisk Tears come from reptiles in Loch Modan's waters. Chief Engineer Hinderweir found another use for their secretions. Mixed with potent spider venom and resonant ogre minerals, a tear gains the chemical properties needed to counter the volatile Dark Iron demolition charges threatening the Stonewrought Dam.

item:crossroads-supply-crate.text: Crossroads Supply Crate. At the Crossroads, a raided caravan has left the settlement short of food, tools, and necessities. Stolen provisions now lie scattered among Razormane camps in the Barrens. Razormane quilboar raided a caravan bound for the Crossroads and carried its supplies into nearby camps. The crates lie among underbrush and dirt dens. Thork, the settlement's commander, seeks their return before the outpost runs dangerously low on food, tools, and necessities.

item:crude-flint.text: Crude Flint. Across the Wetlands, Mosshide gnolls burn living marsh timber, and Rethiel the Greenwarden means to stop them. They carry Crude Flint to kindle their fires.

item:crystal-kelp-frond.text: Crystal Kelp Frond. Murlocs carry Crystal Kelp Fronds from the ocean to Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest. William Pestle in Goldshire seeks them for an invisibility liquor. Crystal Kelp Fronds come from saltwater oceans, which makes them unusual in Elwynn Forest’s fresh water.
