Along Crystal Lake’s shores, murloc tribes gather and keep the fronds for reasons of their own. Alchemists value the fronds for their strange power to distort sight. William Pestle in Goldshire uses them as the chief ingredient in an invisibility liquor meant to help sweethearts slip past watchful family eyes.

item:crystal-phial.text:
Crystal Phial. In Shadowglen, Tenaron Stormgrip gives young night elves a Crystal Phial to carry to a nearby moonwell. There they draw sacred water for rites honoring and nourishing Teldrassil. Atop Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip gives young night elves a Crystal Phial. He sends them to the moonwell just north of the bough to gather its glowing waters. The delicate vessel holds water touched by the sacred legacy of the Well of Eternity.

When they return with a Filled Crystal Phial, the Crown of the Earth pilgrimage begins. The young kaldorei learn about the balance of magic, history, and nature in their new island home.

item:crystalized-scales.text: Crystalized Scales. In Kalimdor, basilisks yield Crystalized Scales for arcane work. Their mineralized hides come from the Charred Vale and Thousand Needles, and Collin Mauren seeks them in Stormwind. Basilisks endure heat and ash in Stonetalon's Charred Vale and the salt flats of Thousand Needles. In both places, their hides harden beneath a crystal crust. The scales hold latent arcane resonance, and wizards across the Great Sea prize them for experiments in rare spellcraft. In Stormwind, the mage Collin Mauren seeks travelers bound for Kalimdor to bring him these scales. He pulverizes their crystalline mineral layers into dust, then uses the powder as a reagent for newly conceived spells and his own arcane research.

item:curative-animal-salve.text:
Curative Animal Salve. Across Darkshore and the Barrens, druids tend sick wildlife with Curative Animal Salve. Herbalists prepare it in both lands, while the Cenarion Circle reads the animals’ afflictions as signs of a wider blight. Druids use Curative Animal Salve on sick wildlife in Darkshore and the Barrens. Alanndarian Nightsong directs young druids to treat sick deer between the Cliffspring River and Ashenvale’s borders. In the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem brews the same remedy for sick gazelles north of the Crossroads.

Each herbalist gathers local herbs and prepares the salve in batches of ten doses. Field druids apply it directly to the animals. Both herbalists work with local authorities to make larger supplies. The salve eases the animals’ suffering, but the Cenarion Circle sees a wider disturbance. In Moonglade, Dendrite Starblaze observes that the afflicted deer on the coast and the suffering gazelles on the savannah are no random casualties. They are unwitting victims of a blight spreading across Kalimdor from several directions.

For initiates, treating the animals tests their dedication to protecting nature and their skill at cleansing poison.

item:daffodil-bouquet.text: Daffodil Bouquet. In Lakeshire, Daffodil Bouquet carries Guard Parker’s thanks to Darcy for packing his lunch. Martie Jainrose gathers the flowers, and her choice stirs gossip between the two women. Guard Parker wants to thank Darcy at the Lakeshire inn for packing his daily lunch. So he asks Martie Jainrose, the town herbalist, to prepare a bouquet of daffodils. Martie names them her favorite flowers. Darcy recognizes them as Martie’s signature bloom and suspects jealousy. Half-joking, she wonders if Martie poisoned the stems out of spite.

item:daggerspine-scale.text:
Daggerspine Scale. Along Hillsbrad Foothills’ southern shore, prowling Daggerspine naga yield tough reptilian scales sought by the Royal Apothecary Society. The scales help activate virulent brews in the Forsaken’s ongoing plague experiments. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks reagents for its toxins, plagues, and concoctions. While refining the experimental Elixir of Agony, its apothecaries found that Daggerspine naga scales react in a useful way. Combined with troll regenerative elixirs and murloc organs, the scales chemically activate dormant contaminating agents suspended in raw mixtures.

To gather the scales, you must hunt along the rocky coastline east of Southshore. The vicious naga tribe and Alliance forces are both nearby. The apothecaries need the scales for their research.

item:dal-bloodclaw-s-skull.text: Dal Bloodclaw's Skull. In northern Ashenvale, Raene Wolfrunner awaits proof that Astranaar is safe from attack. Dal Bloodclaw's Skull carries that proof. The Thistlefur furbolgs north of Astranaar have grown more numerous and aggressive. Like much of Ashenvale's ancient forest, they have fallen to corruption. Raene Wolfrunner, a night elf sentinel, fears they will soon march on Astranaar. So she orders their ranks culled and their leader, Dal Bloodclaw, slain. His skull proves their chieftain is dead and buys Astranaar's defenders time.

item:dalaran-mana-gem.text: Dalaran Mana Gem. Near Ambermill, Kirin Tor mages carry Dalaran Mana Gems to renew their arcane power. Forsaken tailors use the gems to weave enchanted robes. The Kirin Tor’s conjurors and guards carry the gems as well. In the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, Forsaken practitioners prize the gems as a ready store of concentrated magic. Some undead mages share an academic heritage with Dalaran. Yet survival comes first, and the Forsaken see the Kirin Tor as rivals whose stores of magic can be taken. Forsaken bring mana gems taken from fallen Kirin Tor operatives to tailors such as Josef Gregorian in the Undercity. They bring simple linen as well. A tailor cannot channel arcane power directly, but can bind a gem into cloth. The magic strengthens the wearer’s connection to the arcane.

item:dalaran-pendant.text: Dalaran Pendant. In Ambermill, Dalaran Pendants focus the Kirin Tor's magic. The Forsaken seek them to slow the wizards and trace the source of their power. Kirin Tor sorcerers, conjurers, and protectors weave powerful spells in Ambermill. Their work threatens Forsaken control of southern Silverpine Forest. Each carries an attuned Dalaran Pendant. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister sends Forsaken operatives to recover the pendants. He hopes to slow the mages and uncover who guides their magical weave.

item:dalaran-status-report.text:
Dalaran Status Report. At Ambermill, the Kirin Tor rebuild Dalaran in the open, while the Deathstalkers seek their report. During the Third War, the Scourge sacked Dalaran, and Archimonde brought down its towering spires. Early in the rebuilding, the surviving magi removed the city's protective shield and began their work in the open.

The Kirin Tor keeps enclaves such as Ambermill in southeastern Silverpine Forest. Its wizards compile the Dalaran Status Report, which records the city's condition. The Deathstalkers seek its intelligence.

item:dalin-s-heart.text: Dalin's Heart. Near the Greymane Wall in Silverpine Forest, Dalin Forgewright guards refugees with an honorable heart. Undercity warlocks seek the hearts of truly virtuous mortals. They use them to call a succubus and bind her to their service. Dalin Forgewright spends his days defending desperate Lordaeron refugees kept from safety by the sealed Greymane Wall. His selfless devotion makes him a rare offering of unblemished purity, and his heart is carved for rites in the Temple of the Damned.

item:darkhound-blood.text:
Darkhound Blood. In Tirisfal's fields and forests, tainted darkhounds yield Darkhound Blood, a bodily fluid. The Royal Apothecary Society gathers it as an early reagent for experiments to engineer a lethal new plague. Under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Royal Apothecary Society seeks a virulent contagion that can wipe out Arthas and his Scourge. Apothecary Johaan is stationed in Brill. He theorizes that local beasts, corrupted by dark energies and resilient to the surrounding decay, possess unusual biological properties.

By distilling wild darkhound blood, Johaan hopes to uncover compounds that can resist or spread virulent necrotic strains.

item:darkshore-grouper.text: Darkshore Grouper. Along Darkshore, Darkshore Grouper are a familiar catch, though murloc attacks have driven fishermen from their boats. The fish are prized for food and sport, and a good haul takes patience. In Darkshore’s cold waters, Darkshore Grouper are a welcome catch. Around Auberdine, anglers value them for the simple dishes they make. Travelers and residents alike enjoy those meals. A fishing line and basic gear are enough to bring one in. For many fishermen, catching a grouper is as pleasing as eating it. Fishermen such as Gubber Blump once rowed small boats into deeper waters and returned with grouper by the dozen. Now the coastal murlocs are more aggressive, and most boats around Auberdine stay ashore. Anglers fish from shore and dock instead. Locals suspect the murlocs are eating the grouper, so a good haul takes patience.

item:darksoul-shackle.text: Darksoul Shackle. Moonrage Darksouls in Silverpine Forest wear enchanted fetters forged under Archmage Arugal’s direction. At the Sepulcher, Forsaken mages seek them to learn how the magic gripping the region can be undone. Archmage Arugal could not fully command or sustain the worgen he unleashed upon Silverpine Forest. So he bound enchanted implements such as Darksoul Shackles to the beasts. The fetters channel outside sorcery into the Moonrage Darksouls, strengthening them and anchoring the curse that keeps them thrall to Shadowfang Keep.

item:darnassus-marzipan.text:
Darnassus Marzipan. At Hallow's End, Darnassus innkeepers offer visitors marzipan after a dance. Made in the night elven capital for the autumn celebration, it is one of four treats Jesper needs. At Hallow's End, Alliance capitals share a lighthearted trick-or-treating custom. Dwarves offer sharp mints, Stormwind makes chewy nougat, and Darnassus innkeepers prepare delicate marzipan. Dance when an innkeeper asks, and you receive a piece.

Jesper needs the sweet as one of four regional treats. He is a sick orphan in Stormwind's Cathedral Square and cannot go out to collect them himself.

item:darthalia-s-sealed-commendation.text: Darthalia's Sealed Commendation. At Tarren Mill, Darthalia sends word of victories against Hillsbrad's human defenders to Undercity's high command. After the fighting in Hillsbrad Foothills, High Executor Darthalia seals a dispatch of victories against the human defenders and the ruin of their positions. She sends it to Varimathras, the dreadlord who advises Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. In Undercity's Royal Quarter, the report gives Forsaken leaders proof that Alliance enclaves south of Lordaeron can be broken. Then northern garrisons can turn to face the Scourge.

item:deadmire-s-tooth.text: Deadmire's Tooth. In Dustwallow Marsh, Deadmire's tooth carries proof of a hunt brought to an end. Melor Stonehoof on Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff receives it as proof that the ancient crocolisk's suffering has ended. Tauren hunters on Hunter Rise see the hunt as a bond of balance, reverence, and mercy. Deadmire once ranked among the finest crocolisks in Dustwallow Marsh. Age made his final years a torment, though the fierce spirit of his prime remained. His great bones and failing body had become a prison of pain. Deadmire's Tooth proves to Melor Stonehoof that an honorable hunt has ended the beast's suffering.

item:death-cap.text: Death Cap. In Darkshore, Death Cap grows in a cave behind Cliffspring Falls. Night elf herbalists seek the scarce fungus, though the Grove of the Ancients warns against going near the falls. Death Cap grows in a damp cave behind Cliffspring Falls, along Darkshore’s northeastern mountain ridges. Scaber stalks cover the cavern floor, but Death Cap is scarce. Night elf herbalists such as Barithras Moonshade value it for experimental brewing. To find even one, you must enter a cave the Grove of the Ancients warns against, where corruption is taking root.

item:deathstalker-report.text:
Deathstalker Report. In Silverpine Forest, Deathstalker Rane Yorick sends word of Scourge resistance to High Executor Hadrec. Deathstalkers Rane Yorick and Quinn Yorick met a deadly ambush in northern Silverpine Forest. Pinned down among the pines by the Scourge, they gathered their findings into a hurried dispatch. The report describes stronger resistance than the Forsaken expected as they seek to claim the region.

Quinn was gravely injured, so Rane entrusted the report to passing allies. They must carry it without delay to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher.

item:deepfury-s-orders.text: Deepfury's Orders. Beneath the Thandol Span, Deepfury's Orders lie beside the fallen Ol' Rustlocke. Dark Iron dwarves left the crumpled parchment after ambushing the scouting defender. Ol' Rustlocke was a dwarven defender scouting the foundations of the Thandol Span. Dark Iron dwarves cornered and slew him there. Beside his clenched fist lay crumpled orders written by their leader, Deepfury. The orders show a coordinated plot against the bridge between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands.

item:deepmoss-egg.text: Deepmoss Egg. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Deepmoss Eggs draw goblin merchants from Ratchet. Deepmoss spiders lay clustered clutches in the crags and canyons, and Booty Bay pirates prize them for omelettes. Deepmoss spiders nest across the Stonetalon Mountains, especially in Sishir Canyon and beneath the surviving trees of Windshear Crag. There, they leave clustered clutches of viable eggs in thick webbed sacks, sheltered by damp mountain moss. Most travelers have little use for them, but goblin traders see a chance to profit. Booty Bay has taken to spider egg omelettes, an eccentric fad among wealthy pirates and adventurous diners. Local supplies cannot satisfy their appetite, so Mebok Mizzyrix of Ratchet arranges shipments through Wharfmaster Dizzywig. Collectors brave Stonetalon's venomous broods for fresh clutches, and the eggs become valuable cargo.

item:defias-docket.text: Defias Docket. Defias operatives hid their orders at Addle's Stead in western Duskwood. The docket gives Stormwind's search for its missing emissary a lead into the Brotherhood's plans. Master Elling Trias points investigators toward Duskwood as they follow leads on the kingdom's missing diplomat. Watcher Backus has tracked unusual Defias movements converging on Addle's Stead, the derelict farm south of the road from Westfall. A strongbox there holds the Defias Docket. Its records trace the Brotherhood's movements and show that their work reaches beyond highway robbery and local banditry.

item:defias-tower-key.text:
Defias Tower Key. In Westfall, the Defias Tower Key marks a quiet passage past Klaven's Tower's sentries. Stormwind operatives need it as proof that an infiltrator slipped by unseen. Klaven's Tower is a Defias Brotherhood stronghold on the Westfall coast. Recent shipments from Duskwood brought malformed Defias drones to guard it. The drones are undead and covered in spikes.

SI:7 watchers direct field agents to pick the sentries' pockets instead of fighting them. That way, no alarm sounds as the tower's defenses are breached.

item:deliah-s-ring.text: Deliah's Ring. In Silverpine Forest, Deliah's Ring lies among the Rot Hide gnolls’ corpse piles. Its inscription points back to a plague victim taken from Tirisfal’s mass graves. Among the Rot Hide gnoll mounds in Silverpine Forest, a ring rests on the hand of a fairly fresh corpse. The band bears a simple inscription: “For Deliah.” The gnolls do more than scavenge battlefields. They raid the mass graves of Tirisfal Glades and carry human and Forsaken corpses south to Fenris Isle for their own purposes.

item:delivery-to-mathias.text: Delivery to Mathias. Keryn Sylvius sends a sealed parcel from Goldshire to Master Mathias Shaw in Stormwind. The delivery offers a promising rogue a first look at SI:7's inner workings. From the Lion's Pride Inn, a parcel must reach the Stormwind Barracks. For a young rogue, the journey is a test for Stormwind Intelligence. Keryn Sylvius entrusts the package to novice cutpurses, giving them their first meeting with Master Mathias Shaw. They must cross the capital quietly, keep a low profile, and follow discreet orders without questions. The handoff brings an operative to SI:7 headquarters in Old Town. Mathias Shaw uses these deliveries to tell pretenders from true talents. Those who present the parcel without faltering receive field assignments. First come covert reconnaissance and infiltration against Defias smuggling networks in Elwynn Forest.

item:deviate-hide.text:
Deviate Hide. In the Wailing Caverns, Deviate Hide bears the mark of Naralex's dream. Druids seek to turn its taint to useful leather goods. Naralex's slumber beneath the Barrens changed the beasts of the Wailing Caverns. The night elf druid's dream became an Emerald Nightmare, and deviate predators arose with tough, mutated hides. Their pelts carry evil, yet remain supple and resilient for leathercrafting.

Nalpak gathers the hides from his perch high above the cavern mouth, in a skull-shaped rock formation. He studies their properties and fashions them into sturdy utility packs.

item:devlin-s-remains.text: Devlin's Remains. Near Agamand Mills, Devlin's remains tell of a bitter legacy. The younger son of the wealthy family that owned the mills roamed the road by his ruined home as a mindless Scourge thrall. A traveler struck him down and carried his bones to a survivor in Brill, who sought vengeance. Devlin Agamand lived in the shadow of his elder brother Thurman. Thurman was gentle and tall, while Devlin was frail and sharp-tongued. When the Plague of Undeath swept through northern Tirisfal Glades, the Agamand family failed to protect its lands and laborers. Devlin fell among the first. The Scourge raised him as a ravenous ghoul, and his mad chattering haunted the roadside leading to Agamand Mills. Coleman Farthing lives in Brill and holds a deep grudge against the Agamand bloodline. He blames the family for failing his own when the plague came. Farthing sent travelers to lay Devlin to rest and gather his remains. He wanted Devlin's bones on his mantle, to savor how his former masters had been reduced to dust and shattered fragments beneath his heel.

item:dirt-caked-pendant.text: Dirt-Caked Pendant. In the Barrens, Dogran gives up the Dirt-Caked Pendant he carried. It reaches Gan'rul Bloodeye in Orgrimmar, where the keepsake is used to draw a succubus.

item:disarming-colloid.text:
Disarming Colloid. At the Stonewrought Dam, Disarming Colloid may keep Seaforium from exploding when wet. Ashlan Stonesmirk provides it in the Wetlands to neutralize the powder. At Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan, Ashlan Stonesmirk recognizes the powder left by Dark Iron sappers as Seaforium. Its scent and fine silver crystals give it away. Dry, the powder is harmless. Moisture makes it immensely destructive, a grave danger at the waterlogged dam.

Stonesmirk provides Disarming Colloid to stop the reaction before detonation. Mixed with lurker venom, crushed Mo'grosh crystal, and a crocolisk tear, the colloid neutralizes Seaforium's explosive properties.

item:disarming-mixture.text: Disarming Mixture. At Stonewrought Dam, Chief Engineer Hinderweir prepares Disarming Mixture to stop a Seaforium charge planted by Dark Iron saboteurs. The heavy Seaforium charge lies beneath the dam’s foundation, and no Mountaineers are close enough to help. Hinderweir turns to ingredients named by explosives expert Ashlan Stonesmirk. He stirs them into a chemical neutralizer, then mixes it with the powder keg underwater. The reactive compounds are neutralized, and the charge is left harmless.

item:divined-scroll.text: Divined Scroll. At Silverwind Refuge, the Divined Scroll helps the Sentinels trace what taints Mystral Lake. Intact water elemental bracers lend their magic to reveal the summoner’s identity. Mystral Lake’s tainted waters trouble the Sentinels guarding Ashenvale. Sentinel Velene Starstrike gives travelers a blank divining scroll to trace whoever controls the water elementals infesting the lake. Gather intact bracers from the slain elementals and use them as an arcane reagent. Their lingering bindings pass into the parchment, and the Divined Scroll reveals the rogue wizard’s magical signature.

item:divining-scroll.text: Divining Scroll. At Silverwind Refuge, Sentinel Velene Starstrike gives investigators the Divining Scroll to find who summoned the corrupted elementals. Corrupt water elementals rise from Ashenvale’s pools, and the Sentinels know the disturbance is unnatural. Sentinel Velene Starstrike obtains a scroll to find who is responsible. With five intact elemental bracers as a focus, its magic draws out the summoner’s signature. The blank parchment becomes a Divined Scroll and names the guilty party.

item:dogran-s-pendant.text: Dogran's Pendant. In the Cleft of Shadow, Dogran's Pendant draws a succubus to the warlocks of Orgrimmar. Wounded and apart from his mate, Zankaja, Dogran bears the sorrow bound to it. Dogran's Pendant bears the sorrow of an orc parted from Zankaja. Captivity and crippling wounds have darkened their love. The warlocks of the Cleft of Shadow know that succubi prey on love, yearning, and vulnerability. So they use the pendant's grief to draw a succubus across the Twisting Nether and into Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle.

item:dolanaar-delivery.text: Dolanaar Delivery. In Shadowglen, fresh herbs are bound for Dolanaar. Porthannius entrusts the bundle to young travelers for Innkeeper Keldamyr. Fresh herbs gathered in Aldrassil must reach Dolanaar. Porthannius is occupied with the druids of Shadowglen, so he gives the bundle to young travelers heading south along the road. They carry it to Innkeeper Keldamyr. At Dolanaar's inn, Keldamyr receives the parcel with gratitude. The inn offers weary travelers rest, peace of mind, and sanctuary before they venture deeper into Teldrassil.

item:dragonmaw-war-banner.text: Dragonmaw War Banner. Dragonmaw banners now rise over the orc camps in the Wetlands. Their markings show the dwarven defenders of Menethil Harbor how the threat is growing. After the Second War, the Dragonmaw clan broke apart when its orcs lost control of their enslaved red dragons. The enraged drakes turned on their captors and drove the survivors from Grim Batol into the eastern hills. Now the remaining orcs gather strength under Chieftain Nek'rosh. Their banners rise over camps northeast of Menethil Harbor, warning the marsh settlements of their defiance. Captain Stoutfist at Menethil Harbor sends Alliance adventurers into the marsh camps to bring back Dragonmaw banners. Raiders, centurions, and bone-warders carry these trophies. They prove to the dwarven garrison that the camps are being broken before the clan can launch coordinated raids.

item:dried-seeds.text: Dried Seeds. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem gives travelers Dried Seeds to test the power beneath the Barrens' waters.

item:durnan-s-scalding-mornbrew.text: Durnan's Scalding Mornbrew. Inside Anvilmar, Durnan Furcutter waits for his mug of mornbrew as the mountain cold threatens to cool it before it arrives. A courier delayed on the way to Grelin Whitebeard leaves the fresh cup at risk in Coldridge Valley's frost. Carry it up the snowy path to the mountain hall within a few minutes, or Durnan's brew will go cold.

item:durotar-tiger-fur.text: Durotar Tiger Fur. Across the Echo Isles off Durotar's southeastern coast, Durotar Tiger Fur helps the growing Darkspear settlement endure. The trolls make blankets, tents, and armor from the pelts. In Sen'jin Village, the Darkspear must make scarce supplies last. So they let local tigers thrive until their needs call for a cull. Trolls cure the thick hides into goods their settlement needs, including armor and warm blankets for changing seasonal weather. The Echo Isles lie south of Durotar, across open water. The Darkspear once called the islands home, until the witch doctor Zalazane drove them out. Hunters face danger from Zalazane's thralls and from tigers among the thick foliage. Experienced hunters such as Vel'rin Fang speak of spending entire days motionless in the jungle brush to secure a single clean kill.

item:duskbat-wing.text: Duskbat Wing. Around Deathknell, Duskbat wings help the newly risen Forsaken find protection. New Forsaken rise from Deathknell’s soil with little more than rags and brittle bones. Mindless Scourge and hostile wildlife prowl nearby, so they gather what protection they can. Novice Elreth, assistant to Shadow Priest Sarvis, collects Duskbat Wings and wolf paws. Together, they piece the materials into stronger clothing and armor for freshly raised warriors before they enter the wilderness to fight.

item:dusky-crab-cakes.text: Dusky Crab Cakes. In Darkshire, Chef Grual makes Dusky Crab Cakes for the hungry Jitters. Jitters finds the local delicacy exquisite.

item:dust-devil-debris.text:
Dust Devil Debris. Across Westfall, Dust Devils leave charged grit behind. Mages use it to enchant parchment and bind messaging spells into scrolls. Dust Devils sweep across Westfall’s plains as violent whirlwinds. When one falls, the living storm collapses into charged dust and grit called Dust Devil Debris. A faint trace of the elemental vortex lingers in the residue.

In Stormwind, arcane practitioners such as Collin Mauren prize the grit for specialized sorcery. Mixed into enchanted ink and parchment, it helps a wizard bind an airy messaging spell to a scroll, carrying words across the kingdom.

item:dwarven-tinder.text:
Dwarven Tinder. In the Wetlands, Alliance saboteurs carry Dwarven Tinder to burn Dragonmaw siege engines before they reach Menethil Harbor. Alliance scouts found Chieftain Nek'rosh's heavy catapults in the Dragonmaw encampment, and Menethil Harbor faced a crisis. Fighting in Dun Algaz had cut the harbor off from southern reinforcements. Its defenders could not withstand a long siege, so they chose to sabotage the catapults before they could be used.

Volunteers carried Dwarven Tinder into orcish territory and lit it with a struck spark. Its flames burned through the reinforced wooden engines in minutes.

item:ear-of-balgaras.text: Ear of Balgaras. At Dun Modr, the ear of Balgaras proves the warlock’s command has ended. Ironforge’s mountaineers recover it from the Dark Iron commander’s corpse. Balgaras the Foul led the Dark Iron assault on Dun Modr. His forces sabotaged the Thandol Span and destroyed the dwarven garrison, leaving the outpost in ruins. A scheming warlock, Balgaras directed his troops from the shadows and avoided personal combat. Longbraid the Grim, the mountain king’s officer outside the ruins, wants proof that the ringleader has fallen. Balgaras’s severed ear shows his rule at the northern border is over. Dun Modr’s fall cost Longbraid his brother and dozens of stout soldiers when the West Bridge collapsed. The ear cannot mend the span or bring back the dead. Without Balgaras to direct them, the surviving Dark Iron forces scattered through the northern Wetlands are easier for Ironforge’s scouts to contain before another commander arrives from the south.

item:ebonlocke-s-response-to-solomon.text: Ebonlocke's Response to Solomon. In Darkshire, Lord Ello Ebonlocke refuses Solomon's plea for aid in Redridge. His letter says the Night Watch cannot leave Duskwood undefended. Magistrate Solomon asked Duskwood for reinforcements against the blackrock orcs after Stormwind ignored his petitions. Lord Ello Ebonlocke answers in anger and promises no aid. He reminds Solomon that the Night Watch formed because Stormwind abandoned Darkshire when corrupting magic first gripped the woods. If its defenders march to Redridge, Duskwood will be left defenceless and fall to evil before the militia reaches the forest's edge.

item:echeyakee-s-hide.text:
Echeyakee's Hide. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn awaits Echeyakee's Hide, taken from the legendary white lion of the Barrens. Tauren honor Whitemist as an embodiment of mercy and death, while hunters bring his pelt as proof of their prowess. Echeyakee means Whitemist in the Taur-ahe tongue. Among the savannah's predators, the lion earned that name for his stealthy white coat and swift kills. He ended his prey's lives before fear or pain could take hold.

A hunter summons the elusive cat near the giant kodo bones northeast of the Crossroads with a ceremonial horn, then claims his pelt. Bringing it to Sergra Darkthorn proves martial skill and honors Whitemist's silent, merciful end.

item:egalin-s-grimoire.text: Egalin's Grimoire. In the Undercity, Egalin's Grimoire guides warlocks who seek to summon and command a voidwalker. A master warlock wrote it to teach at the Temple of the Damned. Egalin's Grimoire gives the means to call a being of chaos from the Nether. Egalin was a master summoner, famed for commanding voidwalkers with ease. He taught his skill to his students, among them Carendin Halgar. Without the book's formulas and methods of channeling, an unprepared summoner may be torn apart by the being called forth.

item:electropeller.text: Electropeller. In Darkshore, Electropeller parts lie scattered through freshwater after a night outing went wrong. Wizbang Cranktoggle built the electropellers to propel an experimental exploding duck decoy. The gnome inventor works out of Auberdine. After too many drinks, he went scouting along Darkshore's waterways and blacked out. Hours later, he woke with singed hair and an empty pack. His electropellers had tumbled into the freshwater currents, where they remain scattered through rivers and lakes until patient anglers recover them.

item:elixir-of-pain.text: Elixir of Pain. At Tarren Mill, Forsaken apothecaries brew the Elixir of Pain for dangerous trials. They test biological agents meant to advance Lady Sylvanas's darker ambitions. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks formulas to strengthen the Forsaken against their mortal neighbors and the Scourge. The Elixir of Pain is one trial, made with freshly gathered ingredients from the Hillsbrad Foothills. Its makers give little thought to the living subjects. They test volatile substances meant to aid the Dark Lady.

item:elixir-of-suffering.text: Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon tests a new draught for the Royal Apothecary Society. The Society seeks a plague that will kill living humans and the Scourge. Around ruined Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon gathers raw reagents from the wilderness and mixes them into toxic draughts. His work follows the Royal Apothecary Society's charge to devise a plague that will exterminate the living and the dead alike. To test one brew, Lydon gives it to Umpi, his frog assistant.

item:elune-s-tear.text: Elune's Tear. In Ashenvale, night elf healers turn to Elune's Tear when sickness and corruption resist ordinary cures. On a small islet in Iris Lake, east of Astranaar, rests a stone the night elves hold sacred. They believe it bears the purity of the Moon Goddess. Corruption has turned the lake green, and twisted bog beasts roam its shores. Local herbalists and healers, among them Orendil Broadleaf, seek the stone when woodland poultices cannot cleanse deep corruption.

item:embalming-ichor.text:
Embalming Ichor. In northern Tirisfal, Rot Hide gnolls carry a fluid that preserves their decaying bodies. The Forsaken Apothecaries seek to study it against the Scourge. At Garren's Haunt and the nearby mass graves, Rot Hide gnolls dig up plague victims for the Scourge. They are rotting thralls, sent to serve the Lich King's minions.

Embalming Ichor runs through their decayed veins. It preserves their flesh and sustains their unlife. Magistrate Sevren in Brill wants vials recovered from the grave robbers, so the Royal Apothecary Society can study fresh specimens and find ways to turn the fluid against the Scourge.

item:emerald-dreamcatcher.text: Emerald Dreamcatcher. In Starbreeze Village, the Emerald Dreamcatcher lies forgotten after the Gnarlpine furbolgs drove its people away. Druids of Ban’ethil Barrow Den gave the amulet to Tallonkai Swiftroot, hoping it would draw vigor from the Emerald Dream. Gaerolas Talvethren, the druidic warden of Ban’ethil Barrow Den, oversaw the making of the Emerald Dreamcatcher. The druids gave this enchanted amulet to only a chosen few. It draws energy from the Emerald Dream, bringing fortune and protection to its bearer. When maddened Gnarlpine furbolgs overran Starbreeze Village, the amulet stayed in a dresser, left behind in hostile, corrupted territory.

item:empty-blue-waterskin.text: Empty Blue Waterskin. Brine sends the Empty Blue Waterskin north from the Barrens to gather sacred water. The liquid will help her prepare the draught needed to summon and appease the water spirit. Brine gives the Empty Blue Waterskin to a shaman initiate at her hilltop hut in the southern Barrens. The vessel marks the final and most perilous gathering task of early training. To commune with the spirit of water, the initiate must seek pure, undisturbed sources across Kalimdor. The waterskin is meant for a secluded fountain deep within the Ruins of Stardust, along Ashenvale's contested borderlands. The initiate must leave the safety of Horde territory and travel into ancient groves guarded by nature beasts and night elves. At a fountain in the ruined sanctuary deep within the Ruins of Stardust, the waterskin is filled and becomes a Filled Blue Waterskin. With water samples from the Barrens and Tarren Mill, its contents let Brine brew the draught needed to summon and appease the elemental spirit of water.

item:empty-brown-waterskin.text: Empty Brown Waterskin. Brine gives an empty waterskin to a shaman initiate in the Barrens. Brine gives the shaman initiate an empty leather skin for the opening trial of the Call of Water. The initiate carries it to the watering hole beneath her dwelling, then returns with it full. Local quilboar guard the pool and prize its water. Water is scarce in the Barrens, so even a small oasis can sustain life and spark violence.

item:empty-cleansing-bowl.text: Empty Cleansing Bowl. In Auberdine, the Empty Cleansing Bowl carries moonwell water against the Blackwood corruption. Mixed with food samples, the water makes a meal that briefly breaks the satyrs’ demonic hold over the furbolgs. In Auberdine, Thundris Windweaver gives adventurers the Empty Cleansing Bowl to carry sacred water from the local moonwell. The night elves have learned that satyrs use enchanted talismans to drive the northern Blackwood furbolgs into demonic madness. Dip the bowl in the moonwell, then mix its water with nuts, grains, and fruits gathered from the furbolgs. The blessed meal briefly restores the afflicted creatures’ sanity and reveals the satyr overseer behind their madness.

item:empty-cliffspring-falls-sampler.text: Empty Cliffspring Falls Sampler. At Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore, young druids gather water to investigate a poison killing local wildlife. The Cenarion Circle gives them empty samplers for water from the cave mouth. Cliffspring Falls feeds northern Darkshore. Poison in its headwaters puts the local wildlife at risk. When a wasting poison began killing the region’s deer, Dendrite Starblaze of the Cenarion Circle gave empty samplers to young druids from Moonglade. They must gather water at a cave entrance by the falls, overrun by hostile naga.

item:empty-dreadmist-peak-sampler.text: Empty Dreadmist Peak Sampler. At Dreadmist Peak, druids gather water from a tainted pool to learn what is sickening the northern Barrens wildlife. The sample may help Tonga Runetotem find a cure. Dendrite Starblaze suspects the pools atop Dreadmist Peak are tied to a sickness afflicting gazelles and troubling the northern Barrens. The pools influence the weather, and he fears they are spreading the blight. So he sends druid initiates up the mountain with empty samplers to draw water. The Burning Blade, a demon-worshipping cult, now infests the heights.

item:empty-leaden-collection-phial.text:
Empty Leaden Collection Phial. Ozzie Togglevolt gathers Gnomeregan’s radioactive fallout in a leaden phial. He hopes the residue may help cure his afflicted kin, or make an extraordinarily potent drink. Ozzie Togglevolt made a leaden phial to gather the radiation left in Gnomeregan. The city’s vents once flooded its tunnels with toxic radiation to purge the trogg menace. The surviving defenders became leper gnomes, and the invading beasts were irradiated.

Green light still clings to Irradiated Invaders and Pillagers prowling the ruins. The lead shields the handler as the phial draws in the dangerous residue. Once sealed, the collection becomes a Full Leaden Collection Phial for Ozzie’s experiments.

item:empty-red-waterskin.text: Empty Red Waterskin. In Tarren Mill, the Empty Red Waterskin is bound for a well untouched by blight. Brine gives it to shaman initiates for their elemental trials. Brine gives shaman initiates a plain red skin for the Call of Water trials. They carry it across the sea to Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The Forsaken occupy the town, yet its central well still draws fresh spring water. The filled skin brings a sample back to Brine, who blends it into a vial of purest water for the initiate’s trial.

item:empty-sampling-tube.text: Empty Sampling Tube. In Auberdine, Thundris Windweaver gives you an Empty Sampling Tube to test the Cliffspring River. Night elf scholars study the taint threatening Darkshore. Darkshore's waterways are turning foul as blight spreads through the wilderness. In Auberdine, Thundris Windweaver investigates the change. He gives you an empty glass tube for water from the Cliffspring River. Take the sample from the pool beneath the first waterfall north of town. Night elf naturalists will examine it to learn about the corruption flowing toward Mist's Edge.

item:empty-water-tube.text: Empty Water Tube. In Auberdine, the Empty Water Tube is ready to gather sacred moonwell water for the red crystal on Darkshore’s eastern cliffs. Sentinels and scholars seek pure lunar essence to study the mysterious red crystal along Darkshore’s eastern ridge. Ordinary glass or flasks can taint consecrated water, so investigators visiting Auberdine’s moonwell receive this sealed vial. They carry the filled vessel up the mountain slopes to learn how the alien mineral responds to Elune’s magic.

item:enchanted-gaea-seeds.text: Enchanted Gaea Seeds. At Sun Rock Retreat, Enchanted Gaea Seeds are bound for the Charred Vale. Druidic magic helps them take root in ash-choked soil and begin to heal Kalimdor's ravaged land. Horde druids are working to heal the deep scars across Stonetalon Mountains. At Sun Rock Retreat, Tammra Windfield enchants raw Gaea Seeds to endure corruption and elemental blight. Planted in fertile dirt mounds beneath the Charred Vale's soot, they can take root in harsh ground. Yet hostile fire elementals and invasive harpies still rule the vale. The seeds are part of the struggle for Stonetalon's future. Their enchanted husks resist lingering corruption and give native plants a foothold. That returning growth is meant to soothe agitated fire elementals, crowd out feral harpies, and counter the deforestation wrought by the Venture Company's relentless logging.

item:enchanted-resonite-crystal.text: Enchanted Resonite Crystal. In Stonetalon, Mor'rogal has changed resonite crystals with shamanic magic. He made the Enchanted Resonite Crystal to break the cask that holds Goggeroc. In the caverns of the Stonetalon Mountains, raw resonite crystals carry unusual harmonic and earthen properties. Shaman Mor'rogal sensed danger within a sealed underground cask, so he changed the crystals with his elemental powers. The Enchanted Resonite Crystal can break the reinforced Resonite cask and rouse Goggeroc, a giant Earthen, while he is still dazed from his long sleep.

item:encrypted-memorandum.text: Encrypted Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, the Encrypted Memorandum quietly guides new rogues to their trainer. Solm Hargrin disguises his invitation as official communication and calls scoundrels in exile to stand together. In Anvilmar, rogues keep their presence quiet. Their trainer, Solm Hargrin, reaches recruits through the Encrypted Memorandum instead of approaching them in plain view. The coded parchment looks like a directive from distant superiors. It tells fledgling rogues where to find a mentor while keeping local guards and suspicious townsfolk from noticing.

item:encrypted-parchment.text: Encrypted Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Encrypted Parchment calls promising young orc rogues to the Den. Gornek gives it to recruits after their first trials, and its cipher points to Rwag, the hidden trainer. In the Valley of Trials, young orcs prove their strength beneath the open sun. Those gifted in stealth, deception, and bladecraft draw a different notice. After facing the local wildlife, promising orc rogues receive Encrypted Parchment from Gornek. Its coded words call to those who can read a message meant to stay hidden. The cipher guides a novice through the Den, past the other clan trainers, to Rwag. There, the recruit learns that the Shattered Hand arranged the summons. The order works within the Horde's covert network. Answering its call begins a rogue's training in espionage and shadowcraft.

item:encrypted-rune.text: Encrypted Rune. In Coldridge Valley, the Encrypted Rune calls promising new rogues to Anvilmar. Its message bids them decipher the words and seek out Solm Hargrin. A new rogue must read thieves' cant to understand the rune. In doing so, they meet the shadowy craft needed to survive Dun Morogh's harsh wilderness. Its ciphers bear a private summons from Solm Hargrin, the rogue mentor in Anvilmar, for those who show promise in stealth and cunning. Deciphering the rune leads new rogues to Solm Hargrin inside Anvilmar. He hopes to strengthen the valley's covert ranks as local tensions rise. Solm teaches bladecraft and stealth, but also vigilance and camaraderie. With peace strained, rogues need to stand together.

item:encrypted-scroll.text: Encrypted Scroll. In Deathknell, a sealed scroll calls a newly risen rogue to meet David Trias. Its ciphered words point the bearer to the inn and the first steps toward the Forsaken’s covert ranks. A newly awakened Forsaken with a gift for stealth draws notice in Deathknell. After a scout proves capable against the mindless Scourge in the nearby graveyard, the Encrypted Scroll is handed over. Rogue trainer David Trias sealed it and bids the bearer to find him at the local inn. The summons offers a fledgling operative training to serve the Dark Lady, rather than spend a second life as a pickpocket. The scroll’s brief message calls the rogue to make contact in Deathknell before traveling deeper into Tirisfal Glades. Trias watches for promising talent on behalf of the Shadowstalkers, the Forsaken’s covert arm. In Lordaeron, the Forsaken rely on silent blades and cunning scouts against the Scarlet Crusade, surviving Alliance enclaves, and the Scourge left behind. Answering the ciphered summons begins the path into that covert network.

item:encrypted-sigil.text: Encrypted Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Encrypted Sigil calls newly awakened night elf rogues to Frahun Shadewhisper. He begins their training as dangers gather around Teldrassil. New night elf scouts and infiltrators in Shadowglen receive the Encrypted Sigil by discreet means. A quiet messenger brings it on behalf of Frahun Shadewhisper. Its hidden instructions direct each initiate to report to Frahun near Aldrassil. By reading and delivering the token, an initiate shows they can follow subtle directions and carry covert messages. Frahun explains why rogues matter in an unsettled world. Tensions simmer between the night elves and the distant Horde, yet open warfare is not their only danger. Rogues must gather intelligence across Teldrassil as the Kaldorei’s unseen eyes and blades. They must learn to strike before threats take root in the World Tree’s boughs.

item:encrypted-tablet.text: Encrypted Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a coded tablet sends novice troll rogues to Rwag. The rogue trainer inscribes the message and keeps his post inside the Den. Novice troll rogues receive the Encrypted Tablet when they reach the Valley of Trials. Its coded words direct them to Rwag, an orc trainer who lives in the Den’s shaded caves. The slate keeps the local shadow operatives’ business discreet and tests whether new recruits can understand its message. The tablet brings recruits into contact with the Horde’s wider shadow network. When they report to Rwag, scouts learn that syndicates such as the Shattered Hand watch their progress. These syndicates rely on valley trainers to judge whether prospective cutpurses, spies, and assassins are sharp enough to serve the new nation.

item:essence-of-nightlash.text:
Essence of Nightlash. At the Dead Fields, Nightlash's defeat leaves a trace the Forsaken can carry away. High Executor Hadrec needs it as proof that the Scourge force behind the rot hide gnolls has been broken. At the abandoned farmstead called the Dead Fields in northern Silverpine, packs of undead rot hide gnolls hold their ground under Scourge command. Forsaken assaults have failed again and again. The feral gnolls are not the cause; their spectral commander, Nightlash, turns the attackers back.

Her wailing magic strengthens the gnoll lines and routs forces sent from the Sepulcher. When Nightlash is slain, her incorporeal form dissolves into dust, leaving a crystalline magical essence behind. Banshees leave no bodily corpse, so Nightlash's essence is the only physical proof that the spirit has been destroyed. High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher needs it to confirm that the Scourge foothold has fallen. With that proof, the Forsaken can secure their northern perimeter and suppress the rot hide threat.

item:essential-artificial.text:
Essential Artificial. In Ironforge, Essential Artificial parts help gnomish tinkers and engineers rebuild after exile. The gnomes left stockpiles behind when they fled Gnomeregan. Before Gnomeregan fell, tinkers relied on the Essential Artificial as a component for many uses. Gnomish engineers fitted it into contraptions, clockwork wonders and heavy machinery throughout the subterranean halls. Its standard design let smiths and machinists exchange parts with confidence. The trogg invasion and radiation disaster drove the gnomes from Gnomeregan in a desperate rush. Large stores of Essential Artificial parts remained in heavy, steam-powered dispensers called artificial extrapolators, scattered through the deeper passages.

In Tinker Town, master craftsman Klockmort Spannerspan seeks daring adventurers to return to the contaminated ruins and recover the parts. He needs them so research and invention can continue.

item:etched-note.text: Etched Note. At Camp Narache, Lanka Farshot calls a young tauren hunter to begin training. The camp's hunter trainer welcomes the novice to the traditions of the hunt. At Camp Narache, a runner brings young shu'halo a message from Lanka Farshot, the camp's hunter trainer. The note names the hunter the tribe's heart. Natural instinct alone is not enough. The hunter needs rigorous instruction and deep respect for Mulgore's wilderness. For the tauren, hunting is sacred and necessary for survival. It is woven into tribal life. Hunters work alongside warriors, shamans and druids, and the tribe looks to them for guidance and protection. The student brings the note to Lanka to begin learning weaponcraft and how to understand beasts. These lessons prepare the student to defend and sustain the tribes.

item:etched-parchment.text: Etched Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek sends new hunters to Jen'shan for their first lessons in Durotar. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls begin their rites in the Valley of Trials. As recruits prove themselves against local vermin, Gornek helps them find their calling. He gives the Etched Parchment to those who will wield bow, gun, and fang. Its message comes from Jen'shan, a skilled hunter trainer who seeks fresh eyes and steady hands. Taking the parchment to Jen'shan begins a hunter's training in Durotar. She teaches that the wild path demands dedication. Mastering the beasts of the desert takes as much effort as an arcanist's magic or a shaman's work with the spirits. Her summons brings new hunters to lessons in marksmanship and wilderness survival.

item:etched-rune.text: Etched Rune. In Coldridge Valley, the Etched Rune calls promising dwarven hunters to Anvilmar. Hunter trainer Thorgas Grimson sends it to begin their instruction in the wilderness. Dwarven runes mark the Etched Rune, sent to novices who show promise in Coldridge Valley’s snowdrifts. Mountaineer and hunter trainer Thorgas Grimson calls fledgling trackers to Anvilmar. There, they move beyond basic survival and learn the hunter’s craft: respect for Dun Morogh’s beasts, tracking mountain predators, care for ranged weapons, and endurance in the harsh elements.

item:etched-sigil.text: Etched Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Etched Sigil calls new night elf hunters to Ayanna Everstride. Newly awakened night elf hunters receive the Etched Sigil when they enter Shadowglen. Its carved marks carry a welcome from Ayanna Everstride, the hunter trainer who lives high in Aldrassil’s hollowed boughs. The sigil sends each novice to seek her out and begin learning archery and wilderness tracking, along with the night elf bond between stalker and beast.

item:explosive-stick-of-gann.text: Explosive Stick of Gann. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire turns stolen dwarven plans against Bael Modan. He built a charge to sabotage the dwarves’ flying machine. Prospector Khazgorm led the Ironforge excavation into southern Kalimdor. The dwarves drove the Stonespire tauren from their ancestral village and razed their sacred grounds to build Bael Modan. Gann Stonespire reclaimed Khazgorm’s blueprints to avenge his displaced and fallen kin. He studied the plans and built a charge strong enough to wreck heavy machinery.

item:faded-shadowhide-pendant.text: Faded Shadowhide Pendant. In Redridge, a voice now sounds from the Faded Shadowhide Pendant. The Shadowhide gnolls wore it to receive Morganth’s orders, and the voice carries Theocritus’s delayed spell. The Shadowhide gnolls of the Redridge Mountains follow Morganth and use enchanted pendants to coordinate their movements. From his sanctuary at Tower Azora, High Mage Theocritus studied the talismans and devised a spell to break into their link. Weeks passed before his broadcast appeared. Now this faded pendant proves the gnolls’ messages can be intercepted, giving Theocritus a way to hinder Morganth’s reach.

item:fallen-moonstone.text: Fallen Moonstone. At Fallen Sky Lake in Ashenvale, night elves draw stones of healing from the water. Blessed by the moon, Fallen Moonstone can restore strength when frailty runs deep. Southeast of Astranaar, Fallen Sky Lake once held many Fallen Moonstones along its shores and shallows. Night elves prized their healing when ordinary remedies failed. But corrupt Shadethicket bog beasts overran the lake, led by a Shadethicket Oracle. The Oracle hoarded every stone it found on a small island at the lake’s center, leaving the local Kaldorei without a vital source of healing.

item:fandral-s-message.text: Fandral's Message. Across the sea, Fandral's Message carries news from Darnassus to Onu in Darkshore. The sealed dispatch concerns Oracle Glade in Teldrassil. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm writes from the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. His sealed dispatch is addressed to Onu, the Ancient of Lore who dwells in the Grove of the Ancients. Reports about Oracle Glade in Teldrassil have reached Fandral, so he sends a courier south of Auberdine with word for Onu. The journey crosses the waters to Darkshore, from the new World Tree to Kalimdor’s older, shadowed mainland.

item:fang-of-vagash.text: Fang of Vagash. In Dun Morogh, Vagash stalks the rams above Amberstill Ranch. His fang proves the deadly predator has been slain. Above Amberstill Ranch, Vagash hunts the rams under cover of darkness. The high crags shelter fierce predators, but none has troubled the local ranches as much as he has. Ironforge’s troops are stretched thin, so the herdsmen go without the city guard’s protection. His severed fang gives the breeders proof that Vagash is dead and their pasturelands are safe again.

item:fangore-s-paw.text: Fangore's Paw. In the Redridge Mountains, Fangore leads the Shadowhide gnolls against Lakeshire. His severed paw proves his death to Magistrate Solomon and may ease the danger closing around the town. Lieutenant Fangore leads the Shadowhide gnolls across the Redridge Mountains. He serves the renegade mage Morganth and directs attacks on trade roads, outlying farms, and the defenses around Lake Everstill. The gnolls leave no uniforms, seals, or banners behind to identify their dead. So Magistrate Solomon demands Fangore's paw as proof that the lieutenant has been executed, giving Lakeshire some relief amid the dangers around town.

item:farren-s-report.text:
Farren's Report. In Southshore, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle's report carries his findings on the local naga. He hopes the dispatch will win him a return to Stormwind. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle grew weary of Southshore's embattled coast, its leaders, and its remote frontier. He sent adventurers to hunt the Daggerspine naga and gather proof of their threat. Then he shaped their findings into a formal report.

Farren plans to send the dispatch to Major Samuelson, captain of the guard in Stormwind Keep, instead of his commander, Marshal Redpath. Samuelson trained Farren, and Farren hopes the report will prove his competence and earn him an immediate transfer to Stormwind City's comforts.

item:fathom-core.text: Fathom Core. Beneath the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Core records the elements at work in Blackfathom Deeps. The Earthen Ring seeks it to learn how the Twilight's Hammer turns those forces to its own ends. Inside an ancient fathom stone beneath the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Core records the elements. Its account follows their shifts, disruptions, and surges over time. Je'neu Sancrea is an Earthen Ring shaman at Zoram'gar Outpost. He seeks the core to learn how the Twilight's Hammer cultists turn the region's elements to their own ends.

item:feather-charm.text: Feather Charm. In Anvilmar, Feather Charms catch a warlock instructor’s eye. Frostmane novices carry these crude trinkets, which hold a faint magical power. Southwest of Anvilmar, Frostmane novices carry feather charms through snowy caverns. Their tribe is known for territorial savagery, yet its young trolls practice primitive spellcraft. The charms hold a faint but unmistakable power. Alamar Grimm, the warlock instructor in Anvilmar, studies this crude trollcraft with interest. He uses the charms to test fledgling warlocks as they seek to bind their first imp.

item:fel-cone.text: Fel Cone. In Teldrassil, Fel Cones carry corruption beneath the tree's boughs. Night elf defenders use the pods against nearby tricksters. Beneath Teldrassil's boughs, Fel Cones mark corruption in the young tree. The gnarled pine cones have fallen and billow foul green smoke. They lie scattered just east of Dolanaar. Tainted magic has warped the surrounding plants, and the pods are dangerous to touch or eat without care.

item:fel-moss.text: Fel Moss. Across Teldrassil, Fel Moss spreads through the forests on grell and grellkin. Its corruption threatens the World Tree’s wildlife and the native furbolg tribes. Corruption has reached Teldrassil’s boughs. The World Tree was planted to restore the night elves’ immortality and heal the natural world, yet Fel Moss marks the decay. Grell and grellkin infest Shadowglen, with the moss’s unnatural, wicked magic clinging to them and radiating from their growth. The dryad Tarindrella gathers samples to learn how deeply the rot has entered the sacred woodland canopy.

item:felix-s-box.text: Felix's Box. In Frostmane camps southwest of Anvilmar, Felix's Box lies far from the gnome refugee who lost it. Radiation swept through Gnomeregan during the failed attempt to purge the trogg menace. Felix Whindlebolt fled with the gnomes into Coldridge Valley, leaving his possessions and crafting gear along the snowy road to escape the fumes. Frostmane trolls plundered the goods before he could return. They carried his box, chest, and bucket of bolts to their settlements southwest of Anvilmar. Felix is unused to violence and poorly suited to Dun Morogh's wilderness. He needs passing adventurers in Anvilmar to help recover his belongings. Their return would restore some normalcy and give the displaced artisan the means to earn a living. He lost everything when Gnomeregan fell.

item:felix-s-bucket-of-bolts.text: Felix's Bucket of Bolts. In Dun Morogh, Frostmane trolls carry Felix's Bucket of Bolts to their camps. Felix Whindlebolt is missing the tools he brought from Gnomeregan. Felix Whindlebolt fled Gnomeregan with his tools after the disaster with the troggs. Radiation drove thousands of gnomes into Dun Morogh's freezing wilds with whatever they could carry. Felix headed for Anvilmar, but Frostmane trolls from the crags southwest of town ambushed him. They seized his belongings, including his bucket of bolts and parts, leaving the artisan without the materials he needs for his craft in exile.

item:felix-s-chest.text: Felix's Chest. In a Frostmane camp southwest of Anvilmar, Felix's Chest holds what he lost fleeing Gnomeregan. When troggs and toxic radioactive fallout drove the gnomes from Gnomeregan, refugees crossed snowy Dun Morogh carrying what they could. Frostmane trolls scavenged the roads and overtook scattered survivors. They took Felix Whindlebolt's sturdy chest to their camps in the crags, where his toolkits and personal belongings remain among their supplies.

item:felstalker-hoof.text: Felstalker Hoof. In Durotar's Valley of Trials, young shaman face felstalkers to prove they are ready. Their hooves go to Canaga Earthcaller before they learn to commune with the earth spirits. Canaga Earthcaller sends young shaman to face the demonic taint threatening Durotar. North in the Valley of Trials, the Burning Blade Coven's vile familiars share the ground with roaming felstalkers. Taking a felstalker's hoof tests a shaman's endurance, resolve, and spirit. Those who subdue the beasts are ready to learn the secrets of the earth and prepare the ceremonial sapta for communing with elemental spirits.

item:fenwick-s-head.text: Fenwick's Head. Forsaken rogues now hunt Fenwick Thatros along the shores of Lordamere Lake. His head proves his execution, demanded by an order passed down from Lord Varimathras. From the Rogues' Quarter in the Undercity, Mennet Carkad acts on urgent intelligence from dreadlord Varimathras. Fenwick Thatros, a hostile undead leader, has made a foothold near the decaying docks of Lordamere Lake in Silverpine Forest. Carkad fears Fenwick may rally hostile undead against the Forsaken. So he sends promising Deathstalkers to find and kill him, then bring back his head as proof. For Deathstalker operatives, bringing Fenwick's Head to Carkad is a trial beyond claiming a bounty. The severed head proves a rogue can infiltrate and assassinate. Success opens the way to deeper and more specialized instruction in the shadow arts from Forsaken masters.

item:fey-dragon-scale.text: Fey Dragon Scale. Around Stonetalon Peak, faerie dragons give up scales that Jin'Zil covets. The Darkspear witch doctor uses one in a brew meant to mock night elven nature magic. Faerie dragons haunt the wild groves around Stonetalon Peak. Their scales shine with natural magic. Night elves honor them as harmless woodland spirits and allies. Outsiders prize the scales as rare magical ingredients.

item:filled-amethyst-phial.text: Filled Amethyst Phial. In Teldrassil, druids gather water from the Oracle Tree's moonwell. Corithras Moonrage receives it for the Cenarion druids to study the World Tree's troubled growth. Northwest Teldrassil holds the Oracle Glade, where the oldest and most potent moonwell rests beneath the Oracle Tree. Other moonwells across the boughs meet the night elves' daily needs, but this water bears the raw essence of Elune's grace. Druids who tend the World Tree's health collect it in amethyst phials for testing and ritual cleansing.

item:filled-blue-waterskin.text: Filled Blue Waterskin. At the Ruins of Stardust, shamans seek water for their trials. The Filled Blue Waterskin bears a pure sample from an ancient fountain. Call of Water initiates travel north from the Barrens into Ashenvale's dense forests. Beyond Lake Mystral, the Ruins of Stardust rest against the mountains between Ashenvale and Stonetalon. Fierce forest beasts guard the secluded elven sanctuary. At the center of its lake, an untouched fountain holds water free of corruption or drought. A blue waterskin filled there carries the sample shaman masters seek for ritual attunement. Brine lives as a hermit on a hill in the southern Barrens. She knows water well and needs this final sample. Brine combines it with water from contrasting wells and springs, then distills a pure essence to offer. The offering can call forth and soothe water's elemental spirits, completing an initiate's trial.

item:filled-brown-waterskin.text: Filled Brown Waterskin. In the Barrens, the Filled Brown Waterskin brings fresh water from the pond below Brine's hut. Aspiring shaman carry it to her to begin brewing sapta, which lets them commune with water spirits. Below Brine's hut, a pond offers rare fresh water in the Barrens. Nearby quilboar fight fiercely over it. A novice shaman sees how scarcity drives creatures to defend what sustains them.

item:filled-cliffspring-falls-sampler.text: Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler. Near Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore, the Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler holds foul water drawn from the headwaters. The Cenarion Circle needs it to study the sickness striking local deer. Cliffspring Falls carries water from the eastern highlands through much of Darkshore. Now local deer are falling ill with an unnatural sickness. At Dendrite Starblaze’s request in Moonglade, druidic initiates draw water from a cave mouth where hostile naga dwell. The vial holds visibly foul water, proof that the fresh supply is tainted.

item:filled-containment-coffer.text:
Filled Containment Coffer. In the Undercity, Forsaken spellcasters trap erratic magical entities for study. A Cantation of Manifestation reveals and weakens rift spawn in the Apothecarium, letting mages seal them inside coffers. Magical disturbances trouble Algernon's shop in the Apothecarium. Forsaken mage Anastasia Hartwell has called on arcane practitioners to capture the entities behind them. Rift creatures are living magical energy, invisible to the eye, and ordinary cages cannot hold them.

Spellcasters reveal the creatures with a Cantation of Manifestation, defeat them in combat, then snap prepared coffers shut around them. The sealed boxes shield their carriers from volatile magical backlashes and keep the creatures intact for magical dissection. Living mana creatures pose a serious threat in the Undercity. Once sealed inside containment coffers, the beasts are carried to Anastasia Hartwell and the city's scholars. Forsaken mages seek to learn whether the intrusions come from natural rifts in Azeroth's magical fabric or from preliminary probes in a calculated magical assault on the kingdom.

item:filled-crystal-phial.text:
Filled Crystal Phial. In Shadowglen, young night elves gather water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil. Tenaron Stormgrip makes it their first lesson in Teldrassil’s sacred power. Tenaron Stormgrip sends young night elves to gather moonwell water before they venture into the wider world. The moonwell lies in Shadowglen, and its waters hold energies traced to the ancient Well of Eternity. Sentinels honor moonwells as shrines of Elune. Druids use their restorative power to tend nature, while the arcane sorcery of old remains forbidden.

Gathering the water begins a lesson in the sacrifice at Mount Hyjal and the care needed to nurture Teldrassil.

item:filled-cursed-ooze-jar.text: Filled Cursed Ooze Jar. In Felwood, a Filled Cursed Ooze Jar carries a sample for Laris Geardawdle in Ironforge. The gnome scholar seeks the ancient origins of slimes across Azeroth. Laris Geardawdle, a gnome researcher, sees mystery in the vile puddles and caustic slimes others pass by. Slimes thrive across Azeroth, and Forsaken apothecaries gather them with care. These sights led Geardawdle to a bold theory: oozes may be primordial secretions bound to Azeroth's creation. To gather a sample, brave Felwood's blighted woods and defeat a cursed ooze. Scoop its acidic remains into an empty jar before they dissolve. Laris Geardawdle hopes his ooze samples will bring knowledge and a lasting name. A major discovery could secure his reputation in the dwarven-led Explorers' League. Since Gnomeregan fell, many gnome refugees in Ironforge have felt pressed to prove their worth to their dwarven hosts. Geardawdle believes that uncovering ooze's ancient secrets will show them that welcoming gnomes was no mistake.

item:filled-dreadmist-peak-sampler.text:
Filled Dreadmist Peak Sampler. At Dreadmist Peak, Horde druids gather water from the summit pools for study. The Cenarion Circle seeks to learn what is poisoning wildlife in the northern Barrens. Dreadmist Peak’s high crags hold pools whose mists shape weather and rainfall across the northern Barrens. The Burning Blade worship demons and made their coven atop the summit. Soon the water soured. Cenarion druids suspect demonic rites poisoned the vapors that feed the surrounding savanna.

They send initiates to collect a sample in a special sampler. The foul liquid confirms their fears. Its corruption can sicken the herds below.

item:filled-etched-phial.text: Filled Etched Phial. In Thunder Bluff, tauren seek a dryad phial of moonwell water. Its rare spiritual power can quench the eternal flame around a sacred centaur relic. The phial must be filled in night elf territory deep in Ashenvale. Dryads around Raynewood Retreat carry the empty vessels, made to hold pure restorative draughts. A sacred moonwell near the western bank of the Falfarren River fills one with water bound to celestial and nature power. Night elves regard taking the water without leave as desecration. The tauren need it to face a threat farther south.

item:filled-jade-phial.text: Filled Jade Phial. In Dolanaar, a Filled Jade Phial carries sacred water from Starbreeze Village back to the central wells. Young night elves gather it as they learn their people's history. Druids in Darnassus draw sacred water from moonwells across Teldrassil to replenish their central wells. In Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage entrusts young travelers with a jade phial that keeps the pure water safe. The moonwell outside Starbreeze Village lies east of Dolanaar. Initiates gather its water as they tend the World Tree. When you return the Filled Jade Phial to Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage shares another chapter of kaldorei history. He tells how, after the Third War, Nordrassil burned and night elves lost their immortality. The Betrayer was released, and Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage disappeared.

item:filled-pure-sample-jar.text: Filled Pure Sample Jar. In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle studies how corruption changes living matter. A Filled Pure Sample Jar holds primordial ooze from the remote wilds, giving him a clean specimen for comparison. Laris Geardawdle studies oozes across Azeroth and how corruption changes living matter. He found that these shapeless creatures absorb the magic and conditions of their homes, then reflect them. After cataloging tainted slimes in Felwood, he sought a clean sample for comparison. A Filled Pure Sample Jar holds primordial ooze gathered from the wilds of Un'Goro Crater, away from corrupted strains. Oozes change readily, so Laris cannot find pure samples near civilization, demonic blights, or necromantic fallout. The glutinous oozes of Un'Goro Crater's untamed basin remain relatively isolated from outside corruption. That makes them a useful standard for scholars in Ironforge.

item:filled-red-waterskin.text:
Filled Red Waterskin. In Tarren Mill, a well gives clear spring water for a shaman’s trial. The Filled Red Waterskin bears water drawn from the village well, amid ruins held by the Forsaken. Brine sends shaman initiates from her hermitage in the Barrens to Tarren Mill to train with water. The journey leads into the Hillsbrad Foothills, where decay and the dead surround the town. Yet the well at its heart still gives clear spring water.

To Brine, that pure water endures as a sign of life in an unhallowed land. She likens the spring, untouched by corruption, to Warchief Thrall’s resolve through hardship. Gathering the water tests whether an initiate honors its purity, even in hostile surroundings.

item:filled-tainted-ooze-jar.text:
Filled Tainted Ooze Jar. In Felwood, a Filled Tainted Ooze Jar carries samples of corruption to Ironforge. The samples may help explain how life began on Azeroth. Across northern Kalimdor, tainted oozes bear Felwood’s lingering corruption. Gnomish researchers provide jars to hold them safely. Most travelers keep clear of these noxious creatures, yet their remains yield samples for natural philosophy and biological study far from the blighted woods. Laris Geardawdle, a gnome scholar with the Explorers' League in Ironforge, gathers the samples. The commonness of slimes fascinates him, and he has seen the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society take an interest in them too.

Many scholars dismiss Geardawdle's theory. He believes slimes and oozes may be primal secretions tied to Azeroth's creation. He seeks proof, and a place among dwarven scholars after Gnomeregan's tragic fall.

item:filled-tourmaline-phial.text: Filled Tourmaline Phial. At the Pools of Arlithrien, Corithras Moonrage waits for the Filled Tourmaline Phial. Its moonwell water helps him watch the health and balance of the growing World Tree. A moonwell lies on the shores of the Pools of Arlithrien, southeast of the road to Darnassus. The path to its shrine has grown dangerous. The Gnarlpine furbolgs were once peaceful neighbors, but now they are violently mad. Corithras Moonrage asks travelers to brave the hostile groves and bring back the water. He hopes it will help him find the corruption deepening across the land.

item:filled-vessel.text:
Filled Vessel. At Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage gathers Teldrassil’s moonwell waters for Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus. The Filled Vessel carries these samples to aid his study of the World Tree’s ailments. Night elf acolytes gather water from moonwells across Teldrassil. The tree was planted without blessings from the Great Aspects, Alexstrasza and Nozdormu. So its boughs remain open to corruption, strange beasts, and crazed furbolg tribes.

In Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage gathers the phials and pours them into the Filled Vessel for the journey to the capital. Together, the waters offer a sample of Teldrassil’s vitality. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm studies them in the Cenarion Enclave, seeking a remedy for the Great Tree’s flaws.

item:final-clue-to-sanders-treasure.text: Final Clue to Sanders' Treasure. Along Westfall’s coast, Captain Sanders’ final directions send scavengers out to sea. A note in an old jug points west toward his buried treasure. Captain Sanders left his final directions in an old whiskey jug on the Westfall coast. The pirate had scattered cryptic notes along the shoreline, and this one completes the trail. From the jug, the directions point due west into the ocean. Follow them through the surf to a lonely offshore rock, where his ironbound sea chest lies.

item:fine-crab-chunks.text: Fine Crab Chunks. Along Darkshore's coast, Reef Crawlers and Encrusted Tide Crawlers yield Fine Crab Chunks. Gubber Blump seeks them for his cooking. Reef Crawlers and Encrusted Tide Crawlers roam Darkshore's shores. By the water, travelers may find them pests or dangers, while cooks prize their meat. The chunks can be boiled, broiled, fried, or stirred into stews.

item:fine-moonstalker-pelt.text: Fine Moonstalker Pelt. In southern Darkshore, Terenthis seeks the hides of mature moonstalkers. Their thick, healthy pelts can help make an enchanted cloak for those searching for Volcor. Moonstalker sires and matriarchs have coats dense and healthy enough to yield a fine pelt. They keep territory along the Wildbend River and farther south toward Ashenvale’s borders. There, they hunt with patience. Common moonstalkers roam Darkshore’s forests, but their hides are not fine enough.

item:fire-tar.text: Fire Tar. Across the eastern Barrens, Razormane spellcasters carry Fire Tar. Horde shamans bring it to Telf Joolam, who brews it into a Fire Sapta that lets them commune with fire spirits. Razormane geomancers, mystics, and thornweavers carry Fire Tar. The quilboar use it in their harsh magic and rituals, where its power is tuned to flame. Shamanic instructors prize the substance as a worldly reagent. It helps mortal senses reach the raw fury of the elements. Young orc and troll shamans travel high among Durotar's crags to Telf Joolam, where they forge their fire totems. Telf asks them to bring a reagent pouch taken from Burning Blade cultists and Fire Tar gathered from the Razormane. He brews the two ingredients into a fire sapta. A shaman who drinks it can perceive the fire spirits waiting atop the nearby peaks.

item:fizzle-s-claw.text: Fizzle's Claw. In Thunder Ridge, Fizzle Darkstorm’s claw is carried to Razor Hill as proof of his death. The goblin warlock threatened the orcish homeland under the Burning Blade’s banner. Orgnil Soulscar sent forces to root out shadow cults threatening the orcish homeland. He named Fizzle Darkstorm as an instigator spreading corruption in Thunder Ridge. Fizzle served the Burning Blade as a warlock. His claw now proves to Horde commanders that he has been slain. Thunder Ridge lies just northwest of Razor Hill, close enough to threaten the surrounding lands. Horde scouts carried Fizzle’s claw back to Razor Hill. It confirms that his rituals and attempt to establish a Burning Blade foothold have been stopped.

item:flagongut-s-fossil.text: Flagongut's Fossil. At the Wetlands dig, Flagongut seeks answers in an ancient fossil. The Explorers' League keeps the specimen. Flagongut believes the Stone of Relu can help him decipher its secrets. Prospector Whelgar keeps the fossil at his excavation site in the southern hills of the Wetlands. Dwarven expeditions across Khaz Modan unearthed it. Archaeologist Flagongut believes the ancient stone holds forgotten powers, and sees a kinship with artifacts found across the sea in Darkshore.

item:flatland-cougar-femur.text:
Flatland Cougar Femur. Across Mulgore, flatland cougars stalk the plains, and Maur Raincaller needs one of their bones. A Flatland Cougar Femur is part of the remedy he seeks for a venomous bite. Flatland cougars are among Mulgore's most dangerous hunters. They vanish into dry brush, then spring upon their prey. Hunters use their pelts and claws for leatherworking and trophies. Their heavy bones also have a place in local medicine.

Maur Raincaller of Bloodhoof Village bears a venomous wound from Mazzranache, a monstrous pink strider. He urgently needs a cougar femur and parts from other local beasts. Crushed or boiled, the bone yields what he needs for an antitoxin poultice to draw fever and necrotic venom from the festering bite.

item:flatland-prowler-claw.text:
Flatland Prowler Claw. Across Mulgore's plains, young hunters gather Flatland Prowler Claws to prove their resolve and fieldcraft to the elders of Thunder Bluff. Flatland prowlers hunt across Mulgore's plains, springing on prey in tall grass. Their cunning and fierce defense of their territory make them dangerous to travelers. For young hunters, tracking them is a hard test.

Gathering their claws is a recognized tradition. Skorn Whitecloud sends promising wanderers to bring the claws to Melor Stonehoof at Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. The claws prove their resolve and fieldcraft as they follow the hunter's way.

item:foreman-s-blackjack.text: Foreman's Blackjack. In the Valley of Trials, Foreman's Blackjack keeps Durotar's peons at work. Foremen use the leather-wrapped cosh to wake laborers who fall asleep during the Horde's early construction. Durotar needs stockpiles of lumber for the Horde's new home. In the Valley of Trials, peons do the work, and Foreman Thazz'ril keeps the crews moving with Foreman's Blackjack. Its weighted blow jolts laborers awake when they nap beneath the valley's shade trees. It is meant to wake them, not kill them. Peon life in the new Horde means hard, unglamorous work under an iron fist.

item:forged-steel-bars.text:
Forged Steel Bars. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze's forged steel bars are gone. Recovering them proves a warrior's resolve to reclaim stolen property. Thun'grim Firegaze is a visually impaired orc smith with a camp in the northern Barrens. During a night raid, Razormane quilboar took his iron chest. They distracted him with grunts and snorts while others slipped away with it.

The quilboar could not work fine steel, so they left the unopened chest near a ruined wagon in their encampment to the northwest. The bars remain intact for warriors willing to recover them.

item:fragments-of-rok-alim.text: Fragments of Rok'Alim. Across Thousand Needles, Rok'Alim's stone fragments bear witness to a warrior's victory. Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook seeks them as proof Rok'Alim fell in single combat. Rok'Alim the Pounder still walks the canyon flats south of the main thoroughfare. Most elementals faded from Azeroth after the Old Gods were banished, though a few powerful ones endured without mortal summoning. The local centaur know Rok'Alim by the crashes of his stone fists as they crush anything in his path. Defeat leaves jagged pieces of dense, animated rock, proof of a warrior's might. Dorn Plainstalker needs the fragments for the Test of Strength. The tauren hermit holds spiritual and martial rites high in the Weathered Nook. An initiate must face a being of unyielding brute force. Bringing Dorn the battered pieces of Rok'Alim proves the bravery and might needed to survive Kalimdor's harshest perils.

item:frostwolf-banner.text: Frostwolf Banner. In Alterac Valley, Horde initiates seek the Frostwolf Banner in Wildpaw Cavern. Bringing it back is an ancestral rite that awakens their battle spirit and earns their first clan insignia. In Alterac Valley, new warriors seeking a place among the Frostwolf clan face a trial of grit. Warmaster Laggrond sends them south into Wildpaw Cavern, where territorial gnolls fill the damp, hostile corridors. They must reach the hidden banner and bring it back unbroken. That proves their courage, awakens their battle rage, and earns each warrior the Frostwolf initiate's insignia.

item:full-leaden-collection-phial.text:
Full Leaden Collection Phial. In Kharanos, Ozzie Togglevolt seeks a sample from Gnomeregan’s troggs. He hopes it will cure irradiated leper gnomes, or perhaps make a dangerously potent rum. A lead lining shields the bearer from the volatile green fallout saturating Gnomeregan. High Tinker Mekkatorque’s advisors flooded the lower corridors with toxic radiation to stop the invading troggs.
