Instead, the disaster corrupted troggs and surviving gnomes into maddened, irradiated horrors.

Irradiated Invaders and Pillagers leave fluid residue for refugee tinkerers in Kharanos. Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket use it as raw material in their experiments on remedies.

item:fungal-spores.text: Fungal Spores. At the Barrens' oases, Fungal Spores swell within mushrooms along the shores. The waters quicken nearby life, and the Royal Apothecary Society gathers the spores for its alchemy. The Barrens' oases bring unusual life to the dry plains. At the Forgotten Pools, the Lushwater Oasis, and the Stagnant Oasis, the water does more than ease thirst. It quickens and changes nearby plants and wildlife. Along the damp shores, mushrooms swell with spores that carry the waters' concentrated power and spur growth. Naturalists study the change, while the Royal Apothecary Society gathers the mushrooms for its alchemy. Apothecaries abroad gather unusual local ingredients for their laboratories and colleagues. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim sends reagents onward, including to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff. The spores are valuable for brewing potent chemical mixtures. Mysterious forces beneath Kalimdor's soil have altered their natural properties, making them useful to the Forsaken.

item:furen-s-instructions.text: Furen's Instructions. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard gives tested Alliance warriors the list of materials for fire-hardened mail. Furen Longbeard offers a resilient suit of mail to a warrior who has proved himself at simpler smithing work. The dwarven armorer requires the warrior to fetch the rare components himself. His parchment records what is needed and sends the warrior across continents to gather it. The parchment calls for a dangerous journey through the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Dozens of scorched spider fangs come from damp caves in the Wetlands. The hardened links also need horns from fire-breathing chimaeras in the crags of Stonetalon Mountains. The list asks for a galvanized horn from the chimaera matriarch and a vial of volatile phlogiston held deep within Razorfen Kraul, a quilboar bastion.

item:furen-s-notes.text: Furen's Notes. In Stormwind, Furen's Notes carry his discoveries in metallurgy and armorsmithing to Alliance craftsmen. Furen Longbeard forged protective gear for veteran warriors, then sent copies to help fellow smiths refine their work. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Furen Longbeard forges specialized armaments for warriors. As he works, he records his methods and discoveries. Dwarven metalworking keeps changing, so he makes several copies for other smiths to use and build upon. His notes describe ways to temper, reinforce, and shape armor against deadly blows. Furen sends copies to trusted contacts among the Alliance's craftsmen. Grimand Elmore may scoff at a smith he claims to have taught, but the notes still hold useful insights. Some copies cross the Great Sea to night elven craftsmen, including Mathiel on Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace. Shared needs in battle bring their different traditions together.

item:furlbrow-s-deed.text: Furlbrow's Deed. Beside their broken wagon near Westfall's border, Theodore and Verna Furlbrow have lost their farm to the Defias Brotherhood. Their land deed is in bandit hands, and with it went their home and livelihood. Theodore Furlbrow and Verna signed the deed to secure their family farm in Westfall. After the Defias Brotherhood overran the region, bandits drove them from home and carried the deed into Elwynn Forest. Notes on its back show the thieves planned to copy it and forge claims to other properties. The Furlbrows lost their livelihood and took to the road, with no home to return to.

item:furlbrow-s-pocket-watch.text:
Furlbrow's Pocket Watch. In Westfall, Farmer Furlbrow searches for the pocket watch he lost when Defias bandits drove him from home. Verna’s father gave it to him on their wedding day. Defias bandits drove Farmer Furlbrow and Verna from their home at the Furlbrow Pumpkin Patch in the night. In their flight, he left the watch in a wardrobe in the overrun farmhouse. Benny Blaanco and his cutthroats keep watch nearby.

The couple now camps along the road. The watch is one of the few pieces of their former life the outlaws have not ruined.

item:gaea-seed.text: Gaea Seed. Along Mirkfallon Lake, Gaea Seed offers hope for Stonetalon's wounded land. Tauren shamans value its hardy kernels for healing places scarred by war and industry. Gaea Seeds wash ashore or grow along Mirkfallon Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains. Small and fibrous, they resemble coconuts and endure harsh conditions. Conflict and industry have scarred the land, so shamans turn to the seeds to help heal it.

item:gaffer-jack.text: Gaffer Jack. Off Auberdine, Gaffer Jack parts lie beneath Darkshore's waves. Wizbang Cranktoggle lost a crate during his voyage across the sea. Gnome tinkerer Wizbang Cranktoggle booked passage to Auberdine for quiet away from Ironforge's forge-works and taverns. During the voyage, he drank too much and fumbled a whole container of gaffer jacks over the railing. The small fasteners sank into Darkshore's coastal waters. Without them, Wizbang could not tune his stintle pegs. Gaffer jacks sank in the surf along Darkshore's shore, where patient fishermen sometimes catch them on their hooks. Recovering the parts lets Wizbang assemble his strange contraptions. Finding tiny metal hardware in the open sea takes patience and luck.

item:gallywix-s-head.text: Gallywix's Head. In Orgrimmar, the Shattered Hand awaits proof that Puzik Gallywix has been killed. His head will show the Venture Company overseer was executed. Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix directed the Venture Company's work from a tower north of the Sludge Fen. When word came that the Venture Co. planned something on a grand scale, the Shattered Hand sent operatives to dismantle the facility. Bring Gallywix's head to Shenthul in Orgrimmar. It proves the overseer was executed and secures the rogue's standing within the guild.

item:galvanized-horn.text: Galvanized Horn. In the Charred Vale, armorers seek Galvanized Horns from chimaera matriarchs. Their hardened growths go into specialized armor for warriors. Chimaera matriarchs prowl the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains. Ash, flame, and survival harden their horns. Fledgling chimaeras yield brittle, blackened horns, but a matriarch’s is strong as treated metal. Furen Longbeard in Stormwind and Orm Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff each seek one as a test of martial valor and an ingredient for exceptional mail armor.

item:gargantuan-tumor.text:
Gargantuan Tumor. In Teldrassil, a great growth was cut from Oakenscowl near Lake Al'Ameth. Its blight marks the sickness spreading among the creatures there. Oakenscowl lurks in a cavern near the southern bank of Lake Al'Ameth. Once a noble timberling elder, it has fallen to a vile affliction. A huge growth poisoned Oakenscowl and warped its behavior. The tumor also spread taint through the surrounding wildlife.

The growth was severed to end Oakenscowl's rampage and give local researchers a chance to study the blight. They hope to learn how the malady took root in the boughs of the newly grown World Tree.

item:garrick-s-head.text: Garrick's Head. At Northshire's vineyards, Garrick Padfoot's severed head proves the cutthroat is dead. The authorities at Northshire Abbey require it before they pay the bounty. For weeks, Garrick Padfoot and his gang harassed Northshire Valley's farmers and merchants. Stormwind's defenses were stretched thin, and local guards were busy with kobolds and Defias bandits. So Garrick hid in a shack near the vineyards and raided passing trade. Deputy Willem offered a bounty for the outlaw's death, seeking someone to kill him and bring back proof.

item:gazlowe-s-ledger.text: Gazlowe's Ledger. A shipment from Booty Bay is missing, and Gazlowe checks his records against Ratchet's harbor manifest. Gazlowe keeps a personal ledger of trade goods in Ratchet. It records imported crates, outbound cargo, and what is stored in the warehouses. When a shipment from Booty Bay goes missing, he compares the goods he expected with the dock records kept by Wharfmaster Dizzywig.

item:gem-of-anacondra.text:
Gem of Anacondra. In the Wailing Caverns, Lady Anacondra bears one of four dream gems held by the corrupted serpent leaders. The stones are bound to the nightmare spreading through the Barrens. When Naralex fell into deep slumber, he sought to bring water and life back to the arid Barrens. Then the Emerald Nightmare entered his thoughts and twisted his closest disciples. Lady Anacondra and her fellow conspirators left their old ways and became the Druids of the Fang. Their purpose was to restore the land, but it turned into a toxic delusion.

Lady Anacondra carries one of four dream gems held by these serpent leaders. The gem focuses their corrupted bond with the Emerald Dream and anchors the nightmare within the cave system.

item:gem-of-cobrahn.text: Gem of Cobrahn. In the Wailing Caverns, Lord Cobrahn bears a dream gem shaped by corruption. Nara Wildmane needs it as proof of his defeat. Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore Kalimdor's barren plains. His nightmare twisted the Wailing Caverns and turned his disciples from their purpose. Cobrahn forsook the peaceful ways of the Cenarion Circle and took the shape of a serpent. He now carries one of four dream gems that anchor the leaders' hold over the subterranean waterways. Through it, he channels twisted dreams that threaten to make the Barrens a venomous marsh.

item:gem-of-pythas.text:
Gem of Pythas. In the Wailing Caverns, Lord Pythas bears one of four corrupted dream gems. Together, the gems feed the nightmare twisting the underground oasis and threaten the Barrens. Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the arid Barrens. There, his vision became a living nightmare. His foremost followers fell with him and became the Druids of the Fang. Now they seek to remake the surface world as a venomous jungle.

Lord Pythas bears one of four dream gems that anchor the corruption in the caverns. The stone channels the druids’ dark design. It also proves to the druids of Thunder Bluff that Pythas’s twisted trance has been broken.

item:gem-of-serpentis.text: Gem of Serpentis. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, Lord Serpentis keeps the Gem of Serpentis close. The enchanted dream gem binds his will to the corrupted vision reshaping the caverns and threatening the Barrens. Naralex fell into slumber in the Wailing Caverns, and the Emerald Nightmare reached him there. His most devoted followers became the fanatical Druids of the Fang. Lord Serpentis leads one part of the cabal, with three other leaders beside him. Each carries an enchanted dream gem, binding their shared will to the corrupted vision. Recovering Serpentis's gem breaks his hold over the caverns' life and strikes at the leaders directing corruption across the Barrens.

item:gerenzo-s-mechanical-arm.text: Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm. In the Stonetalon Mountains, goblin operatives seek Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm to prove his death and clear out competition. The grafted limb belonged to rogue engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. Above Cragpool Lake, rogue engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle grafted whirring gears and metal onto his failing body. The renegade gnome replaced his natural limbs with intricate machinery. Goblin tinker Ziz Fizziks wants Gerenzo eliminated to impress his superiors. The distinctive arm is the proof he needs of the engineer's death.

item:ghost-hair-comb.text: Ghost Hair Comb. In Duskwood, Madame Eva sends Ghost Hair Comb to Blind Mary, whose grief leaves ghostly hair caught in its teeth. Madame Eva sends Ghost Hair Comb from Darkshire to Blind Mary, who lives in a lonely, dilapidated dwelling on Duskwood’s outskirts. At its sight, the ghost recoils in horror. Mary must face that she is no longer the lovely living woman she remembers. Grief-stricken, she thrusts the comb away, leaving strands of ghostly hair tangled in its teeth.

item:ghost-hair-thread.text: Ghost Hair Thread. In Darkshire, Madame Eva spins Ghost Hair Thread from the spirit world. Its occult power can bind spirits or stitch life into inanimate things, and Abercrombie asks for it to ward his shack against restless ghosts. In Darkshire, Madame Eva spins Ghost Hair Thread, a spectral strand with strange powers. Eva says it can bind malevolent spirits or stitch vitality into inanimate objects. In Duskwood, people use it in rituals and wards.

item:ghoul-fang.text: Ghoul Fang. In Duskwood, travelers face the forest’s encroaching darkness, and Ghoul Fang is gathered for Madame Eva’s protective talismans. The fangs are essential to her work in Darkshire. Ravenous undead haunt Duskwood’s woods and graves. Flesh Eaters lurk near the burial grounds, while Rotted Ones roam among the trees. Taking a fang from these creatures is grim work. It proves survival against the dead threatening Darkshire’s borders. Madame Eva is Darkshire’s fortune teller and mystic. She sees terrible omens around travelers crossing Duskwood, so she enchants the Totem of Infliction with ghoul fangs, skeletal fingers, and arachnid venom. The charm turns the forest’s dark forces against violent assault and protects its bearer.

item:ghoul-rib.text:
Ghoul Rib. In Duskwood, Abercrombie gathers Ghoul Rib to guard his shack from the dead. He says a fearsome effigy will frighten the flesh-eating horrors away from his home. Ghouls haunt Duskwood in many forms. Flesh Eaters, Bone Chewers, Brain Eaters, Rotted Ones and Plague Spreaders are among them.

Abercrombie lives alone in a shack north of Raven Hill Cemetery. He asks travelers for their sturdy, rotted ribs. His home lies beyond the Night Watch’s protection in Darkshire, so he says he needs a fearsome effigy to frighten the dead away.

item:giant-crocolisk-skin.text: Giant Crocolisk Skin. In the Wetlands, Menethil Harbor tradesmen need the thick hides of giant crocolisks. Taking one is perilous work, and hunters have been maimed. The Wetlands' bogs and waterways shelter enormous crocolisks whose hides resist the marsh's damp rot. Menethil Harbor artisans such as James Halloran rely on steady shipments to make rugged leather goods. Reaching a full-grown beast means braving deep water and facing a fierce predator, so every hide comes hard-won.

item:gloom-weed.text:
Gloom Weed. In Tirisfal, Gloom Weed grows between Deathknell and Brill. Gordo gathers it by mistake while searching for doom weed. Gloom Weed grows west of Brill and east of Solliden Farmstead. It is harmless and lacks the alchemical strength sought by the Royal Apothecary Society. Gordo, a lumbering abomination, wanders the road, pulling weeds with clumsy hands. He misunderstood his master's orders, so he keeps gathering the wrong plant.

Then Gordo asks travelers to carry the weeds to Master Holland in the Brill graveyard. The apothecary is annoyed by the mistake.

item:glowing-ember.text: Glowing Ember. At the Shrine of Eternal Flame, a Glowing Ember awakens the brazier for a shaman’s trial. It comes from a Minor Manifestation of Fire on Durotar’s crags. A rising shaman drinks fire sapta to see the fiery spirits on the ridge near Telf Joolam. There, the initiate faces a Minor Manifestation of Fire. When the elemental falls, its physical form leaves only a smoldering ember. Raw elemental heat still pulses within it, carrying the spark needed to awaken the sacred brazier at the Shrine of Eternal Flame.

item:glowing-fruit.text: Glowing Fruit. Beneath strange fronds on Teldrassil, Glowing Fruit shines with its own light. Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth studies how it reacts to the World Tree's soil. Beneath unusual fronds on Teldrassil, Glowing Fruit hangs bright and round. Botanist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth knows it is foreign to the World Tree. He believes its seeds came from distant lands across the sea. Its reaction to Teldrassil's rich, enchanted soil shows how foreign plants can affect the young World Tree.

item:glowing-gem.text: Glowing Gem. At Lake Falathim, the Glowing Gem remains among the murlocs after Teronis died seeking it. Its magic may help restore Dartol's rod. Murlocs hold the Glowing Gem near Lake Falathim. The stone bears latent magic. Teronis came from Astranaar to seek a way to push back the corruption spreading through Ashenvale's forests. He died at the lake, and the gem stayed among the scavengers along the shore.

item:glowing-soul-gem.text: Glowing Soul Gem. In Ordil'Aran, the Glowing Soul Gem serves the Cult of the Dark Strand's work in northern Ashenvale. Shadow sorcery fills the stone, which holds the spirit of an unwitting victim. Northeast of Maestra's Post, the ruins of Ordil'Aran shelter the Cult of the Dark Strand and its shadowy masters. The cult's operatives carry Glowing Soul Gems, enchanted vessels that trap and torment the souls of the dead. The stones channel magical energy and bind spirits to the cult's ends.

item:glutton-shackle.text:
Glutton Shackle. In Silverpine Forest, Glutton Shackle bands lend strength to Arugal’s flawed sorcery. The mad archmage made them for Moonrage Glutton worgen. Feral worgen infest Silverpine Forest, and the Forsaken’s trained mages see them as proof of poor arcane work. Dalar Dawnweaver, an accomplished arcanist stationed at the Sepulcher, holds Archmage Arugal in contempt. He calls Arugal an incompetent hack, unworthy of the Kirin Tor.

Dawnweaver found that Arugal relied on enchanted relics to shore up his fragile spells. The heavy Moonrage Gluttons roaming northern Silverpine wear Glutton Shackles. These magical anchors reinforce the curse binding the beasts.

item:glyph-of-azora.text: Glyph of Azora. From the Tower of Azora, Theocritus watches threats beyond Elwynn. His glyphs carry the Eye of Azora's power farther, so he can read enemies' thoughts and plans. From his tower in Elwynn Forest, Theocritus watches hostile powers. The Eye of Azora lets him see far away, but it cannot reach the minds or plans of his adversaries. So he places small focuses called Glyphs of Azora on distant surfaces. Each one anchors his magic, letting him read enemy intentions and project his voice across miles to speak with field agents.

item:glyphic-letter.text:
Glyphic Letter. At Northshire Abbey, Glyphic Letter calls promising novitiates to arcane study. After serving the garrison, they are summoned upstairs to Khelden Bremen, the resident mage trainer. Khelden Bremen seals Glyphic Letter with his own insignia. Apprentice spellcasters receive it after proving their discipline in Northshire Valley. The summons draws them from basic field duties into dedicated magical instruction within the abbey.

Before they take up the arcane, Bremen tests each student's resolve. Its forces are dangerous, its scrutiny unyielding, and its burdens heavy.

item:glyphic-memorandum.text: Glyphic Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, the Glyphic Memorandum calls novice mages to Anvilmar. Marryk Nurribit wrote it to guide new spellcasters into formal arcane instruction. Novice spellcasters receive the Glyphic Memorandum after their first tasks in Coldridge Valley. Marryk Nurribit, the local mage trainer, summons them inside Anvilmar. He gives plain counsel: learn your incantations, save coin for training and tavern ale, and keep clear of Gnomeregan, ruined by radiation.

item:glyphic-scroll.text: Glyphic Scroll. In Deathknell, the Glyphic Scroll calls newly raised Forsaken magi to the church. Isabella’s seal invites fledgling spellcasters to begin arcane training in undeath. Newly awakened Forsaken mages find a sealed scroll after culling mindless Scourge in Deathknell’s graveyard. Isabella, the settlement’s mage trainer, summons them to the ruined parish sanctuary. There, new magi begin learning the arcane under the Forsaken banner. Death has freed them from mortal weakness, but magic’s corrupting temptations remain.

item:glyphic-tablet.text:
Glyphic Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives novice Darkspear troll mages the Glyphic Tablet. Its summons sends them to Mai'ah for instruction in arcane magic. Darkspear recruits with an affinity for arcane power receive the Glyphic Tablet in the Valley of Trials. Gornek hands it to young mages as they handle early tasks around the red canyons. On the slate, Mai'ah, a seasoned troll mage outside the Den, invites them to meet her.

The Darkspear follow arcane traditions unlike the scholarly academies of humans or high elves. Mai'ah offers instruction and a solemn warning. Raw magic corrupts and deceives, and its dangers to a mage's mind exceed those of any enemy soldier.

item:glyphs-of-summoning.text:
Glyphs of Summoning. In Orgrimmar, warlocks prepare the Glyphs of Summoning to call a voidwalker. The inscriptions come from the ancient Tablet of Verga and draw a creature from the Nether into a summoning circle, where it can be bound to the warlock’s service. In the Cleft of Shadow, warlocks study the dark arts beyond the Warchief’s guards. For an aspiring warlock who learns from Gan'rul Bloodeye, commanding a voidwalker marks an important step. The Glyphs of Summoning draw on the Tablet of Verga and bridge Azeroth and the Nether.

Inside Neeru Fireblade's tent, the warlock lays the glyphs in a summoning circle. They open a threshold and draw a creature of the Void into the mortal realm. Before Gan'rul teaches the final methods of binding, the warlock must defeat the creature in combat.

item:gnoam-sprecklesprocket.text: Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. In the Deadmines, Shoni the Shilent seeks a power source for the effort to reach Gnomeregan. Gnoam Sprecklesprocket can drive drilling machines meant to breach the rock around the lost gnomish home. Deep in the Defias stronghold, Sneed's shredder cuts timber under the goblin taskmaster Sneed's hand. Its compact power core drives heavy logging and cutting blades. The Gnoam Sprecklesprocket gives the machine steady power, making it valuable salvage in Westfall's tunnels. In Stormwind City, the gnomish inventor Shoni the Shilent has chosen the Deadmines shredder for a greater effort. Gnomish forces seek to reclaim Gnomeregan from the troggs who overran it, but sealed underground approaches bar the way. Shoni plans to power heavy gyrodrillmatic excavationators with the Sprecklesprocket. The machines could bore through bedrock around the lost techno-city and open an unexpected route for an underground assault.

item:gnoll-paw.text:
Gnoll Paw. At Sentinel Hill, Gnoll Paw bounties help defend Westfall’s farmsteads from Riverpaw packs. The People's Militia pays for proof that patrols have slain gnolls. The People's Militia defends Westfall from Sentinel Hill. The royal army is absent, and the crown seems blind to troubles in the countryside. So ordinary citizens and volunteers face outlaws, rogue mechanoids, and Riverpaw gnolls.

Captain Danuvin offers bounties for proof that gnolls have been slain. Their paws show that patrols have searched the scrublands instead of resting beneath the watchtower.

item:gnomeregan-gumdrop.text: Gnomeregan Gumdrop. At Hallow's End, Gnomeregan Gumdrops reach travelers from the exiled gnomes. One sweet helps sick Jesper celebrate at the Stormwind orphanage. At Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Talvash del Kissel gives travelers Gnomeregan Gumdrops when they play along with his Hallow's End tricks. Alliance innkeepers offer treats from their own lands, but the exiled gnomes have no capital inn of their own. The radioactive disaster drove them from their underground kingdom. Still, they share their distinct sweets with the Alliance. Sick Jesper stays at the Stormwind orphanage in Cathedral Square and cannot travel the continents to trick-or-treat. So travelers gather four regional sweets from Alliance capitals and bring them to him: Gnomeregan Gumdrop, Stormwind Nougat, Ironforge Mint, and Darnassus Marzipan.

item:gnomish-tools.text: Gnomish Tools. Along Durotar’s coast, Gnomish Tools from Proudmoore’s fleet are being recovered by the Horde. The salvaged devices may teach its craftsmen how Alliance engineering works and how to adapt it for survival. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore’s fleet brought vast supplies of modern equipment to Durotar. Proudmoore led Kul Tiras and Alliance forces to its shores, with sophisticated gear made by their gnomish allies aboard. After the fleet was destroyed along the Scuttle Coast, east of Tiragarde Keep, delicate mechanical kits sank beneath the waves. Waterproof toolboxes still lie among the rotting timbers and barnacle-encrusted hulls in the shallows. Gar'Thok, who oversees Razor Hill, sent Horde scouts to recover tools from the watery grave of Proudmoore’s navy. The orcs know humans and gnomes are skilled in engineering, especially siege engines, shipwrighting, and clockwork mechanics. So the kits travel by caravan to craftsmen and scholars in Orgrimmar. There, the Horde intends to study Alliance contraptions, learn to counter enemy war machines, and adapt foreign innovations for its own survival.

item:gold-dust.text: Gold Dust. In Elwynn Forest, Gold Dust passes from kobold hands to local buyers. Miners still seek whole veins of ore. Kobolds dig through the Fargodeep and Jasperlode mines beneath Elwynn Forest. Rather than refine the gold dust they find, they keep it in pockets and pouches. Local peddlers and fences want those scraps, hoping to profit without paying official smelting tariffs.

item:golm-fragment.text: Golm Fragment. At the southern Wetlands dig, Golm Fragment lies among the four missing pieces of the Goaz Stone. Dwarven archaeologists need it to piece together the ancient Titan inscriptions. Golm Fragment lies among the remains of Whelgar's excavation in the southern Wetlands. Prospector Whelgar found the monumental Goaz Stone shortly before raptors drove the Explorers' League back. Its inscription had been severed in four places. When the dig was overrun, the fragment remained amid dirt and overturned crates, hidden inside an ancient relic box until explorers could retrieve it.

item:gordon-s-crate.text: Gordon's Crate. In the Undercity, Gordon's Crate holds weapons for the remote garrison at the Sepulcher. The Forsaken forces in Silverpine Forest need the shipment. The Forsaken send supplies from the Undercity to hold Silverpine Forest. Gordon's Crate carries weapons for Deathguard Podrig's defenders at the Sepulcher. The sentries there face worgen, wild beasts, and human remnants in the woods. Roads from the capital are dangerous and slow, so valuable shipments travel with the Undercity's bat handlers. Gordon's Crate goes to Michael Garrett, the bat master above the city's trade quarter. He arranges passage on a trained flying bat to Karos Razok's roost at the Sepulcher.

item:grape-manifest.text: Grape Manifest. At Northshire Abbey, Milly Osworth's recovered harvest is bound for the stores after brigands seized it. Northshire Abbey depends on nearby farms for its food and drink. The lost harvest put its stores in danger. Now the crates are reclaimed, and the quartermasters can balance supplies and ready barrels for fermentation. Milly Osworth's manifest records the quantity they need to plan. Brother Neals oversees Northshire Abbey's food and drink. He enjoys sampling its wine in the quiet of the bell tower. Knowing the grapes are coming helps keep the monks and visiting recruits supplied with drink. Each saved bushel strengthens the abbey's stores and brings a blessing from the Holy Light.

item:gray-bear-tongue.text: Gray Bear Tongue. In Hillsbrad Foothills, Apothecary Lydon seeks gray bear tongues for the Royal Apothecary Society's experiments. Gray bears roam the wilds around Tarren Mill in several sturdy varieties. Apothecary Lydon uses their tongues as a base ingredient for lethal solutions, including the Elixir of Suffering.

item:gregor-s-remains.text:
Gregor's Remains. Gregor's Remains are sought to settle an old score. They belonged to Gregor Agamand, of Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest family. Before the Third War, the Agamands held great wealth and broad lands across northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge invaded Lordaeron, the family patriarchs chose pride over flight. They fortified their mills and urged their loyal laborers to stand against the undead.

The defense failed. The estate fell, and those who stood their ground were butchered and raised into undeath. Gregor Agamand became a mindless servant of the Lich King, haunting the mills his family had ruled. Some who escaped the Lich King's control joined the Forsaken, but the memory of that defense still wounds them. Coleman Farthing, a former mill worker now stationed in Brill, blames the Agamands' pride for trapping his soul in eternal rot. He seeks Gregor's remains as personal retribution against the master who led his household into damnation.

item:grelin-s-report.text:
Grelin's Report. In Coldridge Valley, Grelin's Report carries word of the Frostmane trolls to Kharanos. It joins the scouts at Anvilmar with Senir Whitebeard and Ironforge. Grelin Whitebeard has watched the Frostmane trolls in Coldridge Valley and judges them no great threat. Mountaineers already stationed there can handle them, with mercenaries paid from Senate funds. So Grelin entrusts his report to a capable traveler instead of his fumbling apprentice. The journey leads through trogg-infested Coldridge Pass.

The paper shows Mountaineer Thalos that you travel on urgent business. With it, you may pass his blockade and enter the snowy reaches of Dun Morogh. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Senir Whitebeard receives Grelin's field report for Ironforge. His brother has invoked King Magni Bronzebeard's name throughout the document, and Senir takes note with amused resignation. Grelin claims the King's sanction for his actions. Senir expects that appeal to royal authority to ruffle feathers in the Ironforge Senate.

item:grelin-whitebeard-s-journal.text: Grelin Whitebeard's Journal. Grelin Whitebeard records Frostmane troll activity in a field journal in Coldridge Valley. Grik'nir the Cold steals the journal and carries it into the troll cave. Grelin Whitebeard watches the Frostmane trolls near Coldridge Valley and writes down what they do. His leatherbound notebook records their strength, their organization, and the danger they pose. Grik'nir the Cold takes the journal during a confrontation or ambush. The marked troll brute carries it into the troll cave, leaving Grelin without the notes he needs to finish his report. So he asks passing adventurers to retrieve the book.

item:grell-earring.text: Grell Earring. In Bashal'Aran, Grell Earring bears traces of the seal that binds Asterion. Wild Grells and Vile Sprites gather scraps among Bashal'Aran's ruins and shape them into earrings. Most mortals see only trinkets without worth. But Asterion, an ancient night elf bound there as a tormented phantom, studies the magic they retain. He hopes those traces will lead him to the ancient seal that imprisons him.

item:grenka-s-claw.text: Grenka's Claw. In Thousand Needles, Grenka's Claw marks survival in the depths of Roguefeather Den. At the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker receives it as proof of an aspiring adventurer's endurance in the canyon heights. Harpies cache food in Roguefeather Den, west of Freewind Post, and fiercely guard their territory. Dorn Plainstalker sends young champions into the deep roosts to destroy the flock's food reserves and test their strength. Such an intrusion draws Grenka Bloodscreech's fury. Returning her wicked talon proves a warrior endured wave after wave of enraged harpies and survived their matriarch's vicious assault.

item:grimtotem-satchel.text: Grimtotem Satchel. Deep beneath Orgrimmar, Grimtotem Satchel stays in Maur Grimtotem’s grasp. Troggs killed the tauren in Ragefire Chasm, but he shielded the pouch as he died. Its return to Thunder Bluff draws Magatha Grimtotem’s attention. Troggs killed Maur Grimtotem deep inside Ragefire Chasm, beneath Orgrimmar. When his body was found, the tauren still clutched a simple leather pack. He had fought to guard it as the troggs closed around him. What could it hold that made him defend it with his life?

item:grizzled-bear-heart.text:
Grizzled Bear Heart. In Silverpine Forest, grizzled bears yield hearts for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into the New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society works without pause to create a blight that can exterminate both the Scourge and living humanity. In Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel found that toxins from a grizzled bear's heart make a remarkably lethal concoction when joined with arachnid ichor.

Couriers and Forsaken loyalists hunt ferocious grizzled bears, giant grizzled bears, and the roaming beast Old Vicejaw. They carve out the hearts and carry them to Master Apothecary Faranell, deep within the Undercity's Apothecarium.

item:grizzled-scalp.text: Grizzled Scalp. South of Auberdine, grizzled thistle bears roam Darkshore’s forests, and their thick hides find a use with Wizbang Cranktoggle.

item:gryshka-s-letter.text: Gryshka's Letter. Innkeeper Gryshka sends Zargh a note of thanks after receiving fresh meat from the Barrens. Her letter also introduces young Horde couriers to the wind rider routes. Innkeeper Gryshka thanks Zargh for the steaks he sends from the Barrens to Orgrimmar. She remembers when he lost a finger preparing meat. Even bloodied by his trade, she tells him, he still looks handsome. To return Gryshka's Letter to the Crossroads, you report to Doras, the wind rider master atop Orgrimmar's plateau. Show him you have already checked in with Devrak at the Crossroads. Then Doras introduces young couriers to the wyvern flight paths linking settlements in Durotar and the Barrens.

item:gunther-s-spellbook.text: Gunther's Spellbook. In Tirisfal Glades, Bethor's enchantment marks Gunther's Spellbook. The tome may show its owner that other mages have escaped the Lich King's control.

item:gyromechanic-gear.text:
Gyromechanic Gear. In Kharanos, inventors seek Gyromechanic Gears for a bold experiment. They hope to reverse the mutations of leper gnomes. Radiation swept through Gnomeregan while gnomes fought to drive out the troggs. Many survivors became mad, irradiated leper gnomes. Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket will not abandon their twisted kin, so they have planned the Recombobulator. The machine is meant to undo radiation's effects.

Its prototype needs precise mechanisms that can bear the volatile pressure inside, including Gyromechanic Gears and Restabilization Cogs. Gnomeregan's fall ended local manufacturing. Now the inventors must salvage these delicate parts from hostile leper gnomes roaming Dun Morogh.

item:hallowed-letter.text: Hallowed Letter. In Northshire Valley, Priestess Anetta calls young priests to Northshire Abbey. Her letter begins their study of the Holy Light. Priestess Anetta’s personal mark appears on the Hallowed Letter. It reaches fledgling priests after their first trials against the kobold camps of Northshire Valley. She sees a spark of the Holy Light in each novice and urges them to enter the abbey and serve it. Dark forces still linger across Azeroth after the Third War. The priesthood gathers those who can heal, protect, and guide an empire struggling to keep order.

item:hallowed-rune.text: Hallowed Rune. In Coldridge Valley, Branstock Khalder sends novice priests the Hallowed Rune to begin their training at Anvilmar. The Hallowed Rune bears teachings of the Holy Light. A young priest proves their resolve by aiding the valley’s mountaineers and defenders. Then Branstock sends them to Anvilmar, where he teaches them to mend wounds and wield holy power against the troggs threatening Dun Morogh.

item:hallowed-scroll.text: Hallowed Scroll. In Deathknell, the Hallowed Scroll calls newly awakened Forsaken priests to the ruined chapel. Sealed by Dark Cleric Duesten, it begins their training in faith, willpower, and shadow. Newly risen Forsaken priests feel their bond with the world change in a violent way. Deathknell is being reclaimed amid chaos, and the Hallowed Scroll sends them to seek guidance in the settlement’s ruined chapel. Dark Cleric Duesten’s seal marks the parchment. It directs the new priests to report for formal instruction in the practical beliefs of Forsaken priesthood. Dark Cleric Duesten tells priests who answer the summons to leave old teachings behind. The Holy Light, ancestral spirits, and demonic pacts cannot be their crutches. The scroll begins a discipline founded on each priest’s own will. Its teachings call on them to survive and rule through conviction, making faith a means of self-command and mastery.

item:hallowed-sigil.text: Hallowed Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Hallowed Sigil calls young night elf initiates to Aldrassil. Shanda sends it to summon them into service to Elune. Young night elf priests in Shadowglen receive the Hallowed Sigil from a woodland messenger. Holy markings cover the token, which bears a personal summons from Shanda, the priest trainer at Aldrassil. Read the message, then climb to Aldrassil’s great hollow. There, the summons brings the acolyte to the Sisterhood of Elune and begins their service to the Kaldorei as new travelers arrive across Teldrassil.

item:hallowed-tablet.text:
Hallowed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, the Hallowed Tablet calls young Darkspear priests to Ken'jai. Its words begin their lessons in communing with the spirits. Gornek gives the Hallowed Tablet to a promising troll priest taking their first steps through the Valley of Trials. A personal invitation from Ken'jai, the priest trainer outside the Den, is written upon it. Ken'jai reads signs and hears the spirits' whispers.

So when young Darkspear with spiritual potential arrive in Durotar, the spirits make their coming known to him. The tablet tells the initiate to read its message and seek Ken'jai's guidance in channeling spiritual authority.

item:hand-of-dextren-ward.text: Hand of Dextren Ward. In Darkshire, grieving families await proof that Dextren Ward has been executed in the Stormwind Stockade. His severed hand is bound for town as a sign that justice has reached him. Lord Ebonlocke sentenced Dextren Ward to death after he caught him digging up bodies in Duskwood cemeteries. Ward sold those bodies to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Stormwind intervened before Darkshire could execute him and took him to the Stockade. For the grieving families, Ward's hand proves the defiler has been executed, despite the House of Nobles' unwanted leniency.

item:handful-of-oats-classic.text: Handful of Oats (Classic). In Westfall, Old Blanchy needs oats after the Furlbrows' wagon breaks down. Westfall once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind. Now its farms lie overgrown or under the control of Defias bandits and rogue harvest golems. Sacks of grain and oats remain by barns and outbuildings, and in overgrown fields. Travelers and refugees whose wagons break down along the dusty roads can gather the leftover oats for their weary draft horses.

item:handful-of-stardust.text: Handful of Stardust. In the Ruins of Stardust, frost gathers on bushes south of Astranaar. Night elven healers use the powder to cool intense fevers. Stardust clings to shrubs in the Ruins of Stardust, south of Astranaar. Its fine powder shines like frost. Elemental spirits linger among the broken stones, yet plants thrive there and take in a rare glow. Night elven healers make the residue into poultices for dangerous, persistent fevers. They use it when ordinary salves and moonwell waters bring no full relief.

item:hardened-tortoise-shell.text: Hardened Tortoise Shell. Across the Shimmering Flats, racers seek shells tough enough for dangerous fuel. Gnomish racers at the Mirage Raceway prize Hardened Tortoise Shells from sparkleshell tortoises because they resist volatile, corrosive experimental fuels. Sparkleshell tortoises, from snappers to borers, roam the salt flats. Their carapaces shield them from the salt and wandering predators. Gnomish experimental chemistry can corrode or rupture metal fuel tanks. So mechanics such as Wizzle Brassbolts prize the shells as raw material for makeshift tanks that resist acid and hold volatile rocket propellants.

item:hardened-tumor.text: Hardened Tumor. In Silverpine, the Royal Apothecary Society studies a rare growth found in Vile Fin murlocs. Apothecary Berard first recorded it before Arugal's curse left him a mindless servant. Along Lake Lordamere, Vile Fin murlocs sometimes develop a rare, calcified growth. Apothecary Berard recorded it while studying wildlife along Silverpine Forest's eastern borders. It appears only in mature specimens along the shoreline and the Dawning Isles. Its cause remains uncertain, yet the Royal Apothecary Society took notice of the dense tissue.

item:harpy-lieutenant-ring.text: Harpy Lieutenant Ring. In the Dry Hills, Harpy Lieutenant Ring marks the rank of Witchwing Slayers who command the flock. Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads asks for the rings as proof of their deaths. Witchwing Slayers direct attacks on Horde travelers in the Barrens. Their rings mark them as leaders above the ordinary raiders, who fight with little coordination. Darsok Swiftdagger and the defenders at the Crossroads need rings taken from fallen slayers. The rings confirm that part of the harpies’ leadership has been broken.

item:head-of-arugal.text: Head of Arugal. At Shadowfang Keep, Head of Arugal is claimed from the mad archmage who commands the worgen. The Forsaken at the Sepulcher seek it as proof of his fall. Archmage Arugal commands the worgen from Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest. At the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver orders his severed head claimed. The Forsaken see Arugal's fall as a blow against the beasts that hinder Lady Sylvanas's hold over Silverpine. Bring the head to Dawnweaver, and it proves Arugal's sorcery has been cut from the land.

item:head-of-bazil-thredd.text: Head of Bazil Thredd. Warden Thelwater demands proof that the Stockade uprising has been crushed. Bazil Thredd’s severed head is meant to prove the rebel leader is dead and Defias control of Stormwind’s prison has ended. Bazil Thredd led the uprising in the Stockade beneath Stormwind City. From his cell block, he directed the riots with help from loyal Defias inmates. Warden Thelwater distrusts outsiders and struggles to keep order. He demands Thredd’s head to prove the ringleader is dead and test the adventurer’s allegiance to Stormwind.

item:head-of-deepfury.text: Head of Deepfury. In the Stormwind Stockade, Kam Deepfury’s death in the prison riots answers the grievance of Dun Modr’s dwarven defenders. His severed head marks the end of a Dark Iron conspirator. Kam Deepfury was held in the Stormwind Stockade for political reasons, spared execution through human diplomacy. Roggo uncovered that Deepfury had planned the attack on the Thandol Span, where King Magni’s soldiers and Longbraid the Grim’s kin died. The Ironforge mountaineers at Dun Modr could not accept that he remained imprisoned. Bound to his post, Motley Garmason sent Alliance champions into the rioting prison to take Deepfury’s head and deliver dwarven vengeance.

item:head-of-gath-ilzogg.text:
Head of Gath'Ilzogg. In Redridge, Gath'Ilzogg's fall breaks the Blackrock leadership behind Stonewatch Keep's siege and brings Lakeshire desperate relief. Gath'Ilzogg led the Blackrock assault that seized Stonewatch Keep and drove out its defenders. From there, the valley suffered constant raids. Lakeshire stood near ruin, and Stormwind sent almost no military help. So Magistrate Solomon offered a bounty on the warlord.

Gath'Ilzogg fell in the keep's fortified upper levels. His death breaks the local Blackrock leadership. For Lakeshire, it is the first step toward reclaiming the keep for the kingdom.

item:head-of-grimson.text: Head of Grimson. At the Deep Elem Mine, Head of Grimson proves the Forsaken have secured its riches. Dalar Dawnweaver receives the trophy at the Sepulcher, and the mine's minerals can supply Varimathras's campaigns. Darkstalkers, Forsaken scouts, found a threat growing in the southeastern hills. Archmage Arugal's shadowy enchantments corrupted Deep Elem Mine's workers and drove its overseer, Grimson the Pale, mad. From the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver sent champions to kill Grimson and bring back his severed head. The trophy shows the mine is free of rogue magic, leaving its underground wealth for Varimathras's forces.

item:head-of-kelris.text: Head of Kelris. At Blackfathom Deeps, the Argent Dawn seeks Kelris's severed head to confirm his fall and the end of his sacrifices. In Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight Lord Kelris led sacrifices to Aku'mai, a monstrous servant of an Old God. Taking his head marks the end of his rule over the Twilight's Hammer cultists and their naga allies in the cavern. The head must reach the surface so leaders can know his bloody ceremonies have ended. For months, the Argent Dawn believed Kelris dead or lost. Then his influence returned with Kalimdor's encroaching shadows. His head, brought to agents in Darnassus or Thunder Bluff, settles lingering bounties and confirms his attempt to plunge the world into primeval chaos has been stopped.

item:head-of-targorr.text: Head of Targorr. In the Stormwind Stockade, nobles have halted Targorr's execution. The orc once served Gath'Ilzogg in the Redridge Mountains, and Guard Berton in Lakeshire now demands proof of his death. Targorr the Dread was the Blackrock clan warlord Gath'Ilzogg's feared executioner in Redridge. Before his capture, he tortured and slaughtered defenders of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Sentenced to die in the Stormwind Stockade, he was spared when Stormwind nobles intervened. Guardsmen like Berton suspect foul play and corruption in the capital. Guard Berton fears Targorr could become a political pawn or arrange an escape. So he hires an outside champion to enter the volatile prison and finish what the courts delayed. Taking Targorr's head bypasses the stalled legal system. It also gives closure to grieving families and Lakeshire's besieged defenders, who suffered under the executioner's blades.

item:head-of-vancleef.text:
Head of VanCleef. At Sentinel Hill, VanCleef's severed head gives Westfall proof that the Defias leader has fallen. Carried from the Deadmines, it brings the People's Militia a hard-won victory. Westfall's settlers need proof that the danger has passed. For months, Edwin VanCleef directed the Defias Brotherhood's terror from the deepest sanctum of the Deadmines. Armed outlaws, goblin engineers, and a massive war juggernaut guarded him there.

Gryan Stoutmantle leads the People's Militia and demands physical proof before he declares the countryside safe. VanCleef's severed head comes out into daylight. It assures the exhausted defenders that the architect of their ruin can no longer threaten Westfall.

item:heart-of-isha-awak.text:
Heart of Isha Awak. Along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, hunters seek Isha Awak’s heart. Mahren Skyseer wants it as proof that the Deep Doom has been overcome. Isha Awak prowls the sea off the Merchant Coast, south of Ratchet. Sailors and coastal folk both revere and fear the massive thresher called the Deep Doom. It has killed many human trespassers along the shore.

Mahren Skyseer, a tauren mystic, sees an honorable predator rather than a mindless menace. She believes its fierce spirit dwells in its heart. So she sends brave hunters into the waves to defeat Isha Awak in its own domain and claim the heart as a trophy and spiritual offering.

item:heartswood.text: Heartswood. In northwestern Ashenvale, Heartswood is cut from a tree rooted among the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. The tree grew where two ancient lovers died, and its wood draws succubi when warlocks seek to summon them. Among the elven stones of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale, a peculiar tree took root. Legend says Anathera and Latherion, two lovers, fell side by side there during the War of the Ancients thousands of years ago. The Heartswood tree grew from the earth where they died. Even now, wood cut from it carries the memory of their devotion. Those who study emotional and spiritual bonds are curious about it.

item:heartswood-core.text: Heartswood Core. Beneath Stormwind, warlocks use the Heartswood Core to summon a succubus. Gakin the Darkbinder provides the enchanted focus, made from an ancient tree’s wood, to open a passage to the Twisting Nether. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, warlocks perform rites beyond the city watch’s gaze. The Heartswood Core channels the magic that begins a binding ritual. Made from an ancient tree’s wood, it holds enough lingering power to pierce the veil between worlds. At a consecrated summoning circle, an initiate focuses dark arts through the core and opens a passage to the Twisting Nether. A succubus crosses the divide.

item:heavy-leaden-collection-phial.text:
Heavy Leaden Collection Phial. In Kharanos, Ozzie Togglevolt offers the Heavy Leaden Collection Phial for decontamination research. It is meant to draw in unstable irradiated discharge from mutants deep inside Gnomeregan and keep it contained. The Heavy Leaden Collection Phial draws volatile residue from living, irradiated creatures in Gnomeregan. Keeping the fallout inside is difficult. A suitable sample may take several attempts to collect. Ozzie Togglevolt provides the phial to help his research into reversing the terrible mutations afflicting leper gnomes. Earlier samples from surface troggs were too weak for useful chemical analysis.

With the leaden phial, researchers hope to gather samples from virulent beasts, including irradiated slimes and lurkers in the Hall of Gears. They seek the active elements in the city's toxic fallout, then hope to make an effective antidote.

item:hezrul-s-head.text:
Hezrul's Head. At Lushwater Oasis, Hezrul Bloodmark commands the Kolkar centaur of the Barrens. His head goes to Regthar Deathgate, west of the Crossroads, as proof their chieftain has fallen. Hezrul Bloodmark leads his Kolkar clan from Lushwater Oasis, south of the Crossroads. The centaur hold the Barrens' oases and threaten Horde supply routes and young settlements.

Regthar Deathgate is an orc veteran charged with securing the land west of the Crossroads. He sees fierce rage in the Kolkar, but little discipline. So he demands Hezrul's severed head to break the clan's command and scatter its surviving fighters, weakening their attacks on the Horde.

item:high-potency-radioactive-fallout.text:
High Potency Radioactive Fallout. In Gnomeregan's depths, researchers seek potent radioactive fallout. They hope to learn how the sludge afflicted the leper gnomes and find a cure. Deep in the Hall of Gears, irradiated horrors, lurkers, and slimes roam Gnomeregan's lowest tiers. Researchers outside the fallen capital need fallout drawn from these living creatures. Samples scraped from contaminated scavengers outside are too weak for their work.

The sludge decays quickly. It must be sealed in a leaden phial and reach the researchers before its potency fades. Ozzie Togglevolt and his colleagues seek a cure for the leper gnomes. They believe the secrets of the irradiated sludge may show them the way. During the trogg invasion, toxic venting deformed these survivors and drove them mad.

The leper gnomes remain trapped in a living nightmare. For the researchers, dangerous expeditions into the ruins are worth the risk.

item:highborne-relic-classic.text: Highborne Relic (Classic). In Darkshore, spirits still clutch Highborne Relics, and night elf scholars seek to destroy them. Their dormant magic may bring further harm. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne caste brought ruin to ancient Kalimdor with reckless arcane magic. Across Darkshore, their estates lie in shattered ruins. At Ameth'Aran, wailing apparitions wander among crumbling columns, still clutching the tools of their old sorcery. Arcane taint binds the relics to these spirits, who will not let go of the objects tied to their undoing. After the Great Sundering, most night elves turned away from arcane magic. Their scholars now see the relics as a grave hazard. Reports from the Sentinels reached Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine, who sends travelers to wrest the relics from the cursed spirits. Once gathered, the relics are destroyed, so the Highborne's ancient evils and catastrophic mistakes cannot be repeated.

item:highperch-venom-sac.text: Highperch Venom Sac. At Highperch, wyverns carry venom that buyers seek across Kalimdor. Their sacs draw trade even where the beasts do not fly. Wild wyverns nest among Highperch's crags in Thousand Needles. Their barbed tails deliver venom that can paralyze or kill prey. The Horde often domesticates wyverns as wind riders. Across Kalimdor, alchemists, hunters, and merchants pay well for the venom sacs. Highperch venom reaches buyers far from central Kalimdor. In Theramore, the high elf Fiora Longears pays well for fresh sacs gathered from Highperch broods. She seeks sacs swollen with venom, most often found on young wyverns or fertile females. Far from their desert home, she trades these dangerous reagents.

item:highperch-wyvern-egg.text: Highperch Wyvern Egg. At Highperch, Horde trainees seek wyvern eggs to raise as mounts. The nests lie above the mesas of Thousand Needles. Highperch gives native wyverns a place to roost and raise their young above Thousand Needles. Steep paths wind up the canyon walls to the nesting grounds, where adult wyverns guard their nests. Within sturdy, warm shells, hatchlings wait to face Kalimdor's harsh skies. The Horde needs more trained wyverns for its courier and scouting networks across Kalimdor. At Freewind Post, trainees such as the tauren Elu seek intact eggs from wild nests. They raise the hatchlings from the shell, hoping to form the bond that makes a trustworthy mount for a wind rider.

item:hildelve-s-journal.text:
Hildelve's Journal. In Dun Morogh, Hildelve's Journal bears the last words of a dwarf lost to a fierce bear. Its pages tell of the attack and his plea for vengeance. Dwarven pilot Hildelve went alone into Dun Morogh after his steam tank broke down. He left his partner, Hammerfoot, with the tanks and searched the snow-swept crags for rumored chiron ore. In his journal, Hildelve writes that Mangeclaw, a monstrous ice claw bear, stalked him for days before attacking.

Hildelve fought bravely and drove the bear off, but Mangeclaw mauled him and left him gravely wounded in the cold. His final hours were agonizing. Before the bear returned, Hildelve made one plea: whoever found his body should hunt Mangeclaw and avenge his death.

item:hillsbrad-human-skull.text:
Hillsbrad Human Skull. In Hillsbrad, Forsaken gather the skulls of slain humans. At Tarren Mill, they keep them as grim reminders of the assault on local settlements. Forsaken forces from Tarren Mill fight the humans of Southshore and nearby settlements. During the Battle of Hillsbrad, Deathstalkers and soldiers carry out the purge ordered by Darthalia. Guards left on watch want their share of the slaughter.

Deathguard Samsa gathers skulls from fighters on the front lines. He takes pleasure in keeping the remains of people the Forsaken once lived among. The trophies mark the killings as the conflict rages.

item:hillsbrad-town-registry.text:
Hillsbrad Town Registry. In Hillsbrad Fields, the town hall keeps the names and land rights of those who remain. The Hillsbrad Town Registry records the town's civic order, and the Forsaken seek it as they attack the human stronghold. The Hillsbrad Town Registry holds the town's names and rights. It lies in the town hall near Magistrate Burnside's podium. From Tarren Mill, the Forsaken press to break human resistance in the foothills. Darthalia sends Horde champions into the hall to kill the council and seize the ledger.

Its pages record Hillsbrad's population, households, and administrative rights. The Forsaken would use them to undo the town's civic order and learn about its surviving people and their assets.

item:hollow-vulture-bone.text: Hollow Vulture Bone. Across the Shimmering Flats, vultures circle the salt while goblin crews gather their bones. At the Mirage Raceway, mechanics use the hollow remains to lighten rocket cars without weakening them. At the Mirage Raceway, goblin pit crews look for every way to make their rocket cars faster. Weight slows a car, so they use what the desert provides alongside iron and copper. Hollow vulture bones are light yet sturdy enough for steering rigs, internal brackets, and small supports. Pozzik and the other chief tinkerers gather them from local scavengers to save seconds on the track.

item:honorary-picks.text: Honorary Picks. In Ironforge, Honorary Picks are bound for Brock Stoneseeker’s mining apprentices in Thelsamar. Gryphons carry the ceremonial tools to Loch Modan, where they mark students ready to work its ore veins. Mining keeps the great forges burning and brings dwarves the iron and stone they need. In Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker teaches young apprentices to mine. Honorary Picks from Ironforge mark the students ready to work the open ore deposits across Loch Modan. The picks travel through the Alliance gryphon network, linking Ironforge with its outlying settlements. At Ironforge’s Great Forge, Gryth Thurden receives the shipment. He sends it over the mountains to Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar.

item:horn-of-arra-chea.text: Horn of Arra'chea. Across Mulgore, young hunters track Arra'chea at Cairne Bloodhoof's call. The horn proves they can find prey and provide for the Shu'halo. After the Rites of the Earthmother, a youth may take a place atop Thunder Bluff. Yet High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof still asks his people to prove their worth. For the tauren, hunting ties their identity to lasting harmony with the land. So Cairne sends young hunters after Arra'chea, a massive, solitary kodo bull that roams the grasslands below. Taking the bull's horn proves they can track prey across vast distances. Arra'chea's horn helps sustain Thunder Bluff as well as display a hunter's strength. Tauren make use of every part of a slain beast. The trophy tells the High Chieftain where Arra'chea fell. Then gathering parties can descend into the plains and harvest the kodo's thick hide and rich meat for the fledgling capital.

item:horn-of-awakening.text:
Horn of Awakening. On the road to Ashenvale, Kerlonian Evershade carries the Horn of Awakening. It stirs him whenever sleep overtakes him. Kerlonian Evershade has only lately awakened from centuries in the Emerald Dream. Still, wakefulness weighs on him. The Druid of the Claw travels south toward Maestra's Post and entrusts the horn to travelers willing to escort him.

When exhaustion takes Kerlonian on the wilderness trail, a clear blast jolts him awake. He gets back on his feet before wild beasts or cultists can reach him.

item:horn-of-echeyakee.text: Horn of Echeyakee. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn gives hunters the Horn of Echeyakee to sound among the ancient kodo remains northeast of the settlement. Its call brings forth the legendary white predator of the Barrens. Hunters receive the horn when they are tested in the hunt. Its call summons Echeyakee, whose name means “Whitemist” in Taur-ahe. Tauren hunters revere the king of the savannah cats as mercy and death. His swift strike leaves his quarry no time for terror or suffering. The horn belongs at his lair, among the giant kodo bones behind the hills northeast of the Crossroads.

item:huge-gnoll-claw.text: Huge Gnoll Claw. In southwestern Elwynn, Hogger's death is proven by his huge claw. Stormwind's authorities in Goldshire require it before paying the bounty. For months, Hogger has terrorized the southern woodlands of Forest's Edge. Patrols have failed to stop him, and the local garrison cannot corral or subdue the brute. The Stormwind Army is stretched thin across Elwynn, so it has posted an open bounty on his head. Marshal Dughan in Goldshire requires clear proof before paying. Hogger's oversized claw leaves no doubt that the notorious marauder has fallen.

item:humbert-s-sword.text: Humbert's Sword. At Dun Garok, Humbert's Sword rests among the dwarves who took it from his camp. Deathguard Humbert left his post to gather firewood while scouting the stronghold. Deathguard Humbert left his hidden post near Dun Garok one morning to gather firewood for boiling water. High Executor Darthalia had sent him to watch the dwarven presence there. While he was away, a dwarven patrol found his campsite and plundered his gear, including his personal blade. Now Humbert needs Horde agents to search the fortress and recover it. Dun Garok's defenders carried Humbert's belongings behind the stronghold's barricades. Riflemen, mountaineers, and priests pass supplies around the garrison. To find the thief, the search must reach the defenders in the trenches and redoubts.

item:hyacinth-mushroom.text: Hyacinth Mushroom. In Shadowglen, Hyacinth Mushrooms grow among Teldrassil’s trees and roots. Night elf herbalists use them in medicine, while grell and grellkin forage for them. Among the trees and roots of Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Hyacinth Mushrooms help forest healers treat young night elf sentinels and trainees harmed by venomous creatures. The spiders of Shadowthread Cave are among the dangers they face. Healers use the mushrooms in soothing draughts and antivenoms. Corrupted grell also hoard them.

item:hypercapacitor-gizmo.text: Hypercapacitor Gizmo. In Thousand Needles, the Hypercapacitor Gizmo lies among the wreckage of a goblin caravan. A caged panther wore it around its neck, and even its owner does not know what it does. Centaur marauders ambushed a goblin caravan crossing Thousand Needles and plundered nearly everything. Wizlo Bearingshiner, the lone survivor, crawled to safety at Whitereach Post. He left his best gizmo behind, fastened around the neck of a ferocious, enraged panther locked in a transport cage. The centaur feared the beast and left the cage untouched in the burning wreckage. Wizlo proudly calls the Hypercapacitor Gizmo his best gizmo, though he admits he has no idea what it does. The device tangles ambition with volatile parts. Wizlo can only keep tinkering, unsure what practical use it might have.

item:ignition-key.text:
Ignition Key. At Sludge Fen, Wizzlecrank waits for the Ignition Key to free a stolen shredder. Wizzlecrank, Sputtervalve of Ratchet's operative, waits inside a Venture Company shredder at Sludge Fen. Sent to steal the machine, he found its movement column locked. So he feigned mechanical trouble while the foremen watched, hoping someone would fetch the Ignition Key.

Supervisor Lugwizzle keeps the key atop the central oil derrick. It unlocks the shredder's movement column and gives Wizzlecrank control of its arm, speed, and rotation.

item:ilkrud-magthrull-s-tome.text: Ilkrud Magthrull's Tome. At Fire Scar Shrine, Delgren the Purifier turns his attention to Ilkrud Magthrull's Tome. Its pages link the warlock to the cultists at the Tower of Althalaxx. At Fire Scar Shrine in southwestern Ashenvale, Ilkrud Magthrull holds ground poisoned by demonic influence. The formidable orc warlock is surrounded by summoned minions. His personal tome records foul rituals and shadowy communications. Delgren the Purifier, an Argent Dawn paladin, has long known Magthrull is there. The book is urgent to recover because it links the warlock to the dark cultists gathering at the Tower of Althalaxx.

item:incantations-from-the-nether.text: Incantations from the Nether. Beneath Orgrimmar, the Searing Blade holds Incantations from the Nether, a grimoire of demonic magic. Sylvanas Windrunner and Varimathras seek its fel knowledge for the Forsaken. The Searing Blade works in the fiery tunnels of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar's red stone streets. The subterranean sect is tied to the Shadow Council. Its cultists prize Incantations from the Nether, a spellbook of demonic rites given by agents of the Burning Legion. They use its secrets to plot treason in the Orcish capital. Word of the tome has reached the royal quarters of Undercity.

item:incendia-agave.text: Incendia Agave. Beneath Darkcloud Pinnacle, Incendia Agave grows in the Boiling Pool. A skilled shaman can enchant it to kindle the sacred fire of life. In Thousand Needles, Incendia Agave grows in and around the Boiling Pool beneath Darkcloud Pinnacle. Wandering steam elementals guard the scarce plant, making it difficult to harvest. Though it grows underwater, the plant bears natural elements suited to rituals of flame.

item:incendia-powder.text: Incendia Powder. At Darkcloud Pinnacle, Incendia Powder calls a sacred spirit into the open. Magatha Grimtotem enchants it on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise for use in Thousand Needles. Incendia Powder carries shamanic magic to the sacred fire atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. On Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise, Magatha Grimtotem entrusts it to travelers. Scatter it across the consecrated brazier where the dead are laid to rest, and it calls forth Arikara, a vengeful winged serpent.

item:insane-scribbles.text: Insane Scribbles. In Darkshore, cultists carry Insane Scribbles torn from the Twilight Tome, a fragment of dark literature. The dancing script and warped designs unsettle the mind. Ancient forest protectors study the pages to learn the Twilight's Hammer's purpose. The Twilight Tome can put a mortal's sanity at risk. Its script writhes across the parchment, and graceful scrollwork warps into grotesque images before the reader's eyes. Even one torn sheet, called Insane Scribbles, leaves its bearer lightheaded and disoriented. The writing makes little sense, yet the parchment hums with primal, deeply ancient magic tied to dark powers buried beneath Azeroth.

item:inscribed-bark.text: Inscribed Bark. In Teldrassil, Inscribed Bark bears the Oracle Tree's report to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. It tells of the boughs' health and the threats still troubling the woods. The Oracle Tree sends Inscribed Bark to the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus. After you drive the harpies from their nests, the ancient tree gives you its message. It fears the tainted paths through Teldrassil are unsafe for ordinary couriers. The report tells Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm of recent victories and the deeper blight still gripping the woods.

item:intact-raptor-horn.text: Intact Raptor Horn. Across the Barrens, hunters seek whole raptor horns. Mebok Mizzyrix of Ratchet hopes to make tonics from them, trusting rumors that these raptors are clever. Hunters prize raptor hides, talons, and trophies, yet whole horns are harder to take in the field. Mebok Mizzyrix is an eccentric goblin alchemist in Ratchet. He believes Barrens raptors are more cunning than their kin elsewhere, and suspects their intellect lies in their horns. So he hopes to grind whole horns into tonics and bottle that supposed genius in drinks for sale. A horn fit for brewing must come from a particularly vicious predator, not just any young raptor. Sunscale Scytheclaws prowl the southern plains and the northern borders near Ashenvale. Takk the Leaper and the elusive Ishamuhale are notable terrors of the veldt. Their stout horns can survive the clash of the hunt intact.

item:intrepid-strongbox-key.text: Intrepid Strongbox Key. On the Intrepid's wreck, Captain Halyndor still carries the key to his strongbox. The rusted iron key once kept a mysterious item locked aboard the doomed Alliance vessel off the Wetlands. The Intrepid sank with the Third Fleet off the Wetlands. Its crew became restless, cursed spirits. Captain Halyndor watched over a mysterious item inside the ship’s heavy strongbox. Now his ghost prowls the waterlogged deck with the rusted key that opens it.

item:invisibility-liquor.text: Invisibility Liquor. Maybell Maclure slips from her family's sight with Invisibility Liquor to meet Tommy Joe Stonefield. Their households remain bound by a bitter feud. Tommy Joe Stonefield seeks a quiet meeting with Maybell Maclure. But their families' feud keeps the households apart, and their kin watch closely. Ordinary secrecy will not do. Invisibility Liquor lets its drinker cross the disputed farmland unseen.

item:iron-pike.text: Iron Pike. In Lakeshire, builders need Iron Pike supplies to repair the Everstill Bridge. Redridge gnolls seized the shipment from Stormwind, leaving the town short of iron. After Blackrock orc attacks, Lakeshire spent its metal reserves on armor, blades, and ammunition. Builders then asked Stormwind City for more iron, but Redridge gnolls hijacked the caravan on the road. They took crates of iron pikes and rivets north into the hills, and work on the Everstill Bridge stopped. Foreman Oslow oversees the bridge's reconstruction and needs the stolen hardware. Without the heavy pikes to strengthen its stone and timber frame, the bridge leaves Lakeshire partly cut off from the northern road. It also leaves the town open to further incursions.

item:iron-pommel.text: Iron Pommel. In Ashenvale, the Iron Pommel remains the last piece missing from Dartol's Rod. The long-dead wizard Dartol made the rod, and the night elves of Astranaar seek it to slow the furbolg attacks. Druids at Dor'Danil Barrow Den guarded the pommel until their sanctuary was overrun and they were slaughtered. Dartol's Rod was broken apart and scattered across Ashenvale to guard its mystic power. Night elf druids near the road south toward the Barrens took charge of the Iron Pommel. Their circle was massacred at Dor'Danil Barrow Den, and their shelter fell silent among the ruins. In the destruction, the pommel vanished. Bubbling oozes now move through the defiled glade.

item:iron-rivet.text: Iron Rivet. North of Lake Everstill, Iron Rivet shipments from Stormwind lie in gnoll camps. Foreman Oslow needs them to mend Lakeshire's damaged bridge. Lakeshire spent its iron making weapons and armor when Blackrock orcs attacked. After the assaults eased, Foreman Oslow asked Stormwind for supplies to mend the damaged Everstill Bridge. Redridge gnolls ambushed the caravan before it reached town. They hauled its wagons and pack beasts into the hills north of Lake Everstill, scattering iron rivets and pikes among their camps. Heavy iron rivets hold the Everstill Bridge's stone and timber frame together under carts and travelers. Foreman Oslow cannot safely repair it without them. The bridge links Lakeshire to the western valleys. Mending it will help secure the town's perimeter against further incursions.

item:iron-shaft.text: Iron Shaft. Near Felwood, the Iron Shaft remains locked away. Teronis seeks it as one piece of Dartol's Rod, hoping to slow the furbolg assaults on Ashenvale. Dartol made the rod, and its pieces were scattered across Ashenvale. One was entrusted to the druids of Dor'Danil. The Iron Shaft is the rod's sturdy metal core, locked in a chest in a glade near Ashenvale's northern border, close to Felwood.

item:ironband-s-progress-report.text: Ironband's Progress Report. In eastern Loch Modan, troggs have brought Prospector Ironband's excavation to a halt. His report asks for more blastpowder, though the Explorers' League sent supplies weeks ago. Jern Hornhelm receives the dispatch in Thelsamar and forwards it to the Explorers' League in Ironforge. Ironband reports that work has stalled and asks for heavy munitions. The League leaders are baffled. They sent him plenty of blastpowder weeks ago, and now wonder where it went.

item:ishamuhale-s-fang.text:
Ishamuhale's Fang. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer awaits Ishamuhale's Fang, taken from Speartooth, a feared sunscale raptor of the Barrens. The tooth proves a hunter bested one of Kalimdor's deadliest natural predators. Across the central savanna, hunters fear Ishamuhale, the fiercest sunscale raptor alive. Some say the great hunter kills from predatory passion, not hunger. Fresh zhevra meat draws the beast into the open beside a withered tree northwest of Ratchet. There, Ishamuhale gives no quarter.

Taking the massive fang proves to the Horde's hunting instructors that a traveler has overcome the savagery of the plains.

item:ivar-s-head.text: Ivar's Head. In northern Silverpine, Rane Yorick seeks Ivar's Head so her wounded brother Quinn can recover in safety. The ghoul ambushed them while they scouted for High Executor Hadrec. Rane and Quinn Yorick were scouting northern Silverpine Forest on High Executor Hadrec's orders when Ivar the Foul ambushed them at an abandoned farmstead. Forsaken Deathstalkers drove the feral ghoul off, but Quinn was badly mauled. So Rane stayed at the ruined farm to watch over him, unable to leave safely and finish their mission. Ivar's severed head proves he can no longer threaten the estate, giving Quinn time to recover under Rane's care.

item:iverron-s-antidote-item.text: Iverron's Antidote (item). In Shadowglen, Iverron's Antidote must reach a young night elf before it spoils. Dirania Silvershine brews the draught to counter the lethal venom of local Webwood spiders, but it lasts only five minutes. Dirania Silvershine brews Iverron's Antidote in Aldrassil for Iverron, a young night elf bitten by Webwood spiders. Its volatile ingredients and herbal catalysts give the draught a shelf life of only five minutes. Couriers must hurry north to the Webwood cave and deliver it before it spoils.

item:jade-phial.text:
Jade Phial. In Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage entrusts young initiates with the Jade Phial. They carry sacred water from Teldrassil’s moonwells to replenish the druids’ central well in Darnassus. The Jade Phial gathers water from a moonwell near Starbreeze Village. Across Teldrassil, moonwells channel lunar and natural energies that matter to night elf society and druidic worship.

From time to time, druids replenish their central moonwell in Darnassus with water from wells across the great bough. Corithras Moonrage entrusts the phial to young initiates, who collect pure water without disturbing the moonwell’s spiritual potency.

item:jennea-s-flask.text:
Jennea's Flask. At the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind, Jennea Cannon sends apprentices to Mirror Lake for water. They bring a sample back for arcane study. Arcane currents have been torn from their ancient channels by magical struggles across Azeroth. Jennea Cannon wants to learn how these shifts have affected Elwynn Forest. She gives promising apprentices a glass flask and sends them southwest of Stormwind's gates, to the base of Mirror Lake's waterfall.

The flask protects the water sample on the journey back to the Wizard's Sanctum. There, Jennea can examine it for arcane disturbances. With Jennea's flask, Stormwind's mages can test whether shifting ley lines have tainted Mirror Lake. Harmful magic in the water could bring strange afflictions to the surrounding life and to anyone who drinks from it. A sample may reveal magical residue before tainted currents spread through the countryside.

item:jitters-completed-journal.text: Jitters' Completed Journal. In Duskwood, Jitters gives up his completed journal and hopes it will clear his name. He fears Sven Yorgen's vengeance after fleeing the massacre at Sven's farm.

item:johaan-s-findings.text:
Johaan's Findings. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan sends his findings south to the Sepulcher. His research carries recent alchemical work from Tirisfal Glades to Apothecary Renferrel in Silverpine Forest. Apothecary Johaan sends his research from Brill to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher. The Royal Apothecary Society answers Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's demand for a New Plague that can destroy both the living and the Scourge. Its researchers are scattered across Lordaeron's contested ruins, so they share their findings between outposts.

Renferrel directs the Society's efforts from Silverpine Forest, while Johaan records his local tests in Brill. His documents join the Society's wider work to refine its deadly brews.

item:johaan-s-special-drink.text: Johaan's Special Drink. At Brill, Apothecary Johaan offers a drink that tests the Royal Apothecary Society’s developing plague. Its deadly purpose hides behind the look of an ordinary refreshment. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan mixes venomous components with local reagents. The brew looks like a tavern drink, but it tests how virulent the plague is against living beings. Johaan offers it as though to quench a captive’s thirst. The work helps the Forsaken apothecaries create a weapon potent enough to fulfill Sylvanas Windrunner’s designs for Azeroth.

item:jordan-s-ore-shipment.text: Jordan's Ore Shipment. In the northeastern hills of Loch Modan, Mo'grosh ogres hold Jordan's Ore Shipment. The ore came by caravan from the Wetlands for Bailor Stonehand to refine into an alloy for the smith Jordan Stilwell. Jordan Stilwell's ore was bound for Bailor Stonehand, a dwarf who would refine it into his special alloy. The caravan carried it south through the mountains from the Wetlands into Loch Modan. Then Mo'grosh ogres ambushed the travelers and dragged the shipment to their stronghold in the wilderness. The surviving guards died of their wounds, and Jordan's smithing project waits for the ore's return.

item:jordan-s-refined-ore-shipment.text: Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment. Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment arrives in Ironforge for the Test of Righteousness. The metal is prepared for blacksmith Jordan Stilwell to forge a holy weapon. Jordan Stilwell needs rare materials for a weapon worthy of a paladin. He requires a Purified Kor Gem, sturdy Whitestone Oak lumber, his lost smithing hammer, and refined ore. The shipment brings the metal to Ironforge for this sacred labor.

item:jordan-s-smithing-hammer.text: Jordan's Smithing Hammer. Jordan Stilwell waits outside Ironforge for his father's hammer, lost within Shadowfang Keep. Jordan Stilwell is a human blacksmith who works outside Ironforge. His father’s hammer lies within Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest. Without it, Jordan cannot forge a sacred weapon fit for a holy champion, the masterwork he hopes to make.

item:kadrak-s-flag.text: Kadrak's Flag. At the Barrens border, Kadrak sends the Horde's colors into enemy ground. The banner is planted in the Talon Den after Rynthariel is killed. Kadrak sends the Horde flag into the Talon Den on Stonetalon Peak. Rynthariel, the Den's dryad Keymaster, has sent messages across the border. Kadrak decides her death alone will not answer them. He gives you a crimson banner to plant deep inside the Den. There, the Horde colors warn the night elves and dryads that incursions across the Barrens will meet retaliation on Alliance soil.

item:keg-of-shindigger-stout.text: Keg of Shindigger Stout. In Dun Garok, Shindigger Stout fills the dwarves’ kegs and draws interest from Tarren Mill. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks the ale for a purpose darker than drink. Dwarves of Ironforge hold Dun Garok in the southeastern Hillsbrad Foothills. In its barracks and mess halls, defenders share Shindigger Stout through the cold and the siege against their regional enemies. The brew is part of the garrison’s daily life.

item:ken-zigla-s-draught.text: Ken'zigla's Draught. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Ken'zigla prepares a bitter draught for the gravely wounded. Half a dose can restore enough strength to move, but more may make a patient bleed out. Ken'zigla prepares the draught in the Stonetalon Mountains for those near death. Its strength calls for care. More than half a dose at once can make a patient bleed out as their circulation surges. Half a dose gives a wounded person enough vigor to move and flee danger.
