The rest must wait until the body steadies after a full night's rest.

item:khazgorm-s-journal.text: Khazgorm's Journal. At Bael Modan, Prospector Khazgorm leads Ironforge's excavation in the southern Barrens. His journal records the Explorers' League's work on lands claimed by the Stonespire tauren. Prospector Khazgorm directs the machinery and blasting that cut into the southern Barrens hillsides. The excavation has strayed far from the Explorers' League's promised search for knowledge. Its work has displaced the Stonespire tribe. The tauren sought a peaceful settlement, but the dwarves refused. Gann Stonespire wants the journal to learn why Ironforge is in his homeland and how to drive the expedition out.

item:klaven-mortwake-s-journal.text: Klaven Mortwake's Journal. SI:7 operatives recover Klaven Mortwake's Journal from the Defias tower. It records the Brotherhood's search for a way to raise the dead. Master Mathias Shaw leads Stormwind's intelligence service, SI:7. He sought Mortwake's journal to trace the Brotherhood's wider alliances. The notes confirm experiments in reanimation and illicit support linking Duskwood, the Venture Company, and the Defias. For rogues serving the crown, recovering the research is a step toward mastering poisons.

item:kodo-horn.text: Kodo Horn. Across the Barrens, Kodo Horns are gathered for Tonga Runetotem's remedies. He uses them to treat poisoned wildlife. Across the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem uses whole kodo horns in his herbal remedies. He works from the Crossroads, where the horns strengthen his salves. Chips and fragments lack the strength he needs, so he gathers intact horns from mature kodos roaming the plains.

item:kodo-liver.text: Kodo Liver. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn needs Kodo Liver for a strange ale. The wandering brewmaster Chen Stormstout taught him to brew it. Kodos roam the Barrens, hunted by tauren and predators for their hides and meat. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn blends a fresh Kodo Liver with thunderhawk saliva glands and lightning glands to make trogg ale. Chen Stormstout taught him the recipe, and Drohn says the brew has a potent kick for adventurous travelers. Its ingredients come from the wilds of central Kalimdor.

item:kodobane-s-head.text: Kodobane's Head. Near the Forgotten Pools, Barak Kodobane's severed head proves the chieftain is dead. Regthar Deathgate receives it as proof that the centaur threat there has been broken. Kolkar bands in the Barrens have long been divided. Now ambitious warlords threaten to gather them into an army. Barak Kodobane camps by the waters of the Forgotten Pools, where the oasis offers vital resources and nearby paths lie open to raids. Regthar Deathgate is stationed in a bunker west of the Crossroads. He demands Kodobane's severed head to prove the commander can no longer rally his kin against the Horde.

item:kravel-s-crate.text: Kravel's Crate. At the Mirage Raceway, Kravel Koalbeard has a crate to send to the Nesingwary expedition in Stranglethorn Vale. It holds specialized ammunition for hunting the jungle’s deadliest game. At the Mirage Raceway, Kravel Koalbeard hands the crate to travelers. A wealthy dwarven patron ordered it weeks ago, but the shipment was delayed until the buyer had left Kalimdor. The patron had paid for forwarding, and Kravel wants to keep the favor of a wealthy customer. So he trusts passing travelers to carry it across continents to northern Stranglethorn Vale. Salt dust gathers on the crate as it waits in the Shimmering Flats. Inside are heavy, special-gauge rounds made for hunting rifles. The travelers deliver them to the expedition camp north of Grom'gol. The recipient says big-game hunters prize the potent ammunition. Against the predators roaming the jungle canopy, it is vital for survival.

item:kreenig-snarlsnout-s-tusk.text:
Kreenig Snarlsnout's Tusk. At the Crossroads, Thork awaits proof that Kreenig Snarlsnout has fallen. The tusk marks the end of the Razormane leader's attacks on Horde caravans in the northern Barrens. Horde caravans traveling west from Durotar face constant attacks in the Barrens. Under Kreenig Snarlsnout, a fierce Razormane leader, those raids grew bolder. So Thork, commander of the Crossroads watch, ordered Kreenig killed to disrupt the quilboars' coordination.

Kreenig's tusk proves the leader is dead and insults the Razormane. Their resolve weakens, and their fighters are left without central direction.

item:kron-s-amulet.text: Kron's Amulet. Along the Southfury River, Kron’s amulet recalls a young orc hunter who went missing.

item:kuz-s-skull.text: Kuz's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Kuz's Skull marks the fall of a feared Razormane raider. From Razorfen Kraul, Kuz helped lead attacks on Horde outposts until a captive former kin sought vengeance. Kuz, Nak, and their chieftain Lok Orcbane led Razormane attacks across the southern Barrens. Sent from Razorfen Kraul, the three raiders struck travelers and settlements such as the Crossroads. They betrayed Mangletooth, a fellow quilboar, and left him to rot in a cage at Camp Taurajo. From there, Mangletooth revealed Kuz's location to Horde champions willing to kill the raider and take her head.

item:laced-pumpkin.text: Laced Pumpkin. At Apothecary Johaan's hand, Laced Pumpkin tests the reach of Forsaken alchemy. In Brill, the Royal Apothecary Society seeks weapons against the Scourge and living human forces. In Tirisfal Glades, pumpkins look like ordinary produce salvaged from blighted soil. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan treats one with experimental toxins to test the full potential of undeath. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks weapons against the Scourge in the north and living human forces advancing from the south. Even a simple harvest can carry infection and chemical death.

item:laird-s-response.text:
Laird's Response. Along Teldrassil's shore, Laird sends Nessa Shadowsong a curious report. The fish there are larger and more plentiful than those along mainland Darkshore. Laird compares the catches from both sides of the Veiled Sea. Fish from Teldrassil's coast are larger and more plentiful than those from Darkshore's mainland beaches.

In his reply to Nessa Shadowsong, Laird of Auberdine wonders if the newly planted World Tree's unusual presence and vitality are changing the sea life nearby. Travelers carry his letter across the water to Rut'theran Village, where the fisherfolk meet the news with wonder and quiet curiosity.

item:lake-creeper-moss.text:
Lake Creeper Moss. Around the southern Dawning Isles, Lake Creeper Moss grows on aquatic beasts. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks this organic compound as a vital reagent for engineering a lethal new plague. Lake Creeper Moss grows on the hides of freshwater beasts in the waters by the southern Dawning Isles. Lordaeron’s blighted waters give it unusual properties. Before Arugal’s curse claimed his mind, Apothecary Berard recorded the moss in his journal.

He found it resembled traces on fossils of creatures killed by an ancient plague in the lake. Forsaken agents send recovered samples to the Apothecarium in the Undercity, where Master Apothecary Faranell uses them in his research.

item:lake-skulker-moss.text:
Lake Skulker Moss. In northern Lake Lordamere, Lake Skulker Moss draws the Royal Apothecary Society's attention. Apothecary Berard found a use for it in brewing a New Plague before Arugal's curse claimed his mind. Lake Skulker Moss comes from Lake Skulkers and Elder Lake Skulkers on the Dawning Isles. Before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, Apothecary Berard cataloged the plants and creatures of eastern Silverpine Forest. His journal says Lake Skulker and Lake Creeper mosses could stabilize or react with other ingredients.

After the curse made Berard Arugal's mindless servant, his journal was recovered from Pyrewood Village for Apothecary Renferrel. Renferrel sent Forsaken champions to gather moss and a rare tumor from local Vile Fin murlocs. They were to deliver both to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity.

item:large-candle.text: Large Candle. In Elwynn's mines, kobolds carry Large Candles for light and wax. Apothecaries value the wax for their work. Kobolds follow candlelight through the dark shafts beneath Elwynn Forest. They fasten the tapers to their heads, and Kobold Miners, Tunnelers, and Geomancers defend them fiercely from intruders. Large Candles from Fargodeep Mine and Jasperlode Mine hold valuable wax, though they are crudely made. Surface tradesmen cannot produce much wax at once, so the candles serve both as tools for kobolds and as a commodity for alchemists. William Pestle, an apothecary operative from Stormwind City, gathers Large Candles at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. His family runs an apothecary, and he needs rendered wax for its concoctions, balms, and ointments. Pestle hires passing adventurers to clear the infested mines and take candles from the kobolds.

item:large-soran-ruk-fragment.text: Large Soran'ruk Fragment. In Shadowfang Keep, the Large Soran'ruk Fragment lies far from the other shards. Its broken orb once held a disgraced demon of the Burning Legion. Disgraced demons of the Burning Legion may be imprisoned in enchanted orbs. Mages and warlocks aligned with the Legion receive these vessels and draw upon the fel forces within. Even shattered, an orb's bound fiend leaves an essence that still radiates power. So fragments draw those who seek mastery of shadow magic. The orb of Soran'ruk was cracked into two halves long ago. Cultists elsewhere scattered one half into smaller pieces, while a sorcerer in the cursed Shadowfang Keep claimed the larger half. Shadowfang Darksouls carry the Large Soran'ruk Fragment. Its bound spirit remains within, until someone seeks to reforge the ancient vessel.

item:laughing-sister-s-hair.text:
Laughing Sister's Hair. In Ashenvale, weavers seek the natural magic in laughing sisters' hair. Kil'hala at the Crossroads uses the locks to make enchanted robes. Near Raynewood Retreat, laughing sisters are dryads whose hair holds natural magic. They guard the woods and are linked to Cenarius and the night elves. Horde craftsmen prize their hair as a potent material.

Kil'hala, a troll tailor at the Crossroads, spins the locks into enchanted robes for Deino's promising pupils of the arcane.

item:legacy-of-the-aspects.text:
Legacy of the Aspects. In the Horde trial, seekers must find Legacy of the Aspects and remember its lessons. The ancient tome lies in Dor'Danil Barrow Den in southern Ashenvale, where it holds lore about the Great Aspects who shaped ancient Azeroth. Braug Dimspirit sends aspirants to seek Legacy of the Aspects. Earlier trials set by tauren elders test endurance and resolve. This trial tests the mind. Braug waits at the entrance to the Talondeep Path in the Stonetalon Mountains, while the tome lies in the haunted barrow dens of Dor'Danil.

Restless spirits of fallen druids and the vicious creatures that slew them guard the ancient text. It rests on a stone pedestal. Finding the volume is only the beginning. Before returning it, the seeker must commit its contents to memory. Then Braug tests them on its lessons in history.

item:letter-to-delgren.text: Letter to Delgren. Balthule Shadowstrike sends word from the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore. His letter warns Delgren the Purifier of the Dark Strand cult's demonic work and must reach Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. At the Tower of Althalaxx ruins, Balthule Shadowstrike watches the Dark Strand cult gather. He cannot destroy them alone, so he writes to Delgren the Purifier, his tutor in the Holy Light, and asks for aid. Their foul rites threaten more than Darkshore's coast. The letter must travel south through Darkshore into western Ashenvale. There, Delgren works with night elf Sentinels against demonic and undead threats.

item:letter-to-ello.text: Letter to Ello. Abercrombie sends a sealed letter to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke in Darkshire. The hermit lives in a shack just north of Raven Hill Cemetery, claims an old friendship, and writes the missive in an archaic script. After you help Abercrombie with tasks around Duskwood, the old recluse gives you a note for Mayor Ello Ebonlocke. He says the mayor is an old friend who will celebrate what you have accomplished. When Ello breaks the seal, he has no recollection of anyone named Abercrombie and cannot read a single phrase of the archaic script. He sends the note to Darkshire scholar Sirra Von'Indi for translation.

item:letter-to-jin-zil.text: Letter to Jin'Zil. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger sends Jin'Zil news from the northern Barrens. Serena Bloodfeather is dead, and the Bloodfeather threat there has ended. After the harpies at the Dry Hills are wiped out and Serena Bloodfeather is slain, Darsok Swiftdagger writes to an old comrade. The Barrens harpies first roosted in the peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains. Darsok sends word of their fallen matron to Jin'Zil, a witch doctor, and introduces a promising warrior to the wider frontier.

item:letter-to-jorgen.text: Letter to Jorgen. In Stormwind City, a sealed letter calls Jorgen to help find a missing diplomat. A diplomat bound for Theramore never arrived for talks with Lady Jaina Proudmoore. Royal investigators moved quickly to keep the matter quiet. While official agents searched the capital, other channels stirred. The letter bypasses military ranks and seeks Jorgen, a gruff veteran who fishes beneath the great statues in the Valley of Heroes. It invokes old obligations and draws him into a covert inquiry amid rumors of a Defias conspiracy.

item:lewis-note.text: Lewis' Note. At Sentinel Hill, Quartermaster Lewis sends a courier by gryphon to seek armor for Westfall's garrison. The order goes to a private armorer in Stormwind. The People's Militia at Sentinel Hill receives little support from Stormwind's House of Nobles. Skirmishes with the Defias Brotherhood keep wearing down its small supply of gear. So Quartermaster Lewis turns to private trade to keep the defenders equipped. His order goes outside the kingdom's military channels. An Alliance courier must fly by gryphon to Old Town and present it to Osric Strang, who owns Limited Immunity.

item:lieutenant-s-insignia.text: Lieutenant's Insignia. Near Orgrimmar, cultists bear Lieutenant's Insignia and the Burning Blade's mark. Horde adventurers recover it from them. Cultists at Skull Rock on Durotar's eastern shore carry Lieutenant's Insignia. The mark names its bearer an officer of the Burning Blade. Warchief Thrall will not suffer traitors in his new nation. Yet a purge might scatter the cult before its masters are exposed. So he entrusts the badge to a champion, to test those suspected of infiltrating beneath Orgrimmar.

item:lightning-gland.text: Lightning Gland. Across the Barrens, stormhides carry Lightning Glands that Brewmaster Drohn needs in Ratchet. Chen Stormstout taught Drohn to make trogg ale, a fiery brew. Stormhides roam the Barrens savannas among other predators touched by the elements. Their flesh holds Lightning Glands charged with latent electricity. The glands make poor fare on their own, but brewers prize the sting they bring to a brew. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn keeps Chen Stormstout’s brewing traditions alive. For trogg ale, a potent brew, he needs five Lightning Glands, a thunderhawk saliva gland, and a fresh kodo liver. The finished drink has a sharp kick that adventurers find invigorating and potent.

item:logging-rope.text: Logging Rope. At the Warsong Lumber Camp, Logging Rope keeps the mills and machinery supplied. Furbolg tribes have stolen shipments across Ashenvale, and the Warsong must recover the line they need. Foulweald and Thistlefur furbolgs have stolen Logging Rope shipments meant for the Warsong Lumber Camp. They intercepted the line before it could reach the loggers. The ropes are kept in village dens and encampments across northern and central Ashenvale. Corruption has driven the furbolgs mad, and they fiercely defend their ancestral woods. At Splintertree Post, Locke Okarr seeks to recover the stolen supplies before work at the Warsong Lumber Camp stops. The heavy rope secures timber, binds logs, and rigs saw machinery. Furbolg resistance continues across the forest.

item:lok-s-skull.text: Lok's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Lok's Skull marks the fall of a feared Razormane leader. Lok Orcbane led fierce quilboar raids against Horde supply routes, and the skull is his severed head. Lok Orcbane led aggressive Razormane assaults on Horde supply lines in the southern Barrens. He emerged from Razorfen Kraul with his lieutenants Nak and Kuz. After betraying Mangletooth and leaving him captive at Camp Taurajo, Lok became known to orcish defenders for ruthless raids they struggled to contain. Mangletooth directs Horde champions to Lok's camp. Claiming Lok's skull avenges the captive and strikes at the leaders driving the Razormane offensive.

item:lonebrow-s-journal.text:
Lonebrow's Journal. At the base of the Great Lift, Henrig Lonebrow's journal records his final journey. He crossed the Barrens as danger gathered at Razorfen Kraul. Henrig Lonebrow died near the base of the Great Lift, the passage between the Barrens and Thousand Needles. His bones rest on a rocky ledge with the weathered journal still in his grasp.

The pages recount his last travels and ask the finder to carry word to Falfindel Waywarder, a night elf druid at Thalanaar. The outpost lies on the border of Feralas. Lonebrow's notes warn of the quilboar threat growing in the southern Barrens.

item:lorgalis-manuscript.text:
Lorgalis Manuscript. Beneath Ashenvale, the Lorgalis Manuscript lies in the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. The ancient text speaks of the Old Gods, and dark scholars covet its words about sleeping powers. The Lorgalis Manuscript lies at the bottom of Blackfathom Deeps, among the ruins where long-dead elves once lived. Lorgalis wrote of the Old Gods, who raged across Azeroth when the world was new and now lie chained in sleep. The text praises Aku'mai, servant of the Old Gods, who dwells in the Deeps.

Its lore is said to open mystical doorways and stir ancient beings sleeping deep beneath the world. The manuscript rests in a pitted iron chest among the flooded corridors. Cultists and shadow scholars alike seek its words.

item:lunar-fungus.text: Lunar Fungus. In Darkshore's caves, druids gather Lunar Fungus to help heal sick deer. Mixed with Earthroot and water, it strengthens a healing salve. Lunar Fungus grows from Lunar Fungal Blooms in Darkshore's underground caverns. The Cenarion Circle values its power to strengthen remedies. Mixed with soothing water and common Earthroot, it lends strength to a salve that counters debilitating afflictions. Territorial moonkin frequent the damp caves, so gathering the fungus takes care. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong has young druids gather Lunar Fungus as they study nature's healing arts. They learn how physical ingredients such as the fungus can counter poisons in local deer. By studying herbal remedies, initiates prepare to channel natural antidotes through shapeshifting and spiritual power.

item:lurker-venom.text:
Lurker Venom. In Loch Modan, dwarven defenders need Lurker Venom to counter Dark Iron sabotage. Predatory spiders in the rocky hills and woods provide the toxin. Lurker Venom helps dwarves disarm explosives planted by the Dark Iron. Ashlan Stonesmirk, an explosives expert, named spider poison as an ingredient in the mixture Chief Engineer Hinderweir prepares. The solvent joins the venom with rare minerals and tears from the loch’s crocolisks. Together, they form a reactive compound that can disarm complex explosives.

Lurker spiders range from common wood lurkers to the matriarch Shanda the Spinner. Their bites threaten travelers and mountaineers across Loch Modan’s hills and crags.

item:lydon-s-toxin.text:
Lydon's Toxin. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon has made a toxin to disrupt Venture Company logging in the Stonetalon Mountains. Horde adventurers carry it to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff, who must find a way to spread it. Apothecary Lydon made the toxin in the Hillsbrad Foothills to hinder Venture Company loggers in the Stonetalon Mountains. He says it kills on contact and may pass from one target to another.

Before it can reach the goblins near Windshear Crag, the mixture must cross continents to Thunder Bluff. There, Apothecary Zamah, the Royal Apothecary Society's representative, needs the raw toxin to devise a wide-dispersal device called the Toxic Fogger.

item:macgrann-s-dried-meats.text: MacGrann's Dried Meats. In Dun Morogh, Old Icebeard has carried off Tundra MacGrann’s winter meat. Tundra MacGrann hunted game and salted it for the winter. He packed weeks of provisions into a sturdy chest inside a thorium meat locker, to keep scavenging bears and prowling predators from his homestead. Yet he never expected an intruder strong enough to carry away the whole chest. Old Icebeard raided MacGrann’s camp while the dwarf tracked deer. The yeti dragged the heavy chest to his den in Chill Breeze Valley. Its solid thorium plating holds, but MacGrann’s injured leg keeps him from making a swift rescue into the cavern. Without help retrieving his cache before winter, the stranded hunter faces starvation in the mountain snows.

item:mackreel-s-moonshine.text: MacKreel's Moonshine. On the broken Thandol Span, Foggy MacKreel brews moonshine strong enough to fell a sentry. Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore takes a batch to settle Foggy's debt. Foggy MacKreel brews moonshine while guarding the Thandol Span. Even hardened dwarven sentries can be laid low after a night of drinking it. They wake with headaches like siege engines rolling overhead. Travelers prize its warmth against the damp chill of Lordaeron and Khaz Modan. Foggy MacKreel owed a debt to Brewmeister Bilger, Southshore's tavern keeper and master brewer. He sent a batch of moonshine instead of coin to clear his tab. Bilger accepts the liquor in place of gold and adds MacKreel's potent brew to his stock for the chilly coastal days of the Hillsbrad Foothills.

item:maggot-eye-s-paw.text: Maggot Eye's Paw. At Garren's Haunt, Maggot Eye's Paw confirms the gnoll chieftain's execution. It is carried to Brill as proof that he stole corpses for the Scourge. Maggot Eye raided graves and the countryside near Garren's Haunt. He supplied the corpses he stole to the Lich King's armies. So the Forsaken condemned him to death and posted a bounty in Brill. Hunters must bring his severed paw back to town to claim it and close the matter. Executor Zygand accepts the paw as proof of Maggot Eye's death, not mere rumor.

item:maggran-s-reserve-letter.text:
Maggran's Reserve Letter. At Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran Earthbinder sends a reserve warrior south to relieve Grish Longrunner at the Great Lift. The orders let Grish return home and visit his family. From Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran Earthbinder sends orders to the Great Lift. Grish Longrunner, a Horde sentry there, is to be relieved by a replacement warrior.

The Great Lift's wooden winches stand far to the south. Grish has kept watch there, but now the new warrior takes his place. Grish can leave his post and return home to visit his family.

item:mangy-claw.text: Mangy Claw. In Dun Morogh, Mangy Claw marks the end of a deadly hunt. The great ice claw bear Mangeclaw killed a stranded dwarven pilot, and the severed claw proves the beast was slain. Pilot Hildelve’s steam tank broke down in Dun Morogh’s frozen hills. He searched for ore on foot and faced the mountain wilderness alone. In his journal, he tells how he fought off Mangeclaw, an ice claw bear, but was savagely mauled. The bear returned and killed the weakened pilot. Hildelve’s final entry pleaded for vengeance. Taking Mangy Claw from the fallen bear fulfills his request.

item:marshal-haggard-s-badge.text:
Marshal Haggard's Badge. In the hills of Elwynn Forest, Marshal Haggard lives retired from Stormwind's service. Dead-tooth Jack tricked him into surrendering his old badge, which the Defias could use to impersonate city officials. Dead-tooth Jack came to Haggard's farm one night in a Stormwind tabard. The Defias rogue pretended to be Marshal Dughan, Goldshire's garrison commander, and said Haggard's former peers needed the insignia for official business.

The aging marshal handed it over without suspicion. Jack fled into the woods before Haggard saw through the ruse. In Defias hands, the badge still carries the authority of Stormwind's marshals. Outlaws could use it to pass checkpoints or confuse local patrols.

item:mary-s-looking-glass.text: Mary's Looking Glass. In Duskwood, Mary's discarded looking glass passes from a ghoul to a stargazer. Blind Mary once treasured the polished mirror. After her death and the loss of her eyes, her reflection became a painful reminder of what she had lost. She threw the looking glass behind her barn. Duskwood's gloom gathered around it, until an Insane Ghoul found it among the ruined outskirts and carried it south to the crypts of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. In Darkshire, the stargazer Viktori Prism'Antras dreams of looking past Duskwood's eternal twilight to the clear heavens above. His telescope needs special optical lenses and reflective glass. Mary sends adventurers to the ruined chapel in the cemetery, where feral undead hold her looking glass. Viktori needs it as a reflector in his machine for viewing the stars.

item:mathystra-relic.text:
Mathystra Relic. In northern Darkshore, Mathystra's ancient relics still bear traces of magic. The Twilight's Hammer has taken an interest in them. Mathystra once stood on the Kalimdor coast as a city and bastion of elven civilization. Before the Great Sundering, it was a proud place. Now toppled columns and cracked stones lie half-swallowed by brush and sea mist. Restless spirits and lurking beasts move among them.

Relics from that age lie scattered through the ruins. Ten thousand years of neglect have worn them, yet traces of elven arcane craft remain. In careless hands, these relics are dangerous.

item:melenas-head.text:
Melenas' Head. At Fel Rock, Melenas' Head brings Lord Melenas' threat to an end. The satyr commander was encamped there, and the head is proof of his death. Satyrs on Teldrassil's new World Tree shame the night elves who guard Shadowglen and the lands around it. Lord Melenas made his lair in Fel Rock's twisted caverns, just north of the elven settlements. There he rallied aggressive grell warriors to his banner.

The kaldorei prize discretion when corruption draws so near their heartlands. Melenas' Head is private proof that his schemes ended before his influence could spread.

item:menethil-statuette.text:
Menethil Statuette. Off the Wetlands coast, the Menethil Statuette lies lost from a shipwreck. The rare silver likeness honors Lordaeron's fallen king. King Terenas Menethil II is shown as a young paladin, long-haired, with his hammer raised toward the heavens. Humble in life, he disliked monuments to himself, and few likenesses were made in his honor. When the Scourge brought down Lordaeron, almost all those likenesses were destroyed. This surviving effigy is precious to the Alliance. The Blind Princess was carrying the statuette toward the Alliance harbor of Menethil when Bluegill murlocs attacked off the marshy coast. The assault scattered the merchant vessel's cargo, and the statuette came to rest in a half-buried barrel on shore.

Dragonmaw orcs and other local threats remained nearby, so defenders hurried the recovered icon south to Stormwind City. There, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon entrusted it to the Cathedral of Light.

item:merrin-s-letter.text:
Merrin's Letter. At Whelgar's Excavation, Merrin Rockweaver sends urgent word from the Wetlands. Raptors have overrun the dig, but she tells her loved ones she survived. Merrin Rockweaver writes from the ruined dig at Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands. The dwarven expedition had been uncovering enormous prehistoric fossils and relics when they disturbed a nest of Mottled Raptors. The beasts swarmed the trenches, killed several workers, and cut off the surviving researchers.

Amid the chaos, Merrin sends word to her husband Tarrel at Menethil Harbor. She, Prospector Whelgar, and Ormer Ironbraid survived behind a barricaded shelter.

item:middle-of-gelkak-s-key.text: Middle of Gelkak's Key. Off Darkshore, threshadons sank Gelkak Gyromast’s ship and scattered his key in three pieces. Greymist murlocs took the middle fragment. Gelkak Gyromast’s winding key broke when threshadons dragged his ship beneath the waves. The gnome pirate came ashore with his belongings shattered on the rocky shoals. His specialized key was made for his mechanical first mate, but the wreck split it into three pieces scattered along the strand. Coastal beasts carried off the top and bottom pieces. Greymist murlocs prowling the Darkshore surf took the middle piece and kept it in their camps and among the wreckage they hold.

item:milly-s-harvest.text: Milly's Harvest. In the Northshire Vineyards, Milly's Harvest lies abandoned after the Defias arrive. Crates and buckets of grapes risk theft or being crushed beneath the abbey guards' boots. Milly Osworth gathers grapes in the Northshire Vineyards. The harvest matters to local vintners and the abbey community. When armed brigands in red masks enter the fields, Milly flees to the abbey grounds. Her fresh-picked grapes lie scattered between the rows. Stormwind guards watch the valley entrance, but their small numbers leave Northshire vulnerable. The garrison promises to drive out the Defias. Milly fears a long fight between guards and thieves will ruin her harvest. The crates may be trampled or carried off as provisions, costing Northshire one of its few peaceful harvests.

item:miners-gear.text: Miners' Gear. In northern Loch Modan, Miners' Gear waits in the Silver Stream Mine. Kobolds have overrun the tunnels, and the Miners' League wants its tools recovered before the local guards attack. The Silver Stream Mine ran out of ore, so the Miners' League made its quiet tunnels a depot for mining equipment. Kobolds overran the mine, seized the stored goods and made nests among the crates. The league fears an assault by the Mountaineers could wreck the dwarven gear, or scavengers could ruin it. Enter the mine and bring the crates to safety before either fate befalls them.

item:miners-union-card.text:
Miners' Union Card. In Moonbrook, union cards remain with the laborers lost beneath the earth. Workers once carried them through the mines, and now they lie with the skeletal dead in the dark drifts. Before the Defias Brotherhood took control of Moonbrook, miners worked below ground for the guild, drawing valuable ore for the kingdom. Then a tunnel collapsed, crushing a major shaft and killing dozens beneath the rock.

The dead rose as skeletal miners, excavators, and dynamiters. Their union cards remain in bony pockets, the last proof of who they were. In Stormwind, surviving colleagues seek the cards to learn the dead workers' identities and bring closure to their families.

item:minshina-s-skull.text:
Minshina's Skull. On the Echo Isles, Minshina's soul remains bound to his skull by Zalazane's dark magic. Minshina was a Darkspear troll and Master Gadrin's brother. Zalazane seized the isles and drove the tribe away, then used Minshina's skull in his rituals. Minshina was captured and slain when Zalazane seized the Echo Isles and drove out the Darkspear. The traitorous witch doctor bound his soul to his severed skull instead of letting him pass into death. Now the skull lies within a circle of power on the southernmost isle, holding Minshina fast to Zalazane's magic.

Master Gadrin dreams of his brother calling to him, and seeks brave travelers to enter the occupied islands. He asks them to reclaim the skull and break Zalazane's hold over Minshina's spirit.

item:mirror-lake-water-sample.text:
Mirror Lake Water Sample. At Mirror Lake in Elwynn Forest, water is gathered for Jennea Cannon in Stormwind. The mages will test it for signs that the arcane currents have altered local water. Jennea Cannon sends promising apprentices to collect water from Mirror Lake. The lake lies just southwest of the Stormwind Gate, where they fill a specially prepared flask at the foot of its waterfall.

The Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind fears the world's mystic channels remain unsettled after catastrophic conflicts. Its mages will examine the sample for stray magical taint in the waterways people nearby use.

item:mist-veil-s-lockbox.text: Mist Veil's Lockbox. Off Darkshore, coastal murlocs ambushed the Mist Veil and sank it. The night elven vessel now rests beneath the waves with the captain’s log and personal effects in its lockbox. The night elven vessel Mist Veil sank while sailing toward Auberdine. Coastal murlocs overwhelmed it and its sister ship, the Silver Dawning. The captain perished, and the logbook and personal effects remain sealed in the lockbox in the flooded hold. Murlocs still surround the wreck. Surviving sailors reached Auberdine, but they still grieve for their lost vessel and commander. Gorbold Steelhand seeks Mist Veil's Lockbox so the captain's final effects can be honored and laid to rest. Recovering it from the flooded wreck may bring solace to the survivors on the mainland.

item:mo-grosh-crystal.text: Mo'grosh Crystal. In northeastern Loch Modan, Mo'grosh ogres mine and guard rare crystals with unusual alchemical properties. Dwarven engineers use them to neutralize Dark Iron explosives. Mo'grosh ogres mine the crystals at their stronghold in northeastern Loch Modan. Though the clan favors brute strength over delicate metalwork, its members prize these stones. Enforcers, mystic shamans, and towering leaders carry them. The crystals are uncommon, so the ogres guard them closely within the Mo'grosh Stronghold.

item:modr-fragment.text: Modr Fragment. At Whelgar Excavation Site, Modr Fragment lies among relics and loose earth in a raptor-overrun dig. Its ancient Titan script fills one of four gaps in the Goaz Stone. Prospector Whelgar uncovered the Goaz Stone at his Wetlands dig. The massive tablet bears ancient Titan writing. Vicious raptors drove the Explorers' League from the site before its members could finish their work. The translated inscription breaks off at four gaps, leaving warnings of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy unfinished. Modr Fragment is one of the missing pieces, left among relics and overturned soil when the diggers fled for their lives.

item:moldy-tome.text: Moldy Tome. Along the Hillsbrad coast, the Moldy Tome lies ruined after a shipwreck. Once part of the Tome of the Cabal, it still draws warlocks seeking its lore on demonic summoning. The Tome of the Cabal was a rare work of dark arts held in Lordaeron. Someone vandalized it and tore it in two. One half, now called the Moldy Tome, sailed south toward Menethil Harbor and Ironforge. The ship never arrived. It sank in the dangerous waters west of Southshore, and the half that survived washed ashore south of Azurelode Mine. Damp and surf ruined its pages as murlocs scavenged along the Hillsbrad coast.

item:moonpetal-lily.text: Moonpetal Lily. Around Teldrassil’s freshwater pools, Moonpetal Lilies offer petals prized for their restorative power. Healers use them in remedies and healing draughts. Moonpetal Lilies grow along the moist banks of freshwater pools and ponds. They are common northwest of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. Like other plants atop the young World Tree, they draw on the essence of Teldrassil’s sheltered groves. Their broad petals shine beside the water, where the moisture lets them thrive. Night elf healers and herbalists prize Moonpetal Lilies for their healing properties. Mixed with forest plants such as Hyacinth Mushrooms, the lilies help soothe and stabilize. Healers brew antidotes from them for deadly toxins, including the venom of Webwood spiders in Shadowthread Cave.

item:moonstalker-fang.text: Moonstalker Fang. Near Auberdine, travelers collect Moonstalker Fang for Wizbang Cranktoggle's sampling devices. The teeth come from Darkshore's moonstalkers. Moonstalker Fangs come from saber cats that hunt along Darkshore’s forest fringes. Their long teeth can shear flesh and bone. Wizbang Cranktoggle, an eccentric gnome tinkerer, puts them to another use. North of Auberdine near the bridge, Buzzbox 323 grinds the durable fangs to dust for his ecological surveys.

item:moonwell-water-tube.text: Moonwell Water Tube. In Auberdine, moonwell water carries purifying nature magic. The tube is used to test a mysterious red crystal among Darkshore’s eastern ridges. Water from Auberdine’s moonwell fills the tube. The sacred pool is tied to Elune and holds restorative, purifying magic. Even a little can be used against corruption or to test strange mystical forces.

item:mossy-tumor.text: Mossy Tumor. Around Wellspring Lake, mossy tumors spread through Teldrassil's timberlings. Cut from their bark and flesh, these poisonous growths show the corruption taking hold in the young World Tree. Teldrassil's timberlings once tended the great tree's boughs. Many are now hostile and diseased, and their mossy tumors make that sickness plain. Thick with toxins, the growths spread across Mire Beasts, Tramplers, and Elder Timberlings around Wellspring Lake. Rellian Greenspyre and the keepers in Darnassus send travelers to cut them away and burn them thoroughly. Their poison must not take deeper root in the island's soil.

item:mountain-lion-blood.text: Mountain Lion Blood. In Hillsbrad and Alterac, Apothecary Lydon seeks Mountain Lion Blood. At Tarren Mill, he needs fresh blood for the Royal Apothecary Society’s Elixir of Pain. Mountain lions hunt across the highlands and foothills of Hillsbrad and Alterac. Hunters prize their pelts and claws, while Forsaken of the Royal Apothecary Society seek the blood in their veins. Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill believes fresh mountain lion blood can form the base of a potent brew. He means it to bring misery to the living. Apothecary Lydon’s work in Tarren Mill supports the Royal Apothecary Society’s effort to perfect the Forsaken’s New Plague. He gathers blood from vigorous wild beasts to refine a concoction called the Elixir of Pain. His experiments test how local organic compounds can be turned against the enemies of the Dark Lady.

item:muddy-journal-pages.text: Muddy Journal Pages. Muddy Journal Pages were recovered from a murder scene in Duskwood years ago. Weathered and stained with soil, they remain with Tavernkeep Smitts, who kept them without proof of authorship as evidence in an unresolved local investigation.

item:mudsnout-blossom.text: Mudsnout Blossom. In Nethander Stead, Mudsnout Blossom spores and flesh poison the living. Mudsnout gnolls guard the mushrooms, and Apothecary Lydon seeks them for his elixir research. South of Tarren Mill, Mudsnout Blossoms grow in Nethander Stead. Their name suggests flowers, but they are large, foul-smelling mushrooms. They thrive in soiled dirt among the Mudsnout gnolls' camps, and the gnolls defend that ground fiercely. Their spores and flesh poison living things, bringing agony and rapid bodily decay.

item:mudsnout-composite.text: Mudsnout Composite. At Tarren Mill, Mudsnout Composite is bound for research into a new plague. Apothecary Lydon makes it from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered in the Hillsbrad Foothills, then sends it to the Undercity. Apothecary Lydon makes Mudsnout Composite from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The paste is noxious on its own. Master Apothecary Faranell binds it with a colloid of decay, bringing forth its deadlier qualities. Together, the ingredients form a key chemical component in the Dark Lady's Elixir of Agony.

item:mudsnout-mixture.text:
Mudsnout Mixture. In the Undercity, Master Apothecary Faranell prepares a base for a deadly Forsaken poison. Mushrooms sent north from Tarren Mill begin the mixture. Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill seeks to craft a virulent new biological weapon. He sends a composite of Mudsnout Blossoms north to the Undercity. The toxic mushrooms grow at Nethander Stead, held by gnolls.

Master Apothecary Faranell sees promise in the composite and adds his colloid of decay. The resulting Mudsnout Mixture is volatile. It steadies the mushroom compound and prepares its virulent properties for further catalytic refinement in the foothills.

item:murloc-head.text:
Murloc Head. Along the Western Strand, Murloc Head gives Southshore grim proof of a threat it wants controlled. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle gathers the severed heads for Marshal Redpath, who demands evidence that the murlocs are being culled. Aggressive murlocs threaten Southshore's fishermen and travelers on the Western Strand. Alliance fighters often clear the beaches, but Marshal Marcus Redpath wants proof before approving reports that the threat has been reduced.

So Lieutenant Farren Orinelle hires fighters to bring him murloc heads. Farren finds the work repulsive, and the sight has spoiled his appetite for Southshore's seafood.

item:musquash-root.text: Musquash Root. Beneath the Stonewrought Dam, Musquash Root grows in the Wetlands. Few gather it, though a hidden coven beneath Stormwind needs it for a brew. Musquash Root grows in the damp ground beneath the Stonewrought Dam's falls. Mist and seclusion make it hard to gather. Few herbalists seek it, but practitioners of the darker arts prize its chemical and alchemical properties.

item:mysterious-fossil.text: Mysterious Fossil. Along Darkshore's coast, Prospector Remtravel uncovers the Mysterious Fossil. The Explorers' League sends it across the sea for study. Prospector Remtravel uncovers an unusual fossil along Darkshore's wild coast. He arranges for dwarven scholars to receive it rather than leave it in the wilderness. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sees an extraordinary find among the stones of Kalimdor.

item:nak-s-skull.text:
Nak's Skull. Nak's Skull carries weight in the southern Barrens, where Razormane raids trouble the Horde. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth seeks vengeance on the kin who left him to die. Nak, Kuz, and Lok Orcbane lead raids from Razorfen Kraul across the Barrens. Their warbands strike Horde settlements and roads, while Crossroads defenders know nothing of plans beyond ordinary tribal skirmishing.

At Camp Taurajo, the captive Razormane Mangletooth was left to die in a cage by his own people. He now seeks revenge on those former brethren. He demands Nak's, Kuz's, and Lok Orcbane's severed skulls as proof they are dead, delivered by Horde adventurers. With that proof, he means to break the southern raiding parties.

item:nek-rosh-s-head.text: Nek'rosh's Head. In the Wetlands, Nek'rosh's Head reaches Captain Stoutfist as proof the Dragonmaw chieftain has fallen. Menethil Harbor's defenders can now see that the threat has been broken. Across the marshlands, the Dragonmaw clan gathers forces and siege weapons against the Alliance port of Menethil Harbor. After the clan's catapults burn, the port's defense depends on killing Chieftain Nek'rosh. His severed head gives Captain Stoutfist and the Ironforge authorities proof that the warlord's hold over the Wetlands is broken.

item:neru-fragment.text:
Neru Fragment. At Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands, the Neru Fragment preserves part of the Goaz Stone's ancient Titan script. Its words tell of Azeroth's primeval history. Prospector Whelgar led the dwarven expedition that found the Goaz Stone. The relic broke into four pieces: Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru. Then raptors overran the dig and halted the work. The Neru Fragment remained beneath loose soil among the aggressive beasts.

Once recovered, the fragment can join the others to restore the tablet. The surviving words speak of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy. Dwarven scholars have a record to decipher.

item:nessa-s-collection.text: Nessa's Collection. At Rut'theran Village, Nessa's Collection is bound for Laird in Auberdine, carrying proof of the great fish near Teldrassil's roots. Nessa Shadowsong lives in Rut'theran Village at Teldrassil's base. She gathered fish bones and scales to compare island sea life with mainland Kalimdor. Catches from the waters around the Great Tree grow to striking size. So Nessa sent proof across the sea to Laird, a fish merchant along Auberdine's docks. The parcel travels through Vesprystus, Rut'theran's hippogryph master, and shows Teldrassil's growing vitality. In Darkshore, Laird finds that these specimens far outsize their mainland counterparts. The collection holds jawbones nearly twice the size of those from fish native to the Darkshore coast. Its scales are as large as a clenched fist. For coastal night elves, the package shows how greatly Teldrassil's waters differ from northern Kalimdor's somber shores.

item:nether-gem.text: Nether Gem. Across Tirisfal Glades, the Nether Gem bears a mysterious figure from Brightwater Lake to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity. What joins them is yours to uncover.

item:ng-5.text: NG-5. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Gaxim Rustfizzle prepares a distraction with NG-5. The volatile chemical, Nitromirglyceronium, is the ignition compound he needs for wagons loaded with dynamite. Gaxim Rustfizzle is a gnome operative in the Stonetalon Mountains, and NG-5 is the compound he needs for his engineering plans. Its full name is Nitromirglyceronium. The hazardous solution provides the reaction to detonate wagons loaded with dynamite, making a great explosion to distract his adversaries in the region.

item:nida-s-necklace.text:
Hilary's Necklace. In Lakeshire, Hilary searches Lake Everstill for the necklace her father gave her. It slipped beneath the water while she and the other children fished by the docks. Hilary lost her necklace while fishing with her friend Shawn along the Lakeshire shore. Her father gave it to her, and she treasures his gift.

Fierce beasts and aggressive murlocs live in the lake's depths, so local children stay on the docks. Hilary's necklace lies beneath the water, buried in the lakebed silt.

item:nightmare-shard.text: Nightmare Shard. In the Wailing Caverns, Nightmare Shard carries a taint Falla Sagewind cannot ignore. She binds the Emerald Dream's pure, disturbed essence into it and sends it to senior druids with a warning meant for them alone. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, Falla Sagewind examines a glowing shard. Its energy is darker than she expected. It reflects an unnatural affliction in the Emerald Dream, like a waking nightmare. Falla binds this tainted essence into Nightmare Shard and orders it carried without delay to the elder leaders of the Cenarion Circle.

item:nightsaber-fang.text: Nightsaber Fang. In Teldrassil, hunters take fangs from nightsabers prowling the forest. Woodland residents seek the teeth as reagents. Beneath Teldrassil’s canopy, nightsabers hunt as some of northern Kalimdor’s deadliest natural predators. Night elves revere them for their agility, ferocity, and deep spiritual bond with Elune. A hunter who kills one may take its sharp fangs as proof of skill. Yet some figures in the forest seek those fangs for darker rites.

item:nissa-s-remains.text: Nissa's Remains. In northern Tirisfal, Nissa's remains belong to a noblewoman of the once-wealthy Agamand family. The Scourge slew her and her kin during the Third War, then bound them as mindless servants. Now former laborers hunt the family for vengeance. Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest and most influential family. Their prosperous mills stood across the northern hills. When the Plague of Undeath spread through Lordaeron, the patriarchs refused to flee. They fortified their estates and persuaded their retainers and laborers to stay and fight. Their pride cost them their lives. The Scourge slew the Agamands and raised them as mindless thralls bound to the Lich King's will. In Brill, survivors who later broke free under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner still remember the Agamands' fatal pride. Coleman Farthing once labored in their mills, and resents his former masters for luring the workers into undeath. He sends adventurers to put down the risen Agamands and retrieve their physical remains, including Nissa's. For Farthing and other Forsaken, destroying these relics brings a grim sense of closure and revenge.

item:nitroglycerin.text: Nitroglycerin. At Bael Modan, Nitroglycerin lets dwarves press their excavation into tauren lands. Soldiers and officers carry the volatile chemical, which can also be turned against the fortress. At Bael Modan, dwarves dig into the ancestral lands of the Stonespire tauren. Heavy drillers and volatile chemicals help them drive the excavation forward. At the site and its fortified keep, they use nitroglycerin to blast deep holes and break apart hills. Soldiers and officers carry vials as the work continues, among them Lord Cyrik Blackforge.

item:nondescript-letter.text: Nondescript Letter. Calvin Montague sends a Nondescript Letter from Deathknell to Innkeeper Renee in Brill. He asks newly awakened Forsaken to carry it east, giving them reason to leave the valley for the Gallows' End Tavern. Near Deathknell, Calvin Montague asks newly arisen Forsaken to carry an unmarked envelope east to Brill. He says he is weary from fighting zombies and spiders, and that the letter is for Innkeeper Renee. His promise of rich compensation rings hollow. The errand leads travelers out of the valley toward the Gallows' End Tavern.

item:nori-s-mug.text: Nori's Mug. In Dun Morogh, Nori Pridedrift sends a mug of mornbrew to Anvilmar. Travelers bring the drink to Durnan Furcutter, then return the empty mug to its owner. Nori Pridedrift lends his mug for a delivery through Dun Morogh's freezing passes. It carries hot mornbrew to Durnan Furcutter in Anvilmar, where the drink comforts him against the bitter cold. After Durnan drains it, the mug returns to Nori. He reminds travelers that mugs do not grow on trees and expects his sturdy drinking vessel back.

item:notched-rib.text: Notched Rib. At Agamand Mills, the Forsaken are breaking the Scourge's hold on Tirisfal. Across northern Tirisfal Glades, the Scourge gathers skeletons in ruined armor. Cracked Skull Soldiers and Rattlecage Soldiers attack every living being and every creature with free will they meet. Their brittle bones bear the pits and scores of battle. Deathguards need proof that Forsaken scouts and volunteers are killing these mindless intruders. Each notched rib marks another of the Lich King's thralls shattered. Northwest of Brill, the Agamand Mills hold a key position. Should the Scourge settle among the ruined farmsteads and windmills, the undead could strike deep into Tirisfal from that base. Deathguard Dillinger watches the northern roads and sends champions to break up the skeleton ranks before they gather strength. The ribs brought back to Brill show that the Forsaken line holds as it wears down the Scourge vanguard bone by bone.

item:nugget-slug.text: Nugget Slug. Tool buckets at the Sludge Fen hold nugget slugs the Venture Company uses in its heavy equipment. Tinkerers seek the seventeen-point-five-gauge fasteners for work on volatile machinery. At the Venture Company’s extraction sites, nugget slugs fasten heavy equipment. They are made for demanding industrial assemblies and sized at seventeen-point-five gauge. Ordinary trade brings them little use. Yet tinkerers need them for custom goblin hardware.

item:ogre-s-monocle.text: Ogre's Monocle. In southern Duskwood, Zzarc'Vul wears a monocle Viktori Prism'Antras needs for a telescope. Its lens has the size and curve to focus light through the stargazing instrument in Darkshire. Zzarc'Vul, an ogre, wears a monocle made for his massive stature. When Viktori Prism'Antras of Darkshire began building a stargazing instrument from the gnome engineer Cog's blueprints, ordinary lenses proved too small. Zzarc'Vul's eyewear is the only polished glass in the region with the size and curve to focus light through the finished telescope. At the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound in southern Duskwood, Zzarc'Vul lives among his brute brethren. He shows little wish to give up his distinctive accessory. You must defeat him on his own ground to claim the lens, then carry it back to Darkshire so Viktori can turn his gaze to the night skies.

item:okra.text: Okra. At Saldean's Farm, Okra helps feed Westfall's homesteaders. The crop grows in the farm's plots and thickens the stews that sustain them. Saldean's Farm still yields vegetables while much of Westfall lies fallow, threatened by Defias outlaws and rogue harvest golem attacks. Okra grows in the tilled plots around the farm and persists through the harsh conditions. It nourishes local homesteaders when trade and supplies from Stormwind run dry. Salma Saldean's famous Westfall Stew depends on okra. She combines sliced pods with whatever meat settlers can hunt across the dusty plains, including vulture flesh, goretusk snouts, and coastal murloc eyes. The pods break down in the heat, thickening thin broth into a filling, restorative meal. For settlers clinging to their homesteads, fresh okra turns sparse scavenging into a hot supper.

item:ordanus-head.text:
Ordanus' Head. At Raynewood Retreat, Ordanus' Head is sought as proof that Keeper Ordanus has fallen. Braelyn Firehand, a blood elf magus, seeks it in Ashenvale. Keeper Ordanus was an ancient keeper of the grove and one of Cenarius's elder sons. His druids stifled magic at the peak of Stonetalon Mountains, and Braelyn Firehand climbed those heights on her master's orders. She meant to end their hold and take vengeance on Ordanus. Before she could strike, the keeper was spirited away to the heart of Ashenvale.

Braelyn used arcane scrying to peer through the forest canopy and found Ordanus's sanctuary in the boughs of Raynewood Retreat. There she demanded his severed head as proof that the wild demigod's arrogance had been answered.

item:orendil-s-cure.text:
Orendil's Cure. In northern Ashenvale, Orendil Broadleaf brews a draught for a sick child in Astranaar. Rare Bathran's Hair gives Pelturas Whitemoon hope for his daughter, Relara. Relara Whitemoon fell deathly ill while still young, and ordinary remedies failed her in Astranaar. Her father, Pelturas Whitemoon, sought help from Orendil Broadleaf, a hermit who lives in northern Ashenvale and masters natural medicine.

Orendil gathered bundles of rare Bathran's Hair from the haunted ruins of Bathran's Haunt and brewed a draught for Relara. When the vial arrives, Pelturas has hope. Yet the cure only slows the disease, so he must seek the further remedies Orendil suggested.

item:oslow-s-toolbox.text:
Oslow's Toolbox. Beneath Lake Everstill, Oslow's tools lie where Blackrock orcs sank the boat carrying them from Goldshire. Foreman Oslow needs construction tools to keep Lakeshire's defenses and buildings in repair. Blackrock orcs besiege the Redridge Mountains, and the bridge into town lies destroyed. So the shipment from Goldshire crossed Lake Everstill by rowboat.

Blackrock forces struck the vessel with a catapult. The boat and Oslow's heavy chest sank into the depths among the murlocs.

item:osric-s-crate.text: Osric's Crate. At Sentinel Hill, Osric's Crate brings fresh armor from Stormwind to the People's Militia. The defenders face the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls without the Stormwind army. Quartermaster Lewis receives the shipment and shares the protective gear among the volunteer fighters. The crown gives the People's Militia no formal support. These freshly made suits are meant to help the volunteers hold their position. From Dungar Longdrink's roost in Stormwind's Trade District, a gryphon carries the crate to Thor at Sentinel Hill. The flight avoids dangerous roads through Elwynn Forest and across the Westfall border, where bandits may ambush travelers. Gryphons help keep frontier garrisons supplied during wartime.

item:package-of-empty-ooze-containers.text: Package of Empty Ooze Containers. In Ironforge, a package of empty ooze containers is bound for dangerous sampling in Felwood. Laris Geardawdle supplies jars that can hold tainted and cursed ooze without dissolving. Laris Geardawdle sends a dozen empty jars with travelers bound for Felwood. Six are for cursed ooze and six for tainted ooze. Raw specimens are caustic, and ordinary luggage can be eaten away by them. Sturdy, sealed glass keeps the acidic residue contained on the journey across continents to Laris's workbench in Ironforge. Laris Geardawdle's interest in ooze reaches beyond an eccentric hobby. He has seen Forsaken researchers from the Royal Apothecary Society harvesting these strange organisms across Azeroth, and wonders what they know. He suspects slimes may be primordial secretions tied to the world's creation. Field agents gather evidence in his jars, which he hopes will win him acclaim within the Explorers' League.

item:painted-gnoll-armband.text: Painted Gnoll Armband. At Westbrook Garrison, Painted Gnoll Armbands prove Riverpaw gnolls have been slain. Their packs press against Elwynn Forest's western border. Riverpaw warriors and scavengers wear rough bands marked with crude tribal patterns. These armbands come from Riverpaw gnolls along Elwynn Forest's wilderness borders. Stormwind's defenders face a growing threat near Stone Cairn Lake and in the woods south of Westbrook Garrison. Stormwind's Army is stretched thin across the kingdom, leaving Westbrook Garrison hard pressed to guard the western border. Deputy Rainer offers a standing bounty for slaying Riverpaw Outrunners and Riverpaw Runts. The painted bands let the deputies tally bounties and thin the packs near nearby farmlands.

item:panther-cage-key.text: Panther Cage Key. At Whitereach Post, Wizlo Bearingshiner guards the Panther Cage Key. It opens the cage left among the wrecked wagons of an ambushed caravan in Thousand Needles. Wizlo Bearingshiner is a goblin tinker who barely escaped a centaur attack on his caravan north of Whitereach Post. The raiders ransacked the wagons and cargo, yet left a sturdy cage untouched. A rare, ferocious panther waits inside. Around its neck hangs Wizlo’s prized invention, a hypercapacitor gizmo. The snarling beast kept the centaur at a distance, and only Wizlo’s key can open the cage and recover the device.

item:parker-s-lunch.text: Parker's Lunch. In Lakeshire, Darcy packs Parker's Lunch for Guard Parker's patrol. The meal offers a glimpse of the bonds and modest comforts among Redridge's defenders. Darcy works as a waitress at the Lakeshire inn, where she packs a meal for Guard Parker. He patrols the exposed road south toward Duskwood as Redridge faces attacks from gnolls and Blackrock orcs. The garrison is stretched thin and cut off from Stormwind's aid, so its guards keep long, lonely watches. Darcy's small gesture feeds Parker and begins a bashful courtship between them.

item:partially-filled-vessel.text: Partially Filled Vessel. In Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip gives young night elf initiates the Partially Filled Vessel. It carries blessed moonwell water from Shadowglen toward Dolanaar. Young kaldorei initiates gather blessed water from Shadowglen’s secluded moonwell. In Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip pours a sample into the vessel for its journey across Teldrassil. More water from the tree’s moonwells is needed to tend the island’s health. Carry the vessel south through the valley gates, then follow the cobblestone roads west to Dolanaar. The journey leads beyond Shadowglen’s protected nursery and into Teldrassil’s wider wilds. At the central moonwell in Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage takes the vessel and directs the next part of the ritual.

item:pendant-of-shadow.text: Pendant of Shadow. At the Tower of Ilgalar, Morganth bears the Pendant of Shadow while seeking the Scythe of Elune. Theocritus wants it brought to the Tower of Azora as proof Morganth has been slain.

item:pendant-of-the-sea-lion.text: Pendant of the Sea Lion. At the Shrine of Remulos, druids join the Pendant of the Sea Lion's two halves. The finished talisman shows an initiate is ready to learn an aquatic form. A druid must face the dangers of the water to claim the sea lion's aquatic aspect. The pendant has two halves. One grants the agility to slip past aquatic predators, while the other gives the endurance to withstand prolonged submersion. At the Shrine of Remulos in Moonglade, druids join the pieces. Once the pendant is forged, an initiate brings it to an elder mentor. Turak Runetotem waits on the rises of Thunder Bluff, while Mathrengyl Bearwalker is in Darnassus. The talisman proves the initiate completed trials under Dendrite Starblaze. Then the elder can teach the secrets of taking an aquatic form.

item:perenolde-tiara.text: Perenolde Tiara. In the ruins of Alterac, the Perenolde Tiara has surfaced again. Dwarven craftsmen of Ironforge made the emerald-studded heirloom, and collectors in Stormwind seek it. The Perenolde family ruled Alterac until the kingdom fell during the Second War. Among their treasures was a delicate tiara, made by master jewelers in Ironforge and set with brilliant emeralds. After King Aiden Perenolde’s treachery brought Alterac to ruin, the tiara vanished amid the devastation of the high crags. Grel'borg the Miser, an ogre mage, unearthed the tiara while searching Alterac’s ruins for abandoned wealth. Word of the relic reached Count Remington Ridgewell, a wealthy noble in Stormwind who collects famous relics for his family museum. Now the count seeks to take the tiara from the ogre.

item:phial-of-scrying.text: Phial of Scrying. Across Darkshore, scouts reach Onu from perilous ground. Onu provides the Phial of Scrying, whose enchanted waters form a bowl for divination across the corrupted woodlands. Scouts deep in Darkshore use the Phial of Scrying for long-distance divination. Its mystical waters form a temporary bowl on the ground. From perilous places such as the Master's Glaive, they can speak with Onu without returning to his grove.

item:piece-of-krom-zar-s-banner.text: Piece of Krom'zar's Banner. At Regthar Deathgate's bunker west of the Crossroads, a torn banner marks the failed assault. Warlord Krom'zar led the Kolkar retaliatory force east from Desolace. Warlord Krom'zar led his warband east from Desolace to strike back. Kolkar chieftains across the Barrens had fallen, and the enraged centaurs attacked the defensive bunkers west of the Crossroads. A strip cut from Krom'zar's fallen standard proves to Regthar Deathgate that the assault was crushed and the southern trade routes were preserved for the Horde.

item:plainstrider-beak.text: Plainstrider Beak. Across the Barrens, hunters bring Plainstrider Beaks to the Crossroads as proof that threatening birds have been culled. Plainstriders forage near the Crossroads and threaten its supplies. Greater, fleeting, and ornery plainstriders roam the surrounding savannah. Sergra Darkthorn asks arriving hunters to bring back their beaks, proof that the flocks have been driven from supply lines and storehouses.

item:plainstrider-feather.text:
Plainstrider Feather. On Red Cloud Mesa, young hunters gather Plainstrider Feather from the birds roaming Mulgore’s plains. Camp Narache makes clothing and tribal adornments from the feathers, honoring the creatures that provide for the village. Young tauren on Red Cloud Mesa learn to track and hunt for what their tribe needs. Plainstriders roam the grassy plateau and provide food and useful feathers. Camp Narache makes garments and gear from their plumage.

Young hunters bring feathers and fresh meat to Grull Hawkwind to supply the camp. This offering is their first test. Chief Hawkwind recognizes them and welcomes them in Thunder Bluff.

item:plainstrider-kidney.text:
Plainstrider Kidney. Across the Barrens, hunters gather Plainstrider Kidney for Kalimdor’s unusual brewing traditions. Most travelers find the organ unappetizing, but it is essential to an exotic ale. Tall, flightless plainstriders roam the Barrens, and hunters take their feathers and meat for tools and simple rations. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet seeks their kidneys for a different purpose: he says they are needed to recreate Chen Stormstout’s legendary potent ale.

Drohn says the kidneys give the brew a unique kick. The recipe belongs to an unconventional line of brewmasters, passed down through the years.

item:plainstrider-meat.text: Plainstrider Meat. Across Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren gather Plainstrider Meat to help feed Camp Narache. Hunting the birds for food and feathers proves their skill and self-reliance. Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa relies on game from the surrounding grasslands. When food stocks run low, plainstrider meat helps feed the village. The birds also provide feathers for clothing and ceremonial adornments. Tauren depend on the land and take what they need while respecting nature. Grull Hawkwind sends young hunters across Red Cloud Mesa to track swift plainstriders. They gather meat and feathers to prove their tracking skill and self-reliance. Then they appear before Grull's father, Chief Hawkwind.

item:plainstrider-scale.text: Plainstrider Scale. In Mulgore, Maur Raincaller needs a Plainstrider Scale for a remedy in Bloodhoof Village. The tough scale helps counter a spreading infection. Plainstriders roam Mulgore with tough scales over their powerful legs. The scales protect them, though only some are firm enough to grind for folk remedies.

item:plainstrider-talon.text:
Plainstrider Talon. Across Mulgore, tauren shamans gather Plainstrider Talon to cleanse totems. The sharp claws come from large, flightless plainstriders native to the region and help cleanse corrupted water. Large, flightless plainstriders roam Mulgore’s open grasses. Their powerful legs and sharp claws help them forage through tough prairie earth and defend against predators. To the tauren of Bloodhoof Village, every part of a hunted beast carries spiritual meaning.

When goblin ventures tainted sacred sources such as the Winterhoof Water Well, shaman Mull Thunderhorn sought plainstrider talons and prairie wolf paws. In tauren ritual crafting, parts from native predators and foragers channel the land’s spiritual essence into totems that purge unnatural poisons.

item:podrig-s-order.text: Podrig's Order. In Silverpine, Podrig's Order asks the Undercity for weapons to arm the Sepulcher. Deathguard Podrig found the Sepulcher's stores mostly adequate after Executor Hadrec ordered an inventory. Yet replacement weapons were running desperately low. His dispatch names the blades and arms needed by the Deathguards holding the outpost in Silverpine Forest. The Scourge, feral beasts, and other dangers threaten the frontier. The order is addressed to Gordon Wendham, a weapon dealer in the Undercity's Trade Quarter. Silverpine's damp crypts make forging weapons difficult. Couriers take the document to bat master Karos Razok, so Forsaken flight paths can speed the shipment from the capital.

item:pork-belly-pie.text: Pork Belly Pie. In Elwynn Forest, Billy Maclure waits for a pie from Stonefield Farm before he speaks of a missing necklace. Auntie Bernice bakes it despite the families’ long feud. The Stonefield and Maclure families have quarreled over land and pride for years. Young Billy Maclure has a weakness for Auntie Bernice’s pork belly pie. When a valuable Stonefield family necklace goes missing, Billy refuses to share what he knows until an adventurer brings him a warm slice. Bernice bakes it reluctantly, wishing the greedy boy would choke on it.

item:powdered-azurite.text: Powdered Azurite. In Hillsbrad Foothills, workers grind blue stone from Azurelode Mine into Powdered Azurite. Thun'grim Firegaze needs it to forge brutal armor for rising Horde warriors. Human workers dig blue stone from mineral veins beneath Hillsbrad Foothills. They grind and pack it for trade and metalworking. A skilled smith mixes the dust with dense metals, making armor more durable and resilient. Horde blacksmiths prize Powdered Azurite for its strength in metalworking, though the mineral comes from human-held tunnels across the Great Sea. Thun'grim Firegaze is an aging orc armorer in the Barrens. He asks for small amounts alongside refined iron and fiery reagents. Mixed into the smelt, the powder helps him hammer out the heavy plating of his Brutal Armor.

item:powers-of-the-void.text: Powers of the Void. In Northshire, a stolen tome draws Drusilla La Salle's attention. A novice took Powers of the Void from a guarded wing of Northshire Abbey's library while leaving to join the Defias Brotherhood. Drusilla seeks the book for her own study of dark magic. Powers of the Void was kept behind guarded shelves in Northshire Abbey's library. The abbey archives hold holy scripture and clerical records, as well as scholarly works on shadow and nether energies. The archmage Khadgar is believed to have penned the tome. Its subject was dangerous, so abbey authorities kept it under guard and away from casual visitors. That kept Drusilla La Salle, Northshire's warlock mentor, from browsing it without drawing the priesthood's suspicion. A Northshire novice carried the tome away when he abandoned his vows to join the Defias Brotherhood. As he fled into the neighboring vineyards, he took several valuable volumes from the abbey. Drusilla sends promising warlock initiates to the Defias bandit camp to recover the book from their tents. She wants its dark knowledge for her own study. The effort tests whether an initiate has the nerve to bind otherworldly demons.

item:prairie-alpha-tooth.text: Prairie Alpha Tooth. Near Thunder Bluff, prairie wolf alphas roam Mulgore’s open plains. Mull Thunderhorn needs their teeth to cleanse the Wildmane Well. Mulgore’s wells sustain the tauren, and rites of respect and sacrifice keep them pure. Mull Thunderhorn of Bloodhoof Village needs teeth from the prairie wolf alphas beneath Thunder Bluff to cleanse the Wildmane Well. These fierce pack leaders embody the wild’s strength. Their teeth honor the balance between hunter, prey, and the spirits of the earth.

item:prairie-wolf-heart.text: Prairie Wolf Heart. Maur Raincaller in Bloodhoof Village needs a Prairie Wolf Heart to treat a venomous bite. Maur Raincaller lives in Bloodhoof Village, where venom from Mazzranache, the legendary plainstrider, has left him feverish. The bite threatens to spread poison through him. Maur seeks a prairie wolf heart, cougar bone, and bird gizzard for a traditional plains remedy. He hopes to stop the infection before delirium proves fatal.

item:prairie-wolf-paw.text: Prairie Wolf Paw. Across Mulgore, prairie wolves hunt the plains, and their paws are gathered for a shaman's work. In Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn joins them with plainstrider talons to make a cleansing totem. Prairie wolves hunt in packs across Mulgore’s grasses, alongside prairie stalkers and their pack alphas. They threaten young hunters and local livestock. Tauren shamans regard the paws as more than trophies, for they carry the land’s natural vitality and matter to the plains’ spiritual balance. When goblin ventures tainted Mulgore’s sacred water reserves, shaman Mull Thunderhorn needed the land’s aid against the pollution. Joined with plainstrider talons, wolf paws lend spiritual resonance to cleansing totems. Once the totem is made, the work of purifying the Winterhoof Water Well can begin.

item:pridewing-venom-sac.text: Pridewing Venom Sac. Around Mirkfallon Lake, pridewing venom draws the attention of Astranaar’s night elves. Reports say Horde agents gather it for covert attacks, and the Sentinels seek to deny them that poison. Pridewings hunt the crags south of Ashenvale, especially near Mirkfallon Lake. Though native to the Stonetalon Mountains, these flying predators range here, and their venom lies in glands within their bodies. Reports from Theramore say Horde assassins use the poison to coat blades for secret strikes on night elf settlements. So Astranaar’s Sentinels send scouts to hunt the wyverns and collect their glands before Horde agents can claim them.

item:prismatic-punch-card.text:
Prismatic Punch Card. In Gnomeregan, the Prismatic Punch Card bears the highest security clearance. Gnome refugees in Ironforge seek the records it unlocks. When the gnomes fled Gnomeregan, troggs and toxic irradiation drove them from the city. Vast stores of research and civic records remained in its depths. The gnomes guarded high-level systems behind tiers of clearance. To reach the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D in the lower Engineering Labs, a card must pass through a series of terminals.

The card begins white, then advances through yellow, blue, and red. At the final terminal, it is stamped Prismatic. Its encoded clearance is listed as awaiting the invention of an entirely new number.

item:pristine-spider-silk.text: Pristine Spider Silk. In Duskwood, venomous spiders yield the fine thread Stormwind mages need for robes that endure enchantments. Stormwind mages need silk strong enough to bear enchantments and an adept’s wear. Tailors use common spider silk, but strands from carrion recluses and black widow hatchlings in Duskwood are more resilient. Mages from the Wizard’s Sanctum send rising adepts into those woods to gather it. Master tailor Wynne Larson then weaves the silk into a robe for an adept.

item:prowler-claws.text: Prowler Claws. Across the Barrens, Prowler Claws return to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. They prove a hunter can track and defeat the prowlers stalking the plains. Savannah Prowlers wait in the Barrens’ tall grass, ready to strike with patience and cunning. Unlike grazing plainstriders and zhevra, these large cats ambush creatures that enter their hunting grounds. Taking their curved claws means facing predators that rely on stealth and defend their territory. For Horde warriors and scouts, the hunt tests whether they can track a stalker across its own ground and make it the prey. Sergra Darkthorn, the huntress at the Crossroads, asks initiates to bring her Prowler Claws before they face greater trials. The claws prove a hunter can follow tracks through savannah grass and withstand a predator’s attack. Those who return with them have shown they can stay alert among the plains’ dangerous beasts.

item:pure-hearts.text:
Pure Hearts. In the Undercity, Pure Hearts draw a succubus from the Twisting Nether. Carendin Halgar gives these ritual reagents to Forsaken warlocks, who use them to call the demon forth and try to defeat and bind her. Carendin Halgar gives Pure Hearts to warlocks who summon a succubus in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. They set the untainted spiritual essences on the summoning circle. The hearts lure the demon across the Twisting Nether and into the mortal realm.

Once she appears, the warlock must resist her enthralling mind-charms and strike her down. Defeating the succubus proves mystical dominance and sends her back to the Twisting Nether. Then Carendin teaches the warlock the spell to summon her at will.

item:purified-kor-gem.text: Purified Kor Gem. At Jordan Stilwell’s forge outside Ironforge, a Purified Kor Gem is needed to shape a weapon of the Light. First, elven magic must cleanse the corrupted stone. Naga hold the Corrupted Kor Gem in Blackfathom Deeps, beneath Ashenvale’s coast. A paladin carries it to Thundris Windweaver, a night elf in Auberdine. There, Thundris draws on arcane and natural arts to purge its aquatic and shadowy taint. The stone emerges purified, ready to channel holy power. Jordan Stilwell, a human weaponsmith outside Ironforge, needs the gem for a masterwork weapon. He has long held designs for a weapon worthy of the Silver Hand, but lacked the rare materials to forge it. The Purified Kor Gem, Whitestone Oak Lumber, and rare ore give the weapon its spiritual core, to channel a paladin’s righteous wrath.

item:putrid-claw.text: Putrid Claw. Near Brill, Putrid Claw bounties help hold back the Scourge. Mindless undead roam the woods west of town, especially near the old bridge, and Deathguard Dillinger receives the claws as proof. The mindless Scourge keeps crossing into Tirisfal Glades. Rotting dead and ravaged corpses wander the eastern borders, gathering along roads and near the old bridge west of Brill. Deathguards offer bounties on these horrors to protect travelers and garrison supply lines. A severed putrid claw proves one more shambling corpse has been put down for good.

item:pyrewood-shackle.text: Pyrewood Shackle. At Pyrewood Village, enchanted shackles bind its people to Archmage Arugal's strange magic. When night falls, the townsfolk face a dark fate.

item:quinn-s-potion.text:
Quinn's Potion. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel prepares Quinn's Potion for an injured scout. Quinn Yorick needs it after a disastrous patrol in Silverpine Forest. Apothecary Renferrel brews a remedy for Deathstalker Quinn Yorick. Word reached the Royal Apothecary Society at the Sepulcher after Quinn was badly hurt near the Ivar Patch and could no longer move. Renferrel made the draught to help him recover.

Minor field casualties rarely draw Renferrel from his darker research for Lady Sylvanas. Still, he supplied the remedy so Quinn could regain enough strength to travel.

item:ran-bloodtooth-s-skull.text: Ran Bloodtooth's Skull. In Ashenvale, Ran Bloodtooth's Skull reaches the night elves of Astranaar as proof that a fierce threat has fallen. Demonic taint and wilderness corruption have driven Ashenvale's furbolgs into murderous madness. Ran Bloodtooth led one of the fiercest tribes. His skull proves to the night elf Sentinels that he has fallen and his hold over the local furbolgs is broken. Astranaar gains some respite.

item:raptor-head.text: Raptor Head. At the Crossroads, Raptor Head trophies answer Gazrog’s bounty. Guard payroll vanished from a watchtower, and a wild raptor was caught in the theft. A chest of guard payroll was stolen from the Crossroads watchtower, leaving its defenders without their silver. To their disbelief, they caught a wild raptor in the act. Gazrog now offers a bounty on the cunning reptiles prowling the Barrens. Bring their severed heads to the outpost, and the predators can be culled before they steal more Horde supplies.

item:rare-earth.text: Rare Earth. At Dolanaar, Rare Earth awaits a traveler bound for Denalan's camp near Lake Al'Ameth. The soil came from Darnassus for his botanical experiments on Teldrassil. Rare Earth has arrived late in Dolanaar from Darnassus. Denalan, an eccentric botanist on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern shore, requested it to study plants in Teldrassil's young ecosystem. Herbalist Syral Bladeleaf now entrusts the soil to travelers heading south. She hopes it reaches Denalan before its potency fades.

item:rattlecage-skull.text: Rattlecage Skull. In Deathknell, novice Forsaken warlocks gather skulls from mindless undead. Venya Marthand sets this trial before teaching them the dark arts of summoning. In Deathknell, Venya Marthand guides newly raised Forsaken gifted in dark magic. She sends them to subdue Rattlecage Skeletons near the ruined smithy and bring back their skulls. The trial tests whether a young warlock can bend creatures from beyond this world to their command. It prepares them to breach the void and bind their first demonic servant.

item:raven-claw-talisman.text: Raven Claw Talisman. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Raven Claw Talisman waits among relics meant to wake sleeping druids.
