It is one of four Relics of Wakening, used to guide the Druids of the Talon safely back from the Emerald Dream. The Raven Claw Talisman rests in a chest inside Ban'ethil Barrow Den. There, Teldrassil's Druids of the Talon entered a deep meditative sleep. Without the proper ceremonial focus, a druid cut off from the waking world may remain stranded in the Emerald Dream. Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar needs this talisman and three other relics to bring the sleepers back safely: the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The sacred chests and sleeping druids are now in peril. Their desecration has cut the sanctuary off from outside aid, and the relics may be lost or destroyed. Athridas Bearmantle calls on Teldrassil's defenders to brave the den's winding earthen corridors and secure the Raven Claw Talisman before the displaced druids are lost to the Dream forever.

item:razorflank-s-medallion.text:
Razorflank's Medallion. Deep within Razorfen Kraul, Charlga Razorflank carries the medallion that marks her rule. Its return gives the night elf sentinels proof that she has fallen. Charlga Razorflank leads the Razorfen quilboar and carries the medallion. At Thalanaar, Falfindel Waywarder hears of fallen explorers, including Heralath and the dwarf Lonebrow. He sends Alliance adventurers against the quilboar leader.

The medallion confirms Charlga's death to the night elf sentinels who guard Feralas's borders. The gathered forces within the Kraul have lost their leader.

item:reagent-pouch-shaman.text: Reagent Pouch (shaman). In Durotar, Burning Blade cultists carry reagents for a shaman's first fire sapta. Telf Joolam mixes them with fire tar from Razormane quilboar to make a draught that lets a young shaman see the realm of fire. Burning Blade cultists carry reagents for a young shaman's first fire sapta. The hermit Telf Joolam mixes the powders and oils from their pouches with fire tar from Razormane quilboar. Together, these ingredients make a draught that grants sight into the realm of fire and attunes the shaman to the spirits of flame. Burning Blade cultists turn flame toward destruction and fel sorcery. Yet the elements in their pouches still belong to heat and combustion. Shaman teach that elemental forces exist in tension: fire creates as well as destroys. A shaman can use the cultists' tools to awaken true communion with the spirits.

item:reconstructed-tome.text: Reconstructed Tome. In warlocks’ hands, the Reconstructed Tome gathers the cabal’s scattered teachings. Its pages hold rites for summoning and binding a felhunter from the Twisting Nether. Warlocks of the Alliance and Horde seek the torn leaves of the Tome of the Cabal. Once they have pieced the grimoire together, they consult occult scholars. The scholars are eager to glimpse its rare teachings before the finished book is surrendered.

item:recruitment-letter.text: Recruitment Letter. In Durotar, Takrin Pathseeker sends promising adventurers west to serve in the Barrens. His letter directs able-bodied volunteers to Kargal Battlescar's border outpost. Around Razor Hill, Takrin Pathseeker watches young warriors and scouts prove themselves. He chooses those strong enough for frontline service and gives them a letter for duty in the Barrens. Recruits cross the Southfury River bridge, leave Durotar’s sheltered red dirt, and join the Horde’s guard against quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts. Just across the river, Kargal Battlescar receives recruits at the outpost. The grizzled veteran manages the post and evaluates each conscript before signing off on their enlistment. Those he signs are soon sent farther west to the Crossroads, where frontier outposts are stretched thin.

item:red-burlap-bandana.text: Red Burlap Bandana. Near the abbey vineyards in Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem gathers red bandanas from slain Defias thieves. The cloth marks the Brotherhood's low-ranking highwaymen and cutpurses. In Northshire, young recruits and common thugs of the Defias Brotherhood wear red burlap masks. The cheap, rough cloth hides their faces and marks their allegiance to the growing rebellion. They carry these scarves into the eastern orchards, where local guards recognize the red fabric as proof of thieves slain nearby.

item:red-leather-bandana.text: Red Leather Bandana. In Westfall, the Red Leather Bandana marks those who defy Stormwind’s Crown. The Defias Brotherhood wears it to cover their faces and show their cause.

item:red-linen-bandana.text: Red Linen Bandana. Across Elwynn Forest, the red linen bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood and hides its wearers' faces. Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp wants the cloth for garments and bandages. In Northshire Valley, initiates and common thugs wear coarse burlap masks. The crimson linen marks the allegiance of full operatives to Edwin VanCleef's rogue fraternity. It also signals rebellion against Stormwind's crown. Sara Timberlain asks travelers to gather bandanas from outlaw encampments. The masks are tied to bandits, but their linen is respectable. Washed and worked with a needle, the cloth can become sturdy clothing and bandages for the forest's working folk.

item:red-wool-bandana.text: Red Wool Bandana. In the Stormwind Stockade, Red Wool Bandana scraps mark the Defias Brotherhood. Prisoners tear wool from their blankets and wear the red cloth as emblems of defiance. In the Stormwind Stockade, Defias Brotherhood inmates keep their identity alive. They secretly tear scraps from prison wool blankets and stitch them into red bandanas. Guards treat the scarves as contraband, and finding them can spark fatal mutinies. Each bandana declares that the brotherhood and its rebellion endure, even in chains. Red Wool Bandanas are tied to the death of Mac Raskol, a fourteen-year-old prison guard. He caught inmates shredding blankets for scarves and tried to discipline them. Defias convicts stabbed him in the back. His grieving grandmother, Nikova, now seeks adventurers to enter the rioting dungeon, cull the rioters, and bring back a crimson cloth as proof of vengeance.

item:remaining-drops-of-purest-water.text:
Remaining Drops of Purest Water. Across Kalimdor and Lordaeron, Remaining Drops of Purest Water wait for a perilous journey. Brine gathered the water for a draught meant to help shaman. In the Barrens, Brine prepares a draught from water gathered across Kalimdor and Lordaeron. Part of it gives shaman vision of distant elements. The drops left over have a harder purpose.

Shaman carry them to the coast of Silverpine Forest, near the Sepulcher, where the Brazier of Everfount stands. There, they burn the drops with the bracers of a fallen, tainted elemental. The pure water cuts through the undead plague’s corruption and calls an untainted water spirit to commune with the shaman. So their communion with the element is complete.

item:remedy-of-arugal.text: Remedy of Arugal. In Silverpine Forest, Dalar Dawnweaver seeks Arugal's spell to learn how his worgen magic works. Before he took Shadowfang Keep, Archmage Arugal sheltered at an abandoned wheat farm north of the river bridge in Silverpine Forest. Among farm tools and rotting floorboards, he left spellbooks that recorded his strange arts. One scroll, the Remedy of Arugal, describes early methods and magical formulas from his experiments with the transmutations that cursed the local people. At the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver is a Forsaken spellcaster who thinks little of Arugal's standing. He considers Arugal's intellect fragile and transparent. Still, Dawnweaver needs to understand how the worgen curse works. Recovering the Remedy gives Forsaken agents the arcane knowledge he seeks to counter Arugal's spreading menace and secure Silverpine for Lady Sylvanas.

item:rendered-spores.text: Rendered Spores. Across the Barrens, Rendered Spores are being hurried to Thunder Bluff before their emulsion decays. Apothecary Zamah must stabilize it beneath the city. Near the Barrens’ damp oases, Apothecary Helbrim gathers fungal spores and renders them into an active chemical emulsion. The mixture is unstable. After forty-five minutes, it breaks down and can no longer be studied. At his remote outpost, Apothecary Helbrim cannot finish refining the emulsion. It must reach his Forsaken colleague, Apothecary Zamah, beneath Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff. In the Pools of Vision, Zamah has the equipment and reagents to reseal and finish processing the spores for the Royal Apothecary Society.

item:renferrel-s-findings.text: Renferrel's Findings. In Silverpine Forest, Renferrel's Findings carry his research south to Tarren Mill. Apothecary Renferrel gathered the notes at the Sepulcher for Apothecary Lydon, who is helping brew the Forsaken's New Plague. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel records his work on the New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society answers directly to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Dark Lady. Researchers scattered across Lordaeron must join their work to find a breakthrough. So Renferrel sends his findings south to Tarren Mill, where fellow apothecaries can build on his results. Renferrel's papers link Silverpine Forest to Hillsbrad Foothills and the Forsaken's alchemical work. Apothecary Lydon awaits the notes in Tarren Mill, where he can compare them with his own research against the living and the Scourge. The roads through Hillsbrad are contested, so the Society depends on reliable couriers. Without them, its scattered research would soon stall.

item:report-on-the-defias-brotherhood.text:
Report on the Defias Brotherhood. At Stormwind Keep, the findings on the Defias Brotherhood reach the royal court. City Architect Baros Alexston entrusts the report to the adventurer who uncovered the conspiracy. City Architect Baros Alexston prepared the report for Stormwind's leaders after a long investigation into unrest in Westfall and nearby lands. He entrusted it to the adventurer who unraveled the conspiracy.

The report is carried to Stormwind Keep for a personal audience. There, the findings concern the conspirators' schemes and the danger they pose to the kingdom.

item:resonite-crystal.text: Resonite Crystal. In Boulderslide Cavern, kobolds dig frantically for Resonite Crystal. Their work has drawn Mor'rogal's concern at Sun Rock Retreat.

item:restabilization-cog.text:
Restabilization Cog. At Gnomeregan's gates, leper gnomes still carry Restabilization Cogs. In Kharanos, tinkerers need intact cogs for a machine meant to reverse leper mutation. Radiation flooded Gnomeregan in a failed attempt to wipe out the invading troggs. Countless gnomes fell sick and hostile, then fled their home as exiles. Even in their madness, they carry intricate gnomish machinery.

Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket believe the terrible change can be undone. Their prototype Recombobulation Device needs parts taken from the afflicted outside Gnomeregan's gates. Intact Restabilization Cogs will balance its inner combustion systems.

item:ring-of-zoram.text: Ring of Zoram. At Zoram, the ring worn by the city's rulers has surfaced again after millennia beneath the sea. The naga hold it, and Talen seeks the key to an ancient statuette. Before the Well of Eternity collapsed, Zoram stood on Kalimdor's western coast as a jewel of the night elven empire. Its rulers wore the Ring of Zoram, whose inner band bears a strange code in the night elven language. The Great Sundering shattered the continent ten thousand years ago. The ring sank with the city beneath the tides, and now lies beneath the waters of the Zoram Strand. For millennia, silt and ruins hid the ring. Then naga began scouring Ashenvale's coast, and Ruuzel, their leader on an islet off the northern strand, uncovered it among the sunken debris. The night elf scholar Talen seeks it for more than its age. The ring is the only key that can unlock relics salvaged from the depths, including ancient statuettes sealed on the sea floor.

item:robo-mechanical-guts.text:
Robo-Mechanical Guts. In Stormwind, Shoni gathers parts from Gnomeregan’s roaming machines. She needs them to repair tunneling vehicles built to help reclaim the city in Dun Morogh. After High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and the surviving gnomes fled Gnomeregan, thousands of machines remained behind. Automated mechanisms, clockwork sentries, and industrial robots still roam the radioactive city’s corridors.

In Stormwind City, tinker Shoni is assembling gyrodrillmatic excavationators to break through Gnomeregan’s defenses and reclaim the lost city. She sends adventurers into the contaminated halls to salvage working parts from the robots, including springs, wires, and gyro-components.

item:rocket-car-parts.text:
Rocket Car Parts. Across the Shimmering Flats, Rocket Car Parts lie scattered after mishaps at the Mirage Raceway. Gnome and goblin racers push their experimental speeders hard, and merchants gather wreckage to sell back to the teams. At the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats, gnome and goblin engineers compete fiercely. Their racers chase greater speed on land. Breakdowns, misfires, and crashes scatter metal across the salt flats, where scavengers and merchants soon gather what remains.

The dwarf Kravel Koalbeard hires travelers to search the bright expanse and collect the debris. Both racing teams need spare machinery for their next prototypes, so wreckage can return to the teams whose cars left it behind.

item:rod-of-channeling.text:
Rod of Channeling. In the Wetlands, Dragonmaw spellcasters carry the Rod of Channeling. Strahad Farsan needs three for his acolytes to steady a felhunter summoning circle in Ratchet. Warlocks need more than willpower to bind a felhunter. Strahad Farsan asks for three matched rods so his acolytes can channel magic together and steady the summoning circle as the warlock binds the beast. Dragonmaw darkcasters carry the rods for their own workings.

At Angerfang Encampment and in the surrounding Wetlands ruins, Dragonmaw Bonewarders and shadowwarders bear the rods. Combat leaves them worn and nicked, yet they still focus chaotic nether energy.

item:rolf-and-malakai-s-medallions.text: Rolf and Malakai's Medallions. In eastern Elwynn, Rolf and Malakai's Medallions bear the realm's insignia, though their owners vanished on patrol. Guard Thomas seeks the tokens to learn what became of his men. Guard Thomas commands the station in eastern Elwynn. When Rolf and Malakai vanished along the riverbanks, he feared the worst. Their medallions confirm the guards died at the hands of encroaching murlocs. The Stormwind garrison has lost soldiers who held the line against wilderness threats while the kingdom's military was stretched thin. Human guards carry identification medallions on city watch and rural patrols. The tokens show their allegiance and authority under the crown. Returning Rolf and Malakai's medallions to Guard Thomas lets him account for his missing men and record their sacrifice in his field report. He can also warn of aggressive murloc tribes settling near the trade roads.

item:rot-blossom.text: Rot Blossom. In Duskwood, Rot Blossoms rise from desecrated graves, fed by blighted soil and undead remains. Their foul alchemical properties make them sought after. In Duskwood, Rot Blossoms grow in defiled graveyard earth, including the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Local rumors say they take root inside the cracked skulls of Skeletal Horrors and Skeletal Fiends that stalk the barrows. Gathering them is grim work for people in Darkshire. Disturb the soil, and the unrested dead must be faced. Rot Blossoms provide an ingredient for local brews. Their dark essences are needed to make Zombie Juice, a foul draft tied to Duskwood's struggle to survive. Those sent to gather the flowers often aid the Night Watch by cutting down restless skeletons wandering the haunted graves.

item:rot-hide-ichor.text: Rot Hide Ichor. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel gathers Rot Hide Ichor for the Royal Apothecary Society. They hope it will show what corrupted the gnolls and how to oppose them. On Fenris Isle, the Rot Hide gnolls are twisted by an unnatural blight. Their bodies decay, yet a noxious ichor runs through their veins and sustains their animated flesh. The Royal Apothecary Society hopes the fluid will reveal what corrupted the pack and who commands them from within the ruined keep. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel gathers vials of the ichor for study. The Forsaken hope to separate the chemical and magical forces that sustain the gnolls. Then they can find the pack's weaknesses before sending troops across Lordamere Lake in a full assault.

item:rough-quartz.text:
Rough Quartz. In Durotar, a shaman receives Rough Quartz from a Minor Manifestation of Earth. An elder binds the stone into the shaman’s first Earth Totem. In Durotar or Mulgore, a Minor Manifestation of Earth gives Rough Quartz to a shaman who communes with the spirits. To an untrained eye, the stone looks like an ordinary desert pebble. It represents endurance, patience, and unwavering strength.

At the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller binds the quartz into carved wood to make an Earth Totem. The stone becomes the spiritual focus that joins a young shaman to Azeroth’s living soil.

item:rumbleshot-s-ammo.text:
Rumbleshot's Ammo. Near the Grizzled Den, Rumbleshot's Ammo lies abandoned in the snow. Its courier fled from hungry wendigos before the crate could reach gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot in Dun Morogh. Hegnar Rumbleshot keeps a roadside arms shop on the mountain path from Coldridge Pass toward Anvilmar. Ironforge riflemen, mountaineers, and dwarven mortar teams drill in the snowy heights, so his supplies run low as quickly as powder burns.

Loslor sent the shot from Kharanos, but the shipment never reached the shelves. Its courier camped too close to the Grizzled Den. When the wendigos attacked, the courier fled in panic and left the heavy crate in their hunting grounds.

item:rune-inscribed-parchment.text:
Rune-Inscribed Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives aspiring orc shamans a summons from Shikrik. It calls them to guide their people and commune with elemental spirits. New orc shamans train under veteran overseers in the Valley of Trials. During an initiate’s first trials, Gornek gives them a rune-covered message from Shikrik, the local shamanic instructor. It calls them to deepen their bond with the elements.

Among the orcs, shamans mediate between the living and their ancestors. The message marks a turn from brute strength toward disciplined reverence for ancestral ways.

item:rune-inscribed-pendant.text: Rune-Inscribed Pendant. In Silverpine Forest, a Rune-Inscribed Pendant arrives at the Sepulcher in a shipment bound for Ambermill. The Kirin Tor use pendants like it to channel arcane power. A Rune-Inscribed Pendant is found among cartographic supplies bound for the Dalaran enclave at Ambermill. Its fine arcane inscriptions reveal its purpose: to focus and strengthen a wizard’s spells. More channeling pendants are arriving in the region, and the Forsaken at the Sepulcher wonder what the Kirin Tor are preparing.

item:rune-inscribed-tablet.text: Rune-Inscribed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives a stone message to young Darkspear troll shamans. It sends promising mystics to Shikrik for formal spiritual instruction. Gornek gives a rune-carved stone to initiates who prove their mettle in the Valley of Trials. The troll shaman Ishi-yo sends it to Shikrik, the shaman trainer. For Darkspear trolls, the tablet begins a shared path with the orcs. Their old spiritual traditions join the shamanic heritage Warchief Thrall has renewed.

item:rune-of-nesting.text:
Rune of Nesting. At Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Rune of Nesting helps prepare a rite to wake the Druids of the Talon. They sleep in the Emerald Dream, and four sacred relics guide their safe return. Deep in the winding chambers of Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Rune of Nesting lies in the Chest of Nesting. Night elf druids sleep in underground barrow dens and commune with nature through the Emerald Dream.

To return safely, the Druids of the Talon need a careful awakening ritual guided by sacred relics. The Rune of Nesting is one of four, alongside the Raven Claw Talisman, the Black Feather Quill, and the Sapphire of Sky. Together, the relics call the sleeping druids back to the waking world. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den, and its sleeping defenders are in peril. Without the relics, the druids may remain trapped in the Emerald Dream while invaders desecrate their sanctuary. Recovering the Rune of Nesting and its companion relics lets Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar prepare the rite that can wake them safely.

item:runes-of-summoning.text: Runes of Summoning. In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, warlocks draw a voidwalker from the Nether with the Runes of Summoning. The creature enters a circle, where an aspiring warlock can bend it to their will. Carendin Halgar gives the Runes of Summoning to warlocks ready to command a voidwalker. In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Forsaken practitioners study how to manipulate the Nether. A warlock casts the runes in the active summoning circle below Halgar's station. The ritual tears through the Void and draws forth a creature to be overpowered and bound into servitude.

item:sack-of-murloc-heads.text: Sack of Murloc Heads. Along the Hillsbrad beaches, a sack of Murloc Heads is gathered as proof that local shore threats are being culled. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle gives the bundle to passing adventurers for Marshal Redpath in Southshore. Southshore faces attacks from Syndicate outlaws, Forsaken skirmishers, and wild murlocs along the coast. Officers must show the town's leaders that coastal threats are being culled, so they can secure funding and favor. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle gathers severed heads as proof, though he finds the cargo distasteful. His squeamishness sends the sack with travelers to Marshal Redpath instead of carrying the grisly evidence himself.

item:sack-of-supplies.text: Sack of Supplies. Across Razorwind Canyon, the sacks of supplies bound for Rezlak lie scattered among harpy roosts. Dustwind harpies seized the goods as they crossed Durotar. Rezlak needs a steady supply of goods for his work outside Orgrimmar. Gazlowe contracted the goblin engineer from Ratchet to build for the Horde. A caravan carrying a promised shipment passed near the canyon road south of Orgrimmar. Dustwind harpies ambushed it and dragged the cargo into their roosts in Razorwind Canyon, scattering sacks beside their nests in the dirt and scree.

item:salty-scorpid-venom.text: Salty Scorpid Venom. Across Thousand Needles, Salty Scorpid Venom draws gnomes into a dangerous race for speed. Scorpids on the Shimmering Flats carry the desert floor's mineral salts in their venom, and gnomish racers seek it for fuel. Scorpids on the mineral-rich Shimmering Flats carry salt in their venom. Scorpid Reavers and Scorpid Terrors have absorbed those local salts over generations. Fizzle Brassbolts and other gnomish tinkers prize the caustic venom as a possible additive for high-combustion engine fuel, not for antidotes or ordinary poisons. At the Mirage Raceway, gnomes and goblins test ever more dangerous materials in their rocket cars. Fizzle Brassbolts believes boiling down the salted venom, treating it with specialized catalysts, and mixing it into propellant tanks will give his car the fierce heat it needs to outrun goblin racers on the salt pans.

item:samophlange-item.text: Samophlange (item). In the Barrens, Samophlange remains hidden in an automated control console. Goblin mechanics cannot explain what the strange component does. Samophlange lies within a Barrens control console, behind a maze of wiring and hollow tubes. Careful searching is needed to free it from its housing. It looks vital to clockwork and steam machinery, yet goblin tinkerers cannot learn its purpose. They plan to send it to the Tinkers' Union in Undermine, though rough handling may break the fragile piece.

item:samophlange-manual.text: Samophlange Manual. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob seeks the scattered pages of the Samophlange Manual. The handbook explains how to repair and operate the Venture Company's samophlange. Boss Copperplug kept the Venture Company's knowledge of the samophlange close. The ambitious overseer withheld the manual's pages from most workers. He gave loose leaves only to his most loyal subordinates. When the device left company hands, no one could repair it without recovering the torn pages from Copperplug and his crew at the Boulder Lode Mine. Rilli Greasygob left the Venture Company and settled in Orgrimmar to learn how the samophlange was built. Copperplug had never favored him, so Rilli relies on enterprising travelers to retrieve the manual's cover and loose leaves. Once reassembled, the handbook gives goblin tinkerers working with the Horde a rare look at Venture Company engineering.

item:sample-ichor.text: Sample Ichor. In Silverpine Forest, Sample Ichor bears traces of necromancy and warlock sorcery. Apothecary Renferrel refined it from the fluid that sustains the Rot Hide gnolls. Apothecary Renferrel sent Sample Ichor to the Undercity for closer study. He gathered it from the Rot Hide gnolls and their lingering remnants, then reduced the foul liquid to its base components. His findings showed that necromantic rites and warlock magic had shaped the ichor. Since its making reaches beyond simple alchemy, Renferrel sent it to Bethor Iceshard for divination.

item:sample-of-zanzil-s-altered-mixture.text: Sample of Zanzil's Altered Mixture. Across the sea, Sample of Zanzil's Altered Mixture is bound for Tarren Mill. The brew came from the witch doctor Zanzil and leaves its carrier weakened. Serge Hinott may find a cure and learn how the poison works. An operative carries the mixture after entering the Venture Company's tower near the Sludge Fen in the Barrens. The sample came from a cache in Gallywix's lockbox, and Zanzil's brew has left the agent afflicted. Shenthul sends the stricken operative across the Great Sea with it. At Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills, apothecary Serge Hinott can isolate the toxin and learn its components.

item:sample-snapjaw-shell.text: Sample Snapjaw Shell. Across the Barrens, snapjaw shells hold a spark of life from freshwater oases. Tauren druids send them across the Great Sea to aid Silverpine Forest. Snapjaws thrive in the Barrens' strange, lush oases. Their durable shells hold a faint glow and pulse with energy long after the creature is gone. Tauren druids watch the land change swiftly, and see in these shells a resilient spark of Kalimdor's wilderness. Their vigor shows how life can flourish even in harsh, arid lands. Tauren naturalists send couriers across the sea with shells for Mura Runetotem at the Sepulcher. She is stationed in Silverpine Forest's blighted expanses, seeking ways to help the Forsaken heal the northlands. Mura studies the life-force held in snapjaw armor, hoping it can show what will renew an ailing forest and bring growth back to dying soil.

item:samuel-s-remains.text:
Samuel's Remains. Near Deathknell, Samuel’s bones are taken from a Scourge thrall and laid beside Marla. Samuel Fipps and his wife Marla lived in peace in Tirisfal Glades before undeath’s plague swept across Lordaeron. Samuel succumbed and became a mindless servant of the Scourge. Marla escaped undeath, but Samuel struck her down. As she died, she asked to be buried beside him once his cursed form was laid to rest.

Novice Elreth in Deathknell sends newly awoken Forsaken northeast of the settlement. There they must find Samuel’s wandering form, recover his bones, and bury them in the front row of the local cemetery.

item:sapphire-of-aku-mai.text: Sapphire of Aku'Mai. Along Blackfathom Deeps, naga harvest the Sapphires of Aku'Mai. Water spirits cling to the crystals, and Je'neu Sancrea seeks help to seize them before their arcane power is used. At the watery entrances to Blackfathom Deeps, the walls along Ashenvale's Zoram Strand bear Sapphires of Aku'Mai. Water spirits cling to the crystals, whose elemental energy lends power to magic. When scouts reported naga quarrying the gems underground, Je'neu Sancrea, a shaman, sought travelers' help to seize them. In naga hands, the stones could fuel devastating arcane rites.

item:sapphire-of-sky.text: Sapphire of Sky. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Sapphire of Sky helps call sleeping Druids of the Talon back from the Emerald Dream. Night elves keep it as one of four sacred Relics of Wakening. Druids of the Talon sleep in hibernation within Ban'ethil Barrow Den, deep among Teldrassil's roots. There, they commune with the wilds. Waking from that deep trance is perilous, so four sacred relics guard the passage: the Black Feather Quill, the Raven Claw Talisman, the Rune of Nesting, and the Sapphire of Sky. The gem completes the harmony needed to call the sleeping spirits back from the Emerald Dream. Without it, they may be trapped there forever. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den, leaving the sacred relics in their repositories. The Sapphire of Sky lies inside the Chest of the Sky, along the winding underground corridors. The druids still sleep as the furbolgs rampage around them. Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar needs the sapphire and its companion relics to wake the sleepers before they are lost forever.

item:sara-balloo-s-plea.text: Sara Balloo's Plea. In her grief, Sara Balloo asks an Alliance champion to carry her handwritten appeal to King Magni Bronzebeard. Grief keeps Sara from facing the High Seat, so she entrusts her words to an adventurer loyal to the Alliance. She asks King Magni to remember the private mourning and sacrifices of ordinary dwarven families who serve the kingdom.

item:sarilus-foulborne-s-head.text: Sarilus Foulborne's Head. Across the border from the Barrens, Sarilus Foulborne's Head reaches Ashenvale as proof the sorcerer is dead. He defiled Ashenvale's waters, and the Sentinels demanded his head.

item:sarkoth-s-mangled-claw.text:
Sarkoth's Mangled Claw. Across the southern bluffs of the Valley of Trials, Sarkoth's Mangled Claw bears the mark of a wounded hunter. Hana'zua crushed the scorpid's pincer before its venomous sting struck him down. Hana'zua, a young Darkspear troll, met Sarkoth while hunting in the Valley of Trials. The massive scorpid pierced his chest with its venomous stinger, leaving him bleeding beneath a nearby tree.

Before the sting, Hana'zua crushed the beast's pincer. The battered claw proves Sarkoth has been slain. For the wounded hunter, its scar shows that his desperate strike found its mark and preserves his warrior's honor as venom courses through his veins.

item:sarltooth-s-talon.text: Sarltooth's Talon. Above Whelgar's Excavation Site, Sarltooth's Talon is all that remains of the raptor's attack. Ormer Ironbraid wants the claw as proof the beast is dead. Ormer Ironbraid watched from the ridge as raptors overran Whelgar's Excavation Site and butchered the dwarven expedition. He could not stop them. One huge raptor, Sarltooth, seemed to him the pack's leader. Seeking vengeance for his fallen kin, Ormer demanded the beast's death and one of its talons as proof. The claw marks the end of Sarltooth's rule over the ancient dwarven ruins.

item:sathrah-s-sacrifice.text:
Sathrah's Sacrifice. At the Temple of the Moon, Sathrah's Sacrifice offers Lady Sathrah's spirit a chance at peace. Her silvery spinnerets come from the mighty spider who dwells in Teldrassil. Lady Sathrah was a venerable creature of Teldrassil. Then creeping madness and corruption spread through the great tree's boughs and took hold of her. The Sisterhood of Elune asks you to bring back her silvery spinnerets as a consecrated offering. They are not a trophy.

At the fountain in the Temple of the Moon, her remains are bathed in holy water. The rite washes away the taint that poisoned Sathrah's mind and frees her troubled soul. Her spirit appears peacefully within the sanctuary, with the promise of rebirth under Elune's grace.

item:satyr-horns.text: Satyr Horns. In Ashenvale, Satyr Horns draw dryads seeking vengeance and traders bound for Ratchet. They come from satyrs whose corruption has taken root in the ancient forest. Ashenvale’s satyrs bear horns that mark their demonic corruption. At the Shrine of Aessina, the dryad Illiyana gathers them for vengeance over her lost sister, Anilia. Pixel, a traveling goblin resting at Splintertree Post, wants them for trade. Demand has risen in Ratchet, where hunters sell these remnants of slain demons. Satyr Horns must be cut from the satyrs themselves; ordinary suppliers do not sell them. Satyrs hold strongholds across Ashenvale, from the corrupted groves of Xavian to the hollows of Satyrnaar and the ruins of Night Run. Clearing these enclaves pushes back the lingering demonic taint. It also gives grieving guardians and eager merchants proof of the cull.

item:savannah-lion-tusk.text: Savannah Lion Tusk. Across the Barrens, Savannah Lion Tusks pass from hunting trophies into Chen Stormstout's legendary ale. Great cats of the Barrens carry sharp, heavy tusks. Prowlers, huntresses, prides led by patriarchs, and beasts like Humar the Pridelord all bear them. Travelers take the teeth as proof of a successful hunt. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn uses the tusks with plainstrider kidneys and thunder lizard horns to recreate Chen Stormstout's famous brew. The potent ale has a legendary kick few mortal gullets can withstand.

item:scaber-stalk.text: Scaber Stalk. In Darkshore, Barithras Moonshade seeks Scaber Stalks from a cave behind Cliffspring Falls. Behind Cliffspring Falls, Scaber Stalks grow in a cave among Darkshore's northeastern mountains. The pale mushrooms thrive in its damp, secluded passages, far from the forest growth above. Few gather them from so remote a place. Barithras Moonshade in Auberdine sends scouts into the darkness for the rare stalks.

item:scale-of-old-murk-eye.text:
Scale of Old Murk-Eye. Along Westfall's coast, Captain Grayson seeks proof that Old Murk-Eye is dead. The ghost haunts Westfall Lighthouse, where the murloc's attacks left the beacon dark. Old Murk-Eye made Westfall's coast a killing ground. Captain Grayson, the ghost bound to Westfall Lighthouse, says the cunning murloc rallied weaker-minded murlocs to raid the shore. Murk-Eye drove away the keeper's family, leaving the beacon dark when Grayson's ship struck the rocks.

When the family returned to relight the flame, Murk-Eye attacked again and slaughtered them. Grayson seeks one of the creature's scales as proof that the shore is clear of its fiercest predator.

item:scarlet-armband.text:
Scarlet Armband. In Deathknell, Scarlet Armbands mark the zealots pressing into Forsaken territory. Executor Arren gathers them as proof that the newly risen have struck back. Scarlet Armbands mark the Scarlet Crusade's followers, from Initiates to fresh converts. Their red insignia warns the newly risen Forsaken in Deathknell that danger waits nearby. The Crusaders make no distinction between the Scourge's mindless servants and the free-willed subjects of the Dark Lady. To them, every walking corpse must burn.

Executor Arren gathers the armbands to confirm that enemy scouts southeast of Deathknell have died. He needs proof that the new Forsaken can defend their fledgling nation.

item:scarlet-crusade-documents.text:
Scarlet Crusade Documents. At the Crusade's camp near Deathknell, Scarlet Crusade Documents pass through Tirisfal in a messenger's hands. Their orders name field commanders and direct their forces, giving the Forsaken intelligence on Scarlet positions across the Glades. Meven Korgal carried the documents from the Crusade's encampment southeast of Deathknell. The Highlord's orders direct the captains of the Crusade's Tirisfal Regional Command. Captain Perrine must fortify the southwest tower and gather information on the undead in Brill.

Captain Vachon must crush undead movement near the northern tower, while Captain Melrose watches the borders of the Plaguelands. The orders name Scarlet field officers, their posts, and their duties across Tirisfal Glades. Executor Arren sees that Deathknell's local forces cannot make full use of this intelligence. The captured documents become a newly awakened Forsaken's passport out of Deathknell. Carry them northeast, past Cold Hearth Manor, to Brill, and deliver them to Executor Zygand outside Brill Town Hall. With the orders in hand, Forsaken military leaders can plan swift strikes against Scarlet commanders entrenched across the Glades.

item:scarlet-insignia-ring.text: Scarlet Insignia Ring. In Tirisfal Glades, Scarlet Insignia Rings mark the Scarlet Crusade's members. In Brill, the Forsaken collect them as proof that another zealot has fallen. Every Scarlet Crusade fighter in Tirisfal Glades wears an insignia ring. Neophytes and zealous friars wear them, as do captains Melrache and Perrine. The Crusade's fiery sigil marks each ring. It identifies members of an order consumed by paranoia. To outsiders, the rings mark Lordaeron's most fanatical human remnant. Deathguard Burgess in Brill collects the rings on Varimathras's orders. He is Lady Sylvanas's dreadlord lieutenant. The Forsaken see the Scarlet Crusade as a pestilence across their newly claimed homeland. Recruits bring rings back to Brill as proof of a Crusader's death and their loyalty to the throne of the Undercity.

item:scavenged-goods.text: Scavenged Goods. Around Deathknell, Forsaken gather Scavenged Goods from equipment boxes. Newly risen undead rely on discarded supplies to arm and clothe the recruits who follow. New Forsaken rise in Deathknell's graveyard wearing little more than rotting burial shrouds. Nearby settlements and kingdoms offer them no aid, so they must salvage what they need. Deathguard Saltain gathers discarded weapons, tools, and garments from crates across the village. He gives those supplies to the next recruits to rise.

item:scavenger-paw.text:
Scavenger Paw. In Deathknell, Scavenger Paw comes from young, ragged wolves on the hills. Newly awakened Forsaken gather the paws so local caretakers can stitch them into crude protective gear. Newly returned Forsaken in Deathknell have little to spare. The Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade press against Tirisfal, so every scrap of hide and bone finds practical use. Novice Elreth assists Shadow Priest Sarvis by gathering paws from scavenger wolves, along with bat wings.

She makes serviceable garments and armor for Forsaken newly risen from their graves. They are still disoriented by their return.

item:scorched-spider-fang.text: Scorched Spider Fang. Across the Wetlands, Cave Stalkers and Leech Stalkers carry Scorched Spider Fangs. Furen Longbeard in Stormwind needs fifty to strengthen mail for Alliance warriors. In Stormwind, blacksmith Furen Longbeard strengthens mail by unusual means. He needs fifty scorched fangs from the Wetlands' giant spiders. Their dense, venomous substance has toughened in the heat. Furen works it into the mail links as he tempers them. Cave Stalkers and Leech Stalkers bear the fangs Furen needs. They live in the Wetlands' sunken valleys and burrows, amid damp and rot. Their mandibles are hardened and scorched. Gathering fifty means venturing into deep hollows and facing the spiders in their swarms.

item:scroll-of-messaging.text: Scroll of Messaging. In Stonetalon, Gaxim Rustfizzle prepares to send a message that will set off explosives from afar. At the Venture Company's logging operation, Gaxim Rustfizzle will turn a message into a blast. He plans to join the scroll's transmission incantation with volatile NG-5 charges. The explosion will draw the guards away. Then operatives can slip past and steal engineering schematics and confidential correspondence.

item:sea-creature-bones.text: Sea Creature Bones. On Darkshore, Sea Creature Bones wash ashore with the bodies of massive sea creatures. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples for the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where the cause of the strandings is under investigation. Massive sea creatures now fling themselves onto Darkshore’s shallows and perish there. Giant threshers among them are far larger than those native to these waters. To the night elves, this sudden increase is an ominous portent. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde was sent by the Temple of the Moon to Auberdine to gather bones from the beached creatures. Hippogryphs carry the specimens to Darnassus for close examination. The immense carcasses draw local scavengers. Greymist murlocs gather to feed on the dead and dying creatures, then fiercely defend their feeding grounds. They are too weak to hunt beasts of this size. So investigators and adventurers must fight through their packs along Mist's Edge to recover bone fragments for study.

item:sea-turtle-remains.text: Sea Turtle Remains. Along Darkshore, Sea Turtle Remains gather on the coast and beneath the waves. Researchers in Auberdine study the growing number of dead sea turtles. Giant sea creatures wash ashore along Darkshore, while others lie beneath the water near sunken wrecks. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers bone fragments and tissue from their bodies. The Temple of the Moon in Darnassus urgently asks for these samples. Its scholars and priestesses fear the creatures are fleeing an unnatural disturbance in the waters around Teldrassil. Recovering the remains is dangerous. Murloc tribes along the coast gather around the huge carcasses, picking their bones clean and nesting beside them. Scholars need fresh bone fragments and tissue before the scavengers destroy evidence that might explain the creatures' fatal migration.

item:sealed-description-of-thredd-s-visi.text: Sealed Description of Thredd's Visitor. Warden Thelwater seals a report on the man visiting Bazil Thredd in the Stormwind Stockade. The confidential account may help investigators follow someone moving through Stormwind’s political and criminal circles. For years, prisoner Bazil Thredd received no visitors in the Stockade. Then a quiet man began coming once or twice each week with valid papers under the name Maelik. Warden Thelwater took note and recorded the man’s appearance. He sealed the description so meddling eyes could not read it before proper investigators acted.

item:sealed-envelope.text: Sealed Envelope. In Stonetalon, Fizziks has sealed Venture Company secrets in the Sealed Envelope for Sputtervalve in Ratchet. Cast out of the Venture Company's logging operations in the Stonetalon Mountains, goblin engineer Fizziks smuggled away its secrets. Inside the envelope are company manuals, operating procedures, and technical plans. Among them are schematics for the Super Reaper 6000, a machine built for industrial clear-cutting. Fizziks sends the documents south to Sputtervalve, an engineer in Ratchet's neutral goblin port. The Steamwheedle Cartel's rivals have little love or trust for Fizziks. Yet the designs hold clear engineering value. They reveal the Venture Company's mechanical skill and give independent engineers a chance to use its advanced logging methods.

item:sealed-note-to-elling.text: Sealed Note to Elling. In Stormwind, Jorgen sends a sealed dispatch to Elling Trias, proprietor of Trias' Cheese. The fisherman’s message draws Trias into a quiet inquiry about a vanished diplomat. Jorgen gives a strict charge for the sealed note in Stormwind: place it in Elling Trias's hands and keep silent. The stakes leave no room for careless talk. Trias runs a cheese shop in the Trade District. There, Jorgen's message brings the inquiry into the diplomat's disappearance to his counter.

item:sealed-note-to-watcher-backus.text:
Sealed Note to Watcher Backus. In Stormwind, Elling Trias sends a sealed note to Watcher Backus in Duskwood. He asks the Night Watch guard to report Defias activity near Darkshire. Elling Trias agrees to use his contacts to help find the missing diplomat. He seals a note for Watcher Backus, a Night Watch guard stationed in Duskwood.

Trias sends a traveler south through the forest to deliver it by hand. He hopes Backus will report any Defias seen near Darkshire.

item:searing-collar.text:
Searing Collar. At Skull Rock in Durotar, Searing Collars burn the Burning Blade cultists who wear them. The heated torcs help attune them to demonic power. The Burning Blade gathers at Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar, for dark rites. Cultists, neophytes, and thugs wear Searing Collars around their necks. The metal brands and sears their skin as they endure its heat.

Margoz, a hermit, studies the cruel devices. He suspects their burning and enchantments attune the wearers to demonic energies. What part do the collars play in the corruption spreading through orc society under the Horde’s nose?

item:searing-coral.text: Searing Coral. Along the Wetlands coast, Searing Coral is gathered from living iron coral beneath the sea. Tinkerers and smiths prize its heat-resistant mineral for strengthening armor. Searing Coral grows in the cold sea south of Menethil Harbor. Living iron coral thrives in saltwater and yields mineral-rich material that withstands extreme heat. Harvesters must pry the hardened growths loose while wild murlocs and other aquatic beasts roam nearby. Dwarven smiths do not traditionally work Searing Coral. In Ironforge, curious gnome craftsmen such as Klockmort Spannerspan follow methods from veteran armorsmith Furen Longbeard. They smelt the coral and hammer it into metal alloys, making lightweight, durable armor for aspiring warriors.

item:secure-crate.text: Secure Crate. In the Barrens, a Secure Crate is bound for Ratchet. Potions and alchemical goods inside are headed across the sea to the Eastern Kingdoms. Couriers, caravans, and goblin ships carry trade between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. When a Barrens caravan misses its departure, travelers carry fragile cargo like this Secure Crate down to the coast. Inside are potions, alchemical goods, and reagents for associates across the Great Sea. Its seal protects the crate along the Barrens trails and during the sea voyage. The crate’s land journey ends at the Ratchet docks, where Wharfmaster Dizzywig oversees shipping. Ratchet is a neutral port for goods crossing the sea, including cargo bound for Blackwater Cove. Dizzywig works under the Steamwheedle Cartel’s ledger, recording parcels and freight before loading them onto the next departing vessel. Ratchet links the Old World with the frontier.

item:senir-s-report.text:
Senir's Report. In Dun Morogh’s cold foothills, Senir Whitebeard sends his findings on the Frostmane trolls to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. Senir’s report gathers what mountaineers saw while scouting the Frostmane trolls in Dun Morogh’s crags. He also includes his brother Grelin’s account of Coldridge Valley. Grelin acted there with King Magni Bronzebeard’s sanction.

Senir sends the findings to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge’s High Seat. He advises couriers to leave out how much outside help he needed to compile them.

item:serena-s-head.text: Serena's Head. At the Dry Hills, Darsok Swiftdagger seeks Serena Bloodfeather's head as proof of her death. He plans to display it on a Horde supply wagon to warn against further harpy raids.

item:serpentbloom.text:
Serpentbloom. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, Serpentbloom has drawn the Royal Apothecary Society’s keen interest for its potent natural properties. In the Barrens, Serpentbloom thrives in the shadowy, damp tunnels of the Wailing Caverns. Unrestrained Emerald Dream energies have warped the caverns’ ecosystem. Venomous serpents often nest among the herb’s stems.

Hostile beasts and corrupted druids overrun the caves. Few who venture inside return with viable specimens. At the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff, Apothecary Zamah gathers Serpentbloom for the Royal Apothecary Society in Undercity. The Forsaken seek virulent, strange, chemically potent plants across Kalimdor to fuel research for the Dark Lady.

Zamah believes a harvest of Serpentbloom in significant quantities could bring valuable breakthroughs in Forsaken alchemy.

item:sethir-s-journal.text: Sethir's Journal. On Teldrassil, Sethir's Journal was recovered through stealth. Its pages show that corruption from mainland Kalimdor has reached the World Tree.

item:sevren-s-orders.text: Sevren's Orders. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren sends a proven Forsaken agent south to the Undercity. The orders direct the agent to Bethor Iceshard in the Magic Quarter. Forsaken agents who prove themselves against the Scourge in Tirisfal Glades are summoned south as their people strengthen their hold on Lordaeron. Magistrate Sevren writes these orders as an introduction and credentials for Bethor Iceshard, one of the Dark Lady's foremost arcane practitioners in the Magic Quarter. Sevren knows only that the assignment concerns reaching out to an errant lich. The Undercity's high mages give the summons their full authority.

item:shadowhide-pendant.text: Shadowhide Pendant. In Redridge, Shadowhide Pendant charms mark gnolls serving Morganth. Lakeshire takes ten as proof that its law has been upheld. Shadowhide Pendant charms hang from the Shadowhide warriors, brutes, and spellcasters. Deep in the hills of Redridge, Lieutenant Fangore leads the clan, now under Morganth's sway. Morganth is a rogue wielder of the Arcane. To Lakeshire's townspeople, the crude charms mark an organized threat harassing settlements for an enemy of the Crown. Magistrate Solomon upholds Stormwind law, which sets death as the sentence for actively aiding a known criminal of the realm. Royal reinforcements are too few, so Bailiff Conacher at Lakeshire Town Hall relies on adventurers to keep the peace. Ten Shadowhide Pendants prove that gnolls obeying Morganth's orders have faced frontier justice.

item:shaman-voodoo-charm.text: Shaman Voodoo Charm. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Gnarlpine shamans wield the Shaman Voodoo Charm. Its magic can sever a sleeping druid's spirit from the body. On Teldrassil, the Gnarlpine tribe has fallen into madness and corruption. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, its shamans wield magic beyond ordinary wilderness sorcery. Their charms tear a sleeping druid's consciousness from the mortal realm and trap it in the Emerald Dream. The furbolgs then animate the empty body. Night elf protectors become mindless guardians who kill anyone entering the barrows.

item:shard-of-water.text: Shard of Water. Along the Barrens coast, Islen Waterseer receives the Shard of Water from a shaman who has faced corruption. To master water, a shaman must understand balance, life, and preservation. During the Call of Water, you travel to corrupted springs, crossing the sea to blighted Silverpine Forest. There, you purify the tainted waters and receive the Shard of Water. Then you return the crystal token to Islen Waterseer on the rocky Barrens shore. It proves your worth and provides the final key to forge a Water Totem.

item:shaw-s-report.text: Shaw's Report. In Westfall, Shaw's Report carries SI:7 intelligence to Gryan Stoutmantle. Written by Master Mathias Shaw, it tells of the Stonemasons Guild, Edwin VanCleef, and their grievance with the crown after Stormwind was rebuilt.

item:shimmering-frond.text: Shimmering Frond. In the Oracle Glade, a plant from beyond the Great Sea casts a twisting, shimmering aura. Its fronds belong to a species native to the Swamp of Sorrows. Near the Oracle Glade, a radiant plant grows among the trees. Its aura pulses, and its fronds shimmer in the woodland light. Denalan tends planters beside Lake Al'Ameth. He recognizes the leaves as a species from the Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. How seeds from that distant marsh crossed the Great Sea and took root on Teldrassil remains a mystery. Denalan is growing specimens in his own soil to study them.

item:shimmerweed.text: Shimmerweed. On Shimmer Ridge, Frostmane trolls gather shimmerweed for their rituals. Rejold Barleybrew of Brewnall Village wants to test its sharp flavor in his stout. High above Dun Morogh's lowlands, Frostmane trolls tend shimmerweed on Shimmer Ridge's icy crags. They harvest the plant and keep it in woven baskets throughout their camps. There, it fuels their sacred rituals. Few mountaineers beyond troll society pay the herb much mind, though inventive outsiders have taken an interest. In Brewnall Village, brewmaster Rejold Barleybrew suspects shimmerweed may be the missing piece in his attempt to brew the ultimate dwarven stout. He has detected the herb's pungent, unmistakable flavor and wants to test it in his fermenting vats. So Rejold hires travelers to slip into Frostmane camps, evade the hostile trolls and bring back bushels.

item:shindrell-s-note.text:
Shindrell's Note. In Astranaar, Shindrell Swiftfire sends word of corruption near town and along Ashenvale's coast. Her report travels east through the forest to Kayneth Stillwind. Sentinels and druids watch Ashenvale's borders together as unrest spreads through the forest. From Astranaar, Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire reports troubling disturbances along the western coast and among the central canopies.

Her report is addressed to Kayneth Stillwind, a druid at the shrine of Forest Song in the Nightsong Woods to the east. Couriers carry Shindrell's firsthand observations to aid his search for corruption in the sacred groves.

item:shipment-of-boots.text: Shipment of Boots. Along the Barrens coast, the Shipment of Boots remains in a Southsea encampment south of Ratchet. Drizzlik sent the crate from Booty Bay for Gazlowe's trade network, but pirates seized it before it reached port. Gazlowe arranged for Drizzlik, a clothing merchant in Booty Bay, to send boots to Ratchet. Southsea Freebooters ambushed the ship while patrolling the Merchant Coast. They carried the crates to beach encampments south of the harbor and scattered the stolen goods among their tents and shanties. The shipment remains there, far from Ratchet's docks.

item:shipment-of-iron.text:
Shipment of Iron. In Hillsbrad Fields, raw iron waits at the human smithy, where it arms the townsfolk against the Forsaken. Human peasants across the Hillsbrad Foothills resist Tarren Mill. Much of their strength comes from the smithy at the southwestern edge of Hillsbrad Fields. Blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices turn heavy shipments of iron into weapons and armor, working round the clock.

Forsaken commanders have ordered the forge put out, its smiths killed, and its stored metal seized for the Horde war effort. They hope to break the farmers’ resolve.

item:shipping-schedule.text: Shipping Schedule. At Jerod's Landing, the Defias Brotherhood sends contraband along Elwynn's waterways. Its dockmaster guards a schedule of shipments between Redridge and Westfall, and SI:7 wants it. South of Goldshire, Jerod's Landing lies on the Elwynn bank of the Nazferiti River. The Defias Brotherhood seized it as a hub for river traffic. From there, they carry contraband between Redridge and Westfall by waterways beyond the Stormwind Guard's notice. Their dockmaster keeps the Shipping Schedule close, recording each shipment. Master Mathias Shaw leads SI:7, Stormwind's intelligence agency, and ordered the schedule stolen. It can reveal Defias supply lines, and taking it tests new operatives. The theft must happen inside the dock house, from the dockmaster's pockets. If the operative is caught, SI:7 denies any connection. No trail leads back to its barracks in Stormwind.

item:sida-s-bag.text: Sida's Bag. Near Ironbeard's Tomb, Sida's Bag lies swallowed by an ooze. Sida fled to Menethil Harbor after throwing her satchel at one of the slimes during her weekly visit. Now the acidic creatures must be searched for her belongings. Each week, Sida visits Ironbeard's Tomb near Dun Modr. Dreadful, dripping oozes ambushed her there, and panic made her hurl her satchel at one. The ooze swallowed the bag. That gave Sida time to escape alive and return to Menethil Harbor, while her possessions stayed trapped inside an unknown slime. The oozes around Ironbeard's Tomb range from crimson to monstrous, and look much alike. Cut down the marsh slimes until Sida's Bag emerges intact. Acidic muck soaked the durable sack, but its contents remain preserved. Sida reclaims her belongings, then discards the ruined, slime-coated exterior and offers the washed-out container to whoever braved the marsh for her.

item:signed-recruitment-letter.text: Signed Recruitment Letter. From the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar sends a signed letter west with recruits ready for duty. It directs them to report to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. At the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar prepares recruits for service in the Barrens. The post lies east of the Southfury River, where newcomers cross from Durotar. When a conscript proves ready, Kargal stamps and signs a letter of introduction. Its orders send recruits west along the road to the Crossroads, where Sergra Darkthorn coordinates supplies and the defense of the dry plains. Kargal's orders carry his contempt for the officer awaiting the recruit. He calls Sergra Darkthorn an abrasive shaman who talks in circles around soldiers. Kargal openly questions Warchief Thrall's high opinion of her. Even so, the dispatch must reach Sergra before any further assignments at the Crossroads are granted.

item:silithid-egg-the-barrens.text: Silithid Egg (The Barrens). Across the Field of Giants, Silithid Egg lie buried beneath the soil. Horde researchers gather the eggs to learn about the swarm spreading through the southern Barrens. Silithid mounds rise across the Field of Giants as strange insect-like creatures churn the earth. Their eggs lie beneath hardened soil, guarded by territorial silithid. The Horde knows little of them, yet scouts at the Crossroads have seen signs of coordination and intelligence beyond ordinary wild beasts. Unhatched eggs may help scholars in Orgrimmar learn about the silithid’s life cycle and nature. An adapted digging claw is needed to pry Silithid Eggs from the mounds. The creatures defend their underground nurseries fiercely and swarm anyone who threatens their unhatched young. Korran, a troll researcher, needs intact specimens for study before the swarm spreads farther across Kalimdor.

item:silixiz-s-tower-key.text:
Silixiz's Tower Key. At the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen, Silixiz's Tower Key is in Foreman Silixiz's pocket. A Shattered Hand operative must steal it unseen as part of an undercover sabotage assignment. North of the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company guards its tower closely. Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix oversees the isolated lookout, while goblin mercenaries patrol the compound. Foreman Silixiz carries the tower key outside.

A Shattered Hand operative from Orgrimmar must steal the key and keep it. Force will not do. The operative must enter unseen and pick Silixiz's pocket, proving their stealth before climbing into the tower's toxic upper levels.

item:silver-dawning-s-lockbox.text: Silver Dawning's Lockbox. Off the Darkshore coast, Silver Dawning's Lockbox lies in a wreck north of Auberdine. Coastal murlocs sank the ship, and the box holds its captain's personal effects and ship log. The Silver Dawning was sailing toward Auberdine when coastal murlocs attacked. They drove the ship beneath the waves north of the harbor, and the captain died in the assault. The flooded hull still holds the captain's lockbox, with the ship's log and private belongings inside. Recovering them may bring some peace to the surviving crew ashore.

item:silvery-spinnerets.text:
Silvery Spinnerets. Near Wellspring Lake, Silvery Spinnerets are sought for a rite honoring Lady Sathrah. Her silver webs once gathered healing evening dew for the Sisterhood of Elune in Darnassus. By moonlight near Wellspring Lake, Lady Sathrah spun shimmering webs. Her silver silk gathered evening mist into healing dew, prized by the Sisterhood of Elune in Darnassus.

Then corruption reached her in Teldrassil and drove her into violent madness. Sathrah threatened her brood and the surrounding forest. Priestess A'moora asks travelers to end her suffering and recover her spinnerets, showing mercy to a once-revered creature of the great boughs.

item:simple-memorandum.text:
Simple Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, novice gnome warriors are sent to train with Thran Khorman in Anvilmar. They prepare for the war to take back Gnomeregan. Young gnome fighters face wildlife and troggs in Coldridge Valley with letters of introduction in hand. The Simple Memorandum directs its bearer to Thran Khorman, the warrior trainer in Anvilmar.

Gnomes bring intellect and contraptions to battle, but taking back Gnomeregan calls for strength and martial discipline. The memorandum sends its bearer beyond early training to learn the art of war from Thran.

item:simple-rune.text: Simple Rune. In Coldridge Valley, Thran Khorman sends promising young dwarven warriors to Anvilmar for training with the Simple Rune. Young fighters who have begun clearing threats from Coldridge Valley receive Thran’s formal summons. The rune’s martial marks hold no magic; they tell each recruit to report to Thran inside Anvilmar. There, he teaches basic combat and gives practical advice for surviving Dun Morogh’s hostile wilds.

item:simple-sigil.text: Simple Sigil. In Shadowglen, a Simple Sigil calls novice night elf warriors to train with Alyissia. It marks their first step in Teldrassil’s defense. In Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine guides young night elves as they seek their calling. A runner brings a Simple Sigil from Alyissia, the warrior trainer. Ilthalaine gives it to fledgling warriors, and its inscription directs each recruit to report for instruction. Their martial training begins as troubling times come to the World Tree. Alyissia uses the sigil to tell recruits what the kaldorei need. Teldrassil has grown recently, corruption is spreading among forest beasts, and the rediscovery of distant lands such as Feralas has stretched night elven protectors thin. The sigil holds no power. It welcomes each recruit among the guardians charged with shielding their people from emerging threats.

item:simple-tablet.text: Simple Tablet. At the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives new troll warriors a message to carry to Frang. Gornek gives new troll warriors a message from Tar'sere, addressed to Frang, the warrior trainer near the Den. It introduces the recruit to combat training in Durotar and asks them to present themselves to Frang. The message calls them to take up weapons for the Horde.

item:singed-scale.text: Singed Scale. In Durotar, warriors bring Singed Scale from the charred plates of electrified thunder lizards to prove their endurance and learn defense. Horde veterans judge a warrior by the blows they endure while shielding allies. Thunder Ridge is a canyon in western Durotar, where lightning hides and thunder lizards crackle with storm energy. Hunting them means bearing relentless electrical shocks and crushing blows. Their blackened scales show a fighter can withstand punishing assaults and hold firm under pressure. At the Far Watch Post on the border between Durotar and the Barrens, veteran warrior Uzzek asks initiates for five scales before teaching them. He believes they need physical toughness before they can learn stances and tactical defense. Bringing the scales proves they have the fortitude to combine thick hide, heavy armor, and careful footwork into a firm defense against the Horde’s enemies.

item:skeleton-finger.text: Skeleton Finger. In Duskwood, restless dead yield Skeleton Finger to Madame Eva of Darkshire. She gathers them with ghoul fangs and spider venom to make protective talismans. Skeletal raiders and warriors rise across Duskwood, along with necrotic mages and fiends. Most travelers leave their foul remains alone, but fortune tellers and mystics prize their cold essence. Madame Eva, the seer of Darkshire, gathers their bony fingers for the Totem of Infliction. She binds their lingering necrotic energies into a ward that strikes back at attackers.

item:skin-of-sweet-rum.text: Skin of Sweet Rum. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Skin of Sweet Rum is headed for Lakeshire, where war has thinned the tavern's stores. Lakeshire's tavern is running short of drink as the Blackrock orc invasion closes the roads into the Redridge Mountains. Barkeep Daniels needs drink for the town guards and refugees. So he sends travelers to gather regional specialties, including a waterskin of sweet rum from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire.

item:skittering-blood.text: Skittering Blood. In Silverpine Forest, Skittering Blood gives the Royal Apothecary Society material for its New Plague. Forsaken alchemists draw it from arachnids in the Skittering Dark as they seek a weapon against the Scourge and humanity. Skitterweb lurkers, strikers, and their broodmother Krethis the Shadowspinner yield venomous blood. Apothecary Renferrel found that refined with toxins from grizzled bear hearts, it forms the base of an exceptionally lethal elixir. Its contaminating agents also suit the Apothecarium's chemical experiments. In the Undercity, Master Apothecary Faranell directs the Royal Apothecary Society's search for a New Plague. The Forsaken face Scourge hordes and hostile human remnants, so they turn to biological warfare to even the odds. Faranell studies the blood's toxic strength as he works toward a contagion that can destroy unlife and living flesh alike.

item:sleepers-key.text:
Sleepers' Key. At Stonetalon Peak, Sleepers' Key helps protect a sacred druidic vault. Night elf druids made it one of three enchanted keys for the Talon Den Hoard. The Talon Den is a redoubt and sanctum for the druids of Kalimdor on Stonetalon Peak. Night elf keepers built locks and hidden caches to guard sacred relics and potent treasures from unwanted attention. Sleepers' Key is one of three keys that form a protective ward.

Sleepers' Key rests in a secluded cache deep in the den. The Gatekeeper's Key, hidden near the threshold, opens that cache. The Claw Key and the Barrow Key complete the set. Set all three keys into the Talon Den Hoard's stone locks, and the ward fades. Ancient items lie within.

item:smoky-iron-ingot.text: Smoky Iron Ingot. At Windshear, kobolds smelt Smoky Iron Ingots from ore dug in the Stonetalon Mountains. Orcish armorers prize the bars for sturdy mail gear made for Horde warriors. Kobolds smelt Smoky Iron Ingots in the Windshear Crag tunnels of the Stonetalon Mountains. They dig ore from the rocky slopes and heat it over crude, smoking fires. Residue and charcoal cling to the bars, yet the metal stays dense and strong. Thun'grim Firegaze is a near-blind orc armorer at a rugged camp overlooking the Barrens. He asks for these ingots to make armor for proven Horde warriors. With refined iron bars, powdered azurite, and volatile phlogiston, the smoky metal forms a resilient core for Brutal Hauberks.

item:smoldering-embers.text: Smoldering Embers. In the Charred Vale, Smoldering Embers remain when fire elementals are extinguished. Night elf Sentinels gather them as proof that the fires are being subdued. Venture Company logging and industry set the Charred Vale ablaze. Their work stirred destructive forces from deep within the earth. Burning Ravagers, Burning Destroyers, and Rogue Flame Spirits swept across the scorched basin. When a fire elemental is extinguished, an ash-covered core remains. That cinder is a Smoldering Ember, proof that the fires overrunning the vale are being brought under control.

item:snellig-s-snuffbox.text:
Snellig's Snuffbox. At the Lost Fleet, Snellig's Snuffbox stays with its undead owner among the wrecks. First Mate Fitzsimmons in Menethil Harbor wants it as proof that his cursed crewmate has found rest. First Mate Snellig still clutches his snuffbox in a wreck off the northern Wetlands. The Third Fleet of Kul Tiras ran aground there, and its sailors and officers drowned beneath a mysterious power tied to a hidden treasure aboard the ships. Bound to that power, the drowned crew rose again as tortured spirits and skeletal undead.

Snellig haunts the rotting hold of the wreck closest to the coastline. His snuffbox is an ordinary keepsake from his mortal life at sea. First Mate Fitzsimmons, the disaster's sole living survivor, wants it returned as proof that at least one lost shipmate has found release from torment.

item:snufflenose-command-stick.text: Snufflenose Command Stick. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix sends trained gophers into Razorfen Kraul to find blueleaf tubers. Mebok Mizzyrix has trained snufflenose gophers to seek blueleaf tubers deep in Razorfen Kraul. The roots hide beneath thorny tunnels, where finding them is nearly impossible without help. Mebok is a merchant in Ratchet, and he avoids entering the quilboar dens himself. So he gives adventurers the Snufflenose Command Stick to guide the gophers. From as far as fifty paces, the stick directs them to sniff out and uncover the roots.

item:snufflenose-owner-s-manual.text: Snufflenose Owner's Manual. Beside Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet, Snufflenose Owner's Manual shows how to send a trained gopher after Blueleaf Tubers in Razorfen Kraul. Marwig Rustbolt of Snuff Inc. wrote it for that purpose. Marwig Rustbolt of Snuff Inc. wrote the guide for handling the company's trained snufflenose gophers. Their keen noses can find Blueleaf Tubers buried underground from fifty paces away. The manual shows how to release a gopher from a ventilated crate and guide its rooting with a command stick. Prospectors lead it through Razorfen Kraul's thorns and quilboar tunnels in search of tubers.

item:sodium-nitrate.text: Sodium Nitrate. At Bael Modan, Sodium Nitrate goes into the charges the dwarves use against the southern Barrens’ stone. Gann Stonespire seeks the chemical for charges against the fortress. At Bael Modan, dwarven excavators use Sodium Nitrate to break through the southern Barrens’ rock. The Bael'dun expedition entered the Stonespire tribe’s ancestral lands with earthmovers and blasting reagents. Riflemen, soldiers, and officers carry the chemical inside the excavation works and nearby fortress.

item:solomon-s-plea-to-darkshire.text: Solomon's Plea to Darkshire. Lakeshire turns to Darkshire as threats close in. Magistrate Solomon asks Lord Ello Ebonlocke to send the Night Watch north and help defend Redridge. Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and murlocs attack Lakeshire, while few reinforcements come from Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon sends a formal plea to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke in Darkshire, asking him to send Night Watch militia north into Redridge. With central military support failing across southern Azeroth, human settlements must seek help from one another to survive.

item:solomon-s-plea-to-westfall.text: Solomon's Plea to Westfall. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon calls on Westfall for help as Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten Redridge. Stormwind's royal army has not answered, so he asks Gryan Stoutmantle to send the People's Militia. Blackrock orcs and hostile gnolls threaten Redridge, while Magistrate Solomon is isolated in Lakeshire. Stormwind's royal army has not arrived in force to defend the region's borders. With no time to wait for the capital, Solomon writes beyond the regular army. Word has reached him of a volunteer defense force forming in Elwynn to the west, so he appeals to the People's Militia. Solomon addresses his message to Gryan Stoutmantle, a veteran warrior organizing Westfall's frontier defense. He hopes Stoutmantle can spare fighters for Lakeshire until Stormwind sends regular reserves. An adventurer carries the document. Stormwind's outlying territories are poorly coordinated, so local magistrates must arrange mutual aid on their own.

item:soran-ruk-fragment.text: Soran'ruk Fragment. In Blackfathom Deeps, cultists draw on shards of Soran'ruk, a shattered prison orb. The pieces still hold fel energy from the demon once bound within. Soran'ruk's prison orb was shattered after its demon fell from favor with the Burning Legion. Demons who displease their masters may have their spirits sealed in orbs, then given to fel spellcasters as sources of power. In the submerged ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight's Hammer cultists possess smaller shards from one half of the orb. They draw on the lingering demonic essence for their own workings.

item:southsea-treasure.text:
Southsea Treasure. Southsea Treasure lies aboard a pirate ship south of Ratchet, where Wrenix the Wretched seeks the hoard. The Tide Razor's lowest hold sits beneath the Southsea Freebooters' training ground. The Tide Razor lies anchored along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet. The Southsea Freebooters use it as a forward base and training ground. Their plunder, called the Southsea Treasure, waits in the lowest hold.

Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin scoundrel in Ratchet, sets the theft as a test for aspiring pickpockets. He says the last five operatives sent after the chest came back in pieces. Alert pirates guard the ship, and a fierce creature watches the hold.

item:spectral-comb.text: Spectral Comb. South of Darkshire, the Spectral Comb gathers ghost hair from Blind Mary at a ruined farmstead. Ordinary combs cannot reach a spirit’s hair, so few mortal craftsmen can gather it. The Spectral Comb passes through those unseen tresses. At a ruined farmstead south of Darkshire, it is offered to Blind Mary, a weeping ghost who wails alone. Grooming brings her solace, and she willingly takes up the comb. The fibers she leaves behind can be woven into Ghost Hair Thread.

item:spells-of-shadow.text: Spells of Shadow. Beneath Orgrimmar, Spells of Shadow lies among the Searing Blade’s guarded treasures. The Forsaken leadership in the Undercity wants it recovered. In Ragefire Chasm, Searing Blade cultists guard Spells of Shadow among their treasures. The splinter cult is tied to the Shadow Council, and its members wield dark rites granted by demon masters of the Burning Legion. The book holds shadow and fel sorcery. Cultists and warlocks keep it close as they plot beneath the Horde in Durotar. Word of the Searing Blade’s demonic gifts reached the Undercity’s royal quarters. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, judged the relics wasted on cultists with lesser vision. So Varimathras sends Horde adventurers into Ragefire Chasm to seize Spells of Shadow and its companion tome, Incantations from the Nether. Their power is meant to serve the Forsaken cause against the Scourge and the Lich King.

item:spotted-sunfish.text: Spotted Sunfish. At Lake Everstill, Spotted Sunfish draw fishers and hungry murlocs. Their catch brings trade to Lakeshire, while murlocs make the shallows dangerous. Spotted Sunfish bring trade to the Lakeshire piers. Dockmaster Baren buys the lake’s steady catch, supplying food and commerce to a town under strain. Aggressive murloc tribes prowl the shallows and disrupt fishing. At their camps, travelers can take the sunfish they have gathered by force.

item:stalker-claws.text: Stalker Claws. Across Mulgore, tauren shamans use Stalker Claws in a rite to cleanse tainted wells. They bind the claws into totems that purify the poisoned water. Prairie stalkers hunt across Mulgore’s grassy steppes. Their stealth and precision make them deadly, yet they keep a necessary balance in the Earth Mother's design. Mull Thunderhorn needs their claws to help heal the blighted land. He seeks no harm to the beasts, for the natural force of their hunt holds the spiritual strength to counter artificial corruption. Goblin drilling and mining across central Kalimdor have sent chemical poisons into the underground waters that feed ancestral tauren wells. The Thunderhorn Water Well is tainted by vile muck. Tribal shamans bind Stalker Claws and Cougar Claws into a Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem. The totem scours unnatural sludge from the earth's springs.

item:steelgrill-s-tools.text: Steelgrill's Tools. At Steelgrill's Depot, Beldin Steelgrill needs fresh tools to keep his workshop at work. He puts siege engines and equipment through hard use, so Kharanos keeps sending replacements. Beldin Steelgrill is one of Dun Morogh's finest siege engine technicians. Merchants know his rough touch, though. He works without pause on armored tanks and mechanical contraptions, and delicate tools soon break in his hands. Arclight spanners snap and fang-ratchets wear out, so he keeps ordering replacements from Kharanos for his repair benches. At his depot northeast of Kharanos, Beldin services combat vehicles for experienced drivers such as Pilot Stonegear. The tools keep Ironforge's war machines in working order. Fresh wrenches and ratchets keep repairs moving on the siege engines assembled there, supporting local defenses.

item:steelsnap-s-rib.text:
Steelsnap's Rib. In Thousand Needles, Steelsnap's Rib carries proof of a feared hyena’s end. Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff wants it brought to Hunter Rise to show that Steelsnap has been slain. Tauren hunts often seek food, honor, or harmony with nature. Steelsnap is another matter. The alpha hyena roams the canyon floor south of Camp E'thok in Thousand Needles. He terrorizes peaceful wildlife and rallies lesser predators to bloodshed.

Hunt master Melor Stonehoof waits on Hunter Rise. He marks Steelsnap for death and asks for the hyena's rib as proof. With Steelsnap slain, the canyon can be cleansed of his blight.

item:stolen-silver.text: Stolen Silver. At the Crossroads, Stolen Silver has vanished from the guard tower. Sunscale raptors carried the coins south of Ratchet to their nests at the Raptor Grounds. Sunscale raptors carried a strongbox of silver from the Crossroads guard tower. The coins were meant to pay the garrison guards. The raptors dragged the lockbox to their communal nests at the Raptor Grounds, south of Ratchet. Gazrog and the other overseers cannot explain what drove the predators to take it. They wonder whether the raptors prize shiny things or are more cunning than ordinary wild beasts.

item:stone-of-relu.text: Stone of Relu. In the Wetlands, Stone of Relu is lost after raptors ambush Archaeologist Flagongut. He believes it can unlock secrets within ancient fossils. The Explorers' League uncovered Stone of Relu. Archaeologist Flagongut believes the artifact can decipher prehistoric fossils gathered from Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. He plans to study his Wetlands specimens and the fossil Prospector Remtravel unearthed in Darkshore. On a Wetlands road, Archaeologist Flagongut was traveling to meet Prospector Whelgar when mottled raptors ambushed him. In the scramble, the relic was lost, then swallowed by one of the beasts. Now the League seeks the marsh raptors, hoping to cut the ancient stone from their gullets.

item:stonetalon-sap.text: Stonetalon Sap. Near Mirkfallon Lake and Stonetalon Peak, sap beasts carry Stonetalon Sap. Jin'Zil, the Darkspear witch doctor, seeks it for a brew meant for his caged night elf prisoners.

item:stormpike-banner.text: Stormpike Banner. In Alterac Valley, Alliance recruits brave harpies to claim the Stormpike Banner. The trial lies southwest of Dun Baldar in Icewing Cavern. Lieutenant Haggerdin sends new Alliance soldiers into Icewing Cavern, southwest of Dun Baldar. Before facing the Frostwolf orcs, each recruit must brave the harpies and seize the Stormpike Banner. Those who bring it back earn the rank and insignia of an initiate in the Stormpike Guard.
