item:stormpike-s-request.text: Stormpike's Request. From Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike sends Furen Longbeard a commission for a fine dwarven shield. Mountaineer Stormpike stands watch in Loch Modan, where the dwarven frontier brings danger. He needs a sturdy shield and trusts no ordinary smith with such work. Furen Longbeard is the armorsmith whose craft he admires. Furen left Ironforge and now lives among the humans in Stormwind's Dwarven District. Stormpike assumes a king's ransom drew him south, so he relies on travelers to carry his request across the kingdoms. Furen Longbeard receives Stormpike's letter in Stormwind's Dwarven District and agrees to make the shield. The Stormpike clan is proud and established, known across Khaz Modan for martial grit and wealth. Word and business from his northern homeland are welcome. So Furen sets to work on the mountaineer's order.

item:stormwind-armor-marker.text: Stormwind Armor Marker. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain accepts a Stormwind Armor Marker from those who aid the realm. It lets them claim crafted gear from artisans commissioned by Stormwind. Stormwind's commanders issue armor markers to those who serve the realm. Keeping order across Elwynn Forest strains Stormwind's resources. So commanders sometimes use these official slips in place of standard gear at military outposts. A marker confirms the bearer's service and allows a contracted local craftsman to provide tailored armor. Sara Timberlain and other artisans work under commission from the Stormwind Army at Eastvale Logging Camp. The camp lies on Elwynn's eastern frontier, where they use local materials to make protective cloth and leather garments. Present a marker there to receive custom-fitted defense for guarding the surrounding woodlands.

item:stoutmantle-s-response-to-solomon.text: Stoutmantle's Response to Solomon. From Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle sends word to Lakeshire that no soldiers can be spared for Redridge Mountains. Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire asks Sentinel Hill for help as Blackrock orcs and gnolls press his town. Gryan Stoutmantle answers in writing and mourns Lakeshire's losses. Yet Westfall faces a war of its own. The People's Militia formed after the Crown withdrew its garrison, and farmers and volunteers now fight the Defias Brotherhood alone. Stoutmantle's forces are already bleeding and stretched thin, with no men to spare for another abandoned frontier.

item:strange-smelling-powder.text: Strange Smelling Powder. In Loch Modan, Strange Smelling Powder has alarmed engineers investigating sabotage. Chief Engineer Hinderweir fears it may be explosive and seeks an expert's judgment. Strange Smelling Powder was found amid signs of sabotage against Loch Modan's infrastructure. Chief Engineer Hinderweir fears it may be an engineered explosive, unlike the powder usually used in mining. He cannot identify its mixture or origin, and will not tamper with it himself. Even a small spark could bring disaster.

item:strangely-marked-box.text: Strangely Marked Box. On Darkshore, Strangely Marked Box runes point toward naga cargo washed ashore on dead sea turtles. Their presence hints that the turtles did not come ashore by chance. Dead sea turtles and other sea creatures wash onto Darkshore’s beaches. Some bear broken harnesses and carriages strapped to their shells. Among the wreckage lie sealed boxes marked with foreign, winding runes. Greymist murlocs shelter in hollow ribs and broken wagons, feeding on the carcasses and guarding what remains.

item:strigid-owl-feather.text: Strigid Owl Feather. In Teldrassil's boughs, owls leave Strigid Owl Feathers for the taking. Zenn Foulhoof seeks them for his covert dealings.

item:sturdy-dragonmaw-shinbone.text: Sturdy Dragonmaw Shinbone. At the Angerfang Encampment, renegade Dragonmaw orcs yield sturdy shinbones for armor. In the Undercity, Velora Nitely needs them to frame leg guards for warriors. Velora Nitely needs bones strong enough to bear the strain of brutal leg guards. Renegade Dragonmaw orcs at the Angerfang Encampment in the central Wetlands have thick frames, and their shinbones can brace the armor. Each bone is tested by hand. Warriors keep only those that resist breaking.

item:sully-balloo-s-letter.text: Sully Balloo's Letter. Beneath the Thandol Span, Sully Balloo's Letter carries a soldier's farewell to Sara in Ironforge. His words hold the love he bore her through his final days. Beneath the Thandol Span, the road from the Wetlands crosses toward the Arathi Highlands. Under the rushing water, a dwarf's skeletal remains lie pinned. A fragile, waterlogged envelope rests in his grasp. Inside, the letter begins, “My dear Sara...” The parchment has suffered beneath the water, yet the ink still bears the care of the dwarven defender in his final days or hours. He never returned to Ironforge.

item:sunscorched-shell.text: Sunscorched Shell. Beneath Highperch, the desert heat hardens wyvern eggshells. Armorer Mathiel in Darnassus uses them to make lacquer for mail links. Highperch wyverns lay eggs on the mesa needles of southern Kalimdor. Beneath their roosts, discarded shells bake in the desert sun and searing winds. Their brittle remains keep a natural strength that catches the eye of skilled artisans. In Darnassus, armorer Mathiel studies methods first tried by his colleague, the dwarf smith Furen Longbeard. He turns the shells into a fine lacquer for mail armor. The coating strengthens the metal links without burdening the wearer.

item:super-reaper-6000-blueprints.text: Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints. In Windshear Crag, goblin rivals covet the Venture Company’s Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints. They show how to build the mechanized woodcutter deployed in Stonetalon Mountains, under gnome engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle’s supervision. Venture Company operators carry the Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints through Windshear Crag. The plans show how to build the great mechanized lumber harvesters behind the company’s clear-cutting. Goblin engineers resent that Gerenzo, a gnome, was put in charge of the design. After the company ousted goblin engineer Ziz Fizziks, Sputtervalve hired him to steal the plans. Yet Gerenzo’s dense, eccentric notes are nearly as hard to decipher as the blueprints are to seize by force.

item:supplies-for-sven.text: Supplies for Sven. In northwestern Duskwood, Sven Yorgen's camp depends on provisions from Darkshire. The Carevin family keeps his small band supplied as they hold their watch against the shadows. Sven Yorgen and his few followers keep camp in the northwestern wilderness, far from Darkshire. Their numbers are too small to leave the watch and make the journey into town. So the Carevin family sends food, bandages, and other necessities to help the band hold its ground.

item:surena-s-choker.text:
Surena's Choker. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder seeks the bloodstone choker he gave his former apprentice, Surena Caledon. She fled with Erlan Drudgemoor to join the Defias Brotherhood, and Gakin now sends aspiring acolytes to take it back by force. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder once trained Surena Caledon in the dark arts. He saw promise in her youthful charm and magical talent, and gave her a valuable bloodstone choker to aid her studies. But Surena left her training and fled with Erlan Drudgemoor, a rogue aligned with the Defias Brotherhood.

Gakin will not let a traitor keep such a potent artifact. Now he sends initiates seeking mastery over the void to find her at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and reclaim the choker by force. Their deed will prove where their loyalty lies.

item:swoop-gizzard.text: Swoop Gizzard. Across Mulgore, swoops hunt the plains and mesas, and tauren folk remedies put their gizzards to use against deadly toxins. Swoops hunt across Mulgore’s plains and mesas, watching with keen eyes and scavenging for food. Tauren use their feathers and meat in daily life. Herbalists and healers prize their inner organs, especially the gizzard. Combined with cougar bones and wolf hearts, it helps counter venomous bites and festering infections. In Bloodhoof Village, Maur Raincaller tends the wound Mazzranache left on his shoulder. The legendary plainstrider’s venom drives Maur into delirium as the poison spreads through him. To make a poultice that can expel the deadly venom, Maur needs a swoop gizzard, a prairie wolf heart, a flatland cougar femur, and a plainstrider scale.

item:tablet-of-verga.text:
Tablet of Verga. In Skull Rock, the Tablet of Verga remains in Burning Blade hands, while Orgrimmar's warlocks seek its demonic runes. The Tablet of Verga bears ritual runes for summoning creatures from the Nether and bending them to a master's will. The Burning Blade stole the stone and hid it in a chest inside Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar.

Warlocks in the Cleft of Shadow seek the tablet to study its markings and learn to summon a voidwalker. Recovering it also keeps the cult from gaining that same advantage.

item:tainted-heart.text: Tainted Heart. In Teldrassil, Denalan tends a heart that still bears corruption. Its foul moss is gone, but taint remains, and he seeks to cleanse it with rich soil. A blight troubles Teldrassil's natural balance, warping its plants and beasts. Once the foul moss is stripped from a blighted growth, Denalan gives adventurers the Tainted Heart within. Darkness still clings to its tissue. He hopes specially prepared, nutrient-rich earth can counter the taint and restore what was corrupted.

item:tainted-keg.text: Tainted Keg. At Tarren Mill, Tainted Keg carries a deadly brew made by Apothecary Lydon. Stolen dwarven stout bears the poison, bound for imprisoned human farmers as a test of the Royal Apothecary Society’s work. Dun Garok's dwarven riflemen lost a barrel of Shindigger Stout to thieves. Apothecary Lydon mixed it with his newly refined Elixir of Agony. The Forsaken chose an ordinary drink to carry the poison, hoping no one would suspect it. A familiar ale became a swift death sentence.

item:tainted-letter.text: Tainted Letter. Near Northshire Abbey, Drusilla La Salle sends human warlock initiates a sealed summons for secret tutelage, beyond watchful eyes. Initiates returning from nearby kobold camps carry Drusilla's summons toward Northshire Abbey. Priests, paladins, and soldiers train openly across its lawns, but fel practitioners must keep their path quiet. Town guards and clerics may grow suspicious if novice warlocks draw attention while seeking their mentor near the abbey grounds. Drusilla La Salle meets her pupils on the fringes, where sentries are less likely to pry. Elwynn’s ordinary folk distrust warlocks, and the letter begins a lesson in discipline. Arcane and nether magic risk corruption. Those who commune with denizens of the Twisting Nether must temper ambition with patient self-control.

item:tainted-memorandum.text:
Tainted Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, Alamar Grimm urges novice gnome warlocks to leave old paths behind and seek power through the dark arts. At Anvilmar, few celebrate fel practitioners, and many distrust them. Alamar Grimm gives the Tainted Memorandum to young gnomes who study forbidden arts. He rejects the Holy Light and ordinary weapons. To him, Gnomeregan’s fall proves that old ways and tinkering failed their people.

Grimm sees reliance on dwarven charity as a dead end. He urges gnomes to claim undeniable power and summon minions who obey without question. Only then, he believes, can they secure their own future.

item:talisman-of-corruption.text: Talisman of Corruption. In Darkshore, Xabraxxis turns the Blackwood furbolgs against their former allies with the Talisman of Corruption. He keeps it in his personal pouch, and its magic binds the tribe to fel madness. In Auberdine, the night elves seek the cause of the Blackwood furbolgs’ turn against their former allies. Thundris Windweaver found that satyrs brought about the tribe’s fall. Talismans like this carry corrupting sorcery through the wilderness. They taint food and twist peaceful forest spirits into frenzied beasts. Their fel magic grips the minds and wills of local tribes.

item:tallonkai-s-jewel.text:
Tallonkai's Jewel. On Teldrassil, the jewel is missing from Tallonkai's druidic talisman. Ferocitas the Dream Eater prizes the emerald, needed to mend the Emerald Dreamcatcher. Tallonkai Swiftroot received the Emerald Dreamcatcher from Gaerolas Talvethen, warden of the druids in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The talisman is a powerful focus that draws energy from the Emerald Dream. When it was damaged, someone pried out its radiant central emerald and carried it into eastern Teldrassil.

Ferocitas the Dream Eater, a corrupted Gnarlpine, took the jewel and made it into a necklace. Its green light glimmered in the forest gloom, but the furbolg cared nothing for its harmony with the Emerald Dream. To Ferocitas, it was only a trophy until it could be recovered.

item:taming-rod.text: Taming Rod. In Durotar, Taming Rods help new hunters learn to command beasts. Trainers lend them to students for practice before they form lasting bonds with animal companions. In Razor Hill, trainers such as Thotar give Taming Rods to orc and troll hunters who are just beginning. The enchantment helps them practice before they can bind a wild creature for good. A rod pacifies a local predator, such as a dire mottled boar or an armored scorpid. The hunter learns to give commands and fight beside an animal companion, but the bond lasts only briefly. Each Taming Rod's magic fades after a short time, and each is attuned to certain kinds of wild beasts. Novices face trials against different temperaments, from docile foragers to aggressive venomous hunters. Once a student shows they can command these beasts, the rod goes back to the trainer. Then the trainer teaches them to tame, call, and dismiss lifelong companions without an artifact.

item:taragaman-the-hungerer-s-heart.text: Taragaman the Hungerer's Heart. Beneath Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade seeks Taragaman the Hungerer's Heart as proof that the demonic presence is gone. The trophy comes from the felguard ruling Ragefire Chasm's depths.

item:tattered-manuscript.text: Tattered Manuscript. In Thousand Needles, Tattered Manuscript lies hidden in Splithoof Hold. Its torn pages came from the Tome of the Cabal, and warlocks seek them to learn how to summon a felhunter. Once, the Tome of the Cabal was a unique, whole volume kept in the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. An unknown defiler tore almost half its pages from the binding. The spine and pages left behind became known as the Moldy Tome. They were sent south toward Khaz Modan, then lost at sea. The torn leaves crossed the Great Sea to Kalimdor and came into the hands of the Galak centaur inside Splithoof Hold. A battered chest deep in the caverns of Splithoof Hold holds the manuscript. There it endured the dry winds of Thousand Needles. Alliance warlocks work with Krom Stoutarm in Ironforge, while Horde practitioners aid Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Both groups brave the aggressive centaur to reunite the leaves with the Moldy Tome. Together, the books hold dark rituals for summoning and binding a demonic felhunter.

item:tazan-s-satchel.text: Tazan's Satchel. Near Ratchet, Tazan faces pirates along the coast with a locked satchel in hand. The Shattered Hand wants the intelligence within. Near Ratchet, Tazan deals with pirates camped along the Barrens coast. Therzok, a guild master of the Shattered Hand beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, has taken notice. The guild seeks power in secret beyond Warchief Thrall's cautious diplomacy. It has marked Tazan for elimination to seize the intelligence in his satchel.

item:tear-of-the-moons.text:
Tear of the Moons. At Bael Modan in the southern Barrens, dwarven excavators have unearthed the Tear of the Moons. Its strange power grips Feegly, and General Twinbraid fears its influence. Dwarven excavators found the Tear of the Moons during the first digging at Bael Modan. Its strange light captivated the miners, especially Feegly. He said it gave him great strength, but soon grew unstable and turned against his comrades.

General Twinbraid, commander of the expedition, feared the relic's influence and called it cursed. He took the crystal and locked it in his personal strongbox at Bael'dun Keep. Then he cast Feegly out into the Barrens.

item:tear-of-tilloa.text: Tear of Tilloa. Near Darkshire, the Tear of Tilloa draws those seeking rare alchemical reagents. The flower grows on the Mistmantle estate in Duskwood. Outside Darkshire, the Tear of Tilloa grows on Stalvan Mistmantle’s estate. Duskwood’s soil has turned hostile to wholesome vegetation, yet the small white flower persists among the shadowed plots. Rare and secluded, it draws those seeking uncommon reagents beyond lawful markets.

item:techbot-s-memory-core.text: Techbot's Memory Core. In Gnomeregan, Tinkmaster Overspark seeks Techbot's Memory Core to study the automaton's corrupted behavior. Before Gnomeregan fell, Techbot aided Tinkmaster Overspark and his fellow inventors with devices and knowledge. During the city's fall, an errant electrical discharge jolted Techbot and turned its positronic brain to a hostile negatronic state. Now the automaton wanders Gnomeregan's tainted halls and attacks anyone in sight. Overspark hopes the memory core will help him understand the fault and restore his creation to its senses.

item:telescopic-lens.text: Telescopic Lens. Above Ratchet’s harbor, Gazlowe needs the Telescopic Lens to complete his observatory telescope. Southsea pirates took the lens from a ship, and it remains in their camp south of town. Ratchet is known for ruthless commerce, yet Gazlowe, its overseer and chief engineer, has greater mechanical ambitions. His observatory rises above the harbor, built to watch maritime traffic and the stars. The larger lens came safely overland from Durotar. The smaller, vital lens traveled by sea, where Southsea Freebooters prey on merchant lanes off the Barrens coast. When the Southsea Freebooters raided the transport ship, they took anything valuable, including the delicate optics. The lens may lie among the clutter of their beachside camp south of Ratchet. The pirates might not value its craft, or know how to pawn it. Gazlowe needs the unblemished glass returned so his observation deck can come into focus.

item:teronis-journal.text:
Teronis' Journal. In Ashenvale, Teronis' Journal traces a scout's search for a gem tied to a rod he hoped could slow furbolg attacks. Teronis was a longtime friend of Raene Wolfrunner and aided the Sentinels. He searched Ashenvale for a gem he believed belonged to a rod that could slow the furbolg attacks on his people. Near the shore, aggressive creatures ended his journey.

The journal was recovered from his personal effects in remarkably good condition. Its findings about a radiant gem that once formed part of the rod give Astranaar's defenders a trail to follow in his unfinished search.

item:tharil-zun-s-head.text:
Tharil'zun's Head. In Lakeshire, Tharil'zun's Head proves the commander who terrorized Redridge is dead. He led the Blackrock Outrunners occupying Stonewatch. Blackrock orcs at Stonewatch Keep have raided Lakeshire's farms and ambushed travelers on the roads. Tharil'zun led the Blackrock Outrunners behind those attacks.

Marshal Marris will not risk acting on rumors or partial victories. He demands proof of Tharil'zun's death, and the severed head gives it. The Outrunners' coordinated ambushes from the keep have suffered a major blow.

item:tharnariun-s-hope.text: Tharnariun's Hope. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender seeks a cure for the sick thistle bears. His trap calms them long enough to bring them to his camp. Tharnariun Treetender made a trap to calm the sick thistle bears. A mysterious affliction has made them more and more frenzied and violent across Darkshore. He hopes to cure them instead of seeing them killed. Set on the ground, Tharnariun's Hope shines with a soothing light. A rabid thistle bear that crosses it grows calm for a time and can follow a traveler back to Tharnariun's camp for treatment.

item:the-book-of-ur.text: The Book of Ur. In Shadowfang Keep, the Book of Ur draws the interest of Forsaken scholars. Archmage Arugal took it after Ur died. The Dalaran mage wrote of strange beings from other planes. Ur was a Dalaran mage who studied other planes and their creatures. Before the Scourge came, the Kirin Tor knew his work well. He longed to understand magic beyond this world, but wrote down what he found instead of recklessly breaking through the veil. Caution and restraint guided his research. When the Scourge attacked Dalaran, neither his magic nor his care could save him.

item:the-collector-s-schedule.text:
The Collector's Schedule. Near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, The Collector's Schedule marks the passage of illicit gold shipments through Elwynn Forest. Gnolls carry its handwritten itinerary, and Marshal Dughan recognizes the name it records. Gold still leaves Elwynn's mines on a schedule, though Stormwind has not officially worked them for months. Banditry and creature incursions drove the miners away. The itinerary names the days and hours when a figure called The Collector receives each shipment.

The trail leads to a camp near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in eastern Elwynn Forest. Marshal Dughan recognizes the Collector's name when he sees the schedule. Who pays for the stolen gold remains unknown.

item:the-embalmer-s-heart.text: The Embalmer's Heart. In Duskwood, Eliza's buried corpse still holds a beating heart. The Embalmer placed his own heart in his dead wife through dark magic, and it became the anchor of his power. Darkshire remembers the Embalmer as a gentle alchemist. When his wife Eliza died, grief broke his mind. He turned to foul sorcery, cut out his own heart, and placed it in her lifeless chest. The magic stirred her corpse to unlife. But Eliza returned as a ravenous creature, hungry for living human flesh. Horrified by what he had done, the alchemist buried her again.

item:the-general-s-response.text: The General's Response. From Stormwind, General Marcus Jonathan answers Lakeshire's plea for aid as Redridge faces danger. His dispatch acknowledges Magistrate Solomon’s appeal against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls, but sends no immediate reinforcements from Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon asks Stormwind City for troops to defend Redridge from gathering Blackrock orc clans and Gnoll warbands. General Marcus Jonathan replies that he has sent the plea to the throne, but no soldiers are coming now. He orders the letter returned to Lakeshire. Solomon is troubled by the delay and suspects something is wrong with Stormwind’s leaders.

item:the-lich-s-spellbook.text:
The Lich's Spellbook. On Brightwater Lake's island, Bethor Iceshard seeks a spellbook guarded by a free-willed lich. He hopes its pages reveal the lich's skill and who he was in life. A free-willed lich keeps watch over an island in Brightwater Lake with skeletal minions. He distrusts the outside world and mistakes other undead for Scourge thralls. So he orders his guardians to kill anyone who approaches.

Bethor Iceshard seeks skilled necromancers for the Forsaken beneath Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. He sends an emissary into the island camp to take the lich's spellbook. Bethor hopes its pages reveal the master's power and identity before death took Lordaeron.

item:the-state-of-lakeshire.text: The State of Lakeshire. Lakeshire's defenders face attacks, and Magistrate Solomon calls on Stormwind for aid. His report urges General Marcus Jonathan to send royal reinforcements against the crisis in Redridge. Magistrate Solomon writes that attacks threaten Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs and gnolls press the town, and its defenders cannot hold the borders forever. Couriers carry his dispatch west along the road to Elwynn Forest. Solomon asks the Stormwind Army to protect the kingdom's eastern reach. At Stormwind's gates, General Marcus Jonathan receives Solomon's report. He respects the magistrate's standing and understands the danger, but cannot move the army alone. Deployments need the crown's consent. So Lakeshire's plea must wait for a council with the young King and regent Bolvar Fordragon.

item:theramore-medal.text:
Theramore Medal. At Northwatch Hold, the Theramore Medal marks service in the marines and officers defending the outpost on the Merchant Coast. Its mark identifies the Alliance garrison. Marines, marksmen, commandos, and officers serving from Northwatch Hold carry medals stamped with Theramore’s mark. They are loyal to Lady Jaina Proudmoore’s realm. For human troops on the cliffs above the Barrens, the medals show that their service is legitimate and their authority comes from Theramore.

Others see the tokens as trophies from an overzealous foreign garrison. Northwatch treats every vessel approaching the coast as a mortal threat. Northwatch Hold’s gun batteries menace ships along the Merchant Coast, often bombarding privateers and merchantmen alike. After losing ships to those guns, Ratchet privateer Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun seeks the medals.

He wants proof that Northwatch’s trigger-happy ranks have paid in blood for sinking his ships, and that the soldiers responsible have been slain in retribution.

item:thick-bear-fur.text: Thick Bear Fur. In Dun Morogh, Thick Bear Fur helps travelers and soldiers endure the mountain cold. Bears roam the snowfields, and their pelts make insulated clothing and bedding. Bears roam Dun Morogh's ridges through some of the harshest snowfields in the Eastern Kingdoms. Their thick coats shield them from blizzards, and locals and travelers put the pelts to use. Hunters gather them to line clothing, insulate drafty outposts, and pad cold sleeping rolls. Pilot Bellowfiz outfitted his siege tank, Jetsteam, at Steelgrill's Depot for a month in the field on a long mission for the Siege Brigade. Cold iron offered little comfort in the high snowbanks, so he hired local scouts to gather thick bear fur from the snowfields south of the Grizzled Den. The pelts would make warm bedding for his cabin quarters.

item:thistlenettle-s-badge.text: Thistlenettle's Badge. In the Deadmines, Thistlenettle's Badge is all that remains after a tunnel collapse. Before the Defias Brotherhood sealed Moonbrook and the tunnels beneath it, prospectors from Ironforge's Explorers' League worked Westfall's old gold mines. Foreman Thistlenettle and his crew were deep below when a tunnel collapsed and split them apart. His brother Wilder escaped to Stormwind City, but the foreman and several laborers remained trapped underground.

item:thresher-eye.text: Thresher Eye. Along Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle needs Thresher Eyes for his Buzzboxes. He uses them to repair Buzzbox 411, a communication machine on the beach north of Auberdine. Darkshore Threshers hunt the surf and outer shallows off Darkshore. They threaten local fishermen and travelers, and their large eyes have drawn the interest of Wizbang Cranktoggle. The gnome engineer is stationed nearby and fond of crawler wine. He needs the eyes to repair Buzzbox 411, a communication machine on the beach north of Auberdine. Wizbang does not explain how slimy eyes repair delicate machinery. They might serve as crude lenses, chemical agents, or biological gears. Whatever the method, three eyes placed in Buzzbox 411's maintenance hatch restore its communication link. Wizbang then sends supplies through transmissions choked with static.

item:thule-s-head.text: Thule's Head. At the Sepulcher, High Executor Hadrec seeks proof that Thule Ravenclaw is dead. His severed head confirms the Scourge commander on Fenris Isle has fallen and helps the Forsaken hold Silverpine Forest.

item:thunder-lizard-blood.text: Thunder Lizard Blood. Hunters return with Thunder Lizard Blood from the southern Barrens. It comes from the great beasts roaming the plains. Stormsnouts, Stormhides, and Thunderheads are the names given to thunder lizards across the plains. Their heavy steps shake the earth, and their crushing weight can flatten an unwary hunter. Bringing back their blood shows the skill to hunt them and the strength to survive beneath their thundering feet.

item:thunder-lizard-horn.text: Thunder Lizard Horn. In the Barrens, Brewmaster Drohn seeks a Thunder Lizard Horn for Chen Stormstout's legendary brew. Thunder lizards roam the Barrens with crested bodies crackling with lightning. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn prizes their horns for Stormstout ale. His mentor learned the recipe from the wandering pandaren Brewmaster Chen Stormstout and passed it to Drohn. The horn gives the drink its potent kick.

item:thunderhawk-saliva-gland.text: Thunderhawk Saliva Gland. Greater thunderhawks across the Barrens yield the gland Brewmaster Drohn needs to recreate Chen Stormstout's fiery Trogg Ale. Greater thunderhawks hunt across the Barrens' dry savannas. The winged serpents command storms, and the older, more dangerous ones produce a saliva gland rich in natural potency. Travelers steer clear of these deadly beasts. Brewmasters prize the gland as a rare base for exotic drinks. Brewmaster Drohn settled outside Ratchet after Chen Stormstout passed through Kalimdor. Drohn studies the wandering brewmaster's ways of fermentation. To brew Trogg Ale, he needs a fresh thunderhawk saliva gland, stormhide lightning glands, and kodo liver. The fiery spirit has a sure kick and is meant to fortify hardy adventurers.

item:thunderhawk-wings.text: Thunderhawk Wings. Hunters bring Thunderhawk Wings to Camp Taurajo, where Jorn Skyseer receives them as proof of their strength, cunning, and endurance. At Camp Taurajo, hunters prize a pair of intact Thunderhawk Wings. Wind serpents, called thunderhawks by local hunters, strike swiftly from above. Tracking them across the open plains and taking their wings tests a hunter’s skill. For an initiate, returning with the wings proves readiness for the lifelong path of an accomplished hunter.

item:thunderhorn-cleansing-totem.text:
Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem. In Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn prepares a totem for the tainted Thunderhorn Water Well. Ancestral magic within it is meant to purify the water. Mull Thunderhorn entrusts a prepared totem to travelers in Bloodhoof Village. They carry it north to the Thunderhorn clan's sacred spring, where foul agents have tainted the water.

The tauren tribes' ancestral wells nourish their herds and hunting grounds. Through ritual invocation, the totem calms the water's disturbed spirits and cleanses the spring.

item:thurman-s-remains.text:
Thurman's Remains. At Agamand Mills, Thurman's remains lie among the ruins of the family's failed stand against the Scourge. The once-wealthy mill owner fell to the Plague and now wanders his ruined estate as an undead thrall. Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest landowners. They owned extensive mills and employed dozens of local workers. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, Thurman Agamand and his kin fortified their estate instead of fleeing. Sure that their wealth and strong mills could withstand the attack, they persuaded their loyal workers to fight beside them.

The defense failed. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered and made mindless servants of the Lich King. Coleman Farthing, a former worker who rose as Forsaken, now demands the destruction of his former masters. He seeks Thurman's remains as proof that the foolish patriarch paid for dooming his household.

item:thurman-s-sewing-kit.text: Thurman's Sewing Kit. At Larson Clothiers, Thurman's Sewing Kit is needed for the day's tailoring. Young apprentice Thurman Schneider left it at his family's home by the Canals, hoping to spend the day at leisure. Thurman's Sewing Kit holds the needles, shears, and thread he needs for tailoring. Young Thurman studies at Larson Clothiers, deep in Stormwind's Mage Quarter near the Mage Tower. His mother, Rema Schneider, knows he cannot work without the kit. So she asks passersby along the Canals to carry it to the shop. When Thurman gets his tools, his reaction reveals he left them behind on purpose. He hoped to trade a day of stitching garments for leisure.

item:timberling-seed.text: Timberling Seed. Across Teldrassil, Timberling Seed is gathered from plant spirits grown hostile. Naturalists and druids study the seeds to learn why the forest's plants have turned aggressive. Timberlings are nature elementals of Teldrassil, and their temper reflects the World Tree's balance. Lately they have grown angry and hostile, troubling the night elves who tend the boughs. Herbalists such as Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth suspect trouble in the soil. They gather seeds from wild timberlings, hoping purified, carefully tended soil might let docile offspring sprout.

item:timberling-sprout.text: Timberling Sprout. Along Lake Al'Ameth, Timberling Sprouts emerge tainted, and night elf caretakers pull them before they grow into aggressive timberlings. Timberlings are plant spirits bound to Teldrassil's natural vitality. Along Lake Al'Ameth, some seedlings sprout tainted and aggressive instead of healthy and in harmony with the wild. The young sprouts seem beyond cleansing or natural healing, so the caretakers gather and destroy them. They hope to keep hostile timberlings from spreading across the fragile boughs of the newly planted World Tree.

item:tirisfal-pumpkin.text: Tirisfal Pumpkin. At Solliden Farmstead, living humans still tend pumpkins in blighted Tirisfal. The Forsaken take the harvest for the Royal Apothecary Society’s mixtures. West of Brill, crops still grow despite the corruption spreading across Lordaeron. At Solliden Farmstead, living human farmers tend large orange pumpkins under the watch of the nearby Scarlet Crusade. The harvest feeds the farmers. For the Forsaken of Brill, the pumpkins are targets for sabotage and raw materials for Apothecary Johaan. Deathguard Simmer sends young Forsaken into the contested fields to steal pumpkins from the farmers. The vegetables do not feed the dead. They go into the Royal Apothecary Society’s cauldrons, where apothecaries test how natural plants react to plagues and experimental mixtures. Lordaeron’s remaining crops become tools against the living.

item:token-of-thievery.text: Token of Thievery. At Alther's Mill, Lucius puts rogue initiates to a dangerous test. They must recover the Token of Thievery from a locked footlocker among the ruins. Lucius tests promising rogues in the field from Lakeshire. Among the ruins of Alther's Mill, he hides the Token of Thievery in a locked footlocker. Blackrock orcs threaten the area, making each attempt a test of lockpicking under mortal danger. Success earns a Certificate of Thievery.

item:tome-of-the-cabal-quest-item.text: Tome of the Cabal (quest item). In Ratchet, Strahad Farsan gives warlocks the Tome of the Cabal after they gather dangerous components. Its pages teach them to draw a felhunter through the Twisting Nether and bind it. A felhunter is a vicious beast from the chaotic Twisting Nether, feared for devouring mana. To subdue one is a trial for seasoned warlocks. The Tome of the Cabal holds the rites for opening a path to the demon. Strahad Farsan, an experienced conjurer in Ratchet, gives it to an aspirant after they gather the rare and dangerous components its magic requires. Strahad Farsan makes the primary summoning circle in his sanctum. His acolytes use rods of channeling to shape a greater protective boundary. The warlock recites the tome's exact incantations and drags the felhunter into our world. Then the demon must be fought at once and subdued, bound to the warlock's will.

item:top-of-gelkak-s-key.text:
Top of Gelkak's Key. A giant foreststrider bears the Top of Gelkak's Key into the woods near Darkshore. The piece broke from a mechanical key that belongs to the shipwrecked gnome Gelkak Gyromast. Threshadons struck Gelkak Gyromast's ship off Darkshore and dragged it beneath the waves. Gelkak washed ashore with the winding key for his mechanical first mate. The coastal rocks broke the key into three pieces.

Before the dizzy pirate could gather his wits, beasts scavenged the wreckage. A giant foreststrider carried the ornate upper piece into the woods.

item:torch-of-the-dormant-flame.text: Torch of the Dormant Flame. At the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, a shaman stands ready to kindle the Torch of the Dormant Flame. Its fire waits on an ember won atop a mountain in Durotar. A shaman carries the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame up the peaks above Durotar, seeking fire's favor. With fire sapta, the shaman sees a Minor Manifestation of Fire atop the mountain and challenges it. When the spirit falls, its glowing ember is placed in the weathered brazier at the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. Then the shaman touches the torch's head to the white-hot blaze, and the wood awakens as a burning emblem of elemental mastery.

item:torn-fin-eye.text: Torn Fin Eye. Along Hillsbrad's coast, Torn Fin Eyes draw the Royal Apothecary Society's attention. The Forsaken seek them for alchemical work on new plagues. The Royal Apothecary Society uses rare biological parts in its work on the Forsaken's New Plague. Torn Fin Eyes come from murlocs along the Western Strand of Hillsbrad Foothills. Their organic properties help activate volatile alchemical compounds. Mixed with Daggerspine naga scales, restorative troll elixirs, and gnoll-derived sludge, the eyes help stabilize and trigger toxic mixtures meant to spread death through enemy lands.

item:torn-murloc-fin.text: Torn Murloc Fin. Along eastern Elwynn's waterways, murlocs crowd the banks and the Stormwind Army's bounty is being answered. Murlocs have grown numerous along eastern Elwynn's streams and lakes. So the Stormwind Army offers a bounty to thin their numbers. Guard Thomas watches the bridge over the eastern river and gathers severed fins as proof. With soldiers stretched thin by unrest at home and nearby threats, local authorities rely on travelers to show that murloc camps have been cleared.

item:totem-of-hawkwind.text:
Totem of Hawkwind. At Camp Narache, young tauren receive the Totem of Hawkwind before setting out for Bloodhoof Village. They present it to Baine Bloodhoof as proof they have passed their first trials and can continue the Rites of the Earthmother. Chief Hawkwind carves the Totem of Hawkwind atop Red Cloud Mesa for tauren youth coming of age. The token introduces its bearer and proves their passage. Tauren seldom use formal writ; a familiar tribal craft can carry a leader's intent.

After a youth completes the first trials at Camp Narache, Hawkwind sends them along the road into Mulgore with the totem. Its distinct carvings identify the bearer to Baine Bloodhoof and show the spirit and strength for the next trials. The road leads toward the blessing of Thunder Bluff.

item:tough-wolf-meat.text:
Tough Wolf Meat. In Northshire and Coldridge, wolves prowl their valleys and provide meat for hungry locals. Tough Wolf Meat is coarse and stringy. People in Elwynn Forest eat it, and dwarven outfitters in Dun Morogh use it to stock their supplies. Wolves prowl near Northshire Valley and Dun Morogh. They threaten nearby settlements, yet their meat offers a hard-won source of food. Coarse, stringy and chewy, it is prized by resource-strapped frontiersmen.

Outside Northshire Abbey, Eagan Peltskinner hates the vicious beasts but cooks their meat into steaks. He trades basic supplies and gear to those who cull the packs.

item:tourmaline-phial.text: Tourmaline Phial. At the Pools of Arlithrien, travelers gather blessed moonwell water in the Tourmaline Phial for Teldrassil's rituals. Corithras Moonrage gives travelers the Tourmaline Phial for rituals that tend the World Tree. Druids in Dolanaar use gemstone vials to gather pure moonwell water across Teldrassil. This phial is for the moonwell beside the Pools of Arlithrien, southeast of the road to Darnassus. Hostile Gnarlpine furbolgs are growing more troublesome there.

item:toxic-fogger.text:
Toxic Fogger. In Stonetalon, the Toxic Fogger is bound for Venture Company air routes. The Forsaken Royal Apothecary Society filled it with lethal poison to contaminate the company’s flights. Apothecary Zamah sends the Toxic Fogger against the Venture Company's mining work. Apothecary Lydon brewed its toxin in Tarren Mill, and Zamah sent it from Thunder Bluff. She suspects the goblins carry messages and light cargo between Stonetalon and their headquarters by courier flying machine.

Zamah plans to release the poison where those machines land and refuel. The Forsaken mean to strike the company's supply route instead of meeting its mercenary crews in drawn-out skirmishes.

item:translated-letter.text: Translated Letter. In Darkshire, Sirra Von'Indi translates Abercrombie's letter for Mayor Ello Ebonlocke. The message sheds light on the hermit's dealings with the town.

item:treshala-s-pendant.text: Treshala's Pendant. In Razorfen Kraul, Heralath's pendant bears the bond he shares with Treshala. He carried it from their home in Darnassus into southern Kalimdor, where the quilboar tore it from him as he lay dying. On perilous journeys from Teldrassil, Heralath Fallowbrook kept the pendant close. It brought his home to mind, along with his beloved wife, Treshala, and the devotion they shared.

item:trogg-stone-tooth.text: Trogg Stone Tooth. In Loch Modan's hills, Stonesplinter troggs leave rugged, mineralized teeth behind. Dwarven defenders use each tooth as proof that the troggs are being hunted along the southern frontier. Captain Rugelfuss calls for volunteers to hunt Stonesplinter troggs near Loch Modan's southern gate. With the Ironforge Reserve committed to the Alliance Front, local dwarven garrisons are stretched thin across Khaz Modan. Rugelfuss cannot spare the soldiers at the southern gate guard tower to patrol the nearby hills. So volunteers hunt the lurking troggs and bring back Trogg Stone Teeth as crude, undeniable proof of each beast slain.

item:troll-charm.text: Troll Charm. In Ashenvale, Troll Charms have been stolen from Darkspear travelers. The Thistlefur furbolgs took the sacred amulets after ambushing the party on its way to Zoram'gar Outpost. Darkspear trolls wear spiritual charms as marks of dignity. Scout Mitsuwa says a troll without one is as diminished as an orc without battle scars. A party of Darkspear kin traveled beneath Ashenvale's canopy toward Zoram'gar Outpost. Corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs ambushed and slaughtered them. Their spirits were commended to the afterlife, while the furbolgs took the charms as trophies and hid them in chests deep within Thistlefur Hold.

item:trophy-swoop-quill.text: Trophy Swoop Quill. Across Mulgore, swoops circle high over the plains, and their quills mark a hunter’s skill. Tauren bring the feathers to Harken Windtotem in Bloodhoof Village. Swoops circle high above Mulgore’s grasslands, where they are hard to track. Young tauren hunters and travelers in Bloodhoof Village seek a trophy quill to prove their cleverness and resolve. Bringing one to elders such as Harken Windtotem honors a hunter’s clan and shows the sharp senses needed to thrive on the plains.

item:twilight-pendant.text: Twilight Pendant. In Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight Pendants mark the Twilight's Hammer cultists who gather with the naga. The Argent Dawn seeks the pendants as proof of the cult's work along Ashenvale's coast. Beneath Blackfathom Deeps, the Twilight's Hammer gathers with the naga to honor the chaotic Old Gods. Shadowmages, aquamancers, reavers, and loreseekers wear Twilight Pendants to show devotion to their shadowy patrons. The cult keeps to the ruins of a former night elf temple. So the pendants give outsiders one of the few ways to learn how many cultists gather there and hinder their plans. In Darnassus, Argent Guard Manados seeks Twilight Pendants as evidence that the growing darkness is being driven back. Blackfathom Deeps once held a pristine moonwell, and void-worshipers have desecrated it. That threatens Kalimdor. Gathering the pendants shows the Twilight's Hammer foothold in Ashenvale is being dismantled before its patrons unleash greater terror.

item:twilight-whisker.text: Twilight Whisker. In Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil gathers Twilight Whisker for his brew. Twilight runners carry the whiskers through the northern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. Twilight runners prowl the high crags near Stonetalon Peak. Hunters prize their pelts, while Witch Doctor Jin'Zil of Malaka'jin seeks their stiff whiskers for a darker purpose. He seeks vengeance on the night elves captured after defending these woodlands. To mock and poison his captives, Jin'Zil gathers resinous sap, countless eyes, fey dragon scales, and Twilight Whisker for a lethal draught he calls forest magic.

item:twitching-antenna.text: Twitching Antenna. In the southern Barrens, Twitching Antennae mark a hunt that tests a young warrior's speed and skill. Ruga Ragetotem at Camp Taurajo seeks them before their nerves go still. Silithid Grubs, Swarmers, Harvesters, and Creepers carry antennae that twitch after they are cut from the head. The spasms fade soon after the insects die. A young warrior must hunt silithid in the southern wastes, then hurry back across the scrublands while the antennae still twitch. The trial tests speed and skill, and marks a rite of passage for Horde warriors. Silithid antennae point to a danger troubling Camp Taurajo's hunters. The creatures are not native to the Barrens, and their new burrowing mounds at the Field of Giants unsettle the camp. Ruga Ragetotem wants the specimens to study the threat and prepare Horde warriors for the alien menace moving into the plains.

item:ukor-s-burden.text:
Ukor's Burden. At the Valley of Trials, Ukor’s rejected provisions leave him needing help to carry them back to Razor Hill. Ukor, an orc peon, rarely acts on his own. Yet he carried provisions from the inn in Razor Hill to feed young recruits in the Valley of Trials. The journey took him through Durotar’s red dust and dangerous wildlife.

The overseers and instructors refused the food, believing hardship and hunger make true warriors. Now Ukor waits outside the canyon’s mouth, afraid of the beasts on the trail back. He has entrusted the sack to passing travelers and asks them to return it to Innkeeper Grosk.

item:uncloven-satyr-hoof.text: Uncloven Satyr Hoof. In Ashenvale, Uncloven Satyr Hooves hold the power satyrs steal from the ancient forest. Ula'elek uses that power to forge armor in Sen'jin Village. Satyrs haunt the corrupted groves of northeastern Ashenvale, feeding on the ancient forest’s magic. The more they consume, the more corruption twists their demonic bodies. Their hooves swell and lose their cleft, becoming dense stores of the energy they have absorbed. Skilled shamans and leatherworkers can harvest that volatile power. At Sen'jin Village on Durotar’s coast, Ula'elek turns demonic corruption into strength for Horde champions. The troll armorer takes hooves from satyrs that have fed on the forest and draws out their trapped magic. Then he channels that stolen power into brutal gauntlets, armor for young warriors facing the rigors of Kalimdor.

item:underbelly-whelp-scale.text: Underbelly Whelp Scale. South of Lake Everstill, Redridge craftsmen trade Underbelly Whelp Scale. Black dragon whelps provide the pliable scales, valued by local artisans when coin runs short. Black dragons bear tough scales, but an ordinary person cannot safely face a full-grown one. South of Lake Everstill, black dragon whelps nest among the crags. Their back plates may be brittle or coarse, while the softer scales beneath their bellies bend more readily and still protect. So Underbelly Whelp Scale has value in local trade. Craftsmen prize it, and creditors may accept it in place of coin. When coin runs short or trade routes strain, Lakeshire craftsmen sometimes barter. Verner Osgood, the local blacksmith, owes a heavy debt to Argus, a blacksmith in Goldshire. The debt began with a shipment of shoes brought from Goldshire. Argus favors rare trade goods, so Verner relies on travelers to gather underbelly whelp scales. They can help settle what he owes and keep his workshop in good standing.

item:unidentified-ore.text:
Unidentified Ore. At Windshear Crag, Unidentified Ore has drawn the Venture Company's attention. Piznik recovered a sample and gave it to Ziz Fizziks for study in Undermine. The Venture Company has exposed unusual mineral strata in the Stonetalon Mountains through clear-cutting and strip mining at Windshear Crag. Its new boss, Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, ordered large amounts of strange gold-green ore mined.

Demoted goblin worker Piznik stayed loyal to his fired former boss, Ziz Fizziks. He secured a sample while planning his escape from the outfit, then gave it to a traveler bound for the crag's western ridge. Ziz plans to send most of the ore to Undermine for study and keep a small cut for himself.

item:unrefined-ore-sample.text: Unrefined Ore Sample. In Thousand Needles, the Horde seeks a sample of unusual ore. Tatternack Steelforge wants to learn whether it can strengthen Warchief Thrall's armies. South of the Barrens, Gravelsnout kobolds dig beneath the canyon walls of Thousand Needles. Travelers returning north found a curious mineral among slain vermin. It was unlike the usual veins of Kalimdor. They refused to give their find to the Horde. The kobolds who dig and survey the depths carry raw chunks from their excavations. At Camp Taurajo, weaponsmith Tatternack Steelforge works under Warchief Thrall's orders to improve the Horde's arms. Travelers who knew of the deposit angered him by refusing to share it. He saw their refusal as an insult to the Horde's war effort. With a raw sample, Tatternack plans to test the ore's strength and temper. Then he will smelt it and forge a prototype blade for Orgrimmar's approval.

item:ur-s-treatise-on-shadow-magic.text: Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. Stormwind's mages once guarded Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic, fearing what its pages could bring. Now the tome lies hidden in the Tower of Ilgalar, stolen by Morganth. Ur of Dalaran wrote of shadow magic and its subtle, corruptive nature. The mages of Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum feared these arts could bring doom to the unwary, so they sealed the volume against readers. After Morganth gave himself to dark arts and Stormwind's magical circle exiled him, he carried the tome east into the Redridge Mountains. There he made his stronghold in the Tower of Ilgalar.

item:urgent-message.text:
Urgent Message. Brave Moonhorn warns Freewind Post that centaur raids are growing across Thousand Needles. Travelers and the roads are in danger. Near the Great Lift from the Barrens into Thousand Needles, Brave Moonhorn writes Urgent Message. From there, Moonhorn watches the jagged canyons below as centaur tribes renew their raids on Horde travelers.

The letter is bound for Cliffwatcher Longhorn atop Freewind Post. Moonhorn warns that attackers have grown bolder and strike near important roads. The garrison must prepare for more fighting and watch for the unpredictable Grimtotem clan.

item:valdred-s-hands.text: Valdred's Hands. In southern Silverpine Forest, Valdred Moray’s severed hands are sought as proof of vengeance. Raleigh Andrean wants them as a grim trophy for his wife’s murder. The plague ended the friendship between Valdred Moray and Raleigh Andrean. Valdred had murdered Raleigh’s wife, Deliah. Raleigh died and rose as one of the Forsaken, believing he could no longer truly grieve. Yet vengeance still mattered to him. When Valdred fled south past the Greymane Wall toward Gilneas, Raleigh sent an emissary after his former friend. He demanded Valdred’s severed hands as proof the deed was done.

item:velinde-s-journal.text: Velinde's Journal. In Darnassus, Velinde Starsong's journal records her duties and the mystery of her departure. The Night Elf priestess's journal rests in the Sentinel bunkhouse. When Night Elf priestess Velinde Starsong left Darnassus, the Sentinels locked her belongings in a footlocker at their bunkhouse in the Tradesmen's Terrace. Her personal journal was among them, recording her responsibilities and duties. The Sentinels respected Velinde and believed she had gone to attend to private matters. But her words suggest her absence troubles them more than they first thought.

item:velinde-s-key.text: Velinde's Key. In Darnassus, Thyn'tel Bladeweaver keeps Velinde's Key for those who seek the vanished priestess's fate. It guards her writings and belongings. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver keeps Velinde's Key in Darnassus. The simple key opens a footlocker holding Priestess Velinde Starsong's personal belongings. It rests in the Sentinel bunkhouse above the Tradesmen's Terrace. Velinde left night elf lands without warning, so her possessions were set aside. Bladeweaver lends the key only to those who bring genuine proof of their interest in her fate, such as revelations from the Tome of Mel'Thandris.

item:venomtail-antidote.text: Venomtail Antidote. In Durotar, Rhinag lies stricken by scorpid venom, and time is running short. Kor'ghan brews the antidote in Orgrimmar for the scout near the northwestern border. A deep sting from Durotar's venomtail scorpids can kill a warrior within an hour. Rhinag, a troll scout, was envenomed near the northwestern border, far from aid. His only hope is a remedy from Kor'ghan, an apothecary in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. Kor'ghan works beneath Orgrimmar, where he knows desert toxins and harsh remedies. He prepares a vial to purge the venom before it turns fatal. The draught stops the poison and spares Rhinag a humiliating death in the wilderness. Even so, Kor'ghan demands further trials and hunts from the scout to atone for his carelessness.

item:venomtail-poison-sac.text:
Venomtail Poison Sac. In Durotar, a scorpion's venom can bring a hunter near death, and its poison sac holds what alchemists need for a cure. Scorpids roam Durotar’s red rocks. Venomtail Scorpids, Corrupted Scorpids, and the Death Flayer all carry sacs filled with fast-acting venom. Left untreated, the poison can overwhelm even seasoned warriors. Yet those same sacs hold the chief compounds alchemists need for an antidote.

When a scorpion stung the hunter Rhinag outside Orgrimmar, local alchemists needed four fresh poison sacs. They would use them to make a remedy and neutralize the venom in his veins.

item:venture-co-documents.text: Venture Co. Documents. In eastern Mulgore, Venture Co. Documents expose the company's illegal mining in tauren lands. Recovered from a crate in a ruined caravan, the papers record its operations. Venture Co. Documents lay atop mined ore in a ransacked wagon. Their ledgers show that the goblin-led cartel has set up drilling and mining outposts in Mulgore's eastern foothills. Across Kalimdor, the Venture Company is known for ruthless deforestation and uncontrolled excavation. Morin Cloudstalker and the tauren Outrunners study the seized records to judge the threat to their sacred ancestral plains and rally hunters against the trespassers.

item:venture-co-engineering-plans.text: Venture Co. Engineering Plans. At Windshear Crag, Alliance operatives seek the Venture Co. Engineering Plans inside the goblin mill. The schematics show how the logging machines are built. South of Cragpool Lake, inside the lumber mill, the Venture Co. Engineering Plans reveal how the timber machines are built. They show the machines’ strengths and flaws. The Venture Company uses them to strip the forests of Stonetalon, while smoke hangs over Windshear Crag.

item:venture-co-letters.text: Venture Co. Letters. At Windshear Mine, Venture Co. Letters carry word of the cartel’s work in Stonetalon Mountains. Recovered during a covert operation, they give the night elf Sentinels intelligence on goblin operations. Venture Company machines cut timber and strip-mine the ancient woodland around Windshear Crag. Alliance operatives set off covert sabotage to distract the workers and enter Windshear Mine. There, they recover letters with private messages and logistical records of the company’s local work. Sentinel leaders can use them to learn how the defilers arrange their workforce and supply lines.

item:verdant-note.text: Verdant Note. At Camp Narache, Verdant Note calls young tauren druids to their training. Sent for Gart Mistrunner, it guides them toward the rites of the Earthmother. Young tauren gifted in nature receive Verdant Note soon after their trials begin at Red Cloud Mesa. A messenger brings Gart Mistrunner's brief summons to Camp Narache, where each initiate must report to the mentor. Restless spirits and shifting elements trouble Mulgore. The elders need new druids trained quickly. At Camp Narache, Gart Mistrunner teaches initiates to commune with nature. He warns that night elves share a bond with the wild, yet ancient pride keeps them distant from tauren. Tauren druidism centers on reverence for the Earthmother. Initiates learn to hear the land's restless ancestral voices and serve as her living instruments.

item:verdant-sigil.text: Verdant Sigil. In Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine sends young night elf druids toward the start of their training with the Verdant Sigil. Young night elves in Shadowglen receive the Verdant Sigil when they feel the call of the wild. Conservator Ilthalaine gives it to them with a message from Mardant Strongoak, their druid trainer. It directs the novices to climb into Aldrassil's boughs and begin their serious study. There they leave basic chores behind to learn communion with nature spirits and the mysteries of the Emerald Dream. Presenting the Verdant Sigil to Mardant Strongoak begins a young druid's lifelong craft. Novices cannot yet walk the sleeping trance of the Emerald Dream, but the token marks the start of their mentorship. Under Mardant's instruction, they learn to read the wilderness's whispers. They also practice early shapeshifting and healing arts in service of Teldrassil.

item:verna-s-westfall-stew-recipe.text:
Verna's Westfall Stew Recipe. As the Furlbrows prepare to leave their Westfall farm, Verna sends her stew recipe to Salma Saldean. Its familiar comfort may remain for those who stay. Verna and Farmer Furlbrow have made their home in Westfall for years. Now the Defias Brotherhood and rogue harvest golems run rampant across the countryside. The Furlbrows wait for their wagon to be repaired so they can flee toward Stormwind.

While they wait, Verna writes down her beloved Westfall Stew formula. She entrusts it to travelers bound for her neighboring friend, Salma Saldean. That way, those left behind may still know the stew's familiar comfort.

item:verner-s-note.text: Verner's Note. In Redridge, Verner Osgood sends a written requisition west to Smith Argus in Goldshire. It reports Lakeshire's iron shortage and asks for horseshoes from Elwynn. Lakeshire's defense has used nearly all Verner Osgood's iron. The town's blacksmith spent his reserves arming and armoring the Stormwind Guard, stretched thin against invading gnolls and local perils. Meanwhile, the stables have fallen into neglect, and their mounts lack even basic horseshoes. Verner asks Smith Argus in Goldshire to send prepared shoes from Elwynn, so Lakeshire can shoe its horses.

item:verog-s-head.text:
Verog's Head. Regthar Deathgate seeks Verog's Head as proof that the Kolkar leader has fallen. Verog commands forces around the Stagnant Oasis, and his defeat is meant to weaken the tribes threatening the Barrens. The Kolkar threaten Horde travelers and supply routes across the northern Barrens. Verog the Dervish roams the arid scrubland, leaving his command tent at the Stagnant Oasis vulnerable. Horde operatives attack his forces around the pavilion until an alarm sounds.

Verog rushes back to defend his camp, where he is slain and decapitated. Regthar Deathgate receives his head as proof that another dangerous Kolkar chieftain has fallen. Barak Kodobane's head is already displayed beside it.

item:vial-of-innocent-blood.text: Vial of Innocent Blood. In the ruins of Durnholde Keep, Syndicate shadow mages gather Vial of Innocent Blood. The Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill seeks it as a catalyst for experimental toxins. Syndicate shadow mages gather innocent blood among the ruins of Durnholde Keep. The Syndicate's fallen human nobles practice dark arts within the crumbled walls. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon seeks untainted blood for an experimental pacifying agent. He plans to use it against the Venture Company in Stonetalon Mountains, and the Syndicate's stores offer a convenient source.

item:vial-of-phlogiston.text: Vial of Phlogiston. At Razorfen Kraul, phlogiston draws smiths from the Alliance and Horde. Master armorers use it to temper mail for promising warriors, while quilboar guard it in their stronghold. Phlogiston bears volatile fire and has a place in esoteric metalwork. Furen Longbeard, a dwarven smith in Stormwind, needs it, as does Thun'grim Firegaze, a near-blind orc armorer in the Barrens. Both use it to harden warrior armor beyond ordinary physical limits. Without this alchemical agent, neither can complete the specialized forging of Fire Hardened Mail or the Horde's Brutal Armor. A vial of phlogiston lies deep in Razorfen Kraul, amid the tangled thickets at the southern tip of the Barrens. The geomancer Roogug holds it in the bristling redoubt. Whether it is bound for Furen in Stormwind or for Thun'grim's anvil across the dust, reaching it means a perilous descent into hostile quilboar territory.

item:vial-of-purest-water.text: Vial of Purest Water. In the southern Barrens, Brine blesses pure water for a shaman initiate. Islen Waterseer needs it to prepare a water sapta that lets the initiate see elemental spirits. Brine leads the initiate through trials of patience and cleansing, then seals the water in the vial. Its purity is untouched by corruption. Carry it across the Barrens to Islen Waterseer, who watches over a solitary shore. She needs the water to brew a water sapta, for only such pure water lets a shaman commune with spiritual guardians far from the sunbaked flats.

item:vial-of-spider-venom.text: Vial of Spider Venom. In Duskwood, Madame Eva gathers venomous spiders' poison to make a ward against attackers. She needs it alongside undead remains for a Totem of Infliction. Duskwood's thickets shelter venomous spiders, from pygmy venom webs and green recluses to black widows and Naraxis. Their fangs carry poison potent enough to paralyze travelers and decay flesh. Those who kill the spiders can draw the fluid into intact vials. In Darkshire, fortune teller Madame Eva sees ominous portents for travelers setting out into the dark world. She needs five vials of spider venom, ghoul fangs, and skeleton fingers to craft a ward of retribution. Her craft turns the venom’s biting nature against attackers. The Totem of Infliction returns harm to anyone who strikes its bearer.

item:vicious-night-web-spider-venom.text: Vicious Night Web Spider Venom. In eastern Tirisfal, Vicious Night Web Spider Venom preserves an ancient contagion. The Royal Apothecary Society prizes it for the disease strains it holds and studies it in their work on the Forsaken's New Plague. Apothecary Johaan in Brill studies old texts about a plague that killed thousands. The contagion behind that outbreak endured for centuries in the venom of local Night Web spiders. Apothecaries hunt the vicious breed in Venomweb Vale, south of the Scarlet Monastery, then draw out the preserved contagion for their alchemical experiments.

item:vile-familiar-head.text:
Vile Familiar Head. Near the Burning Blade Coven, Vile Familiar Heads test young Horde warlocks. Under Ruzan's guidance, novices gather six gruesome trophies to prove they are ready to bind their first demonic minions. The trial calls for discipline and respect for the danger of the beings they mean to summon. In the Valley of Trials, Ruzan asks novices who seek to learn summoning to bring him six Vile Familiar Heads. The fiery imps called vile familiars lurk outside the Burning Blade Coven. Their elemental cunning makes them dangerous foes. To pass, novices must face and defeat them, proving they can master demonic life rather than be overcome by it.

Warlocks are barely tolerated within Thrall's Horde, so their training demands care. A novice slain by a conjured creature would deepen the dishonor and suspicion cast upon those who practice the dark arts.

item:vile-fin-scale.text: Vile Fin Scale. Along Tirisfal’s northern coasts and waterways, Vile Fin Scale comes from the murloc tribes. In Brill, the Royal Apothecary Society studies these samples while seeking a plague to strike the living and the Scourge. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks a blight that can spread through the living and the Scourge. Simple toxins are easy to brew, but an infectious disease must pass from one population to another. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan studies Vile Fin scales for their natural resilience and mucous coatings. He hopes these traits will steady his experimental contagions and help them spread. The Vile Fin tribe lives along Tirisfal Glades’ northern shores and western shallows. Its members threaten travelers and press into Forsaken territory. Gathering their scales helps check the feral murloc population and gives Johaan’s laboratory fresh organic material for tests in biological warfare.

item:voodoo-charm.text: Voodoo Charm. In Teldrassil’s barrows, Oben Rageclaw’s body remains bound by Gnarlpine enchantment. The Voodoo Charm can break that hold.

item:wailing-essence.text:
Wailing Essence. In the Wailing Caverns, Wailing Essence gathers within roaming ectoplasms. Alchemists seek its potent properties, while nearby druids dread the mutations spreading through the Barrens. Beneath the central Barrens, unnatural energy twists beasts and gives rise to gelatinous ectoplasms. Within them lies a viscous substance called Wailing Essence. Nearby druids watch the waters with growing dread, while goblin traders see a chance for profit.

In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix believes the essence is the missing ingredient for a lucrative line of “smart drinks” meant to sharpen the mind. The eccentric alchemist gives little thought to the corruption they might carry.

item:warsong-axe-shipment.text: Warsong Axe Shipment. In Booty Bay, the Warsong Axe Shipment waits to cross the Great Sea for Ashenvale. The newly forged axes are bound for the Warsong Outriders and the work at their lumber camp. Axes for the Warsong Lumber Camp wait in Booty Bay. The camp’s woodcutters need durable tools, and not every tool can be forged on the front lines. So their orders cross the Great Sea to this neutral goblin port, where the crate rests near Wharfmaster Lozgil. The sharpened axes are meant for Splintertree Post, then can travel onward to the camp. Keeping distant frontier camps supplied takes a long voyage.

item:warsong-oil.text: Warsong Oil. At the Warsong Lumber Camp, Warsong Oil keeps the machinery turning. Satyrs have taken a shipment into their corrupted enclaves. Warsong Oil keeps the Warsong Clan’s logging machinery running in Ashenvale. Goblin-engineered shredders and great sawmills depend on its steady supply. Without the lubricant, timber cutting could stop. Then the lumber needed to build Orgrimmar and strengthen Horde settlements across Durotar and the Barrens would slow. Satyrs ambushed a shipment of Warsong Oil before it could reach Splintertree Post and the logging camps. They carried the containers into corrupted enclaves, including Night Run, Satyrnaar, and Xavian. There, the satyrs use the flammable lubricant in their rituals.

item:warsong-outrider-update.text:
Warsong Outrider Update. Along Ashenvale’s eastern border, a Warsong Outrider prepares the Warsong Outrider Update. Stationed there, the outrider records frontline intelligence for Horde couriers to carry. The reports help secure the crossing toward Azshara and strengthen the orcish foothold against night elf resistance. Beyond Splintertree Post, the eastern road crosses Ashenvale’s volatile borderlands toward the ancient ruins of Azshara. Mounted orcish vanguards patrol this frontier and record tactical sightings, patrol movements, and resource evaluations.

They send their field notes to Kadrak at the northern watchtower, which guards the Barrens border. The reports give Horde commanders a clear view of enemy troop concentrations and territorial threats beneath the forest canopy.

item:warsong-runner-update.text: Warsong Runner Update. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Warsong Runner Update carries word from western Ashenvale to Kadrak. At Zoram'gar Outpost, the Warsong runner watches the coast and nearby threats in western Ashenvale. Scouts gather observations there, and the dispatch records what they see. It travels to Kadrak's watchtower on the Barrens border. The report helps Horde leaders strengthen their position and plan movements into the elves' ancestral woods.

item:warsong-saw-blades.text: Warsong Saw Blades. At the Warsong Lumber Camp, saw blades keep the Horde's logging machines cutting in Ashenvale. The Warsong Clan depends on goblin-made machinery to harvest lumber across the forest. In Ashenvale, the Warsong Clan depends on heavy machinery supplied and maintained by goblin engineers. Axes cannot meet the Horde's demand for Kalimdor lumber, so steam engines and circular saws cut the timber. Ashenvale's ancient hardwood quickly dulls and breaks ordinary blades. Fresh saw blades must reach the mills at the Warsong Lumber Camp to keep them running. Parts must cross disputed territory, where hostile furbolgs and satyrs often intercept logging supplies. Goblin contacts such as Pixel at Splintertree Post handle the saw blade shipments. Lumber master Locke Okarr gathers blades with rope, oil, and axes, keeping the camp operating despite sabotage from Ashenvale's defenders.

item:warsong-scout-update.text: Warsong Scout Update. At Splintertree Post, Warsong scouts send the Horde word on Ashenvale. Warsong scouts watch the woods as the Horde seeks timber and supply routes through Ashenvale. From fortified Splintertree Post, they follow night elf sentinels and movements across the territory. Their observations reach Kadrak at the Barrens-Ashenvale border among routine orders. He uses them to judge troop readiness and coordinate supplies and travel through the contested woods.

item:water-of-the-seers.text: Water of the Seers. In Bloodhoof Village, young tauren drink the sacred Water of the Seers before their tribal trials. The draught opens their minds to the spirit world and calls a Plains Vision to guide them. Young tauren drink the Water of the Seers before the tribal fire in Bloodhoof Village. Tribal mystics prepare the draught for the ancient Rite of Vision. It opens the drinker’s spiritual sight. Then the Plains Vision rises from the embers and guides the way to Seer Wiserunner.

item:water-pitcher.text: Water Pitcher. At Red Cloud Mesa, Water Pitcher carries fresh well water to Camp Narache. Greatmother Hawkwind asks young tauren to bring it back and learn humility, service, and respect for tribal elders. Water Pitcher rests beside the well southeast of Camp Narache. Greatmother Hawkwind asks a novice to fill it and carry it to Chief Hawkwind. The chore tests their character and teaches young braves that no duty is beneath a tribal protector. Tending to their kin’s everyday needs matters as much as bearing a weapon on the hunt.

item:webwood-egg.text: Webwood Egg. In Shadowthread Cave, Webwood Eggs lie in nests in Shadowglen. Naturalists seek viable eggs so they can study the young spiders in secure laboratories. A grown Webwood spider is venomous and too dangerous for one researcher to tame or subdue. So scholars like Gilshalan Windwalker collect unhatched eggs from clutches hidden in Shadowthread Cave. The eggs can be carried safely, and the spiderlings kept contained when they hatch. Naturalists can study them without facing the deadly fangs of adult spiders. Teldrassil’s native wildlife has grown unnaturally aggressive and corrupted, alarming scholars across the boughs. Eggs and gathered venoms secured at Aldrassil are bound for Darnassus. Researchers hope that raising and examining the spiders in controlled settings will reveal more about the dark affliction spreading through the World Tree’s boughs.

item:webwood-ichor.text: Webwood Ichor. In Shadowglen, Webwood Ichor is needed to save Iverron from spider venom. Dirania Silvershine needs it with hyacinth mushrooms and moonpetal lilies to brew an antidote. Webwood spiders in Shadowglen carry venom that has left Iverron gravely ill. Dirania Silvershine asks for their ichor, hyacinth mushrooms, and moonpetal lilies to brew an antidote.

item:webwood-spider-silk.text: Webwood Spider Silk. Among Teldrassil’s boughs, Webwood Spider Silk draws the interest of suspicious figures. Webwood Lurkers spin it in the woods, and crafters put spider silk to many uses. Webwood Lurkers near Dolanaar spin a fine, strong thread that is perilous to gather. Zenn Foulhoof, a satyr along the forest road, asks young adventurers for the silk, nightsaber fangs, and strigid owl feathers. He claims these rare reagents serve his forest business. Newcomers gather them without asking about his corrupt nature or true motives.

item:webwood-venom-sac.text: Webwood Venom Sac. In Shadowglen, naturalists study Webwood Venom Sacs to learn how Teldrassil's growth has changed local wildlife. The sacs come from overgrown spiders, and their venom may offer clues. Webwood spiders haunt Shadowthread Cave and the ground around it. They are cousins to a much smaller breed found elsewhere. Their sudden growth and predatory aggression trouble night elf researchers. Naturalists such as Gilshalan Windwalker study the venom's strength and composition, hoping to learn how Teldrassil's rapid, unblessed growth is changing the creatures on its boughs.

item:well-stone.text:
Well Stone. Across Mulgore, Well Stones rest beside the water wells. Their earth and water magic helps prepare the Water of the Seers for tauren rites of passage. Beside Mulgore’s wells, Well Stones rest in the soft earth. They take in the spiritual resonance of the plains and the waters beneath them. Shaman and seers such as Zarlman Two-Moons know they hold vital magic. They are more than ordinary river pebbles.

With Ambercorn gathered beneath the plains’ mighty trees, the stones’ minerals temper a brew. It awakens visionary trances in young tauren during the sacred Rite of Vision.

item:wendigo-mane.text: Wendigo Mane. Across Dun Morogh, wendigos roam the frozen crags, and their manes keep the mountain cold at bay. Pilot Stonegear has a use for them. Wendigos roam the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh, their coarse fur guarding them from bitter drafts. Outside Kharanos, Pilot Stonegear sends adventurers to Grizzled Den for their heavy manes. He means to weave them into an insulating rug for the interior deck of Trollplow, his prized dwarven siege engine.

item:whitestone-oak-lumber.text: Whitestone Oak Lumber. Beneath Moonbrook, the Defias shape Whitestone Oak Lumber for their fleet. Its strength also draws Alliance smiths seeking a haft for a sacred weapon.

item:wildmane-cleansing-totem.text:
Wildmane Cleansing Totem. At Mulgore’s Wildmane Water Well, one last cleansing remains. After the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells are cleansed, Mull Thunderhorn prepares a totem for the well north of Thunder Bluff. The Wildmane Water Well still needs cleansing. Goblin ventures have poisoned the land and fouled Mulgore’s scarce water. So the tauren turn to sacred ritual against the blight.

After the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells are cleansed, Mull Thunderhorn crafts a final totem for the well north of Thunder Bluff. Natural spirits fill it, and it purifies the fetid water so life can nourish the plains again.

item:wiley-s-note.text: Wiley's Note. At Lakeshire, Wiley the Black writes a confidential note for Gryan Stoutmantle to repay a debt. Its contents point to alliances made by the Defias Brotherhood, drawing Stormwind's intelligence service into the inquiry. Wiley the Black, a rogue in Lakeshire, writes the dispatch in Redridge. He gives it to Gryan Stoutmantle to repay an old favor. In the note, Wiley tells what he knows of the Defias Brotherhood's plans. The Brotherhood has allies among regional gnolls, kobolds, and goblin operatives.

item:william-s-shipment.text: William's Shipment. In Goldshire, William's Shipment is bound for his brother Morgan in Stormwind, carrying candles from Elwynn's kobolds. William Pestle keeps trade moving between Goldshire and the capital. He gathers goods in Elwynn Forest, while his brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot leave his duties to travel north, so couriers carry the wax and candles into the city. Kobold candles from Elwynn's mines fill William's shipment. He gathers the large candles for their wax and packs them for Morgan at Pestle's Apothecary. That wax joins the stock used in the capital's alchemical trade.

item:wine-ticket.text: Wine Ticket. In Stormwind, Renato Gallina draws customers to his family's shop with Wine Tickets. Present one to Suzetta Gallina for a complimentary bottle of Pinot Noir. Near Stormwind's Trade District, Renato Gallina hands out printed tickets to promote the Gallina Winery. The boutique vintage shop sits along the nearby canals. Each ticket offers a complimentary sample of Pinot Noir, drawing curious passersby and newly arrived adventurers to the family business in hope they become loyal customers.

item:winterhoof-cleansing-totem.text:
Winterhoof Cleansing Totem. At Winterhoof Water Well, poisoned water threatens the herds and tribes of Mulgore. Mull Thunderhorn prepares a totem to cleanse the well. Mull Thunderhorn crafts the Winterhoof Cleansing Totem in Bloodhoof Village. Venture Company goblins have tainted Mulgore's underground water through their operations. He charms the carved wood to wash away those foreign poisons.

The totem must be carried past hostile goblin guards to Winterhoof Water Well. There, a focused ritual disperses the contamination. Pure drinking water returns for the plains' wandering herds and native tribes.

item:witchwing-talon.text: Witchwing Talon. In the northwestern Barrens, Witchwing Talons mark fallen harpy raiders. At the Crossroads, Horde scouts seek them as proof while working to secure vital caravan routes. Witchwing harpies raid Horde supply caravans from roosts northwest of the Crossroads. Scout Darsok Swiftdagger coordinates strikes against the flock's hierarchy. He requires proof that each scavenger has been killed, and the talons provide it. With proof of their fall, the scouts can thin the flock before striking higher in its command.

item:wolf-heart-sample.text: Wolf Heart Sample. In the Barrens, Wolf Heart Sample carries diseased wolf tissue from Lordaeron to the Crossroads. The Royal Apothecary Society studies what northern toxins do to Kalimdor’s native beasts. Plagued wolves in Lordaeron’s ruins gave Apothecary Renferrel the hearts packed into Wolf Heart Sample. They crossed the Great Sea for the Forsaken’s Royal Apothecary Society, which studies venom, blights and biological reagents. A courier carries them to the Crossroads, joining Undercity’s experiments in the scarred Eastern Kingdoms to Kalimdor’s frontier outposts.
